Driven by the ideology of 'Manifest Destiny' -- the belief that American expansion was divinely ordained. Involved the Louisiana Purchase (1803), Mexican-American War, Oregon Trail migration, and California Gold Rush. Resulted in massive displacement of Native Americans.

hist_napoleon_bonaparte.label: Napoleon Bonaparte
hist_napoleon_bonaparte.subject: history
hist_napoleon_bonaparte.detail: Rose to power after Directory's instability. Crowned Emperor in 1804. Conquered much of Europe, introduced uniform laws, metric system, protection of private property. Defeated at Waterloo in 1815. Rose to power after Directory collapse. Crowned Emperor 1804. Conquered most of Europe. Uniform laws, metric system. Defeated at Leipzig 1813 and Waterloo 1815. Died in exile on St. Helena 1821.

hist_napoleon_reforms.label: Napoleon's Administrative Reforms
hist_napoleon_reforms.subject: history
hist_napoleon_reforms.detail: Napoleon introduced Civil Code 1804 abolishing birth-based privileges, establishing equality before law, securing property rights. Simplified administrative divisions, abolished feudal system, improved transport. Initially seen as liberator, later as invader. Civil Code 1804 (Code Napoléon) abolished birth privileges, established equality before law, secured property rights. Metric system, uniform administration. Initially hailed as liberator, later resented as invader.

hist_settler_colonialism.label: Settler Colonialism
hist_settler_colonialism.subject: history
hist_settler_colonialism.detail: Form of colonialism where settlers permanently occupy and displace indigenous peoples from their lands. Unlike extractive colonialism (which exploited resources and labour), settler colonialism aimed to replace the native population. Occurred in North America, Australia, South Africa, and parts of South America from the 16th century onward.

hist_urbanisation_london.label: Urbanisation of London
hist_urbanisation_london.subject: history
hist_urbanisation_london.detail: London grew from 1 million (1810) to 6.5 million (1880). Industrialisation drew migrants. Five-six people lived per tenement room. Cholera and typhoid epidemics led to public health reforms and underground railway (1863).

hist_luddites.label: Luddites
hist_luddites.subject: history
hist_luddites.detail: Workers who protested against labour-saving machinery by destroying it, active particularly in 1811-1816 in England. Named after the possibly mythical Ned Ludd. Mainly textile workers (croppers, framework knitters) whose skills were being made obsolete. The government suppressed them harshly with military force and hangings.

hist_urbanisation_industrial.label: Industrial Urbanisation
hist_urbanisation_industrial.subject: history
hist_urbanisation_industrial.detail: Rapid growth of industrial cities like Manchester, Birmingham, Leeds, and Sheffield. Manchester grew from 25,000 (1772) to 300,000 (1850). Cities suffered from overcrowding, pollution, disease (cholera, typhus), lack of sanitation, and child labour. Eventually led to public health reforms and urban planning.

hist_working_class.label: Industrial Working Class
hist_working_class.subject: history
hist_working_class.detail: New social class of wage labourers in factories, mines, and mills. Worked 14-16 hour days in dangerous conditions for low wages. Women and children formed a large part of the workforce. Workers gradually organised into trade unions and Chartist movement to demand rights. Their conditions inspired socialist thought.

hist_lord_dalhousie.label: Lord Dalhousie
hist_lord_dalhousie.subject: history
hist_lord_dalhousie.detail: Governor-General (1848-1856) who aggressively expanded British territory through Doctrine of Lapse and outright annexation. Annexed Satara, Jhansi, Nagpur, Awadh and Punjab. His policies directly provoked many groups who later joined the 1857 revolt.

hist_fifth_report_1813.label: Fifth Report (1813)
hist_fifth_report_1813.subject: history
hist_fifth_report_1813.detail: Report submitted to British Parliament in 1813 on East India Company's administration in India. Over 1000 pages with appendices. Shaped British views of Indian land revenue. Cited extensively by critics of Company misrule. Perspective influenced by colonial revenue collectors.

hist_tantia_tope.label: Tantia Tope
hist_tantia_tope.subject: history
hist_tantia_tope.detail: Military commander who fought alongside Nana Sahib at Kanpur and later with Rani Lakshmibai. Led guerrilla warfare across Central India after fall of major rebel centres. Betrayed by a former associate, captured and executed by the British in April 1859.

hist_congress_of_vienna.label: Congress of Vienna 1815
hist_congress_of_vienna.subject: history
hist_congress_of_vienna.detail: Met in 1815 after Napoleon's defeat. Hosted by Austrian Chancellor Metternich. Restored conservative monarchies, redrew European boundaries to create buffer states. Sought to undo revolutionary changes and balance power. Hosted by Austrian Chancellor Metternich. Restored conservative monarchies, redrew boundaries to create buffer states (Netherlands, Prussia's Rhine gain). Aimed to undo revolutionary ideals.

hist_begum_hazrat_mahal.label: Begum Hazrat Mahal
hist_begum_hazrat_mahal.subject: history
hist_begum_hazrat_mahal.detail: Wife of deposed Nawab of Awadh who led the revolt in Lucknow on behalf of her son Birjis Qadr. Organised military resistance against the British. Countered Queen Victoria's proclamation with her own proclamation. Fled to Nepal after defeat.

hist_hill_stations.label: Hill Stations
hist_hill_stations.subject: history
hist_hill_stations.detail: Colonial settlements at high altitudes: Shimla, Darjeeling, Ooty, Mount Abu. Served as summer capitals and sanatoriums. Shimla became summer capital of British India. Designed to replicate English countryside. Reflected racial segregation and colonial health anxieties.

hist_james_mill_education.label: James Mill on Education
hist_james_mill_education.subject: history
hist_james_mill_education.detail: James Mill attacked Orientalists, arguing education should teach what was useful and practical rather than pleasing natives. Indians should learn Western science and technical advances, not Oriental poetry and sacred literature.

hist_ryotwari_settlement.label: Ryotwari Settlement
hist_ryotwari_settlement.subject: history
hist_ryotwari_settlement.detail: System introduced in Bombay and Madras Presidencies where revenue was settled directly with individual cultivators (ryots). No intermediary zamindars. Revenue demand could be revised periodically. Devised by Thomas Munro and Alexander Read.

hist_raja_rammohun_roy_press.label: Rammohun Roy and Press Freedom
hist_raja_rammohun_roy_press.subject: history
hist_raja_rammohun_roy_press.detail: Published Sambad Kaumudi in Bengali and Mirat-ul-Akhbar in Persian. Protested Press Regulations of 1823 arguing free press needed for reform. Petitioned against censorship as violation of natural rights. Published Sambad Kaumudi (Bengali) and Mirat-ul-Akhbar (Persian). Protested 1823 Press Regulations, argued free press is a natural right.

hist_caste_clothing_india.label: Clothing and Caste in India
hist_caste_clothing_india.subject: history
hist_caste_clothing_india.detail: Strict codes governed what different castes could wear. Shanars/Nadars of Travancore forbidden from covering upper bodies. Their struggle to wear cloth on upper body became a movement for dignity and equality.

hist_mahalwari_settlement.label: Mahalwari Settlement
hist_mahalwari_settlement.subject: history
hist_mahalwari_settlement.detail: Revenue system introduced in North-Western Provinces, Punjab and parts of Central India. Revenue settled with village or mahal as a unit. Devised by Holt Mackenzie. Village headman collected and paid revenue on behalf of the entire village community.

hist_shanar_breast_cloth_movement.label: Shanar Breast Cloth Movement
hist_shanar_breast_cloth_movement.subject: history
hist_shanar_breast_cloth_movement.detail: Shanars of Travancore challenged caste prohibition on covering upper body. Converted Shanars began wearing cloth. Upper castes attacked them. British intervened in 1829 allowing converted Christian women to cover upper bodies.

hist_nana_sahib.label: Nana Sahib
hist_nana_sahib.subject: history
hist_nana_sahib.detail: Adopted son of Peshwa Baji Rao II. Led rebellion at Kanpur. Declared himself Peshwa. His claim to the Peshwa's pension had been denied by the British under the Doctrine of Lapse. Fled and disappeared after British recaptured Kanpur.

hist_trade_unions.label: Trade Unions
hist_trade_unions.subject: history
hist_trade_unions.detail: Workers' organisations formed to collectively bargain for wages, hours, and conditions. Initially illegal under the Combination Acts (1799-1800), legalised in 1824. The Grand National Consolidated Trades Union (1834) and later the Trades Union Congress (1868) were milestones. Unions became a major political force and contributed to the Labour movement.

hist_rani_lakshmibai.label: Rani Lakshmibai
hist_rani_lakshmibai.subject: history
hist_rani_lakshmibai.detail: Queen of Jhansi whose state was annexed under Doctrine of Lapse after her husband's death. Joined the revolt in 1857. Fought fiercely, captured Gwalior fort. Died fighting in June 1858. Became an iconic symbol of resistance. Hugh Rose called her 'the best and bravest' of rebel leaders. Died fighting Gwalior 17 June 1858. General Hugh Rose: "here lay the woman who was the only man among the rebels."

hist_raja_rammohun_roy.label: Raja Rammohun Roy
hist_raja_rammohun_roy.subject: history
hist_raja_rammohun_roy.detail: Founded Brahmo Sabha (later Brahmo Samaj) in Calcutta. Campaigned against sati using ancient texts to show it had no sanction. Advocated Western education and women's rights. Sati was banned in 1829 due to his efforts.

hist_sati_abolition.label: Abolition of Sati
hist_sati_abolition.subject: history
hist_sati_abolition.detail: Practice of widows being burnt on husband's funeral pyre was banned in 1829 through efforts of Rammohun Roy. He used ancient texts to prove it had no scriptural sanction, a strategy adopted by later reformers.

hist_brahmo_samaj.label: Brahmo Samaj
hist_brahmo_samaj.subject: history
hist_brahmo_samaj.detail: Reform association formed in 1830, prohibited idolatry and sacrifice, drew upon Upanishads. Led by Rammohun Roy, later by Keshub Chunder Sen. Critically drew upon ideals of Hinduism and Christianity.

hist_captain_swing.label: Captain Swing Riots
hist_captain_swing.subject: history
hist_captain_swing.detail: From 1830, labourers destroyed 387 threshing machines across southern England, protesting loss of livelihood to mechanisation. Letters signed 'Captain Swing'. Government response severe: 9 hanged, 505 transported to Australia.

hist_decline_indian_textiles.label: Decline of Indian Textiles
hist_decline_indian_textiles.subject: history
hist_decline_indian_textiles.detail: By the 1830s British cotton cloth flooded Indian markets. By the 1880s two-thirds of cotton clothes worn by Indians were British-made. Thousands of weavers and spinners lost their livelihood and became agricultural labourers or migrated.

hist_pathshala_system.label: Pathshala System
hist_pathshala_system.subject: history
hist_pathshala_system.detail: William Adam's report in 1830s found over 1 lakh pathshalas in Bengal and Bihar teaching over 20 lakh children. Flexible system with no fixed fees, timetable or examinations. After 1854, government imposed new rules destroying this flexibility. William Adam's 1830s report found ~1 lakh pathshalas in Bengal and Bihar teaching ~20 lakh children. Post-1854 Wood's Despatch eroded this flexibility.

hist_railways.label: Railways
hist_railways.subject: history
hist_railways.detail: George Stephenson's Rocket (1829) proved the viability of steam-powered railways. The Liverpool-Manchester line (1830) was the first intercity passenger railway. Railways transformed transportation, enabled rapid movement of goods and people, created massive demand for iron and coal, and opened up new markets. By 1850, Britain had 6,000 miles of track. Stephenson's Rocket 1829 proved viability. Liverpool-Manchester 1830 first intercity passenger railway. By 1850, Britain had ~6,000 miles of track.

hist_romantic_nationalism.label: Romantic Nationalism
hist_romantic_nationalism.subject: history
hist_romantic_nationalism.detail: Cultural movement using folk songs, poetry, dance to shape national identity. Grimm Brothers collected folk tales. Karol Kurpinski used polkas and polonaises for Polish national struggle. Language became marker of nationality.

hist_threshing_machine.label: Threshing Machine
hist_threshing_machine.subject: history
hist_threshing_machine.detail: Mechanical device that replaced hand threshing of grain. Its introduction in early 19th century England displaced agricultural labourers, triggering Captain Swing riots. Symbolised conflict between mechanisation and employment.

hist_trail_of_tears.label: Trail of Tears
hist_trail_of_tears.subject: history
hist_trail_of_tears.detail: Forced relocation of approximately 60,000 Native Americans (Cherokee, Creek, Chickasaw, Choctaw, Seminole) from their ancestral lands in the southeastern USA to Indian Territory (Oklahoma) in the 1830s. Thousands died from exposure, disease, and starvation during the march. Resulted from the Indian Removal Act (1830) signed by President Andrew Jackson.

hist_giuseppe_mazzini.label: Giuseppe Mazzini
hist_giuseppe_mazzini.subject: history
hist_giuseppe_mazzini.detail: Italian revolutionary who founded Young Italy and Young Europe. Believed in unitary Italian republic. Inspired nationalists across Europe and India. Metternich described him as 'the most dangerous enemy of our social order'. Italian revolutionary. Founded Young Italy (1831) and Young Europe. Believed in unitary Italian republic. Inspired nationalists across Europe and India. Metternich called him "most dangerous enemy of our social order".

hist_frontier_wars.label: Frontier Wars
hist_frontier_wars.subject: history
hist_frontier_wars.detail: Armed conflicts between settlers and indigenous peoples on expanding colonial frontiers. In North America, these included King Philip's War (1675), the Indian Wars of the 19th century (including the Battle of Little Bighorn, 1876, and Wounded Knee massacre, 1890). In Australia, the frontier wars (1788-1930s) resulted in the deaths of thousands of Aboriginal people.

hist_greek_independence.label: Greek War of Independence
hist_greek_independence.subject: history
hist_greek_independence.detail: Greeks struggled from 1821 against Ottoman Empire. Supported by Western Europeans inspired by ancient Greek culture. Treaty of Constantinople 1832 recognised Greece as independent. Lord Byron participated and died.

hist_reservations.label: Reservations / Reserves
hist_reservations.subject: history
hist_reservations.detail: Designated areas where indigenous peoples were confined after being displaced from their traditional lands. In the USA, the reservation system was formalised in the mid-19th century, confining tribes to often marginal lands. In Australia, Aboriginal reserves served a similar purpose. Represented a drastic reduction of indigenous territory and autonomy.

hist_child_labour_industrial.label: Child Labour in Industrialisation
hist_child_labour_industrial.subject: history
hist_child_labour_industrial.detail: Children as young as 5 worked in factories, mines, and chimneys. Factory Acts gradually restricted child labour: 1833 Act banned children under 9 in textile mills, 1842 Mines Act banned women and children underground. Reform was driven by public outcry, parliamentary investigations, and campaigns by humanitarians.

hist_indentured_labour.label: Indentured Labour Migration
hist_indentured_labour.subject: history
hist_indentured_labour.detail: After slavery abolition, Indian and Chinese workers hired on contracts for Caribbean, Fiji, Mauritius, Malaya plantations. Called 'new system of slavery'. Workers faced deception and harsh conditions. Created Indian diaspora.

hist_english_education_act_1835.label: English Education Act 1835
hist_english_education_act_1835.subject: history
hist_english_education_act_1835.detail: Made English the medium of instruction for higher education in India and stopped promotion of Oriental institutions like Calcutta Madrasa and Benaras Sanskrit College, which were called 'temples of darkness'.

hist_macaulay_minute.label: Macaulay's Minute on Education
hist_macaulay_minute.subject: history
hist_macaulay_minute.detail: Thomas Babington Macaulay argued that Eastern knowledge was inferior, declaring a single shelf of European library worth the whole native literature. Led to the English Education Act of 1835 making English the medium for higher education. Famously declared "a single shelf of a good European library was worth the whole native literature of India and Arabia".

hist_charles_dickens_novels.label: Charles Dickens
hist_charles_dickens_novels.subject: history
hist_charles_dickens_novels.detail: English novelist who depicted hardships of the poor and working class. Oliver Twist (1838) showed life in workhouses. Hard Times (1854) critiqued effects of industrialisation. Serialised in magazines, reaching wide audiences.

hist_james_prinsep.label: James Prinsep
hist_james_prinsep.subject: history
hist_james_prinsep.detail: Officer in the mint of the East India Company who deciphered Brahmi and Kharosthi scripts in the 1830s. Found that most early inscriptions mentioned a king called Piyadassi (Ashoka). This was a breakthrough for early Indian epigraphy.

hist_opium_wars.label: Opium Wars
hist_opium_wars.subject: history
hist_opium_wars.detail: Two wars between China and Britain (1839-42 and 1856-60) triggered by the opium trade. Britain exported Indian opium to China, creating addiction and draining Chinese silver. China's attempts to ban opium led to war. The Treaty of Nanking (1842) ceded Hong Kong, opened five treaty ports, and imposed extraterritoriality. A humiliating symbol of Western imperialism in China. First Opium War 1839-42; Second 1856-60. Treaty of Nanking ceded Hong Kong, opened 5 treaty ports (Canton, Amoy, Foochow, Ningpo, Shanghai), imposed extraterritoriality. Inaugurated China's "century of humiliation".

hist_kalighat_paintings.label: Kalighat Paintings
hist_kalighat_paintings.subject: history
hist_kalighat_paintings.detail: New art style developed by village scroll painters (patuas) and potters (kumors) who moved to Calcutta in early 19th century. Used bold non-realistic style with shading for three-dimensional effect. Later depicted social satire and nationalist themes.

hist_serialised_novel.label: Serialised Novels and Magazines
hist_serialised_novel.subject: history
hist_serialised_novel.detail: Many 19th century novels first published in instalments in magazines and newspapers. This made them affordable for wider readership. Created suspense and discussion around each episode. Expanded reading public.

hist_waste_land_rules.label: Waste Land Rules
hist_waste_land_rules.subject: history
hist_waste_land_rules.detail: Colonial rules aimed at bringing uncultivated land under cultivation. Grazing lands were taken over and given to individuals. Expansion of cultivation reduced pastures available for pastoral communities.

hist_treaty_of_nanking.label: Treaty of Nanking (1842)
hist_treaty_of_nanking.subject: history
hist_treaty_of_nanking.detail: First of the 'unequal treaties' ending the First Opium War. China ceded Hong Kong to Britain, opened five ports (Canton, Amoy, Foochow, Ningpo, Shanghai) to foreign trade, paid an indemnity of 21 million silver dollars, and granted most-favoured-nation status. Inaugurated a 'century of humiliation' for China.

hist_birjis_qadr.label: Birjis Qadr
hist_birjis_qadr.subject: history
hist_birjis_qadr.detail: Young son of deposed Nawab Wajid Ali Shah, proclaimed ruler of Awadh during the revolt. Begum Hazrat Mahal, his mother, effectively led the resistance in Lucknow. Eventually fled to Nepal after British recapture. Represented Awadh's resistance to annexation.

hist_corn_laws.label: Corn Laws
hist_corn_laws.subject: history
hist_corn_laws.detail: Laws restricting import of corn to protect British landowners. Abolished under pressure from industrialists and urban dwellers who wanted cheap food. Abolition opened British markets to cheap imported grain.

hist_corn_laws_global.label: Corn Laws and Global Food Market
hist_corn_laws_global.subject: history
hist_corn_laws_global.detail: Abolition of Corn Laws in Britain opened economy to food imports. British agriculture declined, workers migrated. Global food trade expanded as lands cleared in Americas, Russia and Australia to feed Britain.

hist_1848_revolutions.label: Revolutions of 1848
hist_1848_revolutions.subject: history
hist_1848_revolutions.detail: Liberal revolutions across Europe demanding constitutionalism and national unification. Frankfurt Parliament attempted German unification but was opposed by aristocracy and military. Women attended as observers but denied voting rights. Liberal revolutions across Europe — Paris, Vienna, Berlin, Milan — demanding constitutions and nationalist unification. Frankfurt Parliament attempted German unification; crushed by aristocracy and military.

hist_bombay_parsees_cricket.label: Parsee Cricket in Bombay
hist_bombay_parsees_cricket.subject: history
hist_bombay_parsees_cricket.detail: First Indian community to adopt cricket, founding Oriental Cricket Club in 1848. Set up first Indian cricket club. Played matches against Europeans and helped establish cricket in India.

hist_cricket_india_colonial.label: Cricket in Colonial India
hist_cricket_india_colonial.subject: history
hist_cricket_india_colonial.detail: First Indian cricket club founded in 1848 by Bombay Parsees. Gymkhana tournaments organised on communal lines - Parsees, Hindus, Muslims, Europeans. Pentangular tournament reflected colonial divide-and-rule politics.

hist_doctrine_of_lapse.label: Doctrine of Lapse
hist_doctrine_of_lapse.subject: history
hist_doctrine_of_lapse.detail: Policy of Lord Dalhousie refusing to recognise adopted heirs of Indian rulers, annexing their states. Applied to Satara, Jhansi, Nagpur and other states. Major cause of resentment among Indian aristocracy. Nana Sahib and Rani Lakshmibai were directly affected. Applied to Satara 1848, Jaitpur 1849, Sambalpur 1849, Jhansi 1853, Nagpur 1854. Awadh annexed 1856 on separate pretext of misgovernment.

hist_gold_rush.label: Gold Rush
hist_gold_rush.subject: history
hist_gold_rush.detail: Discoveries of gold attracted massive migration and accelerated settler colonialism. The California Gold Rush (1848-55) drew 300,000 migrants and devastated local Native American populations. The Australian gold rushes (1851 onwards) in Victoria and New South Wales similarly attracted immigrants and displaced Aboriginal peoples.

hist_karl_marx.label: Karl Marx
hist_karl_marx.subject: history
hist_karl_marx.detail: With Friedrich Engels developed theory that capitalist society must be overthrown by workers to create communist society where all property is socially controlled. Argued workers would triumph over capitalists.

hist_marianne_germania.label: Marianne and Germania
hist_marianne_germania.subject: history
hist_marianne_germania.detail: Female allegorical figures representing France (Marianne) and Germany (Germania). Marianne wore red cap and tricolour. Germania wore oak leaf crown, holding sword. Used in coins, statues, stamps to create national identity.

hist_19th_century_globalisation.label: 19th Century Globalisation
hist_19th_century_globalisation.subject: history
hist_19th_century_globalisation.detail: Three types of flows shaped world economy: trade in goods, labour migration, and capital movement. Railways, steamships and telegraph enabled global connections. Britain emerged as centre of world trade.

hist_bombay_deccan_peasants.label: Bombay Deccan Peasants
hist_bombay_deccan_peasants.subject: history
hist_bombay_deccan_peasants.detail: Under ryotwari system, peasants were individually assessed for revenue. Many fell into debt to moneylenders (sahukars/sowcars) due to fluctuating cotton prices and revenue demands. When British courts upheld creditor rights, peasants lost lands through foreclosure.

hist_cricket_victorian_values.label: Cricket and Victorian Values
hist_cricket_victorian_values.subject: history
hist_cricket_victorian_values.detail: Cricket became linked to Victorian culture of fair play, discipline and gentlemanliness. Introduced in schools as physical training. Distinction between 'gentlemen' (amateurs) and 'players' (professionals) reflected class hierarchy.

hist_dress_reform_movement.label: Dress Reform Movement
hist_dress_reform_movement.subject: history
hist_dress_reform_movement.detail: 19th century movement against restrictive women's clothing. American Amelia Bloomer designed loose trousers (bloomers). In India, Jnanadanandini Devi popularised sari draping styles that allowed greater mobility.

hist_gaddi_shepherds.label: Gaddi Shepherds
hist_gaddi_shepherds.subject: history
hist_gaddi_shepherds.detail: Pastoral community of Himachal Pradesh with similar seasonal cycle to Bakarwals. Winter in Siwalik hills, summer in Lahul and Spiti. Stopped in villages to reap summer harvest and sow winter crop during migration.

hist_gujjar_bakarwals.label: Gujjar Bakarwals
hist_gujjar_bakarwals.subject: history
hist_gujjar_bakarwals.detail: Great herders of goat and sheep in Jammu and Kashmir. Migrated in 19th century. Moved between Siwalik hills (winter) and Kashmir valley (summer) through Pir Panjal passes in groups called kafilas.

hist_handloom_survival.label: Survival of Handloom Industry
hist_handloom_survival.subject: history
hist_handloom_survival.detail: Despite factory competition, handloom survived for fine-quality work machines could not produce - saris with intricate borders, traditional patterns. Adapted by using fly shuttle and focusing on niche markets.

hist_managing_agencies.label: European Managing Agencies
hist_managing_agencies.subject: history
hist_managing_agencies.detail: Bird Heiglers, Andrew Yule, Jardine Skinner controlled large sector of Indian industries till WWI. Indian financiers provided capital but Europeans made all business decisions. Indians barred from European chambers of commerce.

hist_pastoral_nomadism.label: Pastoral Nomadism in India
hist_pastoral_nomadism.subject: history
hist_pastoral_nomadism.detail: Pastoral communities moved cyclically between summer and winter pastures. Mountain pastoralists (Gujjar Bakarwals, Gaddis, Bhotiyas) moved between high meadows and low hills. Plains pastoralists (Dhangars, Banjaras, Raikas) moved across agricultural regions.

hist_raikas_rajasthan.label: Raikas of Rajasthan
hist_raikas_rajasthan.subject: history
hist_raikas_rajasthan.detail: Combined cultivation with pastoralism in Rajasthan desert. During monsoons, moved to Barmer, Jaisalmer and Jodhpur for grazing. In dry months, moved to agricultural areas of Haryana for stubble grazing.

hist_taiping_rebellion.label: Taiping Rebellion (1850-1864)
hist_taiping_rebellion.subject: history
hist_taiping_rebellion.detail: Massive civil war in southern China led by Hong Xiuquan, who claimed to be the brother of Jesus Christ. Established the Taiping Heavenly Kingdom with radical social reforms (land redistribution, gender equality, banning opium). Resulted in an estimated 20-30 million deaths. Weakened the Qing dynasty but was eventually suppressed with Western help. Led by Hong Xiuquan (claimed to be brother of Jesus). Taiping Heavenly Kingdom: land redistribution, gender equality, banned opium. 20-30M deaths. Suppressed with Western help; weakened Qing.

hist_victorian_dress_women.label: Victorian Women's Dress
hist_victorian_dress_women.subject: history
hist_victorian_dress_women.detail: Women tightly laced in stays and corsets from childhood to create small-waisted figure. Clothing reflected ideal of women as frail, submissive and docile. By 1830s suffrage movement campaigned for dress reform.

hist_wool_industry_australia.label: Wool Industry (Australia)
hist_wool_industry_australia.subject: history
hist_wool_industry_australia.detail: Sheep farming became the economic backbone of colonial Australia from the 1820s. The merino sheep thrived in Australian conditions. Squatters occupied vast tracts of Aboriginal land for grazing. By 1850, Australia was the world's largest wool exporter. The wool industry drove territorial expansion and Aboriginal dispossession.

hist_commodore_perry.label: Commodore Perry's Arrival
hist_commodore_perry.subject: history
hist_commodore_perry.detail: US Navy Commodore Matthew Perry arrived in Japan with warships in 1853, demanding that Japan open its ports to American trade. The unequal Treaty of Kanagawa (1854) was signed under threat of force. This humiliation exposed Tokugawa weakness and catalysed the movement to overthrow the shogunate and modernise Japan. Arrived Edo Bay 1853 with black warships. Treaty of Kanagawa 1854 under force. Humiliation triggered overthrow of Tokugawa → Meiji Restoration 1868.

hist_railways_urbanisation.label: Railways and Urbanisation
hist_railways_urbanisation.subject: history
hist_railways_urbanisation.detail: First railway 1853 Bombay-Thane. Railways transformed Indian cities: new railway colonies, station architecture (Victoria Terminus), labour migration. Drained hinterland resources to port cities. Created new nodal towns. Railway workshops became centres of working-class consciousness.

hist_bombay_colonial_city.label: Bombay as Colonial City
hist_bombay_colonial_city.subject: history
hist_bombay_colonial_city.detail: Bombay grew as major trading port and textile centre. Population explosion created crowded chawls where 70% working people lived. Victoria Terminus built 1878-87 symbolised colonial power. Reclamation projects expanded the city. Originally seven islands joined through reclamation (Back Bay, Mahim-Salsette linked by 1862). Population swelled in chawls: 70% of working people in one-room tenements.

hist_first_cotton_mill_bombay.label: First Cotton Mill in Bombay
hist_first_cotton_mill_bombay.subject: history
hist_first_cotton_mill_bombay.detail: The first cotton mill in India was set up as a spinning mill in Bombay in 1854. By 1900, over 84 mills operated in Bombay, many established by Parsi and Gujarati businessmen. By 1900, 84 mills operated in Bombay; many established by Parsi and Gujarati businessmen.

hist_indian_textile_industry_19c.label: Indian Textile Industry in 19th Century
hist_indian_textile_industry_19c.subject: history
hist_indian_textile_industry_19c.detail: Indian exports declined as British goods flooded Indian markets. First cotton mill in Bombay 1854, first jute mill in Bengal 1855. Indian industries expanded during WWI when British imports declined.

hist_woods_despatch_1854.label: Wood's Despatch 1854
hist_woods_despatch_1854.subject: history
hist_woods_despatch_1854.detail: Educational despatch issued by Charles Wood emphasising European learning for practical and commercial benefits. Led to establishment of education departments, and universities in Calcutta, Madras and Bombay in 1857. Led to establishment of education departments and universities in Calcutta, Madras and Bombay in 1857.

hist_santhals.label: Santhal Community
hist_santhals.subject: history
hist_santhals.detail: Tribal community in Bengal-Bihar region who cleared forests for agriculture under British encouragement. Exploited by moneylenders (dikus) and zamindars. Rose in rebellion (Santhal Hool, 1855-56) under leaders Sidhu and Kanhu. Carved out separate Santhal Pargana district. Santhal Hool (1855-56) led by brothers Sidhu and Kanhu against dikus (outsider moneylenders and zamindars); Santhal Parganas district carved out in response.

hist_awadh_annexation.label: Annexation of Awadh (1856)
hist_awadh_annexation.subject: history
hist_awadh_annexation.detail: Governor-General Dalhousie annexed Awadh on grounds of alleged misgovernment of Nawab Wajid Ali Shah. Many sepoys were from Awadh and their families suffered under new revenue arrangements. Taluqdars lost land and power. Massive resentment contributed to revolt.

hist_ishwarchandra_vidyasagar.label: Ishwarchandra Vidyasagar
hist_ishwarchandra_vidyasagar.subject: history
hist_ishwarchandra_vidyasagar.detail: Used ancient texts to argue widows could remarry. A law permitting widow remarriage was passed in 1856. Set up schools for girls in Calcutta. Faced boycott from conservatives for his reformist views. Set up schools for girls in Calcutta. Faced boycott by conservative Hindu society for his reform work.

hist_sepoy_grievances.label: Sepoy Grievances
hist_sepoy_grievances.subject: history
hist_sepoy_grievances.detail: Multiple causes: General Service Enlistment Act (1856) requiring overseas service; low pay compared to British soldiers; racial discrimination; fears of forced conversion to Christianity. Bengal Army heavily recruited from upper-caste Hindus whose status was being undermined. Pay data: infantry sepoy Rs 7/month, cavalry sawar Rs 27/month gross (after own uniform + food + mount upkeep = Rs 1-2 net). Racial discrimination from English officers. 47th Regt 1824 Burma refusal was earliest mutiny (disbanded). Crossing sea = caste loss. Afghan war (1839-42) affected caste purity.

hist_widow_remarriage_act_1856.label: Widow Remarriage Act 1856
hist_widow_remarriage_act_1856.subject: history
hist_widow_remarriage_act_1856.detail: Law passed in 1856 permitting widow remarriage, largely through efforts of Ishwarchandra Vidyasagar. Movement spread to Telugu areas under Veerasalingam Pantulu and to north under Dayanand Saraswati.

hist_censorship_colonial_india.label: Censorship in Colonial India
hist_censorship_colonial_india.subject: history
hist_censorship_colonial_india.detail: After 1857, British tightened press control. Seditious Materials Act and Vernacular Press Act used to suppress nationalist publications. Despite restrictions, Indian press played crucial role in building anti-colonial consciousness.

hist_civilian_participation_1857.label: Civilian Participation in 1857
hist_civilian_participation_1857.subject: history
hist_civilian_participation_1857.detail: Not merely a sepoy mutiny but a popular rebellion. Peasants, artisans, small zamindars joined. Awadh saw massive civilian support. Dispossessed taluqdars rallied followers. Rural poor attacked moneylenders and new landlords. Urban poor targeted symbols of colonial authority. Oudh had ~75,000 men in Bengal army. 14,000 sepoy petitions about revenue hardships. Taluqdars lost lands after Awadh annexation (~21,000 estates confiscated). Peasant + artisan + clergy alliance.

hist_delhi_siege_1857.label: Siege of Delhi (1857)
hist_delhi_siege_1857.subject: history
hist_delhi_siege_1857.detail: After sepoys captured Delhi in May 1857, British forces besieged the city for months. Delhi recaptured in September 1857 with massive violence. Bahadur Shah Zafar tried and exiled. British reprisals included executions, confiscations and destruction.

hist_greased_cartridges.label: Greased Cartridges Issue
hist_greased_cartridges.subject: history
hist_greased_cartridges.detail: Rumour that new Enfield rifle cartridges were greased with cow and pig fat, offensive to both Hindu and Muslim sepoys who had to bite them open. Immediate trigger for the revolt. Reflected deeper anxieties about British interference with religious practices and caste.

hist_mangal_pandey.label: Mangal Pandey
hist_mangal_pandey.subject: history
hist_mangal_pandey.detail: Sepoy of 34th Native Infantry who attacked British officers at Barrackpore in March 1857 over greased cartridges issue. Hanged on 8 April 1857. His action predated the main outbreak at Meerut in May. Became a symbol of the revolt. 34th Native Infantry at Barrackpore. Attacked British officers March 1857 over greased cartridges. Hanged 8 April 1857. 19th Native Infantry at Berhampur refused Enfield cartridges in March 1857 — disbanded. Mangal Pandey (34th NI Barrackpore) fired at Sergeant Major next; overpowered, hanged April 8.

hist_revolt_1857.label: Revolt of 1857
hist_revolt_1857.subject: history
hist_revolt_1857.detail: Major uprising against British East India Company beginning May 1857. Started with sepoy mutiny at Meerut, spread across North India. Rebels captured Delhi, restored Mughal emperor Bahadur Shah Zafar as leader. Suppressed by 1858 with severe repression. Led to end of Company rule and direct Crown control. Started at Meerut 10 May 1857; sepoys marched to Delhi, declared BSZ emperor. Spread across Lucknow, Kanpur, Jhansi, Bareilly, Arrah. Suppressed by mid-1858. Meerut sepoys reached Delhi 11 May 1857, crossing the Jamuna. Half of EIC's 2,32,224 sepoys opted out. Bengal + Bombay + Central + Western India in revolt; Madras army remained loyal; Punjab + South largely quiet.

hist_aftermath_1857.label: Aftermath of 1857 Revolt
hist_aftermath_1857.subject: history
hist_aftermath_1857.detail: Government of India Act 1858 transferred power from Company to Crown. Queen Victoria's Proclamation (1858) promised religious tolerance, respect for rights of princes. British Indian Army reorganised to reduce proportion of upper-caste Hindus. Policy of divide and rule adopted. Government of India Act 1858 transferred power to Crown. Army reorganised: reduced upper-caste Hindu proportion in Bengal Army; recruited more Punjabis and Gurkhas. Divide-and-rule policy formalised.

hist_queen_victoria_proclamation.label: Queen Victoria's Proclamation (1858)
hist_queen_victoria_proclamation.subject: history
hist_queen_victoria_proclamation.detail: Issued November 1858 announcing direct Crown rule. Promised: religious non-interference, respect for rights of Indian princes, equal treatment of subjects regardless of race or creed. Became a charter of rights cited by Indian nationalists in later decades.

pol_foreign_companies_india.label: Foreign Companies in India
pol_foreign_companies_india.subject: polity
pol_foreign_companies_india.detail: Foreign companies set up production in India for cheap labour - wages far lower than in developed countries, longer hours, fewer expenses on worker housing. Cost-cutting through lower safety measures. UC plant in Bhopal had far lower safety standards than its US plant in West Virginia.

hist_rashsundari_devi.label: Rashsundari Devi
hist_rashsundari_devi.subject: history
hist_rashsundari_devi.detail: Born in West Bengal around 1800, she wrote Amar Jiban at age 60 -- the first known autobiography by an Indian woman. She secretly taught herself to read and write after marriage, despite the belief that literate women would bring bad luck to their husbands.

hist_railways_colonial.label: Railways Under British Rule
hist_railways_colonial.subject: history
hist_railways_colonial.detail: Introduced in 1850, considered one of the most important British contributions. Had dual impact: enabled long-distance travel breaking geographical and cultural barriers, but also fostered commercialisation of Indian agriculture which harmed village self-sufficiency. Benefits rarely accrued to Indians.

hist_first_jute_mill_1855.label: Jute Industry
hist_first_jute_mill_1855.subject: history
hist_first_jute_mill_1855.detail: India largest producer of raw jute. Mills mostly in West Bengal (Hugli basin). Started 1855. Products: gunny bags, carpets, decoratives. Facing competition from synthetic packaging. Government promotes jute use.

hist_indigo_rebellion.label: Indigo Rebellion (1859-60)
hist_indigo_rebellion.subject: history
hist_indigo_rebellion.detail: Peasant uprising in Bengal against oppressive indigo plantation system. Ryots refused to grow indigo for European planters who used coercive methods. Dinabandhu Mitra wrote 'Nil Darpan' (1860) dramatising peasant suffering. Government appointed Indigo Commission to investigate.

hist_sidhu_kanhu.label: Sidhu and Kanhu Murmu
hist_sidhu_kanhu.subject: history
hist_sidhu_kanhu.detail: Santhal brothers who led the Santhal Hool (1855-56) in Bengal-Bihar against British officials, zamindars, and moneylenders. Promised divine sanction; mobilised tens of thousands. Brutally suppressed; Santhal Parganas district formed in 1856.

hist_dietrich_brandis.label: Dietrich Brandis
hist_dietrich_brandis.subject: history
hist_dietrich_brandis.detail: German expert appointed first Inspector General of Forests in India in 1864. Established Indian Forest Service, helped formulate Indian Forest Act of 1865. Introduced scientific forestry with planned management and restricted felling.

hist_forest_act_1865.label: Indian Forest Act (1865, amd. 1878, 1927)
hist_forest_act_1865.subject: history
hist_forest_act_1865.detail: Enacted 1865, amended 1878 and 1927. 1878 Act divided forests into reserved, protected, and village forests. Villagers barred from reserved forests; customary use of fuel, fodder, mahua, tendu leaves criminalised. Triggered numerous tribal rebellions.

hist_scientific_forestry.label: Scientific Forestry
hist_scientific_forestry.subject: history
hist_scientific_forestry.detail: System where natural forests with diverse species were cut down and replaced with single species plantations like teak and sal. Forest department decided which trees to cut and where. Local people lost customary access.

hist_criminal_tribes_act_1871.label: Criminal Tribes Act (1871)
hist_criminal_tribes_act_1871.subject: history
hist_criminal_tribes_act_1871.detail: Classified many nomadic communities (pastoralists, traders, craftsmen) as "criminal by birth". Required notified village settlement, restricted movement, police surveillance. Affected Korava, Karacha, Yerukula and other Madras Presidency groups.

hist_shifting_cultivation_ban.label: Ban on Shifting Cultivation
hist_shifting_cultivation_ban.subject: history
hist_shifting_cultivation_ban.detail: Swidden agriculture (jhum, podu, dhya, bewar, kumri) banned by colonial forest department because it prevented continuous timber growth and made tax collection difficult. Displaced many adivasi communities; fuel for rebellions.

hist_dhangars.label: Dhangars
hist_dhangars.subject: history
hist_dhangars.detail: Pastoral community of Maharashtra, ~467,000 in early 20c. Shepherds, blanket weavers, buffalo herders. Seasonal movement between Deccan plateau (monsoon) and Konkan (post-harvest). Fed on stubble, manured Konkani peasant fields in exchange for rice.

hist_opium_triangular_trade.label: Opium–Tea Triangular Trade
hist_opium_triangular_trade.subject: history
hist_opium_triangular_trade.detail: British balanced tea imports from China (financed by silver outflow) by smuggling Bengal opium into China. Triangle: Bengal opium → China; China tea → Britain; Britain manufactures → India. Financed EIC tea trade; created Chinese addiction crisis.

hist_enclosure_acts.label: Enclosure Acts (Britain)
hist_enclosure_acts.subject: history
hist_enclosure_acts.detail: Between 1750-1850, British Parliament passed 4,000 Acts enclosing 6 million acres of common land. Late-18c enclosures (vs 16c wool enclosures) were for grain. Landlords displaced poor commoners; set stage for Captain Swing riots. Displaced rural poor migrated to industrial towns, providing factory labour — direct feed into the Industrial Revolution's workforce.

hist_open_fields_commons.label: Open Fields and Commons
hist_open_fields_commons.subject: history
hist_open_fields_commons.detail: Pre-enclosure English rural system. Villagers cultivated strips allocated annually; commons used for grazing, fuelwood, fruit, fishing, hunting. Sustained poor. Swept away by enclosures after 1750.

hist_cyrus_mccormick_reaper.label: Cyrus McCormick's Reaper (1831)
hist_cyrus_mccormick_reaper.subject: history
hist_cyrus_mccormick_reaper.detail: Mechanical reaper invented 1831 in USA. One machine cut as much in a day as 5 men with cradles / 16 men with sickles. Transformed Great Plains wheat harvest; by 20c combined harvesters cut 500 acres in 2 weeks.

hist_us_wheat_bread_basket.label: USA Great Plains Wheat (Bread Basket)
hist_us_wheat_bread_basket.subject: history
hist_us_wheat_bread_basket.detail: Great Plains wheat expansion 1860s-1920s. 45M acres (1910) → 74M acres (1919). Wheat barons controlled 2,000-3,000 acre farms. Steam tractors + combined harvesters. Fed WWI Europe. Later: Dust Bowl 1930s.

hist_maasai_east_africa.label: Maasai Pastoralists (East Africa)
hist_maasai_east_africa.subject: history
hist_maasai_east_africa.detail: East African cattle herders (Kenya+Tanzania). 1885 Anglo-German border split Maasailand; colonial grazing reserves took best lands. Lost 60% of pre-colonial grazing. Serengeti + Maasai Mara game reserves excluded pastoralists. 1933-34 drought killed over half their cattle.

hist_java_dutch_forestry.label: Dutch Colonial Forestry (Java)
hist_java_dutch_forestry.subject: history
hist_java_dutch_forestry.detail: Dutch imposed forest laws in Java from 19c for teak (shipbuilding, railway sleepers). Blandongdiensten system: villagers given rent exemptions in exchange for free labour cutting and hauling teak. Kalangs (skilled forest cutters) co-opted. Surontiko Samin led 1890s tax resistance.

hist_commissioner_lin_zexu.label: Commissioner Lin Zexu
hist_commissioner_lin_zexu.subject: history
hist_commissioner_lin_zexu.detail: Qing Special Commissioner at Canton 1839. Arrested 1,600 opium traders, confiscated 11,000 lbs opium, burnt 20,000 crates. Wrote "Letter of Advice to Queen Victoria" condemning the opium trade. His closure of Canton triggered First Opium War (1839-42).

hist_gothic_architecture_india.label: Gothic and Neo-Classical Architecture
hist_gothic_architecture_india.subject: history
hist_gothic_architecture_india.detail: British built imposing Gothic and Neo-Classical buildings: High Courts, universities, churches, railway stations. Victoria Terminus (now CST) in Bombay is finest example of Venetian Gothic. These buildings asserted imperial authority. Some incorporated Indian motifs (Indo-Saracenic style).

hist_indo_saracenic_style.label: Indo-Saracenic Architecture
hist_indo_saracenic_style.subject: history
hist_indo_saracenic_style.detail: Architectural style blending Hindu, Islamic and European elements. Examples: Gateway of India (Bombay), Madras Law Courts. Evolved as compromise between imperial assertiveness and cultural accommodation. Also used by Indian princes in their palaces (e.g., Mysore Palace by Henry Irwin).

hist_indian_industrialists_19c.label: Indian Industrialists (19c)
hist_indian_industrialists_19c.subject: history
hist_indian_industrialists_19c.detail: Dwarkanath Tagore (Bengal, 1830s), Dinshaw Petit, Jamsetjee Nusserwanjee Tata (Bombay cotton, later TISCO 1912), Seth Hukumchand, G.D. Birla. Rose from trading communities — Marwaris, Parsis, Chettiars, Gujaratis. Barred from European chambers of commerce.

hist_chawls_bombay.label: Chawls of Bombay
hist_chawls_bombay.subject: history
hist_chawls_bombay.detail: Multi-storeyed tenements from 1860s in 'native' parts of Bombay. One-room tenements with no private toilets housing 4-5 people. 90% of millworkers lived in Girangaon chawls within walking distance of mills.

hist_land_reclamation_bombay.label: Land Reclamation in Bombay
hist_land_reclamation_bombay.subject: history
hist_land_reclamation_bombay.detail: Bombay originally seven islands joined through massive land reclamation projects. Back Bay reclamation, Marine Drive construction, linking of Mahim-Salsette completed by 1862. Transformed geography of the city.

hist_haussmannisation.label: Haussmannisation of Paris
hist_haussmannisation.subject: history
hist_haussmannisation.detail: Baron Haussmann rebuilt Paris in 1860s with wide straight boulevards, parks and open spaces. Destroyed old working-class neighbourhoods. Goal was to beautify city and prevent barricade-based revolts.

hist_london_underground.label: London Underground Railway
hist_london_underground.subject: history
hist_london_underground.detail: World's first underground railway opened in London in 1863. Initially people feared travelling underground. Expanded to solve traffic congestion as city grew. Shaped London's suburban development pattern.

hist_london_urbanisation_scale.label: London Urbanisation Scale
hist_london_urbanisation_scale.subject: history
hist_london_urbanisation_scale.detail: London grew from 1M (1810) to 6.5M (1880). Industrial-era migration; 5-6 people per tenement room. Cholera + typhoid drove public-health reform, underground railway (1863), later garden cities.

hist_jyotirao_phule.label: Jyotirao Phule
hist_jyotirao_phule.subject: history
hist_jyotirao_phule.detail: Born 1827, attacked Brahmanical claims of superiority. Founded Satyashodhak Samaj for caste equality. Wrote Gulamgiri (1873) linking Indian caste oppression to American slavery. Set up schools for girls and low castes in Maharashtra.

hist_savitribai_phule.label: Savitribai Phule
hist_savitribai_phule.subject: history
hist_savitribai_phule.detail: First Indian woman teacher (1831-1897). With husband Jyotirao Phule set up India's first girls' school in Pune 1848. Wrote poetry on social reform. Faced abuse from upper castes on her way to teach.

hist_indian_novel_early.label: Early Indian Novel
hist_indian_novel_early.subject: history
hist_indian_novel_early.detail: First modern Indian novels mid-19c. Bankim Chandra's Durgeshnandini 1865 (Bengali), Srinivas Das Pariksha Guru 1882 (Hindi), Chandu Menon Indulekha 1889 (Malayalam). Created a new literary public in regional languages.

hist_raja_ravi_varma.label: Raja Ravi Varma
hist_raja_ravi_varma.subject: history
hist_raja_ravi_varma.detail: From royal family of Travancore, Kerala. Mastered Western oil painting but painted Indian mythological themes from Ramayana and Mahabharata. Set up picture production press near Bombay to mass-produce cheap colour prints.

hist_rise_of_novel_europe.label: Rise of the Novel (Europe)
hist_rise_of_novel_europe.subject: history
hist_rise_of_novel_europe.detail: 18c European novel. Defoe's Robinson Crusoe 1719, Richardson's Pamela 1740. Middle-class reading public. Explored individual choice + everyday life.

hist_gutenberg_print_revolution.label: Gutenberg Print Revolution
hist_gutenberg_print_revolution.subject: history
hist_gutenberg_print_revolution.detail: Johann Gutenberg (Strasbourg) devised movable-type press ~1448. First book: Bible. By 1500 Europe had printed ~20M copies. Knowledge shifted from handcopied manuscripts to mass production. Context for Reformation, later Enlightenment and French Revolution.

hist_battle_plassey.label: Battle of Plassey (1757)
hist_battle_plassey.subject: history
hist_battle_plassey.detail: 23 June 1757. Robert Clive defeated Nawab Siraj-ud-daula of Bengal through bribery of commander Mir Jafar. Marked beginning of effective British political control in India. Mir Jafar installed as puppet Nawab.

hist_battle_buxar.label: Battle of Buxar (1764)
hist_battle_buxar.subject: history
hist_battle_buxar.detail: 22 October 1764. Hector Munro defeated combined forces of Mir Qasim (Bengal), Shuja-ud-daula (Awadh), and Mughal emperor Shah Alam II. Decisive battle that confirmed British supremacy in Bengal; consolidated conquest begun at Plassey.

hist_treaty_allahabad_1765.label: Treaty of Allahabad (1765)
hist_treaty_allahabad_1765.subject: history
hist_treaty_allahabad_1765.detail: After Buxar. Shah Alam II granted EIC the Diwani (right to collect revenue) of Bengal, Bihar, Orissa. EIC became the de facto fiscal ruler. Awadh returned to Shuja-ud-daula on indemnity payment; became buffer state.

hist_diwani_of_bengal.label: Diwani of Bengal (1765)
hist_diwani_of_bengal.subject: history
hist_diwani_of_bengal.detail: EIC's right to collect revenue from Bengal, Bihar, Orissa after Treaty of Allahabad. Dual government under Hastings (nominal Nawab + actual EIC control) until 1772 when EIC took direct control.

hist_siraj_ud_daula.label: Siraj-ud-daula
hist_siraj_ud_daula.subject: history
hist_siraj_ud_daula.detail: Last independent Nawab of Bengal (1756-57). Attacked Calcutta 1756 (Black Hole). Defeated at Plassey 1757 by Clive via Mir Jafar's betrayal. Killed soon after.

hist_mir_jafar.label: Mir Jafar
hist_mir_jafar.subject: history
hist_mir_jafar.detail: Bengal military commander who betrayed Siraj at Plassey. Installed as puppet Nawab 1757-60, restored 1763-65. EIC extracted vast wealth through him — 'the Plassey plunder'.

hist_mir_qasim.label: Mir Qasim
hist_mir_qasim.subject: history
hist_mir_qasim.detail: Nawab of Bengal 1760-63. Installed by EIC replacing Mir Jafar, but resisted Company privileges. Fled to Awadh after defeat; fought at Buxar 1764. Died in obscurity.

hist_robert_clive.label: Robert Clive
hist_robert_clive.subject: history
hist_robert_clive.detail: EIC military commander and governor of Bengal (1757-60, 1765-67). Won Plassey 1757; reorganised revenue administration through Dual Government. Later tried for corruption in Britain.

hist_warren_hastings.label: Warren Hastings
hist_warren_hastings.subject: history
hist_warren_hastings.detail: First Governor-General of Bengal (1772-1785). Abolished Dual Government. Established civil and criminal courts. Patronised Oriental learning (Calcutta Madrasa 1781). Impeached in Britain on return.

hist_regulating_act_1773.label: Regulating Act (1773)
hist_regulating_act_1773.subject: history
hist_regulating_act_1773.detail: First British parliamentary intervention in EIC affairs. Created post of Governor-General of Bengal (Hastings first). Established Supreme Court at Calcutta 1774. Brought EIC under parliamentary control.

hist_pitt_india_act_1784.label: Pitt's India Act (1784)
hist_pitt_india_act_1784.subject: history
hist_pitt_india_act_1784.detail: Established Board of Control in London alongside EIC Court of Directors — dual system for governing Indian affairs. Made Governor-General directly accountable to Parliament. Affirmed Company political role.

hist_charter_act_1813.label: Charter Act (1813)
hist_charter_act_1813.subject: history
hist_charter_act_1813.detail: Ended EIC monopoly on Indian trade (except tea and China trade). Allowed Christian missionaries to operate. Imposed on EIC obligation to spend Rs 1 lakh on Indian education annually (origin of colonial education debate).

hist_charter_act_1833.label: Charter Act (1833)
hist_charter_act_1833.subject: history
hist_charter_act_1833.detail: Ended EIC as commercial body — made it purely administrative. Governor-General of Bengal renamed Governor-General of India. First Indian Law Commission (Macaulay) — produced Indian Penal Code draft 1837.

hist_charter_act_1853.label: Charter Act (1853)
hist_charter_act_1853.subject: history
hist_charter_act_1853.detail: Last of the Charter Acts. Introduced competitive exams for ICS. Separated legislative from executive functions of Governor-General's Council — beginning of Indian legislature.

hist_lord_wellesley.label: Lord Wellesley
hist_lord_wellesley.subject: history
hist_lord_wellesley.detail: Governor-General 1798-1805. Architect of Subsidiary Alliance system. Defeated Tipu Sultan (1799), Marathas (2nd Anglo-Maratha War). Massively expanded British territory; recalled for excessive aggression.

hist_subsidiary_alliance.label: Subsidiary Alliance (Wellesley)
hist_subsidiary_alliance.subject: history
hist_subsidiary_alliance.detail: Wellesley's system (from 1798): Indian ruler paid for British troops stationed in territory, accepted British Resident, forfeited independent foreign relations. States joined: Hyderabad (1798 first), Awadh (1801), Mysore (post-1799), Marathas in stages.

hist_haidar_ali.label: Haidar Ali
hist_haidar_ali.subject: history
hist_haidar_ali.detail: Mysore ruler (1761-1782). Modernised army with French help. Fought 1st and 2nd Anglo-Mysore Wars. Expanded Mysore into major south-Indian power. Father of Tipu Sultan. Polilur victory 1780 celebrated in Tipu's palace murals.

hist_tipu_sultan.label: Tipu Sultan
hist_tipu_sultan.subject: history
hist_tipu_sultan.detail: Ruler of Mysore 1782-99, 'Tiger of Mysore'. Modernised army (rockets), sent embassies to France and Ottomans. Fought 3rd + 4th Anglo-Mysore Wars. Died defending Seringapatam 1799. Introduced commercial treaties, land revenue reform.

hist_anglo_mysore_wars.label: Anglo-Mysore Wars (4, 1767-1799)
hist_anglo_mysore_wars.subject: history
hist_anglo_mysore_wars.detail: Four wars between EIC and Mysore. 1st (1767-69): Treaty of Madras. 2nd (1780-84): Haidar vs British; Treaty of Mangalore. 3rd (1790-92): Tipu ceded half his territory. 4th (1799): Tipu killed at Seringapatam; Mysore annexed (partly).

hist_anglo_maratha_wars.label: Anglo-Maratha Wars (3, 1775-1818)
hist_anglo_maratha_wars.subject: history
hist_anglo_maratha_wars.detail: 1st (1775-82): Treaty of Salbai. 2nd (1803-05): Wellesley vs Sindhia/Bhonsle/Holkar; EIC gains Delhi-Agra region. 3rd (1817-18): Peshwa Baji Rao II defeated; Pune annexed 1818 — end of Maratha power.

hist_first_anglo_sikh_war.label: First Anglo-Sikh War (1845-46)
hist_first_anglo_sikh_war.subject: history
hist_first_anglo_sikh_war.detail: After Ranjit Singh's death 1839, Sikh succession crisis. British provoked war; defeated Sikh army at Mudki, Ferozeshah, Sobraon. Treaty of Lahore 1846: Sikhs lost Kashmir (sold to Dogra Gulab Singh) and paid indemnity.

hist_second_anglo_sikh_war.label: Second Anglo-Sikh War (1848-49) + Punjab Annexation
hist_second_anglo_sikh_war.subject: history
hist_second_anglo_sikh_war.detail: Triggered by Multan revolt 1848. Battles of Chillianwala, Gujrat 1849. Dalhousie annexed Punjab March 1849 — completed British conquest up to Afghan frontier. Last major Indian military state absorbed.

hist_first_anglo_afghan_war.label: First Anglo-Afghan War (1839-42)
hist_first_anglo_afghan_war.subject: history
hist_first_anglo_afghan_war.detail: British invaded Afghanistan to place Shah Shuja on throne (countering perceived Russian threat — 'Great Game'). Kabul occupied 1839 then disastrous retreat 1842; only one European survivor reached Jalalabad. Shuja assassinated. Marked end of British aggressive forward policy briefly.

hist_lord_bentinck.label: Lord William Bentinck
hist_lord_bentinck.subject: history
hist_lord_bentinck.detail: Governor-General 1828-35. Reform-minded: abolished sati 1829, suppressed thuggee (1830s via Sleeman), Macaulay's Minute and English Education Act 1835 during his tenure. Revised land settlements in NW Provinces.

hist_general_service_enlistment_act_1856.label: General Service Enlistment Act (1856)
hist_general_service_enlistment_act_1856.subject: history
hist_general_service_enlistment_act_1856.detail: Required new sepoy recruits to serve overseas if ordered. Violated Hindu orthodoxy (crossing kala pani = loss of caste). One of the major grievances underlying the 1857 revolt.

hist_thuggee_suppression.label: Suppression of Thuggee
hist_thuggee_suppression.subject: history
hist_thuggee_suppression.detail: William Sleeman's campaign 1830s: organised the Thuggee and Dacoity Department. Prosecuted over 3,000 'thugs'. Mix of genuine suppression, orientalist stereotyping, and colonial knowledge production about criminal castes.

hist_chapkan_controversy.label: Western vs Indian Dress Debate
hist_chapkan_controversy.subject: history
hist_chapkan_controversy.detail: During colonial period, Indians debated whether to adopt Western dress or retain traditional clothing. Some reformers wore Western clothes to signal modernity. Others like nationalists rejected Western dress as cultural submission.

hist_cricket_origins_england.label: Origins of Cricket (England)
hist_cricket_origins_england.subject: history
hist_cricket_origins_england.detail: Evolved from stick-and-ball games ~500 years ago. First Laws of Cricket 1744 (22-yard pitch, 22-inch stumps). World's first club at Hambledon 1760s. MCC (Marylebone Cricket Club) at Lord's 1787 became custodian of laws.

hist_sumptuary_laws_france.label: Sumptuary Laws (pre-Revolution France)
hist_sumptuary_laws_france.subject: history
hist_sumptuary_laws_france.detail: 1294-1789 French dress codes by class: only royalty wore ermine, silk, velvet, brocade. Swept away by the Revolution — sans-culottes (no knee breeches), long trousers, red liberty cap, tricolour.

hist_coal_iron_industries.label: Coal and Iron Industries
hist_coal_iron_industries.subject: history
hist_coal_iron_industries.detail: Darby's coke-smelting 1709; Cort's puddling process 1784 revolutionised iron production. Coal powered steam engines and heated furnaces. Underpinned railway construction, shipbuilding, machinery.

hist_meiji_restoration.label: Meiji Restoration
hist_meiji_restoration.stage: East Asia: Meiji Japan + Qing Collapse
hist_meiji_restoration.subject: history
hist_meiji_restoration.detail: The overthrow of the Tokugawa Shogunate and restoration of imperial rule under Emperor Meiji in 1868. Young samurai from Satsuma and Choshu domains led the revolution. The new government launched a rapid programme of modernisation, industrialisation, and Westernisation under the slogan 'Enrich the Country, Strengthen the Military' (fukoku kyohei).

hist_native_americans.label: Native Americans
hist_native_americans.subject: history
hist_native_americans.detail: Indigenous peoples of North America who inhabited the continent for over 15,000 years before European contact. Diverse cultures including agricultural peoples (Iroquois, Pueblo), Plains hunters (Sioux, Comanche), and Pacific Northwest fishers. Devastated by European diseases, dispossession, and warfare. Population fell from an estimated 5-10 million to under 250,000 by 1900.

hist_diseases_depopulation_americas.label: Disease + Indigenous Depopulation
hist_diseases_depopulation_americas.subject: history
hist_diseases_depopulation_americas.detail: European diseases (smallpox, measles, influenza, typhus) devastated Americas and Australia indigenous peoples. ~90% American indigenous population died within a century. Australian Aboriginal communities similarly decimated.

hist_civil_rebellions_overview.label: Civil Rebellions 1763-1856
hist_civil_rebellions_overview.subject: history
hist_civil_rebellions_overview.detail: Bipin Chandra: "From 1763 to 1856, more than 40 major rebellions apart from hundreds of minor ones." Led by deposed rajas/nawabs, impoverished zamindars, landed poligars, ex-retainers. Mass base from rack-rented peasants + ruined artisans + demobilised soldiers. Suppressed piecemeal; established local traditions of resistance.

hist_sanyasi_rebellion.label: Sanyasi Rebellion (1763-1800)
hist_sanyasi_rebellion.subject: history
hist_sanyasi_rebellion.detail: Bengal + Bihar. Displaced peasants + demobilised soldiers led by religious monks + dispossessed zamindars. Bankim Chandra Chatterjee's novel Anand Math (1882) set in this rebellion — source of Vande Mataram.

hist_chuar_uprising.label: Chuar Uprising (1766-1816)
hist_chuar_uprising.subject: history
hist_chuar_uprising.detail: Adivasi uprising covering 5 districts of Bengal + Bihar (Midnapore, Bankura, Jungle Mahal). Against new revenue demands + incursions on tribal land. Active 1766-72 and again 1795-1816.

hist_poligar_revolts.label: Poligar Revolts (South India, 1790s-1800s)
hist_poligar_revolts.subject: history
hist_poligar_revolts.detail: Landed military magnates (poligars) of Tamil Nadu, Malabar, coastal Andhra rebelled against EIC's revenue + dispossession policies. Especially Virapandya Kattabomman of Panchalankurichi (Tirunelveli) executed 1799. Parlekamedi 1813-14.

hist_velu_thampi_travancore.label: Velu Thampi Dalawa Revolt (1805)
hist_velu_thampi_travancore.subject: history
hist_velu_thampi_travancore.detail: Dewan of Travancore Velu Thampi led heroic revolt 1805 against EIC. Published Kundara Proclamation calling Kerala to arms. Defeated; committed suicide to avoid capture. Publicly hanged post-mortem.

hist_paika_rebellion_1817.label: Paika Rebellion (Orissa, 1817)
hist_paika_rebellion_1817.subject: history
hist_paika_rebellion_1817.detail: Buxi Jagabandhu led Paikas (traditional military retainers of Khordha Raja) against British revenue policies after annexation of Orissa 1803. Widespread Paika revolt seized Puri, Cuttack briefly before suppression 1817-18. Considered an important 'first war of independence' by Odia nationalists.

hist_bhil_uprisings.label: Bhil Uprisings (1818-1831)
hist_bhil_uprisings.subject: history
hist_bhil_uprisings.detail: Khandesh/Maharashtra Bhil tribal community repeatedly rose against British administration + moneylenders 1818-31. Sevaram Savara 1823 a known leader. Finally pacified through revenue concessions + Bhil Corps raised by Outram 1825.

hist_kittur_chinnava.label: Kittur Uprising (Rani Chennamma, 1824)
hist_kittur_chinnava.subject: history
hist_kittur_chinnava.detail: Rani Chennamma of Kittur (Karnataka) resisted British annexation under Doctrine of Lapse 1824 after her husband's death. Defeated British in first battle; captured and imprisoned. Early case of woman-led resistance. Chinnava (Sangolli Rayanna) continued guerrilla till executed 1831.

hist_kol_rebellion.label: Kol Rebellion (1820-1837)
hist_kol_rebellion.subject: history
hist_kol_rebellion.detail: Chhotanagpur Kol tribals rose against moneylenders + outsider (diku) settlers + British revenue administration. Leaders Buddho Bhagat, Joa Bhagat. Thousands massacred before British reimposed authority.

hist_ramosi_uprising.label: Ramosi Uprising (Maharashtra, 1826-29)
hist_ramosi_uprising.subject: history
hist_ramosi_uprising.detail: Chittur Singh and Umaji Naik led Ramosi peasant hillmen against British revenue after Peshwa defeat 1818. Plundered British posts. Umaji Naik hanged 1832.

hist_wahabi_movement.label: Wahabi Movement (1820s-1870s)
hist_wahabi_movement.subject: history
hist_wahabi_movement.detail: Islamic revivalist movement led by Sayyid Ahmad Barelvi (1786-1831, d. battling Sikhs at Balakot). Drew on Shah Waliullah tradition. Primary anti-British thrust in Bengal + NWFP. Active through 1857 and beyond. Suppressed after 1870 Wahabi Trials.

hist_faraizi_movement.label: Faraizi Movement (Bengal, 1818-1860s)
hist_faraizi_movement.subject: history
hist_faraizi_movement.detail: Bengal Muslim peasant movement founded by Haji Shariatullah (1781-1840), expanded by son Dudu Miyan. Called for Islamic piety + opposed British landlord + indigo planter exploitation. Crystallised ryot resistance especially to zamindars + indigo planters.

hist_moplah_rebellions.label: Moplah Rebellions (Malabar)
hist_moplah_rebellions.subject: history
hist_moplah_rebellions.detail: Series of 1830s-1920s uprisings of Mappila (Moplah) Muslim peasants in Malabar (Kerala) against Hindu Namboodiri landlords + British revenue. 22 outbreaks between 1836 and 1854. Culminated in major 1921 rebellion during Khilafat/Non-cooperation.

hist_tanjore_paintings.label: Tanjore (Thanjavur) Paintings
hist_tanjore_paintings.subject: history
hist_tanjore_paintings.detail: Maratha Bhonsle rulers patronised 18c+. Painted on glass + wooden boards. Brilliant colours + heavy gold leaf + gemstones + cut-glass embellishments. Mostly smiling Krishna + Hindu deities. Zenith under Sarfoji Maharaj (r. 1798-1832) of Thanjavur — who was also a scholar + ruler under Subsidiary Alliance.

hist_mysore_paintings.label: Mysore Paintings
hist_mysore_paintings.subject: history
hist_mysore_paintings.detail: Wodeyar-era Mysore court patronage, continued under British. Theme: Hindu gods and goddesses. Distinctive gesso paste base (zinc oxide + Arabic gum) giving sheen; muted colours. Two or more figures with one dominant.

hist_bazaar_paintings.label: Bazaar Paintings
hist_bazaar_paintings.subject: history
hist_bazaar_paintings.detail: 19th-century painting school prevalent in Bengal and Bihar. Unlike Company Paintings, it borrowed Roman/Greek (not Indian) techniques — copying classical statues. Paintings depicted Indian bazaar scenes with European backgrounds, Indian courtesans dancing before British officials, and religious themes constrained by European figural rules (no multi-armed or elephant-headed gods).

hist_portuguese_goa_architecture.label: Portuguese Goa Architecture
hist_portuguese_goa_architecture.subject: history
hist_portuguese_goa_architecture.detail: Iberian style + Baroque. Sé Cathedral Goa (1619) late-Gothic. Basilica of Bom Jesus Goa (1604) Baroque, houses St Francis Xavier's body. Diu Fort 1535 with St Paul's (1610), St Thomas + St Francis Churches. Church of St Anne Talaulim (1695).

hist_french_pondicherry_architecture.label: French Pondicherry Architecture
hist_french_pondicherry_architecture.subject: history
hist_french_pondicherry_architecture.detail: French brought Cartesian grid urban planning. Pondicherry + Chandannagar organised on scientific grid. Anonymous architecture (simple facades). Coastal French towns: Mahe (Kerala), Karaikal (Tamil Nadu), Yanam (Andhra). Sacred Heart Church Puducherry.

_period_pre_company_europeans.label: European Arrival + Early Company Trading
_period_pre_company_europeans.subject: history
_period_pre_company_europeans.detail: Portuguese arrival (Vasco da Gama 1498), establishment of trading posts by Dutch, French, English East India Companies (1600). Black Towns, Portuguese Goa architecture, early Bombay (1661 dowry) and Calcutta (1690 Job Charnock). Fort William 1757 on eve of Plassey marks transition to Company rule.

_period_company_ascendancy.label: Company Ascendancy (Plassey→Charter Act)
_period_company_ascendancy.subject: history
_period_company_ascendancy.detail: Plassey 1757 → Charter Act 1813. Clive, Warren Hastings (first Governor-General 1772), Lord Cornwallis (Permanent Settlement 1793), Wellesley's Subsidiary Alliance (1798). Anglo-Mysore wars (4, 1767-1799) vs Haidar Ali + Tipu Sultan. Anglo-Maratha wars 1 & 2 (1775-1805). Regulating Act 1773, Pitt's India Act 1784. Diwani of Bengal 1765 made EIC a fiscal power.

_period_company_paramountcy.label: Company Paramountcy (1813→1856)
_period_company_paramountcy.subject: history
_period_company_paramountcy.detail: Charter Act 1813 → Awadh annexation 1856. Dalhousie's Doctrine of Lapse (Satara, Jhansi, Nagpur, Awadh). Anglo-Sikh wars + Punjab annexation 1849. First Anglo-Afghan war 1839-42. Bentinck reforms (sati abolition 1829, English Ed Act 1835). General Service Enlistment Act 1856 triggers sepoy unrest.

_period_revolt_1857.label: Revolt of 1857
_period_revolt_1857.subject: history
_period_revolt_1857.detail: Great Rising of 1857-58. Meerut → Delhi (11 May 1857). Rebels declare Bahadur Shah Zafar emperor. Major centres: Delhi, Kanpur (Nana Sahib + Tantia Tope), Lucknow (Begum Hazrat Mahal + Birjis Qadr), Jhansi (Rani Lakshmibai), Bihar (Kunwar Singh). Causes: Doctrine of Lapse, revenue pressure, greased cartridges, religious anxiety. Suppressed by mid-1858; Crown rule via Queen Victoria's Proclamation Nov 1858 ends Company era.

_period_colonial_agrarian.label: Colonial Agrarian Systems
_period_colonial_agrarian.subject: history
_period_colonial_agrarian.detail: Three revenue systems: Permanent Settlement (Bengal 1793, Cornwallis + Shore), Ryotwari (Madras/Bombay, Munro + Read 1820), Mahalwari (NW Provinces, Holt Mackenzie 1822). Cash crops: indigo (Bengal ryoti/nij systems, Blue Mutiny 1859-60), opium (Bengal for China trade), cotton (Deccan). Fifth Report 1813. Forest Acts 1865 (Brandis), Criminal Tribes Act 1871. Paharias, Santhals, Jotedars as agrarian actors.

_period_colonial_industry.label: Colonial Industry + Deindustrialisation
_period_colonial_industry.subject: history
_period_colonial_industry.detail: Deindustrialisation — decline of Indian textile trade (Dacca muslin ruined 1830s), wootz steel lost. Calico Act 1720 (British protectionism). EIC textile revenue 1770. First cotton mill Bombay 1854, first jute mill Rishra 1855. Managing agencies (Bird Heilgers, Andrew Yule). Triangular trade: India opium→China tea→Britain→India. Proto-industrialisation + handloom survival.

_period_colonial_cities.label: Colonial Cities + Infrastructure
_period_colonial_cities.subject: history
_period_colonial_cities.detail: Presidency cities grow — Bombay (7 islands reclaimed by 1862, chawls 1860s, cotton mills), Calcutta (Fort William 1757, White/Black town segregation, Bengal Renaissance), Madras (Fort St George). Urban planning asserts colonial authority. De-urbanisation of old cities (Surat, Machilipatnam, Seringapatam). Hill stations (Shimla, Darjeeling). Railways-driven urbanisation from 1853.

_period_education_orientalism.label: Colonial Education + Orientalism
_period_education_orientalism.subject: history
_period_education_orientalism.detail: Orientalist phase: Calcutta Madrasa 1781 (Hastings), Asiatic Society 1784 (William Jones), Benares Sanskrit College 1791, Serampore Mission press 1800. Francis Buchanan + Colin Mackenzie surveyed India. Anglicist turn: James Mill, Macaulay's Minute 1835, English Education Act 1835 (end of Oriental funding), Wood's Despatch 1854 founds universities (Calcutta/Bombay/Madras 1857). Pathshala system eroded.

_period_social_reform_renaissance.label: Social Reform + Bengal Renaissance
_period_social_reform_renaissance.subject: history
_period_social_reform_renaissance.detail: Bengal Renaissance + reform. Raja Rammohun Roy (d.1833) — Brahmo Sabha 1828/Samaj 1830, Sati abolition 1829, press freedom vs 1823 Press Regulations. Ishwarchandra Vidyasagar — Widow Remarriage Act 1856, girls' schools. Young Bengal + Derozio. Rashsundari Devi first woman's autobiography. Jyotirao + Savitribai Phule: first girls' school Pune 1848. Shanar breast cloth movement, dress reform.

_period_colonial_art.label: Colonial Art + Painting + Architecture
_period_colonial_art.subject: history
_period_colonial_art.detail: Portuguese Iberian architecture (Sé Cathedral Goa 1619, Basilica of Bom Jesus 1604). French Cartesian Pondicherry. British Indo-Gothic/Victorian style (Victoria Terminus Bombay 1878). Indo-Saracenic late-19c. Indian painting: Tanjore (Maratha Bhonsle patronage, Sarfoji Raja), Mysore (Wodeyar, gesso paste), Company paintings (Impey/Wellesley — Sewak Ram, Ishwari Prasad, Ghulam Ali Khan), Kalighat pat, Bazaar paintings, Raja Ravi Varma.

_period_indian_resistance_pre1857.label: Indian Resistance (civil + tribal + peasant, pre-1857)
_period_indian_resistance_pre1857.subject: history
_period_indian_resistance_pre1857.detail: Bipin Chandra: 40+ major rebellions 1763-1856. Sanyasi (1763-1800), Chuar (1766-1816), Poligar revolts (Kattabomman 1799), Velu Thampi Travancore 1805, Paika/Buxi Jagabandhu Orissa 1817, Bhil 1818-31, Kittur (Rani Chennamma 1824), Kol 1820-37, Ramosi (Umaji Naik 1826), Wahabi (Sayyid Ahmad Barelvi), Faraizi (Haji Shariatullah Bengal), Moplah (Malabar 1836+), Santhal Hool (Sidhu-Kanhu 1855-56), Indigo Rebellion 1859-60.

_period_parallel_industrial.label: Industrial Revolution + Capitalism (Britain + global)
_period_parallel_industrial.subject: history
_period_parallel_industrial.detail: Britain's Industrial Revolution from 1760. Agricultural Revolution + Enclosure Acts freed labour. Inventions: spinning jenny (Hargreaves 1764), water frame (Arkwright 1769), steam engine (Watt 1769), factory system (Cromford 1771). Adam Smith's Wealth of Nations 1776. Coal + iron (Darby's coke-smelting, Cort's puddling). Railways from Stephenson 1829. Luddites 1811, Trade Unions legalised 1824, Chartists. Urbanisation of Manchester, London 1M→6.5M. Feeds Indian deindustrialisation.

_period_parallel_french_nationalism.label: French Revolution + European Nationalism
_period_parallel_french_nationalism.subject: history
_period_parallel_french_nationalism.detail: Rousseau's Social Contract 1762, American Revolution 1776 backdrop. French Revolution 1789 — Estates General, Bastille, Declaration of Rights of Man, Jacobins + Robespierre, Reign of Terror 1793-94. Napoleon 1804 + Civil Code. Congress of Vienna 1815 restores monarchies. Romantic nationalism (Grimm, Mazzini's Young Italy 1831). Greek Independence 1832, 1848 Revolutions. Set stage for Bismarck + Italian unification (era 8).

_period_parallel_settler.label: Settler Colonialism (Americas + Australia)
_period_parallel_settler.subject: history
_period_parallel_settler.detail: Columbus 1492 → Atlantic slave trade + plantation economy in Americas. Disease kills 90% of Americans. US westward expansion (Appalachian 1800 → Mississippi → Great Plains), Manifest Destiny, Trail of Tears 1830, Indian Removal Act, Gold Rush 1848, wheat bread basket. Australia 1788 — terra nullius, Aboriginal dispossession, wool industry, gold rushes. Stolen Generations (era 8). Maasai East Africa — Anglo-German split 1885.

_period_parallel_east_asia.label: East Asia (Qing China + Tokugawa/Meiji Japan)
_period_parallel_east_asia.subject: history
_period_parallel_east_asia.detail: China: Qing Dynasty decline. Opium Wars (1839-42 + 1856-60), Treaty of Nanking 1842 cedes Hong Kong + 5 treaty ports. Commissioner Lin Zexu's 1839 confiscation. Taiping Rebellion 1850-64 (Hong Xiuquan, 20-30M deaths). Japan: Tokugawa sakoku isolation → Commodore Perry 1853 forces opening → Meiji Restoration 1868 (fukoku kyohei) launches state-led industrialisation. Samurai transformation.

pol_panchayati_raj_history.label: History of Panchayati Raj in India
pol_panchayati_raj_history.subject: polity
pol_panchayati_raj_history.detail: Self-governing village communities (sabhas) existed from earliest times. Modern elected local bodies created after 1882 by Lord Rippon. Government of India Acts of 1919 and 1935 established village panchayats. Gandhi strongly advocated decentralisation. Community Development Programme (1952) promoted local participation. Three-tier system recommended. Gujarat and Maharashtra adopted elected bodies around 1960.

pol_lord_rippon_local_boards.label: Lord Rippon and Local Boards (1882)
pol_lord_rippon_local_boards.subject: polity
pol_lord_rippon_local_boards.detail: Lord Rippon, Viceroy of India, took the initiative in creating elected local government bodies in 1882, called local boards. This marked the beginning of modern local self-government in India. Progress was slow, and the Indian National Congress repeatedly urged making local bodies more effective.

pol_womens_education_struggle.label: Womens Struggle for Education
pol_womens_education_struggle.subject: history
pol_womens_education_struggle.detail: In the nineteenth century, there was strong opposition to educating girls. Women like Rashsundari Devi, Ramabai, and Rokeya Sakhawat Hossain struggled to learn to read and write. Education gave women power to question inequality, write about their experiences, and imagine new possibilities.

pol_rokeya_hossain.label: Rokeya Sakhawat Hossain
pol_rokeya_hossain.subject: history
pol_rokeya_hossain.detail: From a rich Bengali family, she was stopped from learning Bangla and English but learnt with support from siblings. Wrote Sultanas Dream in 1905 imagining a place where women had freedom to study, work, and create inventions. Started a school for girls in Kolkata in 1910.

pol_sedition_act_1870.label: Sedition Act of 1870
pol_sedition_act_1870.subject: polity
pol_sedition_act_1870.detail: British colonial law broadly defining sedition so any person criticising the government could be arrested without due trial. Used as instrument of arbitrary authority. Indian nationalists opposed this as violating rule of law.

pol_rowlatt_act.label: Rowlatt Act 1919
pol_rowlatt_act.subject: polity
