pol_rowlatt_act.detail: British law effective 10 March 1919 allowing imprisonment without due trial. Widely protested by nationalists including Gandhi. Protests in Punjab led to Jallianwala Bagh massacre on 13 April 1919 where General Dyer ordered troops to fire on a peaceful gathering.

eco_de_industrialisation.label: De-industrialisation of India
eco_de_industrialisation.subject: economics
eco_de_industrialisation.detail: Systematic British policy with two-fold motive: reduce India to a mere exporter of raw materials, and turn India into a market for British finished goods. India's world-famous handicraft industries (cotton, silk textiles, metal works) collapsed, creating massive unemployment without a modern industrial replacement.

eco_drain_of_wealth.label: Drain of Indian Wealth
eco_drain_of_wealth.subject: economics
eco_drain_of_wealth.detail: India's large export surplus did not result in gold or silver inflow. Instead, it was used to pay for British administrative expenses in Britain, war expenditures, and import of invisible items. Dadabhai Naoroji articulated this theory of economic drain in 'Poverty and Un-British Rule in India'.

eco_dadabhai_naoroji.label: Dadabhai Naoroji
eco_dadabhai_naoroji.subject: economics
eco_dadabhai_naoroji.detail: Pioneer in estimating India's per capita income during colonial period. Propounded the 'Drain of Wealth' theory. Also the first to discuss the concept of a poverty line using 'jail cost of living' adjusted for children (three-fourths factor). Wrote 'Poverty and Un-British Rule in India'.

eco_vkrv_rao.label: V.K.R.V. Rao
eco_vkrv_rao.subject: economics
eco_vkrv_rao.detail: Among notable economists who estimated India's national and per capita income during the colonial period. His estimates were considered the most significant. Other estimators included Dadabhai Naoroji, William Digby, and Findlay Shirras.

eco_handicraft_industries.label: Indian Handicraft Industries
eco_handicraft_industries.subject: economics
eco_handicraft_industries.detail: Pre-British India was renowned for cotton and silk textiles, metal and precious stone works. Daccai Muslin from Bengal was world famous. These industries enjoyed worldwide markets but were systematically destroyed under British rule through cheap manufactured imports from Britain.

eco_foreign_trade_colonial.label: Foreign Trade Under Colonial Rule
eco_foreign_trade_colonial.subject: economics
eco_foreign_trade_colonial.detail: India became an exporter of primary products (raw silk, cotton, jute, indigo) and importer of finished goods from Britain. Britain maintained monopoly control -- over half of India's trade was restricted to Britain. Suez Canal (opened 1869) further intensified British control over Indian trade.

eco_suez_canal.label: Suez Canal
eco_suez_canal.subject: economics
eco_suez_canal.detail: Artificial waterway in north-eastern Egypt connecting the Mediterranean Sea with the Red Sea. Opened in 1869, it reduced transportation costs and made British access to Indian markets easier, further intensifying colonial control over India's foreign trade.

eco_demographic_condition_colonial.label: Demographic Condition Under Colonial Rule
eco_demographic_condition_colonial.subject: economics
eco_demographic_condition_colonial.detail: First census in 1881. Before 1921 (first stage of demographic transition), population growth was very low. Overall literacy less than 16%, female literacy about 7%. Infant mortality rate about 218 per thousand. Life expectancy only 32 years. Public health facilities were grossly inadequate.

eco_capital_goods_industry_absence.label: Absence of Capital Goods Industry
eco_capital_goods_industry_absence.subject: economics
eco_capital_goods_industry_absence.detail: Colonial India had no significant capital goods industry (industries producing machine tools for further production). The limited industrial base included cotton textiles, jute, sugar, cement, and paper. This prevented further industrialisation and left India dependent on British machinery.

hist_german_unification.label: German Unification
hist_german_unification.subject: history
hist_german_unification.detail: Prussia led German unification under Otto von Bismarck through three wars: with Denmark (1864), Austria (1866) and France (1870). Kaiser William I proclaimed German Emperor at Versailles in January 1871.

hist_italian_unification.label: Italian Unification
hist_italian_unification.subject: history
hist_italian_unification.detail: Led by Sardinia-Piedmont under Chief Minister Cavour through diplomacy and war. Garibaldi's Red Shirts conquered Kingdom of Two Sicilies 1860. Victor Emmanuel II proclaimed King of united Italy 1861.

hist_balkans_nationalism.label: Balkan Nationalism
hist_balkans_nationalism.subject: history
hist_balkans_nationalism.detail: Region of ethnic diversity under Ottoman control. Slavic nationalities demanded independence using romantic nationalism. Rivalries among Balkan states and European powers (Russia, Germany, Austria-Hungary, England) eventually triggered WWI.

hist_otto_von_bismarck.label: Otto von Bismarck
hist_otto_von_bismarck.subject: history
hist_otto_von_bismarck.detail: Chief Minister of Prussia who unified Germany through 'blood and iron' policy of three wars. Pragmatic statesman who used diplomacy and military force rather than liberal democratic means for unification.

hist_phan_boi_chau.label: Phan Boi Chau
hist_phan_boi_chau.stage: East Asia: Meiji Japan + Qing Collapse
hist_phan_boi_chau.subject: history
hist_phan_boi_chau.detail: Vietnamese nationalist who formed Revolutionary Society (Duy Tan Hoi) in 1903. Led 'Look East' movement sending students to Japan for modern education. Wrote play about Trung sisters as patriotic symbols.

hist_scholars_revolt_1868.label: Scholars' Revolt 1868
hist_scholars_revolt_1868.stage: East Asia: Meiji Japan + Qing Collapse
hist_scholars_revolt_1868.subject: history
hist_scholars_revolt_1868.detail: Early anti-French resistance led by officials at imperial court. Opposed spread of Christianity and French control. Though suppressed, inspired later nationalist movements.

hist_gandhi_satyagraha_local.label: Gandhi's Early Satyagrahas
hist_gandhi_satyagraha_local.subject: history
hist_gandhi_satyagraha_local.detail: Champaran (1917) against indigo plantation system, Kheda (1917) for peasant crop failure relief, Ahmedabad (1918) cotton mill workers strike. Built Gandhi's reputation as mass leader and tested satyagraha methods.

hist_rinderpest_africa.label: Rinderpest in Africa
hist_rinderpest_africa.subject: history
hist_rinderpest_africa.detail: Cattle plague arriving from British Asia in 1880s-90s killed 90% of cattle in Africa. Destroyed African livelihoods and enabled European colonisers to force Africans into labour market for mines and plantations.

hist_jobber_system.label: Jobber System
hist_jobber_system.subject: history
hist_jobber_system.detail: Industrialists used jobbers to recruit workers from villages. Jobbers were trusted old workers who got villagers jobs, helped them settle. Became figures of authority who demanded money and gifts for favours.

hist_indian_industrialists.label: Indian Industrialists
hist_indian_industrialists.subject: history
hist_indian_industrialists.detail: Dwarkanath Tagore, Dinshaw Petit, Jamsetjee Nusserwanjee Tata, Seth Hukumchand, G.D. Birla established Indian enterprises. Many came from traditional trading communities - Marwaris, Parsees, Chettiars.

hist_swadeshi_mills.label: Swadeshi and Indian Mills
hist_swadeshi_mills.subject: history
hist_swadeshi_mills.detail: During nationalist movements, boycott of foreign goods boosted Indian industries. WWI created demand for Indian manufactured goods. Indian mills produced military supplies. Demand for government protection of Indian industries grew.

hist_orient_strike_bombay.label: Labour Movements in Indian Mills
hist_orient_strike_bombay.subject: history
hist_orient_strike_bombay.detail: Indian workers resisted exploitation through strikes over wages, working conditions and dismissals. General strikes in Bombay mills became important political events. Trade unions formed during early 20th century.

hist_garden_city_movement.label: Garden City Movement
hist_garden_city_movement.subject: history
hist_garden_city_movement.detail: Ebenezer Howard's planned green suburbs with cottages, gardens and open spaces as solution to urban overcrowding. Led to New Earswick near York designed by Raymond Unwin. Influenced town planning worldwide.

hist_bombay_cinema.label: Bombay Cinema Industry
hist_bombay_cinema.subject: history
hist_bombay_cinema.detail: Harishchandra Sakharam Bhatwadekar shot first Indian film in 1896. Dadasaheb Phalke made first Indian feature film Raja Harishchandra (1913). By 1925, Bombay became centre of Indian cinema industry.

hist_plague_bombay_1898.label: Plague in Bombay 1898
hist_plague_bombay_1898.subject: history
hist_plague_bombay_1898.detail: Bubonic plague hit Bombay in 1898 killing thousands. Colonial government demolished inner-city dwellings, quarantined populations. Over 30,000 people fled the city. Led to new public health measures and city expansion.

hist_vernacular_press_act_1878.label: Vernacular Press Act 1878
hist_vernacular_press_act_1878.subject: history
hist_vernacular_press_act_1878.detail: Modelled on Irish Press Laws, gave government extensive rights to censor reports in vernacular newspapers. If newspaper published seditious content, press could be seized. Sparked strong protests from Indian nationalists.

hist_bal_gangadhar_tilak_kesari.label: Tilak and Kesari Newspaper
hist_bal_gangadhar_tilak_kesari.subject: history
hist_bal_gangadhar_tilak_kesari.detail: Tilak edited Kesari (Marathi) and Mahratta (English) newspapers which became strongest critics of British rule. Arrested for sedition multiple times. Newspapers became key instruments of nationalist mobilisation.

hist_indian_novel.label: Indian Novel Tradition
hist_indian_novel.subject: history
hist_indian_novel.detail: First modern Indian novels appeared in mid-19th century. Bankim Chandra's Durgeshnandini (1865) in Bengali, Chandu Menon's Indulekha (1889) in Malayalam, Srinivas Das's Pariksha Guru (1882) in Hindi.

hist_bankim_chandra.label: Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay
hist_bankim_chandra.subject: history
hist_bankim_chandra.detail: Wrote Anandamath (1882) containing hymn Vande Mataram which became anthem of nationalist movement. His novels created pride in Indian past and shaped Bengali literary culture. Also wrote satirical novels on colonial society.

hist_novel_nationalism.label: Novel and Indian Nationalism
hist_novel_nationalism.subject: history
hist_novel_nationalism.detail: Novels helped imagine the nation before it politically existed. Bankim's Anandamath, Rabindranath's Ghare Baire portrayed nationalist struggles. Novels in regional languages united communities through shared reading experience.

hist_novel_women_reform.label: Novels and Women's Question
hist_novel_women_reform.subject: history
hist_novel_women_reform.detail: Novels became medium for discussing women's condition. Rokeya Hossain's Sultana's Dream (1905) imagined gender-reversed world. Many novels criticised child marriage, sati, dowry. Urdu novels encouraged women's education.

hist_novel_caste.label: Novels and Caste Reform
hist_novel_caste.subject: history
hist_novel_caste.detail: Novels in many Indian languages addressed caste oppression. Adiga Veera Shaiva novels in Kannada, Potheri Kunhambu's Saraswativijayam (1892) in Malayalam critiqued caste hierarchy. Dalit literature emerged as powerful genre.

hist_rabindranath_novels.label: Rabindranath Tagore's Novels
hist_rabindranath_novels.subject: history
hist_rabindranath_novels.detail: Ghare Baire (The Home and the World, 1916) explored tensions within Swadeshi movement. Gora (1910) addressed nationalism and identity. His novels probed complexities of modern Indian experience.

hist_second_industrial_revolution.label: Second Industrial Revolution
hist_second_industrial_revolution.subject: history
hist_second_industrial_revolution.detail: Phase of industrialisation from roughly 1870-1914 characterised by steel, chemicals, electricity, and petroleum. Germany and the USA overtook Britain. Key developments: Bessemer steel process, internal combustion engine, telegraph and telephone, and assembly line production. Led to modern corporate capitalism and imperialism.

hist_stolen_generations.label: Stolen Generations (Australia)
hist_stolen_generations.subject: history
hist_stolen_generations.detail: Australian government policy (c. 1910-1970) of forcibly removing Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander children from their families and placing them in institutions or white foster homes. Aimed at cultural assimilation ('breeding out' Aboriginal identity). An estimated 100,000 children were taken. Formally apologised for by Prime Minister Kevin Rudd in 2008.

hist_meiji_reforms.label: Meiji Reforms
hist_meiji_reforms.stage: East Asia: Meiji Japan + Qing Collapse
hist_meiji_reforms.subject: history
hist_meiji_reforms.detail: Comprehensive modernisation programme: abolished feudalism and samurai privileges, created a conscript army, established a modern education system (compulsory from 1872), built railways and telegraph, adopted Western legal codes, created a constitution (1889) with an elected Diet. Sent missions abroad (Iwakura Mission, 1871) to study Western systems.

hist_meiji_constitution.label: Meiji Constitution (1889)
hist_meiji_constitution.stage: East Asia: Meiji Japan + Qing Collapse
hist_meiji_constitution.subject: history
hist_meiji_constitution.detail: Japan's first modern constitution, promulgated in 1889, modelled on the Prussian constitution. Established a bicameral legislature (Diet), but sovereignty resided with the Emperor. The cabinet was responsible to the Emperor, not the Diet. Limited suffrage. It balanced modernisation with traditional imperial authority.

hist_japan_industrialisation.label: Japanese Industrialisation
hist_japan_industrialisation.stage: East Asia: Meiji Japan + Qing Collapse
hist_japan_industrialisation.subject: history
hist_japan_industrialisation.detail: State-led rapid industrialisation after 1868. Government built model factories, railways, and shipyards, then sold many to private zaibatsu (industrial conglomerates like Mitsubishi, Mitsui). Textile industry (especially silk) led early growth. By 1900, Japan was Asia's first industrial power. Heavy industry expanded after the Russo-Japanese War (1905).

hist_zaibatsu.label: Zaibatsu
hist_zaibatsu.stage: East Asia: Meiji Japan + Qing Collapse
hist_zaibatsu.subject: history
hist_zaibatsu.detail: Large Japanese industrial and financial conglomerates that dominated the economy from the Meiji era through World War II. Major zaibatsu included Mitsubishi, Mitsui, Sumitomo, and Yasuda. They had close ties with the government and controlled banking, manufacturing, mining, and trade. Dissolved after WWII but reformed as keiretsu.

hist_japan_imperialism.label: Japanese Imperialism
hist_japan_imperialism.stage: East Asia: Meiji Japan + Qing Collapse
hist_japan_imperialism.subject: history
hist_japan_imperialism.detail: Japan became an imperial power after modernisation. Defeated China in the Sino-Japanese War (1894-95), gaining Taiwan. Defeated Russia in the Russo-Japanese War (1904-05), the first Asian victory over a European power. Annexed Korea (1910). Expanded into Manchuria (1931) and Southeast Asia in WWII.

hist_russo_japanese_war.label: Russo-Japanese War (1904-05)
hist_russo_japanese_war.stage: East Asia: Meiji Japan + Qing Collapse
hist_russo_japanese_war.subject: history
hist_russo_japanese_war.detail: War between Japan and Russia over influence in Manchuria and Korea. Japan's victory stunned the world as it was the first modern military victory of an Asian power over a European one. Boosted Japanese confidence and imperial ambitions. Inspired anti-colonial movements across Asia. Treaty of Portsmouth (1905) ended the war.

hist_boxer_rebellion.label: Boxer Rebellion (1899-1901)
hist_boxer_rebellion.stage: East Asia: Meiji Japan + Qing Collapse
hist_boxer_rebellion.subject: history
hist_boxer_rebellion.detail: Anti-foreign, anti-Christian uprising in China by the 'Righteous Harmony Fists' (Boxers). Besieged foreign legations in Beijing. Suppressed by an eight-nation alliance. The Boxer Protocol (1901) imposed heavy indemnities and further humiliated China. Accelerated the fall of the Qing dynasty.

hist_sun_yat_sen.label: Sun Yat-sen
hist_sun_yat_sen.stage: East Asia: Meiji Japan + Qing Collapse
hist_sun_yat_sen.subject: history
hist_sun_yat_sen.detail: Chinese revolutionary and political leader (1866-1925), called the 'Father of the Nation'. Founded the Tongmenghui and later the Kuomintang (KMT). His Three Principles of the People (nationalism, democracy, people's livelihood) guided the 1911 Revolution. Briefly served as provisional president of the Republic of China.

hist_1911_revolution.label: Chinese Revolution of 1911
hist_1911_revolution.stage: East Asia: Meiji Japan + Qing Collapse
hist_1911_revolution.subject: history
hist_1911_revolution.detail: Revolution that overthrew the Qing Dynasty and established the Republic of China, ending over 2,000 years of imperial rule. Triggered by the Wuchang Uprising. Sun Yat-sen became provisional president but ceded power to Yuan Shikai. China descended into warlordism. Also called the Xinhai Revolution.

hist_kuomintang.label: Kuomintang (KMT / Nationalist Party)
hist_kuomintang.stage: East Asia: Meiji Japan + Qing Collapse
hist_kuomintang.subject: history
hist_kuomintang.detail: Chinese nationalist party founded by Sun Yat-sen in 1912 (reorganised 1919). After Sun's death (1925), Chiang Kai-shek became leader. Initially allied with the Communists against warlords (First United Front), then turned on them in the Shanghai Massacre (1927). Governed mainland China until 1949, then retreated to Taiwan.

hist_three_principles.label: Three Principles of the People
hist_three_principles.stage: East Asia: Meiji Japan + Qing Collapse
hist_three_principles.subject: history
hist_three_principles.detail: Sun Yat-sen's political philosophy comprising: Minzu (nationalism -- freeing China from foreign domination and Manchu rule), Minquan (democracy -- popular sovereignty and constitutional government), and Minsheng (people's livelihood -- equitable distribution of wealth and land reform). Influenced both the KMT and, partially, the CCP.

hist_cunningham.label: Alexander Cunningham
hist_cunningham.subject: history
hist_cunningham.detail: First Director-General of the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI), often called the father of Indian archaeology. Noted brick-robbing at Harappa in 1875. Was focused on Early Historic period and missed the significance of Harappan artefacts initially.

hist_deccan_riots_1875.label: Deccan Riots (1875)
hist_deccan_riots_1875.subject: history
hist_deccan_riots_1875.detail: Peasant uprising in Poona and Ahmednagar districts of Bombay Presidency against moneylenders. Ryots attacked moneylenders' houses, burning debt records. Triggered by foreclosures under ryotwari system. Government appointed Deccan Riots Commission leading to Deccan Agriculturists' Relief Act 1879.

hist_new_delhi_lutyens.label: New Delhi (Lutyens' Delhi)
hist_new_delhi_lutyens.subject: history
hist_new_delhi_lutyens.detail: Capital shifted from Calcutta to Delhi 1911, announced by King George V at Delhi Durbar. Designed by Edwin Lutyens and Herbert Baker. Rashtrapati Bhavan, Secretariat buildings on Raisina Hill, India Gate, Rajpath. Consciously incorporated Indian elements in imperial architecture.

hist_edwin_lutyens.label: Edwin Lutyens
hist_edwin_lutyens.subject: history
hist_edwin_lutyens.detail: British architect who designed the central administrative area of New Delhi including the Viceroy's House (now Rashtrapati Bhavan). Created a grand imperial capital with broad avenues and monumental buildings. Incorporated some Indian architectural elements despite initial resistance.

hist_delhi_durbar_1911.label: Delhi Durbar (1911)
hist_delhi_durbar_1911.subject: history
hist_delhi_durbar_1911.detail: Grand ceremonial assembly where King George V announced the transfer of British Indian capital from Calcutta to Delhi. Decision based on Delhi's historical significance as seat of Mughal power. Also announced reversal of Bengal partition (1905).

hist_plague_bombay_1896.label: Bombay Plague (1896)
hist_plague_bombay_1896.subject: history
hist_plague_bombay_1896.detail: Devastating plague epidemic that killed thousands in Bombay. Government used it as pretext for urban 'improvement': demolishing densely populated areas, widening roads. Plague Committee's intrusive inspection methods caused resentment. Tilak criticised heavy-handed government response.

hist_mahatma_gandhi.label: Mahatma Gandhi
hist_mahatma_gandhi.subject: history
hist_mahatma_gandhi.detail: Mohandas Karamchand Gandhi (1869-1948). Returned from South Africa to India in 1915. Transformed the nationalist movement through satyagraha (truth-force), ahimsa (non-violence) and mass mobilisation. Called 'Mahatma' by Rabindranath Tagore. Assassinated 30 January 1948 by Nathuram Godse.

hist_champaran_satyagraha.label: Champaran Satyagraha (1917)
hist_champaran_satyagraha.subject: history
hist_champaran_satyagraha.detail: Gandhi's first major satyagraha in India. Peasants in Champaran (Bihar) forced to grow indigo by European planters under tinkathia system. Gandhi investigated conditions, negotiated with planters and government. Established his method of grassroots mobilisation and fact-finding.

hist_rowlatt_act.label: Rowlatt Act (1919)
hist_rowlatt_act.subject: history
hist_rowlatt_act.detail: Legislation giving government powers to detain political prisoners without trial. Based on Rowlatt Committee recommendations. Gandhi called it 'Black Act' and organised nationwide hartal (6 April 1919). Led to Jallianwala Bagh massacre (13 April 1919). Catalysed mass nationalist movement.

hist_jallianwala_bagh.label: Jallianwala Bagh Massacre (1919)
hist_jallianwala_bagh.subject: history
hist_jallianwala_bagh.detail: General Dyer ordered troops to fire on unarmed gathering at Jallianwala Bagh, Amritsar on 13 April 1919 (Baisakhi day). Hundreds killed, thousands wounded. Dyer later called it a 'moral duty'. Deeply shocked India. Rabindranath Tagore renounced knighthood in protest.

hist_satyagraha_concept.label: Satyagraha
hist_satyagraha_concept.subject: history
hist_satyagraha_concept.detail: Gandhi's philosophy of non-violent resistance, literally 'truth-force'. Developed in South Africa against racial discrimination. Applied in India through mass movements. Combined moral force with political action. Included boycotts, strikes, civil disobedience, constructive programme.

hist_swadeshi_movement.label: Swadeshi Movement (1905-08)
hist_swadeshi_movement.subject: history
hist_swadeshi_movement.detail: Movement against partition of Bengal (1905) by Lord Curzon. Boycott of British goods, promotion of Indian-made goods. Led by Tilak, Bipin Chandra Pal, Lala Lajpat Rai (Lal-Bal-Pal). Revolutionised nationalist politics. Brought new methods: strikes, passive resistance.

hist_muslim_league.label: All India Muslim League
hist_muslim_league.subject: history
hist_muslim_league.detail: Founded 1906 at Dhaka by Aga Khan and Nawab Salimullah. Demanded separate electorates (achieved in Morley-Minto Reforms 1909). Under Jinnah from 1930s, demanded Pakistan from 1940. Performed poorly in 1937 elections but swept Muslim seats in 1946.

hist_separate_electorates.label: Separate Electorates
hist_separate_electorates.subject: history
hist_separate_electorates.detail: System where Muslims voted only for Muslim candidates in reserved constituencies. Introduced by Morley-Minto Reforms (1909). Expanded by Lucknow Pact (1916), Communal Award (1932). Congress opposed it as divisive. Became foundation for two-nation politics.

hist_agaria_iron_smelters.label: Agaria Iron Smelters
hist_agaria_iron_smelters.subject: history
hist_agaria_iron_smelters.detail: Community specialising in iron smelting in Central India. They helped discover iron ore at Rajhara Hills that later supplied Bhilai Steel Plant. Many were devastated by famines and forest laws in the late nineteenth century.

hist_tisco.label: TISCO
hist_tisco.subject: history
hist_tisco.detail: Tata Iron and Steel Company set up at Jamshedpur on banks of river Subarnarekha, began producing steel in 1912. Became the biggest steel industry within the British empire. WWI created huge demand enabling expansion.

hist_tagore_santiniketan.label: Tagore's Santiniketan
hist_tagore_santiniketan.subject: history
hist_tagore_santiniketan.detail: Established by Rabindranath Tagore in 1901, 100 km from Calcutta. Envisioned as an 'abode of peace' where children could learn creatively in natural surroundings. Combined modern Western civilisation with best of Indian tradition.

hist_arya_samaj.label: Arya Samaj
hist_arya_samaj.subject: history
hist_arya_samaj.detail: Founded by Swami Dayanand Saraswati in 1875 to reform Hinduism. Supported widow remarriage and established schools for girls in Punjab. Sought to return to Vedic traditions.

hist_satyashodhak_samaj.label: Satyashodhak Samaj
hist_satyashodhak_samaj.subject: history
hist_satyashodhak_samaj.detail: Association founded by Jyotirao Phule to propagate caste equality. Argued that Shudras and Ati Shudras should unite to challenge caste discrimination imposed by Aryan invaders.

hist_pandita_ramabai.label: Pandita Ramabai
hist_pandita_ramabai.subject: history
hist_pandita_ramabai.detail: Sanskrit scholar who wrote about miserable lives of upper-caste Hindu women. Founded a widows' home at Poona providing shelter and economic training to widows treated badly by their husbands' relatives.

hist_swami_vivekananda.label: Swami Vivekananda
hist_swami_vivekananda.subject: history
hist_swami_vivekananda.detail: Born Narendra Nath Dutta (1863-1902), disciple of Ramakrishna Paramhansa. Founded Ramakrishna Mission stressing salvation through social service. Spoke at World Parliament of Religions at Chicago in 1893.

hist_aligarh_movement.label: Aligarh Movement
hist_aligarh_movement.subject: history
hist_aligarh_movement.detail: Mohammedan Anglo-Oriental College founded by Sayyid Ahmed Khan in 1875 at Aligarh, later became Aligarh Muslim University. Offered modern education including Western science to Muslims.

hist_prarthana_samaj.label: Prarthana Samaj
hist_prarthana_samaj.subject: history
hist_prarthana_samaj.detail: Established in 1867 at Bombay. Sought to remove caste restrictions, abolish child marriage, encourage women's education and end ban on widow remarriage. Drew upon Hindu, Buddhist and Christian texts.

hist_abanindranath_tagore.label: Abanindranath Tagore
hist_abanindranath_tagore.subject: history
hist_abanindranath_tagore.detail: (1871-1951). Nephew of Rabindranath Tagore. Founder of Bengal School of Art and Indian Society of Oriental Art (1907). Principal of Calcutta Government School of Art. Revived Indian traditional idioms against Western academic realism. "Bharat Mata" (1905) became a national-movement icon. Taught a generation including Nandalal Bose. Also children's author under pseudonym "Aban Thakur".

hist_nandalal_bose.label: Nandalal Bose
hist_nandalal_bose.subject: history
hist_nandalal_bose.detail: (1882-1966). Student of Abanindranath Tagore. Principal of Kala Bhavan Santiniketan 1922-51. Pioneered "contextual modernism" in Indian art. Painted the "Haripura Panels" for 1938 Haripura Congress Session — Santiniketan-style depictions of Indian rural life. Later designed illustrations for the Indian Constitution manuscript (1949-50). Awarded Padma Vibhushan 1954.

hist_bharat_mata_prints.label: Bharat Mata Prints
hist_bharat_mata_prints.subject: history
hist_bharat_mata_prints.detail: With the spread of nationalism in early 20th century, popular prints began carrying nationalist messages showing Bharat Mata as a goddess with national flag, nationalist heroes, and gods slaughtering the British.

hist_inc_founding.label: Indian National Congress Founded
hist_inc_founding.subject: history
hist_inc_founding.detail: Established in December 1885 when 72 delegates met at Bombay. Early leaders included Dadabhai Naoroji, Pherozeshah Mehta, Badruddin Tyabji, W.C. Bonnerji, Surendranath Banerji. A.O. Hume played a role in uniting Indians.

hist_moderates.label: Moderate Phase of Congress
hist_moderates.subject: history
hist_moderates.detail: First twenty years of Congress (1885-1905). Demanded greater Indian representation in government, civil service exams in India, separation of judiciary from executive. Used petitions, speeches and newspaper articles.

hist_radicals_tilak.label: Radical Nationalists
hist_radicals_tilak.subject: history
hist_radicals_tilak.detail: Leaders like Tilak, Lala Lajpat Rai and Bipin Chandra Pal criticised Moderate 'politics of prayers'. Tilak's slogan 'Freedom is my birthright and I shall have it!' Advocated self-reliance, mass mobilisation and boycott.

hist_partition_bengal_1905.label: Partition of Bengal 1905
hist_partition_bengal_1905.subject: history
hist_partition_bengal_1905.detail: Viceroy Curzon partitioned Bengal separating East Bengal from main province. British motives were to curtail Bengali political influence. Triggered the Swadeshi movement, the strongest mass protest yet.

hist_russian_revolution_1917.label: Russian Revolution 1917
hist_russian_revolution_1917.subject: history
hist_russian_revolution_1917.detail: Two phases: February Revolution (monarchy fell, Tsar abdicated 2 March) and October Revolution (24 October, Bolsheviks seized power). Led to world's first socialist state. Inspired anti-colonial movements worldwide including India.

hist_tsar_nicholas_ii.label: Tsar Nicholas II
hist_tsar_nicholas_ii.subject: history
hist_tsar_nicholas_ii.detail: Autocratic ruler of Russian Empire who refused to share power with parliament (Duma). Dismissed first two Dumas, packed third with conservatives. WWI defeats and food shortages destroyed his authority. Abdicated 2 March 1917.

hist_bloody_sunday_1905.label: Bloody Sunday 1905
hist_bloody_sunday_1905.subject: history
hist_bloody_sunday_1905.detail: On a Sunday in 1905, procession of workers led by Father Gapon to Winter Palace was attacked by police and Cossacks. Over 100 killed, 300 wounded. Started the 1905 Revolution leading to creation of Duma.

hist_bolsheviks.label: Bolsheviks
hist_bolsheviks.subject: history
hist_bolsheviks.detail: Faction of Russian Social Democratic Workers Party led by Lenin. Believed in disciplined, restricted membership party. Seized power in October 1917 through Military Revolutionary Committee under Trotsky.

hist_lenin.label: Vladimir Lenin
hist_lenin.subject: history
hist_lenin.detail: Leader of Bolsheviks who returned from exile in April 1917 with April Theses: end war, transfer land to peasants, nationalise banks. Led October Revolution. Renamed party to Communist Party. Dismissed Constituent Assembly.

hist_february_revolution.label: February Revolution 1917
hist_february_revolution.subject: history
hist_february_revolution.detail: Began 22 February with factory lockouts and women-led strikes on International Women's Day in Petrograd. Cavalry refused to fire on demonstrators. Soldiers mutinied and formed Petrograd Soviet. Tsar abdicated.

hist_october_revolution.label: October Revolution 1917
hist_october_revolution.subject: history
hist_october_revolution.detail: On 24 October 1917 Bolsheviks seized government buildings, ship Aurora shelled Winter Palace. Ministers surrendered. Congress of Soviets approved Bolshevik action. Banks and industries nationalised, land declared social property.

hist_socialism_concept.label: Socialism as Ideology
hist_socialism_concept.subject: history
hist_socialism_concept.detail: Opposed private property as root of social ills. Robert Owen built cooperative New Harmony. Louis Blanc wanted government-encouraged cooperatives. Socialists formed Second International in 1870s. Labour Party in Britain formed 1905.

hist_russian_civil_war.label: Russian Civil War
hist_russian_civil_war.subject: history
hist_russian_civil_war.detail: 1918-1920 war between Bolsheviks (Reds), Socialist Revolutionaries (Greens) and pro-Tsarists (Whites) backed by French, American, British and Japanese troops. Bolsheviks won by January 1920 through cooperation with non-Russian nationalities.

hist_weimar_republic.label: Weimar Republic
hist_weimar_republic.subject: history
hist_weimar_republic.detail: Democratic republic established after WWI defeat. Suffered Versailles Treaty humiliation, hyperinflation of 1923, Great Depression unemployment of 6 million. Proportional representation and Article 48 made it vulnerable to dictatorship.

hist_treaty_versailles.label: Treaty of Versailles
hist_treaty_versailles.subject: history
hist_treaty_versailles.detail: Harsh peace imposed on Germany after WWI. Lost overseas colonies, 10% population, 13% territories, 75% iron, 26% coal. War Guilt Clause made Germany pay £6 billion compensation. Rhineland occupied.

hist_deforestation_colonial.label: Colonial Deforestation
hist_deforestation_colonial.subject: history
hist_deforestation_colonial.detail: Between 1880 and 1920, cultivated area in India rose by 6.7 million hectares. Forests cleared for commercial crops (jute, sugar, wheat, cotton), railways (sleepers), shipbuilding and plantations. Colonial state saw forests as unproductive wilderness.

hist_indian_forest_act_1865.label: Indian Forest Act
hist_indian_forest_act_1865.subject: history
hist_indian_forest_act_1865.detail: Forest laws restricted customary rights of forest communities. Forests classified as reserved (no access), protected (limited access) and village forests. Forest department created to manage timber for railways and trade.

hist_bastar_rebellion_1910.label: Bastar Rebellion 1910
hist_bastar_rebellion_1910.subject: history
hist_bastar_rebellion_1910.detail: People of Bastar (Dhurwas, Bhatra, Muria Gonds) rebelled in 1910 when colonial government reserved two-thirds of their forests. Led by Gunda Dhur. Bazaars looted, grain redistributed. Suppressed by British troops.

hist_forest_villages.label: Forest Villages and Labour
hist_forest_villages.subject: history
hist_forest_villages.detail: Colonial forest department established forest villages to provide cheap labour. Villagers worked for free for the forest department in exchange for living in forests. This was a form of forced labour (begar).

hist_java_forest_management.label: Dutch Forest Management in Java
hist_java_forest_management.subject: history
hist_java_forest_management.detail: Dutch controlled Java's forests using same scientific forestry. Imposed Blandongdiensten system of forced wood-cutting and transport. Surontiko Samin of Randublatung village led resistance movement against Dutch forest policies.

hist_railway_timber_demand.label: Railway Timber Demand
hist_railway_timber_demand.subject: history
hist_railway_timber_demand.detail: By 1946, railway network of over 765,000 km laid in India required vast quantities of sleepers. Each mile of railway needed 1,760-2,000 sleepers. Forests in Madras Presidency were completely denuded for sleeper supply.

hist_forest_communities_impact.label: Impact on Forest Communities
hist_forest_communities_impact.subject: history
hist_forest_communities_impact.detail: Forest laws criminalised everyday practices of forest dwellers - collecting firewood, grazing cattle, hunting. Many communities forced to steal into forests or face punishment. Livelihoods destroyed, forcing migration.

hist_dhangar_shepherds.label: Dhangar Shepherds
hist_dhangar_shepherds.subject: history
hist_dhangar_shepherds.detail: Important pastoral community of Maharashtra, population around 467,000 in early 20th century. Stayed in central plateau during monsoon, migrated to Konkan in October. Flocks manured Konkani peasants' fields in symbiotic relationship.

hist_colonial_grazing_restrictions.label: Colonial Grazing Restrictions
hist_colonial_grazing_restrictions.subject: history
hist_colonial_grazing_restrictions.detail: Waste Land Rules, Forest Acts and Criminal Tribes Act restricted pastoral movement. Grazing taxes collected per head of cattle. Pasture lands converted to cultivation. Pastoralists criminalised as suspect communities requiring surveillance.

hist_criminal_tribes_act.label: Criminal Tribes Act 1871
hist_criminal_tribes_act.subject: history
hist_criminal_tribes_act.detail: Colonial act that classified certain communities as criminal by nature and birth. Pastoral and nomadic groups forced to live in notified village settlements, could not move without permit. Repealed only in 1952.

hist_maasai_pastoralists.label: Maasai Pastoralists of Africa
hist_maasai_pastoralists.subject: history
hist_maasai_pastoralists.detail: East African pastoral community in Kenya and Tanzania whose grazing lands were severely reduced by colonial boundaries and game reserves. Lost 60% of pre-colonial lands. Elders lost authority as young warriors (murran) sought new livelihoods.

hist_american_wheat_farming.label: American Wheat Farming
hist_american_wheat_farming.subject: history
hist_american_wheat_farming.detail: US Great Plains opened for wheat farming from 1860s. Government gave 160 acres free (Homestead Act). Mechanisation with John Deere plough, combine harvesters. Led to Dust Bowl of 1930s from aggressive ploughing.

hist_ranji_cricket.label: Ranjitsinhji
hist_ranji_cricket.subject: history
hist_ranji_cricket.detail: Indian prince from Kathiawar who played for England and Sussex in 1890s. His success challenged racial claims about English superiority in cricket. Named after him, Ranji Trophy became India's premier domestic tournament.

hist_rational_dress_society.label: Rational Dress Society
hist_rational_dress_society.subject: history
hist_rational_dress_society.detail: Founded in 1881 in England to challenge restrictive Victorian women's clothing. Promoted practical dress that did not deform or impede movement. Part of wider women's emancipation movement.

hist_bastar_rebellion.label: Bastar Rebellion (1910)
hist_bastar_rebellion.subject: history
hist_bastar_rebellion.detail: Adivasi uprising in Chhattisgarh (Bastar) against 1905 forest reservations + shifting cultivation ban. Leader Gunda Dhur. Villages burned schools, police posts, bazaars. British suppressed by May 1910; reserved area reduced to half of plan.

hist_birsa_munda.label: Birsa Munda
hist_birsa_munda.subject: history
hist_birsa_munda.detail: Munda tribal leader (1875-1900) in Chhotanagpur. Led Ulgulan movement against landlord + missionary + colonial encroachment. Died in Ranchi jail 1900. Symbol of adivasi identity.

hist_imperial_forest_research_dehradun.label: Imperial Forest Research Institute (Dehradun)
hist_imperial_forest_research_dehradun.subject: history
hist_imperial_forest_research_dehradun.detail: Set up 1906 in Dehradun to research and teach scientific forestry. First forestry school in British Empire.

hist_modernisation.label: Modernisation (concept)
hist_modernisation.stage: East Asia: Meiji Japan + Qing Collapse
hist_modernisation.subject: history
hist_modernisation.detail: Process of economic, political, social transformation: industrialisation, nation-building, democratisation, secularisation. Japan + China followed distinct paths in response to Western imperialism.

hist_pabna_agrarian_league.label: Pabna Agrarian League 1873
hist_pabna_agrarian_league.subject: history
hist_pabna_agrarian_league.detail: Agrarian league formed in Yusufshahi Parganah of Pabna district (Bengal) in May 1873 to resist zamindars' illegal rent enhancements and forced evictions. Organised rent-strikes and court battles. Spread across East Bengal through 1870s-80s. Hindu-Muslim peasant unity. Result: Bengal Tenancy Act 1885. Supported by Indian Association (Surendranath Banerjee, Ananda Mohan Bose, Dwarkanath Ganguli) and intellectuals Bankim and R.C. Dutt.

hist_deccan_agriculturists_relief_act.label: Deccan Agriculturists' Relief Act 1879
hist_deccan_agriculturists_relief_act.subject: history
hist_deccan_agriculturists_relief_act.detail: Legislative response to Deccan Riots 1875. Protected Ryotwari peasants of Maharashtra against rapacious moneylenders (mostly Marwari/Gujarati outsiders). Gave peasants protections against summary execution of debt decrees and curbed predatory lending. Product of pressure from Poona Sarvajanik Sabha's campaign.

hist_bengal_tenancy_act.label: Bengal Tenancy Act 1885
hist_bengal_tenancy_act.subject: history
hist_bengal_tenancy_act.detail: Legislative response to Pabna agrarian unrest and decade-long campaigns by the Indian Association and nationalist press. Gave tenants occupancy rights and some protection against illegal rent enhancement, but Indian Association criticised it for benefitting non-cultivating middlemen (jotedars).

hist_vasudev_balwant_phadke.label: Vasudev Balwant Phadke 1879
hist_vasudev_balwant_phadke.subject: history
hist_vasudev_balwant_phadke.detail: Educated clerk in Maharashtra who organised a Ramosi peasant band of ~50 men in 1879 for social banditry against British rule and moneylenders. Regarded as an early rebel of the nationalist tradition. Captured and tried; died in prison.

hist_kuka_revolt.label: Kuka Revolt 1872
hist_kuka_revolt.subject: history
hist_kuka_revolt.detail: Namdhari Sikh messianic movement in Punjab led by Baba Ram Singh. Anti-British and reformist (opposed cow slaughter, British education). Came to violent climax in 1872 when 49 Kukas were blown up by cannon on orders of Deputy Commissioner Cowan at Malerkotla. Baba Ram Singh exiled to Burma.

hist_mappila_outbreaks.label: Mappila Outbreaks (Malabar)
hist_mappila_outbreaks.subject: history
hist_mappila_outbreaks.detail: Recurring uprisings of Muslim (Mappila) peasants of Malabar against Hindu landlords and British authorities from the 1830s to the Mappila Rebellion of 1921. Driven by agrarian exploitation but expressed in religious idiom. Twenty-nine outbreaks between 1836 and 1854 alone.

hist_neel_darpan.label: Neel Darpan (1860)
hist_neel_darpan.subject: history
hist_neel_darpan.detail: Bengali play by Dinabandhu Mitra depicting brutalities of indigo planters against ryots. Translated into English by Michael Madhusudan Dutt. Reverend James Long (translator-publisher) was imprisoned for a month and fined for its publication. Galvanised intellectual support for the Indigo Revolt.

hist_ilbert_bill.label: Ilbert Bill 1883
hist_ilbert_bill.subject: history
hist_ilbert_bill.detail: Proposed by Law Member C.P. Ilbert under Viceroy Lord Ripon to allow Indian magistrates to try Europeans in criminal cases. Violent European ('White Mutiny') opposition forced the bill's dilution. Exposed British racism and taught nationalists the power of organised agitation — a crucial lesson behind founding of INC in 1885.

hist_arms_act_1878.label: Arms Act 1878
hist_arms_act_1878.subject: history
hist_arms_act_1878.detail: Passed under Viceroy Lord Lytton. Prohibited Indians from possessing arms without a licence while exempting Europeans and Eurasians. A racial slight that became a major nationalist grievance and campaign point.

hist_ao_hume.label: Allan Octavian Hume
hist_ao_hume.subject: history
hist_ao_hume.detail: Retired British ICS officer (Secretary to Dept. of Revenue, Agriculture and Commerce in 1878). Chief organiser of the Indian National Congress in 1885. The 'safety valve theory' — that Hume founded the Congress on Viceroy Dufferin's secret instructions to forestall revolt — has been disproved: Hume acted on his own initiative and Dufferin was actually hostile from May 1885 onwards.

hist_safety_valve_theory.label: Safety Valve Theory
hist_safety_valve_theory.subject: history
hist_safety_valve_theory.detail: Myth first stated in William Wedderburn's 1913 biography of Hume and popularised by Lala Lajpat Rai (1916) and R. Palme Dutt (India Today). Claims INC was engineered by Hume on Viceroy Dufferin's instructions as a safety valve to forestall mass revolt. Bipin Chandra demonstrates the theory's evidence is fabricated (the 'seven volumes of secret reports' were occult communications from Theosophical mahatmas, not CID files).

hist_wc_bonnerjee.label: W.C. Bonnerjee
hist_wc_bonnerjee.subject: history
hist_wc_bonnerjee.detail: Womesh Chandra Bonnerjee — Calcutta barrister, first President of the Indian National Congress at its Bombay session, December 1885. Defined Congress objectives as 'fuller development and consolidation of sentiments of national unity.'

hist_surendranath_banerjee.label: Surendranath Banerjee
hist_surendranath_banerjee.subject: history
hist_surendranath_banerjee.detail: 'Indian Burke.' Founded Indian Association 1876 with Ananda Mohan Bose. Organised All-India National Conferences 1883 and 1885. Leader of Bengal Moderates. First Indian journalist jailed for duty (1883, Bengalee editorial on Justice Norris). Merged his conference with INC in 1886. Later split from INC in 1918 and opposed Non-Cooperation.

hist_pherozeshah_mehta.label: Pherozeshah Mehta
hist_pherozeshah_mehta.subject: history
hist_pherozeshah_mehta.detail: 'Lion of Bombay.' Bombay barrister influenced by Dadabhai Naoroji. Co-founded Bombay Presidency Association 1885 and INC. Dominant figure in Congress from mid-1890s till his death in 1915. Brilliant debater in the Imperial Legislative Council (1895-1901), organised India's first legislative walk-out. Led the Moderate hard-line at the 1907 Surat Split.

hist_g_subramaniya_iyer.label: G. Subramaniya Iyer
hist_g_subramaniya_iyer.subject: history
hist_g_subramaniya_iyer.detail: Founded The Hindu newspaper in 1878 (along with M. Viraraghavachariar) and Swadesamitran. Co-founder of Madras Mahajan Sabha (1884). One of the 72 founding delegates of the INC 1885. Early economic nationalist.

hist_mg_ranade.label: Justice Mahadev Govind Ranade
hist_mg_ranade.subject: history
hist_mg_ranade.detail: 'Doyen of reformers in Maharashtra.' Bombay High Court judge, economist, social reformer. Founded Poona Sarvajanik Sabha (1870), Prarthana Samaj (co-founder with Atmaram Pandurang). Wrote on Indian economics — trained Gokhale and influenced the entire Moderate school. Advocated industrialisation.

hist_indian_association_1876.label: Indian Association (Bengal)
hist_indian_association_1876.subject: history
hist_indian_association_1876.detail: Founded in Calcutta by Surendranath Banerjee and Ananda Mohan Bose as a more militant alternative to the zamindar-dominated British Indian Association. Campaigned against ICS age limit (1877-79), Vernacular Press Act, Arms Act. Organised the first All-India National Conferences (1883, 1885). Merged with INC in 1886.

hist_poona_sarvajanik_sabha.label: Poona Sarvajanik Sabha
hist_poona_sarvajanik_sabha.subject: history
hist_poona_sarvajanik_sabha.detail: Founded 1870 in Poona under the leadership of Justice M.G. Ranade. Organised peasant campaigns against land revenue settlement of 1867 (contributed to Deccan Riots 1875). Supported Deccan Agriculturists' Relief Bill. Published influential Quarterly Journal. Predecessor institution to INC.

hist_madras_mahajan_sabha.label: Madras Mahajan Sabha 1884
hist_madras_mahajan_sabha.subject: history
hist_madras_mahajan_sabha.detail: Founded in Madras by M. Viraraghavachariar, G. Subramaniya Iyer and P. Ananda Charlu. Regional nationalist platform feeding into INC the next year.

hist_bombay_presidency_association.label: Bombay Presidency Association 1885
hist_bombay_presidency_association.subject: history
hist_bombay_presidency_association.detail: Founded 1885 by Pherozeshah Mehta, K.T. Telang, Badruddin Tyabji, breaking away from older Dadabhai Framji and Dinshaw Petit. Western-India nationalist platform that fed into INC founding.

hist_british_indian_association_bengal.label: British Indian Association (Bengal)
hist_british_indian_association_bengal.subject: history
hist_british_indian_association_bengal.detail: Founded 1851 in Calcutta — earliest organised Indian political association. Initially progressive but became dominated by big zamindars (Maharaja Jotendra Mohan Tagore, etc.) and lost its anti-British edge by the 1870s — which spurred the formation of Indian Association 1876.

hist_amrita_bazar_patrika.label: Amrita Bazar Patrika
hist_amrita_bazar_patrika.subject: history
hist_amrita_bazar_patrika.detail: Founded 1868 as a Bengali weekly by Sisir Kumar Ghosh and Motilal Ghosh. Became English-language overnight in 1878 to evade the Vernacular Press Act — a famous piece of anti-colonial cunning. Long-running nationalist daily, most fearless critic of British rule.

hist_the_hindu_newspaper.label: The Hindu
hist_the_hindu_newspaper.subject: history
hist_the_hindu_newspaper.detail: Founded 1878 in Madras by G. Subramaniya Iyer and five others (the 'Triplicane Six'). Became a leading English-language nationalist daily of South India. Still published.

hist_tribune_newspaper.label: The Tribune (Lahore)
hist_tribune_newspaper.subject: history
hist_tribune_newspaper.detail: Founded 1881 in Lahore by Dyal Singh Majithia. Major nationalist English daily of Punjab. Consistently Moderate and then Congress-aligned.

hist_bengalee_newspaper.label: Bengalee (newspaper)
hist_bengalee_newspaper.subject: history
hist_bengalee_newspaper.detail: Calcutta English newspaper purchased by Surendranath Banerjee in 1879. Editorial vehicle for Moderate Bengal nationalism. Source of the 1883 editorial on Justice Norris for which Banerjee became first Indian journalist to be jailed for contempt of court.

hist_mahratta_newspaper.label: Mahratta (newspaper)
hist_mahratta_newspaper.subject: history
hist_mahratta_newspaper.detail: English weekly founded by B.G. Tilak and G.G. Agarkar in 1881 (companion to Marathi Kesari). Tilak took sole charge from 1888.

hist_keshab_chandra_sen.label: Keshab Chandra Sen
hist_keshab_chandra_sen.subject: history
hist_keshab_chandra_sen.detail: Brahmo leader after Debendranath Tagore. Split from Tagore in 1866 to found Brahmo Samaj of India — more radical on caste and women's rights. Further split in 1878 (Sadharan Brahmo Samaj) after his daughter's marriage as minor. Influential on religious universalism ('all established religions are true').

hist_theosophical_society.label: Theosophical Society
hist_theosophical_society.subject: history
hist_theosophical_society.detail: Founded in New York in 1875 by Madame Helena Blavatsky and Colonel Henry Olcott. Moved headquarters to Adyar (Madras) in 1882. Promoted revival of Eastern religions and spiritualism. Annie Besant became President in 1907 and used the Society as base for Indian political work and Home Rule League.

hist_ramakrishna_mission.label: Ramakrishna Mission
hist_ramakrishna_mission.subject: history
hist_ramakrishna_mission.detail: Founded 1 May 1897 in Belur (near Calcutta) by Swami Vivekananda in honour of his guru Sri Ramakrishna Paramahamsa. Combined Vedantic spirituality with practical service ('service to humanity is service to God'). Ran schools, hospitals, famine relief.

hist_narayana_guru.label: Sri Narayana Guru
hist_narayana_guru.subject: history
hist_narayana_guru.detail: Kerala social reformer from Ezhava (backward) caste. Consecrated a Shiva temple at Aruvippuram in 1888 in defiance of caste restrictions. Founded Sri Narayana Dharma Paripalana Yogam (SNDP) in 1903. Slogan: 'One caste, one religion, one God for mankind.'

hist_syed_ahmed_khan.label: Syed Ahmed Khan
hist_syed_ahmed_khan.subject: history
hist_syed_ahmed_khan.detail: Muslim reformer and educator. Founded Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental College at Aligarh 1875 (later Aligarh Muslim University 1920). Advocated modern education for Muslims and reconciliation of Islam with modernity. Argued for Muslim political quiescence and cooperation with British. Precursor to Aligarh Movement.

hist_rc_dutt_economic_history.label: R.C. Dutt's 'Economic History of India'
hist_rc_dutt_economic_history.subject: history
hist_rc_dutt_economic_history.detail: Two-volume Economic History of India (1902, 1904) by Romesh Chandra Dutt, retired ICS officer and INC President 1899. Systematic nationalist indictment of British economic policies — drain, deindustrialisation, revenue exploitation. Cornerstone of Moderate economic critique.

hist_poverty_un_british_rule_book.label: 'Poverty and Un-British Rule in India'
hist_poverty_un_british_rule_book.subject: history
hist_poverty_un_british_rule_book.detail: 1901 book by Dadabhai Naoroji culminating his decades of Drain Theory advocacy. Argued British rule was 'un-British' — alien to Britain's own professed ideals — because it systematically drained Indian wealth.

hist_gk_gokhale.label: Gopal Krishna Gokhale
hist_gk_gokhale.subject: history
hist_gk_gokhale.detail: Moderate leader, economist, trained by M.G. Ranade and G.V. Joshi. Entered Imperial Legislative Council 1902. Budget speech of 26 March 1902 made him India's 'greatest parliamentarian.' Founded Servants of India Society 1905. Gandhi's political guru. Died 1915. Recognised as 'Leader of the Opposition' in the Imperial Council.

hist_tilak_sedition_trial_1897.label: Tilak Sedition Trial 1897
hist_tilak_sedition_trial_1897.subject: history
hist_tilak_sedition_trial_1897.detail: Tilak arrested July 1897 under IPC 124A for Kesari's 'Shivaji's Utterances' and his Shivaji Festival speech, which the prosecution portrayed as incitement after the Chaphekar brothers' assassination of plague officer Rand in Poona. Judge Strachey defined 'disaffection' as 'absence of affection' — notorious jurisprudence. Eighteen months rigorous imprisonment. Earned him the title 'Lokamanya.'

hist_tilak_sedition_trial_1908.label: Tilak Sedition Trial 1908
hist_tilak_sedition_trial_1908.subject: history
hist_tilak_sedition_trial_1908.detail: Second sedition trial of Tilak, 24 June 1908, for Kesari articles on the Muzaffarpur bomb. Six years' transportation by Justice Davar; sent to Mandalay jail in Burma (released 1914). Massive Bombay textile mill strike in protest (6 days, 16 killed) — Lenin hailed it as 'the entrance of the Indian working class on the political stage.'

hist_chaphekar_brothers.label: Chaphekar Brothers 1898
hist_chaphekar_brothers.subject: history
hist_chaphekar_brothers.detail: Damodar and Balkrishna Chaphekar of Poona assassinated Rand (Chairman of Plague Committee) and Lt. Ayerst on 27 June 1897 in protest against brutal anti-plague measures. Earliest assassination of British officials in modern Indian politics. Provided the pretext for Tilak's 1897 prosecution.

hist_ganapati_festival_tilak.label: Tilak Ganapati & Shivaji Festivals
hist_ganapati_festival_tilak.subject: history
hist_ganapati_festival_tilak.detail: Tilak began using the Ganapati festival (1893) and the Shivaji festival (1896) to transform private religious observance into public nationalist assembly — songs, speeches, symbols. Reached large non-literate audiences. Major innovation in mass political mobilisation; also criticised later as communalising the public sphere.

hist_sisir_motilal_ghosh.label: Sisir Kumar & Motilal Ghosh
hist_sisir_motilal_ghosh.subject: history
hist_sisir_motilal_ghosh.detail: Brothers, editors of Amrita Bazar Patrika (founded 1868). Led the paper's famous overnight conversion to English in 1878 to evade the Vernacular Press Act.

hist_indian_councils_act_1861.label: Indian Councils Act 1861
hist_indian_councils_act_1861.subject: history
hist_indian_councils_act_1861.detail: First constitutional enactment after 1857. Enlarged Governor-General's Executive Council with 6-12 additional members (half non-official) to form 'Imperial Legislative Council' for lawmaking. No powers of discussion over budget, administration or major bills. Met ~25 days/year till 1892. Restored portfolio system and decentralised legislation to Bombay and Madras presidencies.

hist_indian_councils_act_1892.label: Indian Councils Act 1892
hist_indian_councils_act_1892.subject: history
hist_indian_councils_act_1892.detail: Expanded council membership to 10-16, allowed some indirect elections through municipal/district boards. Gave members right to discuss the annual budget (but not vote) and to ask questions (but not supplementaries). Official majority preserved. Nationalists condemned it as a mockery and began demanding elected majority and self-government from 1904 onwards.

hist_madan_mohan_malaviya.label: Madan Mohan Malaviya
hist_madan_mohan_malaviya.subject: history
hist_madan_mohan_malaviya.detail: Moderate leader, journalist, educationist. Three-time INC president (1909, 1918, 1932). Founded Banaras Hindu University 1916. Opposed Lucknow Pact's separate electorates. Title 'Mahamana.'

hist_rash_behari_ghosh.label: Rash Behari Ghosh
hist_rash_behari_ghosh.subject: history
hist_rash_behari_ghosh.detail: Moderate leader, Calcutta barrister. Congress president at the aborted Surat session December 1907 (Extremists objected to his election, triggering the Split). Re-elected president at Madras session 1908.

hist_lord_curzon.label: Lord Curzon (Viceroy 1899-1905)
hist_lord_curzon.subject: history
hist_lord_curzon.detail: Viceroy 1899-1905. Imperial absolutist. Partitioned Bengal 1905. Founded Archaeological Survey re-org 1902; Indian Universities Act 1904. Convocation Address 1905 claiming 'truth as a Western conception' was famously ridiculed by Amrita Bazar Patrika. 'My policy has been to reduce the Congress to impotence' (1903).

hist_bande_mataram_song.label: Bande Mataram
hist_bande_mataram_song.subject: history
hist_bande_mataram_song.detail: Sanskrit hymn from Bankim Chandra's novel Anandamath (1882, written 1870s). Became the movement anthem of the Swadeshi Movement (1905-08) and all subsequent nationalist movements. Later adopted as national song of India.

hist_aurobindo_ghose.label: Aurobindo Ghose
hist_aurobindo_ghose.subject: history
hist_aurobindo_ghose.detail: Extremist leader, ideologue of Swadeshi. Principal of Bengal National College 1906. Edited Bande Mataram and Karmayogin. Accused in Alipore Bomb Case 1908; acquitted. Retired to Pondicherry in 1910 for spiritual life.

hist_bipin_chandra_pal.label: Bipin Chandra Pal
hist_bipin_chandra_pal.subject: history
hist_bipin_chandra_pal.detail: Extremist leader, journalist, orator — the 'Lal-Bal-Pal' trio. Extensive lecture tour of Madras presidency galvanised south India in Swadeshi. Retired from active politics after 1908.

hist_lala_lajpat_rai.label: Lala Lajpat Rai
hist_lala_lajpat_rai.subject: history
hist_lala_lajpat_rai.detail: 'Punjab Kesari.' Extremist leader of the 'Lal-Bal-Pal' trio. Deported to Mandalay in 1907 alongside Ajit Singh for agitation in Punjab. Died 1928 of police lathi injuries during Simon Commission protest — catalyst for revolutionary response.

hist_bengal_national_college.label: Bengal National College
hist_bengal_national_college.subject: history
hist_bengal_national_college.detail: Founded 1906 with Aurobindo Ghose as first Principal in response to the Swadeshi call for national education. National Council of Education (Aug 1906) was its coordinating body. Model for the parallel indigenous education system.

hist_jagdish_chandra_bose.label: Jagdish Chandra Bose
hist_jagdish_chandra_bose.subject: history
hist_jagdish_chandra_bose.detail: Pioneer Indian scientist at Presidency College Calcutta. Work on plant physiology, wireless (crescograph 1901). Symbolic figure of Swadeshi-era scientific self-reliance.

hist_surat_split_1907.label: Surat Split (Congress) 1907
hist_surat_split_1907.subject: history
hist_surat_split_1907.detail: December 1907 INC session on banks of Tapti river. Extremists (Tilak, Aurobindo) and Moderates (Pherozeshah Mehta, Gokhale) clashed over the four Calcutta resolutions (Swadeshi, Boycott, National Education, Self-Government) and the election of Rash Behari Ghosh as president. A shoe was thrown, chairs hurled; police dispersed the hall. Congress split — Extremists excluded until Lucknow 1916. Immediate British crackdown followed.

hist_morley_minto_reforms_1909.label: Morley-Minto Reforms (Indian Councils Act 1909)
hist_morley_minto_reforms_1909.subject: history
hist_morley_minto_reforms_1909.detail: Act of 1909 increased elected members in Imperial and Provincial councils (still mostly indirect). Allowed an Indian on Governor-General's Executive Council (S.P. Sinha first). Permitted resolutions, question-answer, some budget voting. Introduced SEPARATE ELECTORATES for Muslims — divide-and-rule instrument that would poison communal politics thereafter. Morley explicitly disclaimed any step towards parliamentary self-government.

hist_anushilan_samiti.label: Anushilan Samiti
hist_anushilan_samiti.subject: history
hist_anushilan_samiti.detail: Revolutionary secret society founded in Calcutta 1902 (P. Mitra, Sarala Devi Chaudhurani, Aurobindo). Dhaka branch under Pulin Behari Das 1906. Inspired by Irish and Russian revolutionaries. Conducted swadeshi dacoities and assassinations. Key node in Bengal revolutionary terrorism.

hist_jugantar.label: Jugantar / Yugantar
hist_jugantar.subject: history
hist_jugantar.detail: Bengal revolutionary society and newspaper (Yugantar), split from Anushilan around 1906 under Aurobindo's brother Barindra Ghose. Advocated armed revolution. Involved in the Alipore Bomb Case 1908.

hist_abhinav_bharat_savarkar.label: Abhinav Bharat 1904
hist_abhinav_bharat_savarkar.subject: history
hist_abhinav_bharat_savarkar.detail: Secret revolutionary society founded in 1904 in Nasik by Vinayak Damodar Savarkar and his brother Ganesh. Modelled on Mazzini's Young Italy. Active in Maharashtra; organised smuggling of arms from London to India.

hist_khudiram_bose.label: Khudiram Bose & Prafulla Chaki 1908
hist_khudiram_bose.subject: history
hist_khudiram_bose.detail: On 30 April 1908, Khudiram Bose (18) and Prafulla Chaki threw a bomb at a carriage they believed carried the unpopular Muzaffarpur judge Kingsford — killing two English ladies (Mrs Kennedy and her daughter) by mistake. Chaki shot himself; Khudiram was tried and hanged on 11 August 1908. Nationalist martyr; folk songs composed across Bengal.

hist_alipore_bomb_case.label: Alipore Bomb Case
hist_alipore_bomb_case.subject: history
hist_alipore_bomb_case.detail: Trial arising from the Muzaffarpur bomb attempt 1908. Thirty-eight revolutionaries including Aurobindo Ghose and his brother Barin arrested. Aurobindo acquitted in 1909 after Chittaranjan Das's famous defence. Turning point in Extremist-era revolutionary terrorism.

hist_madan_lal_dhingra.label: Madan Lal Dhingra 1909
hist_madan_lal_dhingra.subject: history
hist_madan_lal_dhingra.detail: Punjabi revolutionary in London linked to Savarkar's India House. Assassinated Sir Curzon Wyllie at Imperial Institute on 1 July 1909. Executed 17 August 1909. His courtroom statement is a canonical text of revolutionary nationalism.

hist_rash_behari_bose.label: Rash Behari Bose + Indian Independence League (1942)
hist_rash_behari_bose.subject: history
hist_rash_behari_bose.detail: Veteran revolutionary (associated with Hardinge Bomb attempt 1912). Escaped to Japan 1915. Founded Indian Independence League at Tokyo Conference March-June 1942 — co-ordinating body of Indian nationalists in Japan-occupied SE Asia. First Supreme Commander of the Indian National Army (INA) formed in Aug-Sept 1942 under Mohan Singh. Handed over to Subhas Bose at Singapore 4 July 1943. Died 21 January 1945.

hist_vd_savarkar.label: V.D. Savarkar
hist_vd_savarkar.subject: history
hist_vd_savarkar.detail: Vinayak Damodar Savarkar (1883-1966). Early revolutionary leader (Indian War of Independence 1909). Wrote "Essentials of Hindutva" (1923) — founding text of Hindu nationalism; defined Hindutva as cultural-racial unity distinct from religion. President of Hindu Mahasabha 1937-42. Coined two-nation theory for Hindus before Jinnah did for Muslims. Tried (and acquitted) in Gandhi assassination 1948.

hist_shyamji_krishna_varma.label: Shyamji Krishna Varma
hist_shyamji_krishna_varma.subject: history
hist_shyamji_krishna_varma.detail: Founder of India House in Highgate, London (1905) and The Indian Sociologist. Sanctuary and training ground for Indian revolutionaries abroad — Savarkar, Dhingra, Har Dayal, Madam Cama all passed through.

hist_madame_bhikaji_cama.label: Madame Bhikaji Cama
hist_madame_bhikaji_cama.subject: history
hist_madame_bhikaji_cama.detail: Parsi revolutionary in Europe. Unfurled the first version of the Indian national flag at the International Socialist Conference, Stuttgart, 22 August 1907. Published Bande Mataram and Madan's Talwar from Paris/Geneva. Called 'Mother of Indian Revolution.'

hist_har_dayal.label: Lala Har Dayal
hist_har_dayal.subject: history
hist_har_dayal.detail: Punjabi radical, briefly Stanford lecturer, exiled to California. Founded the Hindi Association of Portland May 1913 and the Ghadar Party in San Francisco Nov 1913. Arrested in US March 1914 for anarchist propaganda and fled. Ideologue of Ghadar — secular, egalitarian, internationalist.

hist_ghadar_party.label: Ghadar Party / Movement
hist_ghadar_party.subject: history
hist_ghadar_party.detail: Founded Nov 1913 in San Francisco by Punjabi immigrants in North America; main organisers Sohan Singh Bhakna, Kartar Singh Sarabha, Har Dayal, Barkatullah, Ram Chandra. Published 'Ghadar' (Urdu and Gurmukhi) and 'Ghadar di Goonj.' On WWI outbreak, issued Ailan-e-Jung (Proclamation of War) and sent thousands back to India for armed revolt. CID penetrated the organisation; Feb 1915 mutiny pre-empted; conspiracy trials in Punjab and Mandalay — 45 death sentences, 200+ long imprisonments.

hist_komagata_maru.label: Komagata Maru Incident 1914
hist_komagata_maru.subject: history
hist_komagata_maru.detail: Japanese freighter chartered by Gurdit Singh, carried 376 Indian (mostly Sikh) passengers from Hong Kong to Vancouver via Yokohama. Canadian authorities refused entry after a 2-month standoff and forced the ship back. Eventually docked at Budge Budge near Calcutta 27 September 1914; police clash killed 18 passengers. Galvanised Punjabi nationalism and fed the Ghadar revolt.

hist_hardinge_bomb_attack.label: Hardinge Bomb Attack (Delhi) 1912
hist_hardinge_bomb_attack.subject: history
hist_hardinge_bomb_attack.detail: On 23 December 1912, Rash Behari Bose's conspiracy threw a bomb at Viceroy Lord Hardinge during his ceremonial procession in Chandni Chowk entering the new capital Delhi. Hardinge wounded; attendant killed. Rash Behari escaped detection for years. Landmark revolutionary action outside Bengal.

hist_defence_of_india_act_1915.label: Defence of India Act 1915
hist_defence_of_india_act_1915.subject: history
hist_defence_of_india_act_1915.detail: Wartime emergency legislation giving Government of India sweeping detention and trial powers. Used against the Ghadarites and later against Home Rule agitators. Set the template for Rowlatt Act 1919.

hist_tilak_home_rule_league.label: Tilak Home Rule League 1916
hist_tilak_home_rule_league.subject: history
hist_tilak_home_rule_league.detail: Founded by Tilak at Bombay Provincial Conference, Belgaum, April 1916. Operated in Maharashtra (except Bombay city), Karnataka, Central Provinces, Berar. 14,000 members by April 1917. Six tightly organised branches. Tilak's slogan: 'Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it.'

hist_besant_home_rule_league.label: Annie Besant Home Rule League 1916
hist_besant_home_rule_league.subject: history
hist_besant_home_rule_league.detail: Founded September 1916 by Annie Besant with George Arundale as Organising Secretary. Operated in rest of India (outside Tilak's area). 200 branches, 7,000 members by March 1917. Papers: New India and Commonweal. Besant interned June 1917 with Arundale and Wadia — triggered nationwide protest and Montagu Declaration.

hist_annie_besant.label: Annie Besant
hist_annie_besant.subject: history
hist_annie_besant.detail: British Fabian socialist and Theosophist. Arrived India 1893 to work for Theosophical Society (Adyar, Madras). Founded Home Rule League 1916. First woman President of INC at Calcutta session, December 1917. Founded Central Hindu College Banaras (became BHU nucleus).

hist_lucknow_pact_1916.label: Lucknow Pact 1916
hist_lucknow_pact_1916.subject: history
hist_lucknow_pact_1916.detail: Congress-Muslim League pact at December 1916 Lucknow session. Tilak and Besant brokered reunion of Moderates and Extremists in Congress and Hindu-Muslim agreement. Congress accepted separate electorates for Muslims, both parties jointly demanded constitutional reforms. Recognised Muslim League's representation of Muslim political interests.

hist_montague_declaration_1917.label: Montagu Declaration 1917
hist_montague_declaration_1917.subject: history
hist_montague_declaration_1917.detail: 20 August 1917 House of Commons statement by new Secretary of State Edwin Montagu: policy of 'increasing association of Indians in every branch of administration and gradual development of self-governing institutions with a view to the progressive realisation of responsible government in India as an integral part of the British Empire.' First official acceptance of responsible government as goal. Led to Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms (Government of India Act 1919).

hist_servants_of_india_society.label: Servants of India Society
hist_servants_of_india_society.subject: history
hist_servants_of_india_society.detail: Founded 12 June 1905 in Poona by G.K. Gokhale to train 'national missionaries' devoted to full-time constructive and political work in selfless service. Ran on Jesuit-like discipline. Many members joined Home Rule agitation in 1917.

hist_gandhi_south_africa.label: Gandhi in South Africa
hist_gandhi_south_africa.subject: history
hist_gandhi_south_africa.detail: Gandhi in Natal and Transvaal from 1893 to early 1915. Organised Indians against anti-Asian laws. Founded Phoenix Settlement (1904) near Durban. Launched first Satyagraha against Asiatic Registration ('Black') Act 1906. Tolstoy Farm (1910). Wrote Hind Swaraj (1909). Compromise with Smuts 1914. Returned to India January 1915.

hist_phoenix_settlement_1904.label: Phoenix Settlement 1904
hist_phoenix_settlement_1904.subject: history
hist_phoenix_settlement_1904.detail: Intentional community founded by Gandhi near Durban in 1904, inspired by Ruskin's 'Unto This Last.' Basis of Gandhi's experiments with communal living, manual labour, self-sufficiency and journalism (Indian Opinion).

hist_tolstoy_farm_1910.label: Tolstoy Farm 1910
hist_tolstoy_farm_1910.subject: history
hist_tolstoy_farm_1910.detail: Gandhi's second settlement, founded near Johannesburg 1910 on land donated by Hermann Kallenbach. Named after Leo Tolstoy (with whom Gandhi corresponded). Base for Transvaal Satyagraha. Extended communal experiments in self-reliance.

hist_hind_swaraj_1909.label: Hind Swaraj (1909)
hist_hind_swaraj_1909.subject: history
hist_hind_swaraj_1909.detail: Gandhi wrote Hind Swaraj or Indian Home Rule in 1909 on ship between London and South Africa (Kildonan Castle). Radical critique of modern Western civilisation, industrialism, and parliamentary politics. Argued true Swaraj is self-rule over oneself. Sought to redirect Indian revolutionary energy into passive resistance and constructive programmes.

hist_kheda_satyagraha.label: Kheda Satyagraha 1918
hist_kheda_satyagraha.subject: history
hist_kheda_satyagraha.detail: March-June 1918 peasant satyagraha in Kheda (Gujarat) led by Gandhi, Sardar Patel and Indulal Yagnik. Peasants demanded revenue remission after crop failure. Government eventually suspended collection from poor peasants. Patel's emergence as leader.

hist_ahmedabad_mill_strike.label: Ahmedabad Mill Strike 1918
hist_ahmedabad_mill_strike.subject: history
hist_ahmedabad_mill_strike.detail: February-March 1918 strike by Ahmedabad textile workers over wage-bonus. Gandhi mediated, undertook first fast in India (3 March) to keep strikers firm. Settled with 35% wage increase via arbitration. Birthplace of Majoor Mahajan Sangh (Textile Labour Association) 1920. Gandhi's method of arbitrated satyagraha on industrial disputes.

hist_indian_society_oriental_art.label: Indian Society of Oriental Art
hist_indian_society_oriental_art.subject: history
hist_indian_society_oriental_art.detail: Founded 1907 in Calcutta by Abanindranath Tagore, Gaganendranath Tagore and British art-critic E.B. Havell. Institutional spine of the Bengal School of Art. Nandalal Bose was the first recipient of its scholarship. Promoted the revival of indigenous aesthetic traditions against Victorian naturalism.

hist_dramatic_performances_act_1876.label: Dramatic Performances Act 1876
hist_dramatic_performances_act_1876.subject: history
hist_dramatic_performances_act_1876.detail: Passed by Viceroy Lord Northbrook's government in 1876 to censor 'scandalous, defamatory, seditious or obscene' plays. Direct response to anti-British political plays in Bengali and Marathi theatre (Neel Darpan had been staged in Bengali). Forerunner of Vernacular Press Act 1878. Continued in force for decades.

hist_parsi_theatre.label: Parsi Theatre
hist_parsi_theatre.subject: history
hist_parsi_theatre.detail: Commercial theatrical tradition centred in Bombay, 1850s-1920s. Plays in Gujarati, Urdu, Marathi and Hindustani. Blended Western proscenium staging with Indian music, dance and melodrama. Themes: romance, humour, historical. From the 1930s its practitioners migrated into Indian cinema — major influence on early Bollywood.

hist_girish_chandra_ghosh.label: Girish Chandra Ghosh
hist_girish_chandra_ghosh.subject: history
hist_girish_chandra_ghosh.detail: Bengali theatre pioneer, actor and playwright. Founded the first commercial Bengali theatre (National Theatre, 1872). Wrote historical and mythological plays. 'Father of Bengali Theatre.' Associated with staging plays from Nil Darpan onwards.

hist_bengali_modern_theatre.label: Bengali Modern Theatre
hist_bengali_modern_theatre.subject: history
hist_bengali_modern_theatre.detail: Modern Bengali theatre emerged mid-19th C with Belgachia Natyashala, Shobhabazar Natyashala, National Theatre (1872). Western proscenium stage adapted with Indian content; became a vehicle for social and political critique. Neel Darpan (1860), Chaitali, others staged regularly.

hist_dadasaheb_phalke.label: Dadasaheb Phalke
hist_dadasaheb_phalke.subject: history
hist_dadasaheb_phalke.detail: Dhundiraj Govind Phalke — 'Father of Indian Cinema.' Produced and directed Raja Harishchandra (1913), India's first full-length silent feature film. Went on to make ~95 films between 1913-1937. The Dadasaheb Phalke Award (India's highest cinema honour) is named after him.

hist_raja_harishchandra_film.label: Raja Harishchandra (1913)
hist_raja_harishchandra_film.subject: history
hist_raja_harishchandra_film.detail: India's first full-length silent feature film, directed by Dadasaheb Phalke, released 3 May 1913 at Coronation Cinematograph, Bombay. 40 minutes long. Based on the Puranic story of King Harishchandra. Launched the Indian film industry.

hist_vn_bhatkhande.label: Vishnu Narayan Bhatkhande
hist_vn_bhatkhande.subject: history
hist_vn_bhatkhande.detail: Musicologist (1860-1936) who systematised Hindustani classical music. Classified ragas into 10 thaats. Founded Marris College of Music at Lucknow in 1926 (renamed Bhatkhande Music Institute). Organised first all-India music conferences from 1916. Published multi-volume Hindustani Sangeet Paddhati.

hist_vd_paluskar.label: Vishnu Digambar Paluskar
hist_vd_paluskar.subject: history
hist_vd_paluskar.detail: Musician and music educator (1872-1931). Founded Gandharva Mahavidyalaya at Lahore in 1901 — first modern institution for systematic training in Hindustani classical music. Composed 'Raghupati Raghava Raja Ram' bhajan. Brought classical music out of court patronage into public education.

period_post_1857_crown_admin.label: Crown Administration + Press Laws
period_post_1857_crown_admin.subject: history
period_post_1857_crown_admin.detail: Queen Victoria's Proclamation (1 Nov 1858) ended Company rule and transferred India to the Crown. Government of India Act 1858 established the Secretary of State for India in London and reorganised the Governor-General's council. Post-1857 administrative reorganisation created the Imperial Legislative Council (1861), Indian Councils Act 1892 (elected members), revised criminal and press law — Sedition in IPC §124A (1870), Vernacular Press Act 1878 (Lytton), Arms Act 1878, Dramatic Performances Act 1876. Lord Ripon's Local Self-Government Resolution 1882 (Panchayati Raj history). Ilbert Bill controversy 1883 exposed White racism.

period_agrarian_revolts_tribal.label: Agrarian Revolts + Tribal Uprisings
period_agrarian_revolts_tribal.subject: history
period_agrarian_revolts_tribal.detail: Post-1857 peasant and tribal movements — specific, regional, limited in scope. Bengal Indigo Revolt 1859-60 (Bishnu and Digambar Biswas). Pabna Agrarian League 1873 (East Bengal). Deccan Riots 1875 → Deccan Agriculturists' Relief Act 1879. Kuka Revolt 1872 (Baba Ram Singh, Punjab). Phadke's Ramosi uprising 1879. Birsa Munda's Ulgulan 1895-1900 (Chotanagpur). Bastar Rebellion 1910 (Gunda Dhur). Mappila outbreaks (Malabar). Neel Darpan (1860) by Dinabandhu Mitra.

period_forest_pastoral_policy.label: Forest + Pastoral Policy
period_forest_pastoral_policy.subject: history
period_forest_pastoral_policy.detail: Colonial forest policy institutionalised from 1864. Dietrich Brandis appointed Inspector-General of Forests. Indian Forest Act 1865 (revised 1878) classified forests as Reserved/Protected/Village. Imperial Forest Research Institute at Dehradun (1906). Scientific Forestry displaced shifting cultivation (jhum). Criminal Tribes Act 1871 (administrative violence against nomadic groups). Pastoralists — Dhangar shepherds in Maharashtra — were squeezed by grazing restrictions and railway timber demand.

period_inc_founding_moderates.label: INC Founding + Moderates
period_inc_founding_moderates.subject: history
period_inc_founding_moderates.detail: Pre-INC associations: British Indian Association Bengal (1851), Indian Association Bengal (1876, Surendranath Banerjee + Ananda Mohan Bose), Poona Sarvajanik Sabha (1870, M.G. Ranade), Madras Mahajan Sabha (1884), Bombay Presidency Association (1885, Pherozeshah Mehta). INC founded 28 Dec 1885 at Bombay, 72 delegates, W.C. Bonnerjee 1st President; A.O. Hume as chief organiser. 'Safety Valve' theory (Wedderburn 1913 → Lajpat Rai → R. Palme Dutt) myth that INC was engineered by Dufferin — Bipin Chandra disproves it. Moderate phase (1885-1905): petitions, resolutions, National Fund, All-India National Conference.

period_economic_critique_legislatures.label: Economic Critique + Legislatures
period_economic_critique_legislatures.subject: history
period_economic_critique_legislatures.detail: Three-generation Moderate economic critique: Dadabhai Naoroji's Drain Theory (1867), his Poverty and Un-British Rule in India (1901), R.C. Dutt's Economic History of India (1902, 1904), G.V. Joshi, Ranade on industrialisation, Gokhale's famed budget speeches (from 1902). Legislatures: Indian Councils Act 1861 (Imperial Legislative Council), 1892 (indirect elections), Morley-Minto 1909 (separate electorates). Moderates critiqued foreign capital, free trade, de-industrialisation of handicrafts, famine policy, drain via Home Charges. Key legislative interventions by Pherozeshah Mehta, Gokhale, Madan Mohan Malaviya in Imperial Legislative Council.

period_swadeshi_partition_bengal.label: Swadeshi + Partition of Bengal
