period_swadeshi_partition_bengal.subject: history
period_swadeshi_partition_bengal.detail: Partition of Bengal announced July 1905 by Viceroy Curzon — effected 16 Oct 1905 (day of mourning). Triggered Swadeshi and Boycott Movement. Boycott Resolution at Calcutta Town Hall 7 Aug 1905. 'Bande Mataram' became anthem. Extended boycott into education (Bengal National College 1906, Aurobindo Principal; National Council of Education Aug 1906), art (Abanindranath's Bharat Mata 1905), industry (Swadeshi mills, P.C. Ray's Bengal Chemicals 1901), organisation (Swadesh Bandhab Samiti — Ashwini Kumar Dutt in Barisal). Spread beyond Bengal via Tilak (Bombay), Lajpat Rai and Ajit Singh (Punjab), Chidambaram Pillai (Madras), Bipin Chandra Pal (lecture tour).

period_split_revolutionary_terror.label: Congress Split + Revolutionary Terror
period_split_revolutionary_terror.subject: history
period_split_revolutionary_terror.detail: Surat Split December 1907 over Rash Behari Ghosh's election and the four Calcutta resolutions. Shoe thrown at the dais; Congress dispersed. Extremists excluded until Lucknow 1916. Government cracked down: Tilak six years to Mandalay (1908), Ashwini Kumar Dutt deported, Aurobindo retired to Pondicherry. Morley-Minto Reforms / Indian Councils Act 1909 introduced separate electorates for Muslims (divide-and-rule). Revolutionary terrorism — Anushilan Samiti (1902), Jugantar/Yugantar, Abhinav Bharat (Savarkar 1904). Alipore Bomb Case (Khudiram and Prafulla Chaki, April 1908; 38 revolutionaries including Aurobindo tried). Madan Lal Dhingra assassinated Curzon-Wyllie in London (July 1909). Rash Behari Bose's Hardinge bomb attack Delhi Dec 1912. India House London under Shyamji Krishna Varma; Madam Bhikaji Cama unfurled first flag at Stuttgart Socialist Congress 1907.

period_wwi_ghadar_homerule.label: WWI + Ghadar + Home Rule
period_wwi_ghadar_homerule.subject: history
period_wwi_ghadar_homerule.detail: WWI (1914-18) reshaped Indian politics. Ghadar Party founded San Francisco Nov 1913 by Har Dayal + Sohan Singh Bhakna; paper 'Ghadar' in Urdu and Gurmukhi. Komagata Maru incident May-Sept 1914 (376 Indians turned back from Canada; clash at Budge Budge killed 18). Ghadar Mutiny attempt February 1915 pre-empted; 45 death sentences, 200+ imprisonments. Defence of India Act 1915. Home Rule Leagues launched 1916: Tilak's (Belgaum, April 1916) covered Maharashtra-Karnataka-CP-Berar; Annie Besant's (September 1916) covered rest of India. Lucknow Congress December 1916: Tilak-Besant reunion of Moderates and Extremists; Congress-Muslim League Lucknow Pact (accepted separate electorates). Government interned Besant, Arundale, Wadia (June 1917) — triggered Montagu Declaration 20 Aug 1917 accepting responsible government as goal.

period_colonial_industry_labour.label: Colonial Industry + Labour
period_colonial_industry_labour.subject: history
period_colonial_industry_labour.detail: Indian-owned industry took root despite colonial disabilities. Bombay cotton mills (first 1854); jobber system recruited migrant labour from hinterland. Swadeshi Movement (1905) boosted Indian mills. TISCO founded 1907 at Jamshedpur (Jamsetji Tata's vision, J.R.D Tata era). Agaria iron smelters of Central India, Bombay labour movements 1908 after Tilak's conviction. Despite tariff protection demanded by nationalists, British policy kept import duties low (free trade bias) until 1921 — hobbling industrial takeoff.

period_colonial_cities_planning.label: Colonial Cities + Lutyens Delhi
period_colonial_cities_planning.subject: history
period_colonial_cities_planning.detail: Presidency cities continued expanding; colonial urban form matured. Bombay land reclamation pushed out island shore. Bombay plague 1896-98 prompted plague committee, slum clearance, chawls for mill workers. Indo-Saracenic architecture (Gateway of India style, Victoria Terminus) and Gothic/Neo-Classical style dominated. Lord Curzon's Delhi Durbar 1911 announced shift of capital from Calcutta. New Delhi designed by Edwin Lutyens and Herbert Baker (1911-31) in Neo-Roman monumental style. Bombay Cinema industry launched with Dadasaheb Phalke's Raja Harishchandra (1913) at Coronation Cinematograph. Garden City Movement (Ebenezer Howard 1898) influenced planning ideals.

period_socio_religious_reform.label: Akali + Temple Entry + Social Reform (1920-47)
period_socio_religious_reform.subject: history
period_socio_religious_reform.detail: Akali Movement 1920-25 — SGPC + Shiromani Akali Dal Dec 1920, Nankana Tragedy Feb 1921, Keys Affair Oct 1921, Guru-Ka-Bagh Aug 1922, Jaito 1923, Sikh Gurdwaras Act July 1925. Vaikom Satyagraha 1924-25 (K.P. Kesava Menon, Periyar, Gandhi). Guruvayur Satyagraha 1931-32 (K. Kelappan, A.K. Gopalan, P. Krishna Pillai). Travancore Temple Entry Proclamation Nov 1936. Madras Temple Entry Act 1938 (Rajagopalachari). Child Marriage Restraint Act 1929. Gandhi's Harijan work. Women's movements (AIWC 1927, Sarojini Naidu, Aruna Asaf Ali, Sucheta Kripalani).

period_press_literature_journalism.label: Press + Literature + Journalism
period_press_literature_journalism.subject: history
period_press_literature_journalism.detail: The press was the political instrument of the era. Vernacular Press Act 1878 (Lytton) repealed by Ripon 1881. Key newspapers: Kesari + Mahratta (Tilak 1881), Amrita Bazar Patrika (Ghosh brothers 1868, English since 1878), The Hindu (Subramaniya Iyer 1878), Tribune (Lahore 1881), Bengalee (Banerjee 1879). Literature: Bankim Chandra's Anandamath (1882) gave Bande Mataram; Rabindranath Tagore's fiction (Gora, Ghare Baire, Chokher Bali); Premchand's Hindi/Urdu novels; novels addressing women's question and caste. Dramatic Performances Act 1876 (Viceroy Northbrook) censored political theatre.

period_visual_performing_arts.label: Visual + Performing Arts + Cinema
period_visual_performing_arts.subject: history
period_visual_performing_arts.detail: Revival + renewal in Indian art. Raja Ravi Varma — South Indian + European oil style (Ramayana-based prints). Bengal School (Abanindranath Tagore's Bharat Mata 1905, Nandalal Bose, Indian Society of Oriental Art founded 1907 with E.B. Havell) rejected Victorian naturalism for indigenous aesthetics inspired by Mughal/Rajput/Ajanta. Company Paintings (18th-19th C hybrid) and Bazaar Paintings (Bengali Greco-Roman). Modern Indian theatre — Parsi Theatre 1850s-1920s, Bengali Modern Theatre (National Theatre 1872, Girish Chandra Ghosh). Indian Cinema — Dadasaheb Phalke's Raja Harishchandra 1913 inaugurated the industry. Classical music revival — Vishnu Digambar Paluskar (Gandharva Mahavidyalaya Lahore 1901) and Vishnu Narayan Bhatkhande (Marris College Lucknow 1926). Alexander Cunningham as first DG Archaeological Survey (1861) identified Harappa. Ranjitsinhji, English cricket.

period_gandhi_arrival_satyagrahas.label: Gandhi's Arrival + First Satyagrahas
period_gandhi_arrival_satyagrahas.subject: history
period_gandhi_arrival_satyagrahas.detail: Gandhi's arc from 1893 South African satyagraha to 1919 Rowlatt agitation. South Africa 1893-1914: Natal Indian Congress 1894, Phoenix Settlement 1904 (inspired by Ruskin), Tolstoy Farm 1910. Hind Swaraj written on ship 1909. Returned to India January 1915. Champaran indigo satyagraha 1917 (ryots of Bihar), Kheda revenue satyagraha 1918 (Patel, Indulal Yagnik), Ahmedabad Mill Strike 1918 (Gandhi's first fast). Rowlatt Act 6 April 1919 → first all-India Gandhian satyagraha. Jallianwala Bagh massacre 13 April 1919 (General Dyer, Amritsar). Tagore renounced knighthood. End of Moderate-Extremist era; Gandhi now the leader of a nationwide movement heading into era-9 Non-Cooperation 1920.

period_parallel_european.label: European Nationalism + Industry
period_parallel_european.subject: history
period_parallel_european.detail: Post-Napoleonic consolidation of European nation-states. Italian unification completed 1861 (Cavour, Garibaldi, Victor Emmanuel II). German unification completed 1871 under Bismarck through Franco-Prussian War (Treaty of Frankfurt). Second Industrial Revolution (electricity, chemicals, steel) shifted economic hegemony from Britain to Germany and USA. Socialism emerged as ideology (Marx 1848-94; German SPD 1875). Balkan nationalism under Ottoman collapse → First Balkan War 1912, World War I 1914-18. Treaty of Versailles 1919 ended WWI and created Weimar Republic; punitive reparations sowed seeds of Nazi rise (era 9).

period_parallel_russia.label: Russia: Tsar → Revolution
period_parallel_russia.subject: history
period_parallel_russia.detail: Late Tsarist Russia — Nicholas II (1894-1917), industrialisation and serfdom legacy. 1905 Revolution (Bloody Sunday 9 Jan). WWI devastated Russian economy and army. February Revolution March 1917 forced Tsar's abdication; Provisional Government. October Revolution November 1917 (Lenin, Trotsky) put Bolsheviks in power. Russian Civil War 1918-22 (Reds vs Whites); 1917 Revolution became reference point for Indian communist and socialist nationalists.

period_parallel_east_asia.label: East Asia: Meiji Japan + Qing Collapse
period_parallel_east_asia.stage: East Asia: Meiji Japan + Qing Collapse
period_parallel_east_asia.subject: history
period_parallel_east_asia.detail: East Asia underwent unequal responses to Western imperialism. Japan's Meiji Restoration 1868 ended 250 years of Tokugawa rule; Meiji reforms (abolition of samurai class, conscription, modern industry, Zaibatsu conglomerates, Meiji Constitution 1889) made Japan Asia's first industrial power. Japanese Imperialism defeated China 1894-95 and Russia 1904-05 (Russo-Japanese War — first modern defeat of European power by Asian state; electrified Indian nationalists). Qing China faced Boxer Rebellion 1899-1901; Sun Yat-sen's Three Principles (nationalism, democracy, people's livelihood). 1911 Revolution ended Qing dynasty; Kuomintang emerged (to split into Nationalist-Communist rivalry in era 9). Vietnamese nationalism — Phan Boi Chau (1903), Scholars' Revolt 1868.

period_parallel_settler_global.label: Settler Colonialism + Global Events
period_parallel_settler_global.subject: history
period_parallel_settler_global.detail: Settler colonialism and global movements of people/disease. USA's westward expansion displaced Native Americans (Dawes Act 1887, reservations). Australia's Stolen Generations policy (1910-70) forcibly removed Aboriginal children. American Wheat Farming on Great Plains transformed global food trade. Haussmann's Paris (1850s-70s) modernised urban form — boulevards, sewers — influencing Bombay, Calcutta. London Underground opened 1863. Rinderpest epidemic in Africa (1890s) killed 90% of cattle — collapsed Maasai pastoral economy, opened door to European settler expansion. Ebenezer Howard's Garden City idea (1898, Letchworth) influenced Lutyens and later Indian planning.

pol_constituent_assembly.label: Constituent Assembly
pol_constituent_assembly.subject: polity
pol_constituent_assembly.detail: Body that drafted the Indian Constitution. Formed in 1946 under Cabinet Mission Plan. Had 299 members. Worked from Dec 9, 1946 to Nov 26, 1949. Chaired by Dr Rajendra Prasad. Drafting Committee chaired by Dr B.R. Ambedkar.

pol_objective_resolution.label: Objective Resolution
pol_objective_resolution.subject: polity
pol_objective_resolution.detail: Moved by Jawaharlal Nehru on December 13, 1946. Laid down the philosophy and guiding principles for constitution-making. Later became the basis of the Preamble. Declared India to be an independent sovereign republic with guaranteed fundamental rights.

pol_drafting_committee.label: Drafting Committee
pol_drafting_committee.subject: polity
pol_drafting_committee.detail: Seven-member committee chaired by Ambedkar tasked with preparing the draft constitution. Other members included Alladi Krishnaswami Ayyar, N. Gopalaswami Ayyangar, K.M. Munshi, Syed Mohammad Saadulla, N. Madhava Rau, T.T. Krishnamachari.

pol_cabinet_mission.label: Cabinet Mission Plan
pol_cabinet_mission.subject: polity
pol_cabinet_mission.detail: 1946 British mission that proposed the framework for forming the Constituent Assembly. Members elected by provincial legislatures through indirect election. Also proposed a three-tier federal structure which was eventually rejected.

pol_gandhi_on_decentralisation.label: Gandhi on Decentralisation
pol_gandhi_on_decentralisation.subject: polity
pol_gandhi_on_decentralisation.detail: Gandhi strongly pleaded for decentralisation of economic and political power. He envisioned every village as a republic, self-sustained and capable of managing its affairs. His concept of Gram Swaraj saw local self-governance as the foundation of democracy. Life would be a pyramid with apex sustained by the bottom. Influenced the creation of Panchayati Raj institutions.

pol_motilal_nehru_report.label: Motilal Nehru Report (1928)
pol_motilal_nehru_report.subject: polity
pol_motilal_nehru_report.detail: Reaffirmed the conception of Indian citizenship and universal franchise. Declared that every person of either sex who has attained the age of twenty-one is entitled to vote. Showed that universal franchise was integral to Indian nationalism long before independence. Influential precursor to constitutional provisions on citizenship and voting rights.

pol_league_of_nations.label: League of Nations
pol_league_of_nations.subject: polity
pol_league_of_nations.detail: International organisation created after WWI to prevent war. Despite initial success, it failed to prevent WWII. The UN was founded as its successor in 1945 with lessons learned from its failure.

pol_refugee_crisis_1947.label: Refugee Crisis of 1947
pol_refugee_crisis_1947.subject: polity
pol_refugee_crisis_1947.detail: Partition caused massive displacement with about 80 lakh people migrating across borders. Refugees faced violence, abductions of women, separation of families. Rehabilitation of refugees was a major challenge for the new government.

pol_khan_abdul_ghaffar.label: Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan
pol_khan_abdul_ghaffar.subject: polity
pol_khan_abdul_ghaffar.detail: Known as Frontier Gandhi, undisputed leader of NWFP. Staunchly opposed the two-nation theory but his voice was ignored and NWFP was merged with Pakistan.

pol_vp_menon.label: V.P. Menon
pol_vp_menon.subject: polity
pol_vp_menon.detail: Secretary in the Ministry of States under Sardar Patel. Played a crucial role in administrative and diplomatic negotiations for the integration of princely states. Drafted the Instrument of Accession.

pol_bombay_plan.label: Bombay Plan (1944)
pol_bombay_plan.subject: polity
pol_bombay_plan.detail: A joint proposal drafted by a section of big industrialists in 1944 for setting up a planned economy. Wanted the state to take major initiatives in industrial and economic investments. Significant because even private industrialists supported state-led planning.

pol_akali_dal.label: Akali Dal
pol_akali_dal.subject: polity
pol_akali_dal.detail: Sikh political party founded 1920 during Gurdwara reform movement. Key post-1947 role in Punjab politics — demand for Punjabi Suba (granted 1966), Anandpur Sahib Resolution 1973 (more state autonomy), Dharam Yudh Morcha 1982, led Punjab crisis leading to Operation Blue Star 1984 and Rajiv-Longowal Accord 1985.

pol_karachi_resolution_1931.label: Karachi Session Resolution (1931)
pol_karachi_resolution_1931.subject: polity
pol_karachi_resolution_1931.detail: Indian National Congress resolution at Karachi session outlined how independent India's constitution should look. Committed to universal adult franchise, fundamental rights, and protection of minorities. Shaped the eventual Constituent Assembly deliberations.

eco_partition_economic_impact.label: Economic Impact of Partition
eco_partition_economic_impact.subject: economics
eco_partition_economic_impact.detail: India's partition in 1947 adversely affected agriculture as highly irrigated and fertile land went to Pakistan. India's jute industry suffered severely since almost all jute-producing areas became East Pakistan (now Bangladesh). India had enjoyed world monopoly in jute goods.

hist_ho_chi_minh.label: Ho Chi Minh
hist_ho_chi_minh.subject: history
hist_ho_chi_minh.detail: Vietnamese communist leader who founded Viet Minh (Vietnam Doc Lap Dong Minh Hoi) in 1941. Inspired by Russian and Chinese revolutions. Declared Vietnam independent in 1945. Led resistance against French and Americans.

hist_vietnam_independence.label: Vietnamese Independence
hist_vietnam_independence.subject: history
hist_vietnam_independence.detail: Vietnam gained formal independence in 1945 but faced decades of fighting. French defeated at Dien Bien Phu 1954. Country divided at 17th parallel. NLF (Vietcong) fought US-backed South Vietnam. Reunified 1975.

hist_hoa_hao_movement.label: Hoa Hao Movement
hist_hoa_hao_movement.subject: history
hist_hoa_hao_movement.detail: Religious movement founded by Huynh Phu So in 1939 drawing on Buddhist traditions. Opposed French colonialism, rejected needless spending and promoted social reforms. French tried to suppress it by declaring So mad.

hist_ncm_detailed.label: Non-Cooperation Movement (Detailed)
hist_ncm_detailed.subject: history
hist_ncm_detailed.detail: Launched 1920 uniting Khilafat and Swaraj demands. Involved surrender of titles, boycott of councils, courts, schools. Foreign cloth imports halved 1920-22. Suspended after Chauri Chaura Feb 1922 where 22 policemen killed.

hist_cdm_detailed.label: Civil Disobedience Movement
hist_cdm_detailed.subject: history
hist_cdm_detailed.detail: Began with Salt March 1930. People broke salt law, picketed liquor and cloth shops, refused to pay revenue. Government responded with ordinances, arrests of 100,000. Gandhi-Irwin Pact 1931 led to suspension.

hist_khilafat_movement.label: Khilafat Movement
hist_khilafat_movement.subject: history
hist_khilafat_movement.detail: Led by Muhammad Ali and Shaukat Ali brothers after British imposed harsh treaty on Turkish Sultan (Khalifa) in 1920. Gandhi supported it for Hindu-Muslim unity. Merged with Non-Cooperation Movement.

hist_simon_commission.label: Simon Commission
hist_simon_commission.subject: history
hist_simon_commission.detail: British Commission of 1927 with no Indian member sent to decide India's political future. Met with protests across India with banners saying 'Simon Go Back'. Lala Lajpat Rai died from injuries during anti-Simon protest.

hist_gandhi_irwin_pact.label: Gandhi-Irwin Pact
hist_gandhi_irwin_pact.subject: history
hist_gandhi_irwin_pact.detail: Signed in March 1931 between Gandhi and Viceroy Irwin. Government agreed to release political prisoners. Gandhi agreed to participate in Round Table Conference in London. Civil Disobedience suspended.

hist_round_table_conferences.label: Round Table Conferences
hist_round_table_conferences.subject: history
hist_round_table_conferences.detail: Three conferences held in London (1930-32) to discuss constitutional reforms. First boycotted by Congress. Gandhi attended second but returned disappointed. Led to Government of India Act 1935.

hist_alluri_sitarama_raju.label: Alluri Sitarama Raju
hist_alluri_sitarama_raju.subject: history
hist_alluri_sitarama_raju.detail: Led militant guerrilla movement of tribal people in Andhra against colonial forest policies during 1920s. Claimed Gandhi had authorised use of force. Killed by British in 1924.

hist_salt_satyagraha_women.label: Women in Salt Satyagraha
hist_salt_satyagraha_women.subject: history
hist_salt_satyagraha_women.detail: Thousands of women participated in Civil Disobedience, picketing liquor and foreign cloth shops. Initially Gandhi opposed women's participation until Sarojini Naidu persuaded him. Women became integral to national movement.

hist_depressed_classes_national_movement.label: Depressed Classes and National Movement
hist_depressed_classes_national_movement.subject: history
hist_depressed_classes_national_movement.detail: Ambedkar demanded separate electorates for dalits at Round Table Conference. Gandhi opposed this leading to Poona Pact 1932 with reserved seats within joint electorates. Tension between Congress and dalit leadership.

hist_poona_pact.label: Poona Pact 1932
hist_poona_pact.subject: history
hist_poona_pact.detail: Agreement between Gandhi and Ambedkar replacing separate electorates for dalits with reserved seats within general electorate. Gandhi undertook fast unto death against separate electorates. Shaped future reservation policy.

hist_great_depression_global.label: Great Depression
hist_great_depression_global.subject: history
hist_great_depression_global.detail: 1929 Wall Street crash caused worldwide economic crisis. US lending stopped, prices fell, factories closed. India's agricultural exports and food prices crashed, devastating peasants while British continued to collect revenue.

hist_bretton_woods.label: Bretton Woods System
hist_bretton_woods.subject: history
hist_bretton_woods.detail: 1944 conference established IMF and World Bank for post-war economic stability. Fixed exchange rates pegged to US dollar anchored to gold. Decision-making controlled by Western powers. Collapsed in 1970s.

hist_premchand_novels.label: Premchand's Novels
hist_premchand_novels.subject: history
hist_premchand_novels.detail: Munshi Premchand wrote about Indian peasant life, caste oppression, and colonial exploitation. Godan (1936) depicted tragedy of peasant Hori. Rangbhoomi explored social conflicts. Brought Hindi novel to literary maturity.

hist_long_march.label: Long March (1934-35)
hist_long_march.subject: history
hist_long_march.detail: Epic retreat of the Chinese Communist Red Army over 9,000 km from Jiangxi to Shaanxi province to escape Nationalist encirclement. Of about 100,000 who started, only 8,000-10,000 survived. Mao emerged as the undisputed CCP leader during the march. Became a founding myth of the People's Republic.

hist_john_marshall.label: John Marshall
hist_john_marshall.subject: history
hist_john_marshall.detail: Director-General of ASI who announced the discovery of a new Indus Valley Civilisation to the world in 1924. First professional archaeologist to work in India. Made India 'three thousand years older'. However, his horizontal excavation method ignored stratigraphy.

hist_rem_wheeler.label: R.E.M. Wheeler
hist_rem_wheeler.subject: history
hist_rem_wheeler.detail: Director-General of ASI from 1944. Introduced stratigraphic excavation methods to Indian archaeology, rectifying Marshall's approach. Excavated at Harappa in 1946. Initially proposed Aryan invasion theory for Harappan decline based on skeletal evidence, later challenged.

hist_non_cooperation_movement.label: Non-Cooperation Movement (1920-22)
hist_non_cooperation_movement.subject: history
hist_non_cooperation_movement.detail: Launched by Gandhi in 1920 against Rowlatt Act and Jallianwala Bagh massacre. Indians boycotted councils, courts, schools, foreign cloth. Tilak Swaraj Fund raised Rs 1 crore. Suspended after Chauri Chaura violence (February 1922) where 22 policemen were killed by mob.

hist_salt_march.label: Salt March / Dandi March (1930)
hist_salt_march.subject: history
hist_salt_march.detail: Gandhi marched 240 miles from Sabarmati to Dandi (12 March - 6 April 1930) to break salt law. Launched Civil Disobedience Movement. Brilliantly chosen issue as salt tax affected every Indian. International media coverage. Led to Gandhi-Irwin Pact (1931) and Round Table Conference.

hist_quit_india_movement.label: Quit India Movement (1942)
hist_quit_india_movement.subject: history
hist_quit_india_movement.detail: Launched 8 August 1942 with Gandhi's call 'Do or Die'. Demanded immediate British withdrawal from India. All Congress leaders arrested immediately. Spontaneous mass protests, strikes, sabotage across India. Severely repressed by British. Demonstrated depth of popular support for independence.

hist_civil_disobedience.label: Civil Disobedience Movement (1930-34)
hist_civil_disobedience.subject: history
hist_civil_disobedience.detail: Began with Salt March. Indians broke salt laws, boycotted foreign goods, refused to pay taxes. Massive participation including women. Over 60,000 arrested. Suspended for Gandhi-Irwin Pact (1931). Resumed 1932 after Second Round Table Conference failed. Formally withdrawn 1934.

hist_chauri_chaura.label: Chauri Chaura Incident (1922)
hist_chauri_chaura.subject: history
hist_chauri_chaura.detail: Violent mob killed 22 policemen at Chauri Chaura (UP) on 5 February 1922. Gandhi immediately suspended the Non-Cooperation Movement, insisting on non-violence. Decision shocked many Congress leaders but showed Gandhi's uncompromising commitment to ahimsa.

hist_cripps_mission.label: Cripps Mission (1942)
hist_cripps_mission.subject: history
hist_cripps_mission.detail: Sir Stafford Cripps sent to India in March 1942 offering dominion status after war, with right of provinces to opt out. Congress rejected as too little too late. Muslim League found opt-out clause interesting for Pakistan demand. Gandhi called it 'a post-dated cheque on a crashing bank'.

hist_ina_trials.label: INA Trials (1945)
hist_ina_trials.subject: history
hist_ina_trials.detail: British put Indian National Army officers on trial at Red Fort, Delhi. INA was formed by Subhas Chandra Bose with Japanese support. Trials united Indian public opinion against British. Congress defended INA soldiers. Demonstrated that Indian armed forces could no longer be relied upon by British.

hist_government_of_india_act_1935.label: Government of India Act 1935
hist_government_of_india_act_1935.subject: history
hist_government_of_india_act_1935.detail: Major constitutional legislation providing for provincial autonomy, federal structure, and separate electorates. Congress won majority in 1937 elections in most provinces. Formed governments in 8 of 11 provinces. Muslim League performed poorly outside Muslim-majority areas. Framework for 1946 elections.

hist_lahore_session_1929.label: Lahore Congress Session (1929)
hist_lahore_session_1929.subject: history
hist_lahore_session_1929.detail: Congress session under Jawaharlal Nehru's presidency declared Purna Swaraj (complete independence) as goal on 31 December 1929. 26 January 1930 celebrated as first Independence Day. Authorised Gandhi to launch Civil Disobedience Movement.

hist_rn_strikes_1946.label: Royal Indian Navy Mutiny (1946)
hist_rn_strikes_1946.subject: history
hist_rn_strikes_1946.detail: Mutiny by Indian sailors of Royal Indian Navy in Bombay (February 1946) against racial discrimination and poor conditions. Spread to other naval establishments. Demonstrated that Indian armed forces were unreliable for British. Along with INA trials, hastened British decision to leave India.

hist_partition_1947.label: Partition of India (1947)
hist_partition_1947.subject: history
hist_partition_1947.detail: Division of British India into India and Pakistan on 14-15 August 1947. Largest mass migration in history: 15 million displaced, estimated 1 million killed. Punjab and Bengal divided. Accompanied by horrific communal violence. Radcliffe Line drawn hastily as boundary.

hist_lahore_resolution_1940.label: Lahore Resolution (1940)
hist_lahore_resolution_1940.subject: history
hist_lahore_resolution_1940.detail: Muslim League resolution demanding autonomous and sovereign Muslim-majority areas in northwestern and eastern India. Did not use the word 'Pakistan' explicitly. Became basis for demand for separate Muslim state. Sometimes called Pakistan Resolution.

hist_two_nation_theory.label: Two-Nation Theory
hist_two_nation_theory.subject: history
hist_two_nation_theory.detail: Theory that Hindus and Muslims were two separate nations with distinct histories, cultures and social systems. Used by Jinnah and Muslim League to justify demand for Pakistan. Challenged by Congress and secular nationalists. Savarkar and some Hindu Mahasabha members also endorsed Hindu nationalism.

hist_cabinet_mission_1946.label: Cabinet Mission (1946)
hist_cabinet_mission_1946.subject: history
hist_cabinet_mission_1946.detail: British mission proposing federal structure with three groups of provinces (Hindu-majority, Muslim-majority NW, Muslim-majority East) sharing centre for defence, foreign affairs and communications. Both Congress and League initially accepted but later disagreed on interpretation, leading to its failure.

hist_direct_action_day.label: Direct Action Day (16 August 1946)
hist_direct_action_day.subject: history
hist_direct_action_day.detail: Called by Muslim League after withdrawing acceptance of Cabinet Mission Plan. Led to massive communal riots in Calcutta ('Great Calcutta Killing') with over 4,000 dead. Violence spread to Noakhali, Bihar and elsewhere. Demonstrated that communal peace could not be maintained.

hist_mountbatten_plan.label: Mountbatten Plan (June 1947)
hist_mountbatten_plan.subject: history
hist_mountbatten_plan.detail: Lord Mountbatten, last Viceroy, advanced independence date to August 1947 from June 1948. Plan for partition accepted by Congress (reluctantly), Muslim League and Sikhs. Radcliffe Boundary Commission appointed to draw borders. Princely states given choice to join India or Pakistan.

hist_radcliffe_line.label: Radcliffe Line
hist_radcliffe_line.subject: history
hist_radcliffe_line.detail: Boundary between India and Pakistan drawn by Sir Cyril Radcliffe who had never visited India. Drawn in just 5 weeks, dividing Punjab and Bengal. Announced on 17 August 1947, two days after independence. Affected millions who found themselves on the wrong side.

hist_communal_violence_partition.label: Communal Violence During Partition
hist_communal_violence_partition.subject: history
hist_communal_violence_partition.detail: Horrific violence in Punjab, Bengal, Delhi and elsewhere. Massacres, abductions of women, forced conversions, destruction of property. Trains carrying refugees arrived with dead bodies. Women sometimes killed by their own families to prevent 'dishonour'. Gandhi fasted to stop Delhi violence.

hist_1946_elections.label: 1946 Elections
hist_1946_elections.subject: history
hist_1946_elections.detail: Crucial elections held under Government of India Act 1935. Congress swept general seats. Muslim League won every Muslim seat in Central Assembly and most in provinces, validating its claim to represent Muslims. Demonstrated communal polarisation. Formed basis for partition demand.

hist_noakhali_riots.label: Noakhali Riots (1946)
hist_noakhali_riots.subject: history
hist_noakhali_riots.detail: Communal violence in Noakhali (Bengal) in October 1946 targeting Hindu minority. Gandhi walked through Noakhali villages for months promoting communal harmony. Retaliatory violence against Muslims in Bihar. These events deepened communal divide and made partition seem inevitable.

hist_interim_government_1946.label: Interim Government (1946)
hist_interim_government_1946.subject: history
hist_interim_government_1946.detail: Formed September 1946 under Nehru as Vice President of Viceroy's Executive Council. Muslim League joined in October but obstructed functioning. Deadlock between Congress and League in interim government convinced many that partition was unavoidable.

hist_gandhis_role_partition.label: Gandhi's Opposition to Partition
hist_gandhis_role_partition.subject: history
hist_gandhis_role_partition.detail: Gandhi opposed partition till the very end, calling it 'vivisection of India'. Fasted in Calcutta (August-September 1947) to stop communal violence. Fasted in Delhi (January 1948) to protect Muslims and ensure payment of Rs 55 crore to Pakistan. Assassinated partly for these stances.

hist_constituent_assembly.label: Constituent Assembly
hist_constituent_assembly.subject: history
hist_constituent_assembly.detail: Elected in July 1946 under Cabinet Mission plan. 296 members for British India, reduced after partition. First meeting 9 December 1946. Drafting Committee under Ambedkar appointed 29 August 1947. Completed work on 26 November 1949. Constitution came into effect 26 January 1950.

hist_objectives_resolution.label: Objectives Resolution
hist_objectives_resolution.subject: history
hist_objectives_resolution.detail: Moved by Jawaharlal Nehru on 13 December 1946. Declared India a sovereign democratic republic guaranteeing justice, equality, freedom. Adequate safeguards for minorities. Became Preamble of the Constitution. Debated extensively by members from all communities.

hist_drafting_committee.label: Drafting Committee
hist_drafting_committee.subject: history
hist_drafting_committee.detail: Seven-member committee appointed 29 August 1947 under Ambedkar's chairmanship. Other members: N. Gopalaswami Ayyangar, Alladi Krishnaswami Ayyar, K.M. Munshi, Syed Mohammad Saadulla, N. Madhava Rau (replaced B.L. Mitter), T.T. Krishnamachari (replaced D.P. Khaitan).

hist_princely_states_integration.label: Integration of Princely States
hist_princely_states_integration.subject: history
hist_princely_states_integration.detail: 562 princely states had to decide between India and Pakistan. Sardar Patel and V.P. Menon convinced most to accede to India. Hyderabad integrated through Operation Polo (1948). Junagadh through plebiscite. Kashmir's accession triggered Indo-Pak conflict. Completed by 1949.

hist_government_of_india_act_1935_const.label: Government of India Act 1935 (as template)
hist_government_of_india_act_1935_const.subject: history
hist_government_of_india_act_1935_const.detail: About 250 clauses of the Constitution were adapted from the 1935 Act. Provided administrative framework including federal structure, provincial governance, public service commissions. Critics called it overly influenced by colonial legislation, but framers argued practical continuity was essential.

hist_khadi_nationalism.label: Khadi and Nationalism
hist_khadi_nationalism.subject: history
hist_khadi_nationalism.detail: During the national movement, Mahatma Gandhi urged boycott of imported textiles and use of hand-spun hand-woven cloth. Khadi became a symbol of nationalism and the charkha was placed at the centre of the Congress tricolour in 1931.

hist_gandhi_on_education.label: Gandhi on Education
hist_gandhi_on_education.subject: history
hist_gandhi_on_education.detail: Gandhi argued colonial education created inferiority complex, enslaved Indians, and made them strangers in their own land. Advocated education in Indian languages with focus on handicrafts, practical knowledge and all-round development of body, mind and spirit.

hist_br_ambedkar.label: B.R. Ambedkar
hist_br_ambedkar.subject: history
hist_br_ambedkar.detail: Born into Mahar family, experienced caste prejudice in school. Studied in US, wrote extensively on upper-caste power. Started temple entry movement in 1927. Led Dalit movement for social equality and became Chairman of Constitution's Drafting Committee.

hist_periyar.label: E.V. Ramaswamy Naicker (Periyar)
hist_periyar.subject: history
hist_periyar.detail: Founded Self Respect Movement. Argued untouchables upheld original Tamil and Dravidian culture subjugated by Brahmans. Criticized Hindu scriptures including Manu's codes and Ramayana for establishing Brahman authority.

hist_child_marriage_act_1929.label: Child Marriage Restraint Act 1929
hist_child_marriage_act_1929.subject: history
hist_child_marriage_act_1929.detail: Passed in 1929 without bitter debates. Set minimum marriage age at 18 for men and 16 for women. Subsequently raised to 21 for men and 18 for women.

hist_salt_march_1930.label: Salt March / Dandi March
hist_salt_march_1930.subject: history
hist_salt_march_1930.detail: In 1930 Gandhi marched 240 miles from Sabarmati to Dandi to break salt law. Related freedom to a specific grievance shared by all. Thousands arrested. Led to Civil Disobedience Movement with mass participation.

hist_quit_india_1942.label: Quit India Movement
hist_quit_india_1942.subject: history
hist_quit_india_1942.detail: Launched August 1942 with Gandhi's 'do or die' call. Leaders jailed immediately but movement spread. By end of 1943, over 90,000 arrested, around 1,000 killed. People set up their own governments in many areas.

hist_bhagat_singh.label: Bhagat Singh
hist_bhagat_singh.subject: history
hist_bhagat_singh.detail: Revolutionary nationalist who founded HSRA in 1928. Assassinated officer Saunders in 1928 for Lajpat Rai's death. Threw bomb in Central Legislative Assembly in 1929. Executed on 23 March 1931 at age 23.

hist_subhas_bose_ina.label: Subhas Chandra Bose and INA
hist_subhas_bose_ina.subject: history
hist_subhas_bose_ina.detail: Radical nationalist with socialist leanings. Secretly left India in 1941, went to Singapore via Germany. Raised Azad Hind Fauj (INA). Attempted to enter India through Imphal-Kohima in 1944 but campaign failed.

hist_purna_swaraj_1929.label: Purna Swaraj Resolution 1929
hist_purna_swaraj_1929.subject: history
hist_purna_swaraj_1929.detail: Congress resolved to fight for complete independence in 1929 under presidentship of Jawaharlal Nehru. Independence Day observed on 26 January 1930 all over the country.

hist_stalin_collectivisation.label: Stalin's Collectivisation
hist_stalin_collectivisation.subject: history
hist_stalin_collectivisation.detail: From 1929 Stalin forced peasants into collective farms (kolkhoz). 'Kulaks' eliminated, land and implements transferred to collectives. Peasants resisted, destroyed livestock. Bad harvests 1930-33 caused famine killing over 4 million.

hist_five_year_plans_ussr.label: Five Year Plans (USSR)
hist_five_year_plans_ussr.subject: history
hist_five_year_plans_ussr.detail: Centralised planning with government-set targets for five-year periods. First two plans (1927-38) led to 100% increase in oil, coal and steel production. New factory cities built but with poor working conditions.

hist_ussr_formation.label: Formation of USSR
hist_ussr_formation.subject: history
hist_ussr_formation.detail: Union of Soviet Socialist Republics created from Russian empire in December 1922. Non-Russian nationalities given political autonomy. Became one-party state with trade unions under party control and secret police (Cheka/OGPU/NKVD).

hist_adolf_hitler.label: Adolf Hitler
hist_adolf_hitler.subject: history
hist_adolf_hitler.detail: Born 1889 in Austria. Joined German Workers Party in 1919, renamed it Nazi Party. Became Chancellor in 1933. Established dictatorship through Enabling Act. Pursued racial ideology and territorial expansion. Committed suicide April 1945.

hist_nazi_party.label: Nazi Party
hist_nazi_party.subject: history
hist_nazi_party.detail: National Socialist German Workers' Party renamed from German Workers' Party by Hitler. Got 2.6% votes in 1928 but became largest party with 37% by 1932 during Great Depression. Used propaganda, rallies and spectacle.

hist_enabling_act_1933.label: Enabling Act 1933
hist_enabling_act_1933.subject: history
hist_enabling_act_1933.detail: Passed 3 March 1933, established dictatorship by giving Hitler power to sideline Parliament and rule by decree. All parties and trade unions banned except Nazi Party. State controlled economy, media, army and judiciary.

hist_holocaust.label: The Holocaust
hist_holocaust.subject: history
hist_holocaust.detail: Systematic murder of 6 million Jews, 200,000 Gypsies, 1 million Polish civilians, 70,000 disabled Germans. Gas chambers at Auschwitz, Treblinka, and other death camps in Poland. Nuremberg Tribunal sentenced 11 Nazi leaders to death.

hist_nuremberg_laws.label: Nuremberg Laws 1935
hist_nuremberg_laws.subject: history
hist_nuremberg_laws.detail: Laws denying citizenship to Jews, forbidding Jewish-German marriages, confiscating Jewish property. Led to three stages: Exclusion (1933-39), Ghettoisation (1940-44), and Annihilation (1941 onwards).

hist_great_depression.label: Great Depression
hist_great_depression.subject: history
hist_great_depression.detail: Started with Wall Street crash on 24 October 1929 when 13 million shares sold in one day. US national income halved. Germany worst hit: industrial production fell to 40% of 1929 level, 6 million unemployed.

hist_hyperinflation_1923.label: German Hyperinflation 1923
hist_hyperinflation_1923.subject: history
hist_hyperinflation_1923.detail: When Germany refused to pay reparations, France occupied Ruhr. Germany printed money recklessly. Dollar went from 24,000 marks in April to trillions in December. Germans carried cartloads of currency for bread.

hist_nazi_racial_ideology.label: Nazi Racial Ideology
hist_nazi_racial_ideology.subject: history
hist_nazi_racial_ideology.detail: Racial hierarchy placing Nordic German Aryans at top and Jews at bottom. Drew from Darwin and Herbert Spencer's survival of fittest. Lebensraum (living space) concept demanded eastward territorial expansion.

hist_gestapo.label: Gestapo and SS
hist_gestapo.subject: history
hist_gestapo.detail: Gestapo (secret state police), SS (protection squads), criminal police and Security Service (SD) created to control society. Extra-constitutional powers to detain, torture, deport without legal procedures.

hist_wwii_europe.label: World War II in Europe
hist_wwii_europe.subject: history
hist_wwii_europe.detail: Germany invaded Poland September 1939 starting WWII. Tripartite Pact with Italy and Japan 1940. Invaded USSR June 1941. Defeated at Stalingrad. War ended May 1945 with Hitler's suicide and Allied victory.

hist_dust_bowl.label: Dust Bowl of 1930s
hist_dust_bowl.subject: history
hist_dust_bowl.detail: Terrifying black blizzards of dust in US Great Plains in 1930s. Over-ploughing had destroyed topsoil. Drought worsened conditions. By 1930s, over 38 million acres grassland ploughed recklessly for wheat.

hist_pentangular_tournament.label: Pentangular Tournament
hist_pentangular_tournament.subject: history
hist_pentangular_tournament.detail: Cricket tournament in Bombay with five teams based on community: Europeans, Parsees, Hindus, Muslims and The Rest. Gandhi and nationalists criticised it for dividing Indians along communal lines. Replaced by Ranji Trophy.

hist_bcci.label: Board of Control for Cricket in India
hist_bcci.subject: history
hist_bcci.detail: Established in 1928 to administer cricket in India. By late 20th century became the richest cricket board in the world due to India's massive television audience and commercial potential of the sport.

hist_swadeshi_clothing.label: Swadeshi and Clothing Politics
hist_swadeshi_clothing.subject: history
hist_swadeshi_clothing.detail: During national movement, Indian clothing became political. Gandhi adopted short dhoti and chaddar, rejecting Western dress. Swadeshi movement advocated burning of imported cloth and wearing khadi as political statement.

hist_gandhi_clothing_politics.label: Gandhi's Clothing Politics
hist_gandhi_clothing_politics.subject: history
hist_gandhi_clothing_politics.detail: Gandhi deliberately adopted the dress of the poorest Indian - short dhoti, chaddar, no shoes. This was a political statement about identifying with the masses and rejecting British sartorial standards. Charkha became national symbol.

hist_subhas_chandra_bose.label: Subhas Chandra Bose
hist_subhas_chandra_bose.subject: history
hist_subhas_chandra_bose.detail: Radical nationalist who disagreed with Gandhi's methods. Elected Congress President 1938-39 but forced to resign. Escaped to Germany (1941), then to Japan. Founded Azad Hind Fauj (INA) and Azad Hind government. Gave call 'Give me blood, I will give you freedom'. Died 1945.

hist_jinnah.label: Muhammad Ali Jinnah
hist_jinnah.subject: history
hist_jinnah.detail: Leader of Muslim League, called Quaid-e-Azam. Initially an ambassador of Hindu-Muslim unity in Congress. Grew disillusioned with Congress, especially after 1937 provincial governments. Advocated Two-Nation Theory. Demanded Pakistan from 1940 Lahore Resolution. Became first Governor-General of Pakistan.

hist_nehru.label: Jawaharlal Nehru
hist_nehru.subject: history
hist_nehru.detail: First Prime Minister of independent India. Congress president during Lahore session (1929). Led Congress negotiations during Cabinet Mission and partition. Reluctantly accepted partition to avoid civil war. Delivered 'Tryst with Destiny' speech on 14 August 1947.

hist_sardar_patel.label: Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel
hist_sardar_patel.subject: history
hist_sardar_patel.detail: Deputy Prime Minister and Home Minister of India. Integrated 562 princely states into Indian Union. Early advocate of accepting partition to consolidate India. Organised mass integration of princely states including Hyderabad, Junagadh and Kashmir through diplomacy and force.

hist_lord_mountbatten.label: Lord Mountbatten
hist_lord_mountbatten.subject: history
hist_lord_mountbatten.detail: Last Viceroy of India (March-August 1947), then first Governor-General of independent India. Accelerated partition timeline. Worked closely with Nehru. Appointed Radcliffe Boundary Commission. His hasty decisions are debated for contributing to partition violence.

hist_ambedkar.label: B.R. Ambedkar
hist_ambedkar.subject: history
hist_ambedkar.detail: Chairman of the Drafting Committee. Dalit leader and constitutional scholar, studied at Columbia and London. Argued for abolishing caste and ensuring fundamental rights for depressed classes. Key architect of provisions on equality, untouchability abolition and reservation.

hist_rajendra_prasad.label: Rajendra Prasad
hist_rajendra_prasad.subject: history
hist_rajendra_prasad.detail: President of the Constituent Assembly. Later became first President of India (1950-1962). Lawyer from Bihar who participated in Champaran Satyagraha. Presided over Assembly deliberations and signed the completed Constitution on 24 January 1950.

hist_treaty_of_sevres.label: Treaty of Sèvres (May 1920)
hist_treaty_of_sevres.subject: history
hist_treaty_of_sevres.detail: May 1920 treaty with Ottoman Turkey that formalised dismemberment of the Turkish/Ottoman Empire. Signed after WWI, it convinced Indian Muslims that British promises to preserve the Caliphate had been broken, pushing the Khilafat Committee to adopt Gandhi's non-cooperation programme on 9 June 1920 at Allahabad.

hist_hunter_committee.label: Hunter Committee (1919-20)
hist_hunter_committee.subject: history
hist_hunter_committee.detail: Official British inquiry into Jallianwala Bagh and Punjab disturbances. Widely seen as a whitewash — minor criticism of Dyer but effectively exonerated British officials. The House of Lords voted in favour of Dyer and Morning Post raised 30,000 pounds for him, outraging Indian opinion and pushing Congress toward Non-Cooperation.

hist_calcutta_special_session_1920.label: Calcutta Special Session (Sept 1920)
hist_calcutta_special_session_1920.subject: history
hist_calcutta_special_session_1920.detail: Special session of INC held September 1920. Adopted Non-Cooperation Movement despite opposition led by C.R. Das to boycott of legislative councils. First major Congress endorsement of Gandhian extra-constitutional methods.

hist_nagpur_session_1920.label: Nagpur Session (Dec 1920)
hist_nagpur_session_1920.subject: history
hist_nagpur_session_1920.detail: Annual INC session December 1920. C.R. Das moved the main resolution on Non-Cooperation. Congress creed changed from "self-government by constitutional and legal means" to "Swaraj by peaceful and legitimate means". New Congress constitution (Gandhi's drafting) introduced Working Committee of 15, PCCs on linguistic basis, membership reduced to 4 annas, village/mohalla committees, Hindi as working language.

hist_ali_brothers.label: Ali Brothers (Mohammed Ali & Shaukat Ali)
hist_ali_brothers.subject: history
hist_ali_brothers.detail: Mohammed Ali and Shaukat Ali — foremost Khilafat leaders. Travelled nationwide with Gandhi during Non-Cooperation. Mohammed Ali's July 1921 Karachi declaration that it was "religiously unlawful for Muslims to serve in British Army" led to his arrest and the famous 4 October 1921 manifesto by 47 Congressmen.

hist_tilak_swaraj_fund.label: Tilak Swaraj Fund (1921)
hist_tilak_swaraj_fund.subject: history
hist_tilak_swaraj_fund.detail: Fund launched by Congress at Vijayawada AICC (April 1921). Target of Rs 1 crore was oversubscribed. Used for national schools, charkha distribution, and Congress organisation. Symbol of mass popular support for NCM — Congress membership reached ~50 lakhs.

hist_congress_volunteer_corps.label: Congress Volunteer Corps (1921)
hist_congress_volunteer_corps.subject: history
hist_congress_volunteer_corps.detail: Uniformed parallel "people's police" that grew during Non-Cooperation. Marched in formation, organised protests, enforced boycott. Declared illegal by government in December 1921; arrests of Corps members triggered wave of Congress leader arrests (~30,000 in 2 months).

hist_prince_of_wales_visit.label: Prince of Wales Visit (Nov 1921)
hist_prince_of_wales_visit.subject: history
hist_prince_of_wales_visit.detail: 17 November 1921 — Prince of Wales landed in Bombay to empty streets and hartal. Clashes between welcome-party attendees and boycott crowd returning from Gandhi's meeting led to three-day riots in Bombay; 59 dead. Parsis, Christians, Anglo-Indians targeted as loyalists. Gandhi fasted 3 days. Disturbed Gandhi about mass violence risk.

hist_ahmedabad_session_1921.label: Ahmedabad Session (Dec 1921)
hist_ahmedabad_session_1921.subject: history
hist_ahmedabad_session_1921.detail: Annual INC session Dec 1921. Appointed Gandhi as sole authority on mass civil disobedience. Under pressure from rank-and-file to escalate, Gandhi announced Bardoli as site of CD but withdrew after Chauri-Chaura.

hist_cr_das.label: C.R. Das (Chittaranjan Das)
hist_cr_das.subject: history
hist_cr_das.detail: Deshbandhu (1870-1925). Bengali nationalist, lawyer. Initially opposed legislative-council boycott at Calcutta 1920 but moved the Non-Cooperation resolution at Nagpur Dec 1920 after voter turnout collapsed. Arrested Dec 1921 along with his wife Basanti Debi. Later co-founded Swaraj Party with Motilal Nehru (1923). Died June 1925.

hist_oudh_kisan_sabha.label: Oudh Kisan Sabha (Oct 1920)
hist_oudh_kisan_sabha.subject: history
hist_oudh_kisan_sabha.detail: Non-Cooperator alternative to UP Kisan Sabha, founded 17 October 1920 at Pratapgarh. Integrated 330+ village kisan sabhas across Avadh. Founded by Gauri Shankar Misra, Jawaharlal Nehru, Baba Ramchandra, Mata Badal Pande, Deo Narayan Pande, Kedar Nath. Demands: refuse to till bedakhli land, no hari/begar forced labour, solve disputes via panchayats. Ayodhya rally of 100,000 peasants on 20-21 Dec 1920.

hist_baba_ramchandra.label: Baba Ramchandra
hist_baba_ramchandra.subject: history
hist_baba_ramchandra.detail: Maharashtrian Brahmin sadhu who became rallying figure for Avadh peasant movement in mid-1920. Arrested 28 August 1920 on trumped-up theft charge; peasant mobilisation secured his release. Central to Oudh Kisan Sabha. At Ayodhya rally, appeared bound in ropes to symbolise kisan oppression.

hist_eka_movement.label: Eka Movement (1921-22)
hist_eka_movement.subject: history
hist_eka_movement.detail: Peasant "unity" movement in Hardoi, Bahraich, Sitapur (northern Avadh) late 1921. Grievances: rent 50% above record rates, thekedar oppression, share-rents. Ritual oaths taken around water-filled "Ganges" pit. Leadership passed to Madari Pasi and low-caste leaders who rejected non-violence discipline. Unlike Kisan Sabha, included small zamindars. Crushed by March 1922.

hist_moplah_rebellion_1921.label: Moplah (Mappila) Rebellion (1921)
hist_moplah_rebellion_1921.subject: history
hist_moplah_rebellion_1921.detail: August-December 1921 uprising of Muslim Mappila tenants in Malabar, Kerala. Initial impetus from Manjeri Conference April 1920 that supported tenants' cause. Merged with Khilafat movement. Triggered 20 Aug 1921 by raid on Tirurangadi mosque to arrest Ali Musaliar. Initial targets: Hindu landlords (jenmies), courts, police stations. After martial law, rebellion acquired communal character with forced conversions. Leaders: Ali Musaliar, Kunhammed Haji. Suppressed by Dec 1921: 2,337 dead officially, 45,404 captured. Drove wedge between Mappilas and NCM; political isolation lasted till independence.

hist_bardoli_satyagraha_1928.label: Bardoli Satyagraha (1928)
hist_bardoli_satyagraha_1928.subject: history
hist_bardoli_satyagraha_1928.detail: No-tax movement in Bardoli taluq, Surat district, Feb-Aug 1928. Triggered by 30% land-revenue reassessment recommended by Jayakar; Bardoli Inquiry Committee 1926 found it unjustified. Vallabhbhai Patel led — earned title "Sardar" from women of Bardoli. Organisation: 13 Chhavanis (workers' camps), 100 workers + 1,500 volunteers, Bardoli Satyagraha Patrika daily. Intelligence wing monitored waverers. Women (Mithuben Petit, Maniben Patel, others) and Kaliparaj tribal base mobilised. Governor Irwin pressured Bombay to retreat; Broomfield-Maxwell enquiry reduced enhancement to 6.03%. Massive win preceded CD 1930.

hist_kaliparaj_raniparaj.label: Kaliparaj → Raniparaj Uplift Work
hist_kaliparaj_raniparaj.subject: history
hist_kaliparaj_raniparaj.detail: Bardoli Congress workers' social reform project among tribal "Kaliparaj" (dark people, 60% of taluq) from 1922. Ashram network (6 ashrams) taught literacy, exposed Hali hereditary-labour system. Kunverji Mehta and Keshavji Ganeshji developed "Kaliparaj literature". Gandhi renamed them "Raniparaj" (forest inhabitants) in 1927. Built base that later supported Bardoli Satyagraha against upper-caste landlord counter-mobilisation.

hist_aituc.label: All India Trade Union Congress (AITUC)
hist_aituc.subject: history
hist_aituc.detail: Founded 1920 as first all-India labour federation. Lala Lajpat Rai first president, Dewan Chaman Lal first General Secretary. Tilak was a moving spirit in its formation. Its manifesto urged workers to participate in nationalist politics: "political freedom is of no worth without economic freedom". C.R. Das presided over 3rd and 4th sessions. 1928 Jharia session saw Communist dominance; corporatist trend led by N.M. Joshi split away at the Nehru-presided subsequent session.

hist_dewan_chaman_lal.label: Dewan Chaman Lal
hist_dewan_chaman_lal.subject: history
hist_dewan_chaman_lal.detail: First General Secretary of AITUC (1920). Major figure in Indian labour movement. Moved resolution at 2nd AITUC session declaring Swaraj must be "not for the capitalists but for the workers".

hist_ahmedabad_tla.label: Ahmedabad Textile Labour Association (TLA)
hist_ahmedabad_tla.subject: history
hist_ahmedabad_tla.detail: Founded 1918 by Gandhi. 14,000 workers at peak — largest single trade union of its time. Built on Gandhi's trusteeship principle and arbitration (capitalist as trustee of workers' interests). Won 27.5% wage hike in 1918 dispute. Model of non-confrontational labour-capital relations that also retained radical potential (workers were "real masters" per Gandhi).

hist_workers_peasants_party.label: Workers' and Peasants' Parties (WPP)
hist_workers_peasants_party.subject: history
hist_workers_peasants_party.detail: By early 1927, Communist groups organised as WPPs in different parts of India, functioning as left-wing within Congress. Leaders: S.A. Dange, Muzaffar Ahmed, P.C. Joshi, Sohan Singh Josh. Gained strength in Congress provincial and all-India organisation. Dissolved after Meerut Conspiracy arrests 1929 and Communist shift away from united front.

hist_sa_dange.label: S.A. Dange
hist_sa_dange.subject: history
hist_sa_dange.detail: Shripad Amrit Dange. Early Communist leader, WPP figure, accused in Meerut Conspiracy Case (1929-33). Later General Secretary of CPI. Prolific trade unionist and writer.

hist_muzaffar_ahmed.label: Muzaffar Ahmed
hist_muzaffar_ahmed.subject: history
hist_muzaffar_ahmed.detail: Founding member of Communist Party of India. WPP Bengal leader. Arrested in Kanpur Bolshevik Conspiracy Case (1924) and Meerut Conspiracy Case (1929). Senior figure in Bengal labour and peasant movements.

hist_pc_joshi.label: P.C. Joshi
hist_pc_joshi.subject: history
hist_pc_joshi.detail: Puran Chand Joshi. Communist leader; later General Secretary of CPI (1935-47). Instrumental in CPI's decision to support WWII as "people's war" from 1941 (after Nazi attack on USSR) and to dissociate from Quit India 1942.

hist_girni_kamgar_union.label: Girni Kamgar Union (1928)
hist_girni_kamgar_union.subject: history
hist_girni_kamgar_union.detail: Communist-led Bombay textile union. Rose to pre-eminence after the historic six-month Bombay Textile Strike (April-September 1928). Membership jumped from 324 to 54,000 by Dec 1928. Fell to ~800 by end 1929 after Communist withdrawal from united national front.

hist_bombay_textile_strike_1928.label: Bombay Textile Strike (April-Sept 1928)
hist_bombay_textile_strike_1928.subject: history
hist_bombay_textile_strike_1928.detail: Six-month general strike by Bombay textile workers, April-September 1928. Communist-led under Girni Kamgar Union. Historic scale — unified Bombay working class, cemented Communist influence in labour movement, and alarmed the colonial government into the repressive legislation (Public Safety Act, Trade Disputes Act) that followed.

hist_meerut_conspiracy_case.label: Meerut Conspiracy Case (1929-33)
hist_meerut_conspiracy_case.subject: history
hist_meerut_conspiracy_case.detail: Government prosecution launched March 1929 against 32 Communist, WPP, and trade union leaders on charges of conspiring to deprive the King of his sovereignty. Trial lasted four years. Made Communist leaders nationally famous; Nehru, Gandhi and others publicly defended the accused. Severely damaged organised left but generated sympathy for its cause. Key accused included S.A. Dange, Muzaffar Ahmed, Shaukat Usmani, Philip Spratt, Ben Bradley.

hist_public_safety_trade_disputes_acts.label: Public Safety Act + Trade Disputes Act (1929)
hist_public_safety_trade_disputes_acts.subject: history
hist_public_safety_trade_disputes_acts.detail: Twin 1929 laws passed by colonial government to crush organised labour. Trade Disputes Act restricted strike action in public utilities and made lightning strikes illegal. Public Safety Bill aimed at deporting foreign communists, dropped after Bhagat Singh-Batukeshwar Dutt bomb in Central Legislative Assembly 8 April 1929 protesting these bills.

hist_royal_commission_labour_1929.label: Royal Commission on Labour (1929) — Whitley Commission
hist_royal_commission_labour_1929.subject: history
hist_royal_commission_labour_1929.detail: Set up 1929 under J.H. Whitley. Dual-purpose move — concession to wean moderate labour from militant stream while Meerut Conspiracy Case crushed radicals. Report (1931) formed basis of later factories, industrial disputes and labour welfare legislation.

hist_sholapur_uprising_1930.label: Sholapur Textile Workers Uprising (May 1930)
hist_sholapur_uprising_1930.subject: history
hist_sholapur_uprising_1930.detail: 7-16 May 1930 — textile workers of Sholapur went on rampage after police fired on anti-British procession during Civil Disobedience Movement. Attacked government offices, courts, police stations, railway stations. Rebels held city for several days; national flag hoisted over town. Martial law imposed. Multiple workers hanged. One of the high points of CDM worker participation.

hist_post_telegraph_strike_1946.label: All India Post & Telegraph Strike (1946)
hist_post_telegraph_strike_1946.subject: history
hist_post_telegraph_strike_1946.detail: Landmark nationwide strike 1946 by Post & Telegraph Department workers. Symbolic of post-war economic grievances (high prices, food scarcity, drop in real wages, post-war demobilisation) and pre-independence anticipation. Part of 1945-47 worker upsurge.

hist_akali_movement.label: Akali Movement (1920-25)
hist_akali_movement.subject: history
hist_akali_movement.detail: Sikh reform movement 1920-25 to free Gurdwaras from corrupt mahants who collaborated with British (e.g. Amritsar priests honoured General Dyer with saropa). >30,000 imprisoned, ~400 killed, 2,000+ wounded. SGPC formed Nov 1920; Shiromani Akali Dal formed Dec 1920 (political arm). Non-violent creed adopted under NCM influence. Jat peasantry backbone, nationalist intellectual leadership. Culminated in Sikh Gurdwaras Act July 1925.

hist_sgpc.label: Shiromani Gurdwara Prabandhak Committee (SGPC)
hist_sgpc.subject: history
hist_sgpc.detail: Central body elected by 10,000-strong Sikh assembly Nov 1920 — committee of 175 to manage Golden Temple, Akal Takht and other Gurdwaras. Became statutory elected body after Sikh Gurdwaras Act 1925. Passed May 1921 resolution for non-cooperation: boycott of foreign goods/liquor, panchayats instead of British courts.

hist_nankana_tragedy.label: Nankana Tragedy (Feb 1921)
hist_nankana_tragedy.subject: history
hist_nankana_tragedy.detail: 20 February 1921 — at Nankana, birthplace of Guru Nanak, Mahant Narain Das's 500 mercenaries opened fire on peaceful Akali jatha entering the Gurdwara to pray. ~100 Akalis killed. Kartar Singh Jhabbar's jathas liberated the Gurdwara. Gandhi, Shaukat Ali, Lajpat Rai visited in solidarity. Turning point that integrated Akali movement with national struggle.

hist_keys_affair_1921.label: Keys Affair (Oct-Nov 1921)
hist_keys_affair_1921.subject: history
hist_keys_affair_1921.detail: October 1921 — government attempt to keep possession of keys of Golden Temple Toshakhana triggered mass Akali protest. Baba Kharak Singh, Master Tara Singh arrested. Government climbed down, released all, surrendered keys to Baba Kharak Singh (SGPC head). Gandhi telegrammed: "First battle for India's freedom won. Congratulations." Major symbolic Akali victory.

hist_guru_ka_bagh.label: Guru-Ka-Bagh Morcha (Aug-Sept 1922)
hist_guru_ka_bagh.subject: history
hist_guru_ka_bagh.detail: 9 August 1922 onwards — Akali non-violent struggle at Guru-Ka-Bagh Gurdwara near Amritsar. Over 4,000 Akalis arrested for tree-cutting "theft". Police beatings (instead of arrests) on volunteers who refused to yield. C.F. Andrews called the oppression a "moral defeat of England". Climbed down when retired govt servant leased disputed land. National outrage, Congress investigation committee appointed.

hist_sikh_gurdwaras_act_1925.label: Sikh Gurdwaras Act (July 1925)
hist_sikh_gurdwaras_act_1925.subject: history
hist_sikh_gurdwaras_act_1925.detail: Legislation passed July 1925 — handed control over all Punjab Gurdwaras to an elected body of Sikhs (statutory SGPC). Culmination of Akali Movement 1920-25. Model of successful religious-reform movement that remained non-communal in its popular base.

hist_vaikom_satyagraha.label: Vaikom Satyagraha (1924-25)
hist_vaikom_satyagraha.subject: history
hist_vaikom_satyagraha.detail: Temple-entry Satyagraha at Vaikom, Travancore, begun 30 March 1924 — demanded right for avarnas (Ezhavas, Pulayas) to use temple roads. Led by K.P. Kesava Menon (Kerala Provincial Congress). Nationwide support: Akali jatha from Punjab, E.V. Ramaswami Naicker (Periyar) led jatha from Madurai (jailed). Savarna jatha of 1,000+ marched to Trivandrum Oct 1924. Maharani refused. Gandhi toured Kerala March 1925, negotiated compromise: outer temple roads opened to avarnas; inner Sankethan remained closed.

hist_kp_kesava_menon.label: K.P. Kesava Menon
hist_kp_kesava_menon.subject: history
hist_kp_kesava_menon.detail: Kerala Congress leader who led Vaikom Satyagraha (1924-25). Co-founder of Mathrubhumi newspaper 1923. Major figure in Malabar Congress and Kerala anti-untouchability movement.

hist_guruvayur_satyagraha.label: Guruvayur Satyagraha (1931-32)
hist_guruvayur_satyagraha.subject: history
hist_guruvayur_satyagraha.detail: Temple-entry Satyagraha at Guruvayur, launched 1 November 1931 by KPCC. Led by K. Kelappan. Jatha of 16 volunteers led by poet Subramanian Tirumambu ("Singing Sword of Kerala") marched from Cannanore. A.K. Gopalan and P. Krishna Pillai (future Communist leaders) mercilessly beaten. Kelappan fasted unto death 21 Sept 1932; Gandhi intervened, Kelappan broke fast 2 October 1932. Temple opened only in 1947 but campaign thrived.

hist_k_kelappan.label: K. Kelappan
hist_k_kelappan.subject: history
hist_k_kelappan.detail: Kerala Gandhian leader. Led Guruvayur temple-entry Satyagraha 1931-32. Fasted unto death 21 Sept 1932 demanding temple opening. Broke fast 2 October on Gandhi's intervention. Major figure in Kerala nationalist and anti-untouchability movements; later active in Bhoodan movement.

hist_ak_gopalan.label: A.K. Gopalan
hist_ak_gopalan.subject: history
hist_ak_gopalan.detail: Started as Gandhian, became Communist leader of Kerala. Beaten mercilessly at Guruvayur Satyagraha 1931. Led 1,000-mile Kerala jatha after Kelappan's fast. Later founded All India Kisan Sabha Kerala branch. First leader of Opposition in Indian Parliament 1952-54 (CPI).

hist_travancore_temple_entry_1936.label: Travancore Temple Entry Proclamation (Nov 1936)
hist_travancore_temple_entry_1936.subject: history
hist_travancore_temple_entry_1936.detail: 12 November 1936 — Maharaja of Travancore issued proclamation throwing open all government-controlled temples to all Hindus irrespective of caste. Landmark — first major princely/government implementation of temple entry for depressed classes. Result of sustained Kerala temple-entry agitation and Congress pressure.

hist_madras_temple_entry_1938.label: Madras Temple Entry Act (1938)
hist_madras_temple_entry_1938.subject: history
hist_madras_temple_entry_1938.detail: 1938 — Madras Congress Ministry headed by C. Rajagopalachari passed Temple Entry Authorisation Act. Other Congress-ruled provinces followed. Concrete achievement of Congress provincial rule 1937-39 for anti-untouchability movement.

hist_swaraj_party.label: Swaraj Party (Jan 1923)
hist_swaraj_party.subject: history
hist_swaraj_party.detail: Congress-Khilafat Swaraj Party, founded 1 January 1923 by C.R. Das (President) and Motilal Nehru (Secretary) after the Gaya Session defeated council-entry (1748 vs 890). Programme: contest elections, enter legislatures, wreck "sham reforms" from within via "uniform, continuous and consistent obstruction". Won 42/101 Central Legislative Assembly seats Nov 1923; majority in Central Provinces; largest party in Bengal. Made Vithalbhai Patel CLA President 1925. Formally part of Congress after Belgaum Dec 1924.

hist_gaya_session_1922.label: Gaya Congress Session (Dec 1922)
hist_gaya_session_1922.subject: history
hist_gaya_session_1922.detail: Annual INC Dec 1922, presided over by C.R. Das. Das and Motilal Nehru moved "mend or end" councils resolution — defeated 1748 vs 890 by No-Changer camp of Vallabhbhai Patel, Rajendra Prasad, C. Rajagopalachari. Das and Motilal resigned from Congress offices; announced formation of Swaraj Party within a week. Welcomed AITUC and formed committee to assist its work.

hist_pro_changers_no_changers.label: Pro-Changers vs No-Changers (1922-24)
hist_pro_changers_no_changers.subject: history
hist_pro_changers_no_changers.detail: Post-NCM withdrawal split in Congress. Pro-Changers (Das, Motilal) argued for council entry to fill political void and wreck reforms from within. No-Changers (Gandhi, Patel, Rajendra Prasad, Rajagopalachari) argued for continued boycott and constructive programme. Both agreed mass civil disobedience wasn't possible immediately; differed on non-active-phase politics. Settled Nov 1924: Gandhi signed joint statement with Das/Motilal letting Swaraj Party work in councils on behalf of Congress.

hist_vithalbhai_patel.label: Vithalbhai Patel
hist_vithalbhai_patel.subject: history
hist_vithalbhai_patel.detail: Elder brother of Sardar Patel. Leading Swarajist. Elected first Indian President of Central Legislative Assembly March 1925. Famously told the government: "We want you to carry on the administration of this country by veto and by certification... treat the Government of India Act as a scrap of paper." Also President of Bombay Corporation. Died 1933 in Europe — befriended Bose in exile.

hist_cr_das_death.label: Death of C.R. Das (June 1925)
hist_cr_das_death.subject: history
hist_cr_das_death.detail: 16 June 1925 — C.R. Das died, depriving Swaraj Party of its most charismatic leader and effectively beginning its decline. Also split Bengal Congress leadership into Subhas Bose wing (with Yugantar support) and J.M. Sengupta wing (with Anushilan support).

hist_belgaum_session_1924.label: Belgaum Congress Session (Dec 1924)
hist_belgaum_session_1924.subject: history
hist_belgaum_session_1924.detail: Dec 1924 Congress session — the only one Gandhi personally presided over. Endorsed the Gandhi-Das-Motilal joint statement that Swaraj Party would work in legislatures as an integral part of Congress. Gandhi gave Swarajists majority on his Working Committee. Marked reconciliation of pro-changer and no-changer wings.

hist_public_safety_bill_1928.label: Public Safety Bill (1928)
hist_public_safety_bill_1928.subject: history
hist_public_safety_bill_1928.detail: 1928 government attempt to deport "undesirable" foreign communists suspected of Comintern activity. Opposed by all nationalists — Lajpat Rai ("The greatest danger we are in, is from the capitalists and exploiters"), Motilal Nehru ("Slavery of India, Bill No. 1"), Chaman Lal, and even capitalists Purshottamdas Thakurdas and G.D. Birla. Government unable to pass; responded by arresting 31 Communist/trade union/Left leaders at Meerut (March 1929) for the Meerut Conspiracy Case. Also triggered Bhagat Singh-B.K. Dutt bomb in Assembly 8 April 1929.

hist_responsivists.label: Responsivists (1926)
hist_responsivists.subject: history
hist_responsivists.detail: Faction within Swaraj Party from 1926 that wanted to work the 1919 reforms and hold office wherever possible, shifting from obstruction to cooperation. Joined government in Central Provinces. N.C. Kelkar and M.R. Jayakar key figures; Lajpat Rai and Madan Mohan Malaviya separated from Swaraj Party on Responsivist and communal grounds. Responsivist drift triggered Swaraj Party's March 1926 decision to withdraw from legislatures.

hist_gandhian_constructive_programme.label: Gandhian Constructive Programme
hist_gandhian_constructive_programme.subject: history
hist_gandhian_constructive_programme.detail: Multi-faceted grassroots work during passive phases of national movement: khadi and spinning, national education, Hindu-Muslim unity, anti-untouchability, Adivasi uplift, boycott of foreign cloth. Centred in hundreds of ashrams across India (Vedchi Ashram in Bardoli taluq, Ravishankar Maharaj among Baraiyas in Kheda). Served as recruitment channel for political cadres and the steel frame of Satyagraha phases.

hist_hra.label: Hindustan Republican Association (HRA, Oct 1924)
hist_hra.subject: history
hist_hra.detail: Founded October 1924 at Kanpur by Ramprasad Bismil, Jogesh Chandra Chatterjea and Sachindranath Sanyal. Goal: armed revolution to establish "Federal Republic of the United States of India" with adult franchise. Manifesto stood for "abolition of all systems which make the exploitation of man by man possible". Main action: Kakori Robbery 1925. Reorganised as HSRA in 1928.

hist_ramprasad_bismil.label: Ramprasad Bismil
hist_ramprasad_bismil.subject: history
hist_ramprasad_bismil.detail: Co-founder of HRA 1924. Mastermind of Kakori Robbery 9 Aug 1925. Hanged in Gorakhpur Jail 19 December 1927. Wrote poetry including the revolutionary anthem "Sarfaroshi ki tamanna" and a message from the death cell asking youth to give up revolvers and work in "the open movement", establish Hindu-Muslim unity, and unite under Congress.

hist_sachindranath_sanyal.label: Sachindranath Sanyal
hist_sachindranath_sanyal.subject: history
hist_sachindranath_sanyal.detail: HRA co-founder. Author of Bandi Jivan (Incarcerated Life), which served as the textbook of the revolutionary movement. Twice sentenced to Andamans Cellular Jail (life terms). Linked Bengal and Northern India revolutionary strands.

hist_kakori_conspiracy.label: Kakori Train Robbery (Aug 1925)
hist_kakori_conspiracy.subject: history
hist_kakori_conspiracy.detail: 9 August 1925 — ten HRA men held up the 8-Down train at Kakori near Lucknow, looted official railway cash. Purpose: fund armed revolution. Government crackdown — Kakori Conspiracy Case. Ashfaqulla Khan, Ramprasad Bismil, Roshan Singh, Rajendra Lahiri hanged (Dec 1927); 4 sent to Andamans for life; 17 others long terms. Chandrashekhar Azad escaped.

hist_ashfaqulla_khan.label: Ashfaqulla Khan
hist_ashfaqulla_khan.subject: history
hist_ashfaqulla_khan.detail: HRA revolutionary. Key participant in Kakori Robbery Aug 1925. Hanged at Faizabad Jail 19 December 1927. Symbol of Hindu-Muslim unity in the revolutionary movement.

hist_chandrashekhar_azad.label: Chandrashekhar Azad
hist_chandrashekhar_azad.subject: history
hist_chandrashekhar_azad.detail: Joined HRA after Kakori; one of only senior leaders to escape arrest. Overall leader of reorganised HSRA from 1928. Pledged "Azad rahunga, azad maruga" (Shall remain free, shall die free). Died in a shooting encounter at Alfred Park, Allahabad, 27 February 1931 — self-shot to avoid capture.

hist_hsra.label: Hindustan Socialist Republican Association (HSRA, Sept 1928)
hist_hsra.subject: history
hist_hsra.detail: Reconstituted at Ferozeshah Kotla ground, Delhi, 9-10 September 1928. Leaders: Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev, Bhagwati Charan Vohra, Bejoy Sinha, Shiv Varma, Jaidev Kapur (North India) + Chandrashekhar Azad (overall). Adopted socialism as explicit goal. Major actions: Saunders assassination (Dec 1928), Assembly Bomb (April 1929), Lahore Conspiracy (1929-31). Key document: Philosophy of the Bomb.

hist_lajpat_rai_death.label: Death of Lala Lajpat Rai (Nov 1928)
hist_lajpat_rai_death.subject: history
hist_lajpat_rai_death.detail: 30 October 1928 — "Sher-e-Punjab" Lala Lajpat Rai led anti-Simon Commission demonstration at Lahore. Brutal lathi charge by Scott (Superintendent of Police); blows by J.P. Saunders. Lajpat Rai died 17 November 1928 from injuries. Last words: "Every blow aimed at me today will be a nail in the coffin of British rule." HSRA took vengeance.

hist_saunders_murder.label: Saunders Assassination (Dec 1928)
hist_saunders_murder.subject: history
hist_saunders_murder.detail: 17 December 1928 (note: Bipin Chandra says Nov 17 but historically Dec 17) — HSRA revenge for Lajpat Rai's death. Bhagat Singh, Rajguru, and Chandrashekhar Azad shot dead J.P. Saunders, Assistant Superintendent of Police (mistaken for James Scott who had led the lathi charge). Escaped Lahore with famous poster: "J.P. Saunders is dead. Lala Lajpat Rai is avenged". Led to Lahore Conspiracy Case.

hist_assembly_bomb_1929.label: Central Assembly Bomb (April 1929)
hist_assembly_bomb_1929.subject: history
hist_assembly_bomb_1929.detail: 8 April 1929 — Bhagat Singh and B.K. Dutt threw two deliberately-harmless bombs in Central Legislative Assembly in protest against Public Safety Bill and Trade Disputes Bill. Leaflet declared "to make the deaf hear". Did not flee; arrested deliberately to use trial as propaganda platform. Inquilab Zindabad slogan popularised. Led to Lahore Conspiracy Case and Bhagat Singh's later hanging.

hist_batukeshwar_dutt.label: Batukeshwar Dutt (B.K. Dutt)
hist_batukeshwar_dutt.subject: history
hist_batukeshwar_dutt.detail: HSRA revolutionary. Threw Assembly bomb with Bhagat Singh 8 April 1929. Arrested deliberately; sentenced to life imprisonment in the Andamans. Released 1938 after failing health. Participated in Quit India 1942. Survived to see independence.

hist_rajguru.label: Shivaram Rajguru
hist_rajguru.subject: history
hist_rajguru.detail: HSRA revolutionary. Participated in Saunders assassination (Dec 1928). Arrested later. Hanged at Lahore Central Jail on 23 March 1931 along with Bhagat Singh and Sukhdev. Famously insisted on going first to the gallows.

hist_sukhdev.label: Sukhdev Thapar
hist_sukhdev.subject: history
hist_sukhdev.detail: Close associate of Bhagat Singh. Co-organiser of Lahore Students Union and Naujawan Bharat Sabha. Tried in Lahore Conspiracy Case. Hanged alongside Bhagat Singh and Rajguru on 23 March 1931.

hist_jatin_das_death.label: Jatin Das Hunger-Strike Death (Sept 1929)
hist_jatin_das_death.subject: history
hist_jatin_das_death.detail: Jatin Das, fellow HSRA revolutionary, joined Bhagat Singh's jail hunger strike demanding that political prisoners be treated differently from ordinary criminals. Died 13 September 1929 on 63rd day of fast. 6-lakh-strong two-mile procession carried his coffin through Calcutta — cemented national sympathy for the revolutionaries.

hist_lahore_conspiracy_case.label: Lahore Conspiracy Case (1929-31)
hist_lahore_conspiracy_case.subject: history
hist_lahore_conspiracy_case.detail: Follow-up to Saunders assassination and Assembly bomb — HSRA revolutionaries prosecuted in Lahore. Defiant attitude, Inquilab Zindabad slogans, revolutionary songs ("Sarfaroshi ki tamanna", "Mera rang de basanti chola") won national sympathy. Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev, Rajguru sentenced to death — hanged 23 March 1931 at Lahore Central Jail. Country in mourning; Gandhi-Irwin Pact (March 1931) could not secure their reprieve.

hist_naujawan_bharat_sabha.label: Naujawan Bharat Sabha (1926)
hist_naujawan_bharat_sabha.subject: history
hist_naujawan_bharat_sabha.detail: Founded by Bhagat Singh 1926, served as open (legal) wing of HSRA. Carried political work among youth, peasants, workers. Villages branches, magic-lantern political lectures. Six rules included: "have nothing to do with communal bodies" and "create the spirit of general toleration". Bhagat Singh and Sukhdev also organised Lahore Students Union as open youth body.

hist_philosophy_of_bomb.label: Philosophy of the Bomb (1930)
hist_philosophy_of_bomb.subject: history
hist_philosophy_of_bomb.detail: Foundational HSRA ideological document, written by Bhagwati Charan Vohra, Chandrashekhar Azad and Yashpal. Defined revolution as "independence, social, political and economic aimed at establishing a new order of society in which political and economic exploitation will be an impossibility". Marked HSRA's shift from mere terrorism to socialist revolutionary theory.

hist_bhagwati_charan_vohra.label: Bhagwati Charan Vohra
hist_bhagwati_charan_vohra.subject: history
hist_bhagwati_charan_vohra.detail: HSRA chief ideologue and bomb-maker. Co-author of Philosophy of the Bomb. Died 28 May 1930 while testing a bomb meant to rescue Bhagat Singh from jail — bomb exploded prematurely in his hands on banks of Ravi river.

hist_why_i_am_atheist.label: "Why I am an Atheist" by Bhagat Singh (1930)
hist_why_i_am_atheist.subject: history
hist_why_i_am_atheist.detail: Essay written by Bhagat Singh in Lahore Central Jail, few weeks before his hanging. Critiqued religion and religious philosophy. Traced his path from belief ("mythology and doctrines of Sikhism") to atheism and materialism. Argued revolutionaries need "criticism and independent thinking". Reflected his Marxist turn.

hist_chittagong_armoury_raid.label: Chittagong Armoury Raid (April 1930)
hist_chittagong_armoury_raid.subject: history
hist_chittagong_armoury_raid.detail: 18 April 1930 — 65 revolutionaries in the Indian Republican Army (Chittagong Branch) under Surya Sen seized Chittagong Police Armoury (Ganesh Ghosh) and Auxiliary Force Armoury (Lokenath Baul), cut telegraph/telephone, dislocated rail. Failed to locate ammunition. Surya Sen hoisted National Flag, proclaimed Provisional Revolutionary Government. Retreated to Jalalabad hills; fierce battle 22 April — 80 British troops, 12 revolutionaries died. Villagers sheltered them 3 years. Surya Sen arrested 16 Feb 1933, hanged 12 Jan 1934. Major impact on Bengal youth — 1930-32 revolutionary revival.

hist_surya_sen.label: Surya Sen (Masterda)
hist_surya_sen.subject: history
