hist_surya_sen.detail: Leader of Chittagong Armoury Raid. National-school teacher ("Masterda"). Active in NCM 1920-22. Arrested 1926-28. Secretary of Chittagong District Congress 1929. Organiser of the April 1930 raid. Captured 16 Feb 1933, hanged 12 Jan 1934. Included Muslims (Sattar, Mir Ahmad) in his revolutionary cadre — rare departure from Bengal revolutionary Hindu religiosity.

hist_pritilata_waddedar.label: Pritilata Waddedar
hist_pritilata_waddedar.subject: history
hist_pritilata_waddedar.detail: Female revolutionary in Surya Sen's Chittagong group. Led 24 September 1932 raid on Pahartali European Club (sign: "Dogs and Indians not allowed"). Injured during escape; swallowed potassium cyanide to avoid capture. Among the first female martyrs of India's armed struggle.

hist_kalpana_dutt.label: Kalpana Dutt (Joshi)
hist_kalpana_dutt.subject: history
hist_kalpana_dutt.detail: Female revolutionary, Chittagong group under Surya Sen. Arrested and tried alongside Surya Sen, sentenced to transportation for life. Released 1939. Later joined CPI, married P.C. Joshi.

hist_santi_suniti_shot_dm_1931.label: Santi Ghosh & Suniti Chowdhury Shoot DM (Dec 1931)
hist_santi_suniti_shot_dm_1931.subject: history
hist_santi_suniti_shot_dm_1931.detail: 14 December 1931 — two Comilla schoolgirls, Santi Ghosh (14) and Suniti Chowdhury (14), shot and killed District Magistrate C.G.B. Stevens at Comilla. Both imprisoned rather than hanged (juvenile). Emblematic of young women in Bengal revolutionary movement's new phase 1930-32.

hist_bina_das.label: Bina Das Fires at Governor (Feb 1932)
hist_bina_das.subject: history
hist_bina_das.detail: 6 February 1932 — Bina Das fired her pistol at Stanley Jackson, Governor of Bengal, at Calcutta University Convocation. Missed. Sentenced to 9 years rigorous imprisonment. Released 1939. Later participated in Quit India 1942.

hist_death_chandrashekhar_azad.label: Death of Chandrashekhar Azad (Feb 1931)
hist_death_chandrashekhar_azad.subject: history
hist_death_chandrashekhar_azad.detail: 27 February 1931 — at Alfred Park, Allahabad, surrounded by police after a tip-off. After exchange of fire, Azad reportedly shot himself to fulfill his pledge to never be captured alive. Marked the practical end of the HSRA revolutionary phase in North India.

hist_madras_session_1927.label: Madras Congress Session (Dec 1927)
hist_madras_session_1927.subject: history
hist_madras_session_1927.detail: Annual INC session December 1927. Resolved to boycott Simon Commission. Jawaharlal Nehru moved a snap resolution declaring Purna Swaraj (complete independence) as the goal — passed in heated atmosphere. Gandhi in Young India 12 Jan 1928 urged action, not just resolutions.

hist_simon_boycott_landing.label: Simon Commission Landing Protests (Feb 1928)
hist_simon_boycott_landing.subject: history
hist_simon_boycott_landing.detail: 3 February 1928 — Simon Commission landed Bombay; nationwide hartal, "Go Back Simon" demonstrations with black flags in Calcutta, Lahore, Lucknow, Vijayawada, Poona. Firing in Madras killed one. T. Prakasam bared his chest before armed police. Innovative protests: kite-and-balloon slogans in Lucknow, lorry-alongside-train in Poona. Lathi charges on Nehru and Govind Ballabh Pant in Lucknow. Fatal attack on Lajpat Rai at Lahore 30 Oct 1928.

hist_all_parties_conference_1928.label: All-Parties Conference (1928)
hist_all_parties_conference_1928.subject: history
hist_all_parties_conference_1928.detail: Series of meetings Feb, May, August 1928 — Indian response to Lord Birkenhead's challenge to produce an agreed constitutional scheme. Drafted the Nehru Report under Motilal Nehru as principal author. Rejected separate electorates (kept reservation for Muslim minorities in provinces where they were a minority). Proposed Dominion Status, universal adult suffrage, equal rights for women, dissociation of state from religion.

hist_jinnah_fourteen_points_1929.label: Jinnah's Fourteen Points (Mar 1929)
hist_jinnah_fourteen_points_1929.subject: history
hist_jinnah_fourteen_points_1929.detail: March 1929 — Muhammad Ali Jinnah's response to the Nehru Report's rejection of separate electorates in Muslim-majority provinces. Fourteen demands reiterating separate Muslim electorates, one-third representation in Central Legislature, residuary powers to provinces, federal system with autonomous provinces, separation of Sind from Bombay, full religious liberty, constitutional reforms requiring Muslim consent. Marked Jinnah's shift from "ambassador of Hindu-Muslim unity" to explicit communal politics.

hist_irwin_declaration_1929.label: Irwin Declaration (Oct 1929)
hist_irwin_declaration_1929.subject: history
hist_irwin_declaration_1929.detail: 31 October 1929 — Viceroy Lord Irwin, after consultations with Labour PM Ramsay MacDonald, announced that Dominion Status was the "natural issue of India's progress" implicit in the 1917 Declaration. Promised a Round Table Conference after Simon submitted its report. Response: Delhi Manifesto (Nov 1929) demanded RTC be to formulate scheme for Dominion Status, not whether. Failed negotiations with Gandhi 23 Dec 1929 preceded Lahore Congress and Purna Swaraj.

hist_delhi_manifesto_1929.label: Delhi Manifesto (Nov 1929)
hist_delhi_manifesto_1929.subject: history
hist_delhi_manifesto_1929.detail: Nov 1929 — issued by Gandhi, Motilal Nehru, Jinnah, Patel, Sapru and others after Irwin Declaration. Demanded that purpose of Round Table Conference be to frame a Dominion Status constitution, not whether/when to grant it. Also demanded amnesty for political prisoners and predominant Congress representation at the RTC. Rejected by British 5 Nov 1929 House of Lords debate; Irwin told Gandhi on 23 Dec 1929 he could not give the assurance.

hist_independence_day_pledge.label: Independence Day Pledge (26 Jan 1930)
hist_independence_day_pledge.subject: history
hist_independence_day_pledge.detail: 26 January 1930 — first Independence Day, observed simultaneously across Indian villages and towns. Pledge read out in local languages at public meetings; tricolour hoisted. The pledge text (drafted by Gandhi) indicted British rule on political, economic, cultural and spiritual grounds, and committed to non-violent civil disobedience for Poorna Swaraj. Established 26 January as Republic Day of the future Republic of India.

hist_eleven_point_ultimatum.label: Gandhi's Eleven-Point Ultimatum (Jan 1930)
hist_eleven_point_ultimatum.subject: history
hist_eleven_point_ultimatum.detail: 31 January 1930 — Gandhi's 11-point demand sent to Viceroy Irwin before launching CDM. Included: total prohibition, reduction of rupee-sterling ratio, 50% cut in land revenue, abolition of salt tax, halving of military expenditure and civil services salaries, protective tariff for textiles, reservation of coastal shipping for Indians, release of political prisoners except those on violence charges, abolition of CID, arms licenses for self-defence. Ignored by Irwin — led to Salt March.

hist_dharasana_salt_raid.label: Dharasana Salt Raid (May 1930)
hist_dharasana_salt_raid.subject: history
hist_dharasana_salt_raid.detail: 21 May 1930 — 2,000 Satyagrahis led by Sarojini Naidu (first Indian woman Congress president), Imam Saheb (Gandhi's South African comrade), and Manilal Gandhi (Gandhi's son) marched on Dharasana Salt Works. Police rushed with steel-tipped lathis; non-resisting volunteers fell one after another, 320 injured and 2 dead by 11 am. American journalist Webb Miller's report carried image of non-violent heroism worldwide.

hist_sarojini_naidu.label: Sarojini Naidu
hist_sarojini_naidu.subject: history
hist_sarojini_naidu.detail: "Nightingale of India". Poet and orator. President of Indian National Congress 1925 (Kanpur) — first Indian woman Congress president. Led Dharasana Salt Satyagraha 21 May 1930. Jailed during CD and Quit India. Post-independence first woman Governor (United Provinces, 1947-1949).

hist_khudai_khidmatgars.label: Khudai Khidmatgars (Red Shirts)
hist_khudai_khidmatgars.subject: history
hist_khudai_khidmatgars.detail: Non-violent Pashtun movement founded by Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan in NWFP ~1929. "Servants of God" — members wore red shirts (Surkhposh). Played major role in CD 1930 — Peshawar uprising 23 April 1930 virtually held the city for a week. Garhwali Rifles troops refused to fire on the unarmed Khudai Khidmatgar crowd. Faced ferocious colonial repression through 1931-32. Ghaffar Khan's mass organisation was non-violent, Gandhian, and Pashtun-national in inspiration.

hist_garhwali_refusal_1930.label: Garhwali Rifles Refuse to Fire on Peshawar Crowd (April 1930)
hist_garhwali_refusal_1930.subject: history
hist_garhwali_refusal_1930.detail: 23-24 April 1930 — during the mass upsurge in Peshawar after arrest of Khudai Khidmatgar leaders, Garhwali Regiment soldiers (Chandra Singh Garhwali led) refused to fire on the unarmed crowd. Unprecedented mutinous act. Court-martialled; Chandra Singh Garhwali and others sentenced to long imprisonment. Symbolic blow to British confidence in Indian troops.

hist_first_rtc_1930.label: First Round Table Conference (Nov 1930-Jan 1931)
hist_first_rtc_1930.subject: history
hist_first_rtc_1930.detail: London, 12 Nov 1930 - 19 Jan 1931. Boycotted by Congress (all leaders in jail). Attended by Princes, Liberals (Sapru, Jayakar, Sastri), Muslim League (Jinnah, Aga Khan, Ali brothers), Hindu Mahasabha (Moonje), Sikhs, Christians, Parsis, Labour representatives, Justice Party (Madras). Princes accepted federal scheme. PM Ramsay MacDonald hinted Congress participation essential — led to Gandhi-Irwin Pact.

hist_no_rent_campaign_up_1930.label: No-Rent Campaign in UP (1930-31)
hist_no_rent_campaign_up_1930.subject: history
hist_no_rent_campaign_up_1930.detail: October-December 1930 — Jawaharlal Nehru got UP Congress Committee to sanction no-rent/no-revenue campaign. Zamindars (loyalists) refused to pay revenue; tenants refused rent. Active in Agra and Rae Bareli. Severe government repression drove peasants into flight. Continued into Jan 1931.

hist_chowkidara_tax_refusal.label: Chowkidara Tax Refusal Movement (Bihar 1930)
hist_chowkidara_tax_refusal.subject: history
hist_chowkidara_tax_refusal.detail: May 1930 onwards — Bihar's contribution to CD since it was land-locked (no salt satyagraha possible). Villagers refused the chowkidara tax (funding rural guards who acted as government spies and zamindari retainers). Chowkidars induced to resign. Centres: Monghyr, Saran, Bhagalpur districts. Bihpur occupation of Congress ashram became flashpoint. Rajendra Prasad injured in lathi charge.

hist_karachi_session_1931.label: Karachi Congress Session (March 1931)
hist_karachi_session_1931.subject: history
hist_karachi_session_1931.detail: 29 March 1931 at Karachi — endorsed Gandhi-Irwin Pact, reiterated Poorna Swaraj goal. Held six days after hanging of Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev, Rajguru; black flag demonstrations greeted Gandhi. Passed two landmark resolutions drafted by Gandhi and Nehru: (1) Resolution on Fundamental Rights, and (2) Resolution on National Economic Programme. These remained the basic political-economic programme of Congress.

hist_karachi_fundamental_rights.label: Karachi Resolution on Fundamental Rights (1931)
hist_karachi_fundamental_rights.subject: history
hist_karachi_fundamental_rights.detail: Drafted by Nehru, passed at Karachi 1931. First time Congress defined what Swaraj meant for the masses. Guaranteed: free speech/press/assembly/association, equality before law regardless of caste/creed/sex, state neutrality in religion, universal adult franchise, free compulsory primary education. Economic: substantial reduction of rent and revenue, living wage for workers, limited hours, right to unionise, state ownership/control of key industries, mines, transport. Basis of later Indian Constitution's Fundamental Rights and Directive Principles.

hist_second_rtc_1931.label: Second Round Table Conference (Sept-Dec 1931)
hist_second_rtc_1931.subject: history
hist_second_rtc_1931.detail: Gandhi as sole Congress representative, sailed 29 August 1931. "Chchello Katoro Jer" (drink this last cup of poison). Hand-picked Indian delegates mostly loyalists, communalists, landlords and princes used by Government to neutralise Gandhi. Winston Churchill opposed negotiating with "seditious fakir". No concessions made. Irwin replaced by Willingdon; Samuel Hoare became Secretary of State. Gandhi returned 28 Dec 1931 empty-handed; CD resumed 4 Jan 1932.

hist_cd_round2.label: Civil Disobedience Round 2 (1932-34)
hist_cd_round2.subject: history
hist_cd_round2.detail: 4 Jan 1932 — government pre-emptive crackdown: Gandhi arrested, ordinances imposing "Civil Martial Law". Congress and allied orgs declared illegal, ashrams seized, peaceful picketers beaten, property confiscated. Over 80,000 Satyagrahis jailed in first four months. At Ras village, Gujarat, non-paying peasants were stripped and whipped publicly. Press action against 109 journalists and 98 presses. Crushed by mid-1932 (convictions fell from 80,000 to 3,047 by August). Formally withdrawn April 1934. Shattered faith in British rule.

hist_communal_award_1932.label: Communal Award (Aug 1932)
hist_communal_award_1932.subject: history
hist_communal_award_1932.detail: 16 August 1932 — British PM Ramsay MacDonald's award allotted separate electorates to Depressed Classes (Scheduled Castes), treating them as distinct minority community (alongside Muslims, Sikhs, Christians). Aimed to divide Hindus politically. Triggered Gandhi's epic fast 20 September 1932; resolved by Poona Pact. Congress opposed separate electorates but pragmatically accepted the rest as it was not willing to change the Award without minority consent.

hist_gandhi_epic_fast_1932.label: Gandhi's Epic Fast (Sept 1932)
hist_gandhi_epic_fast_1932.subject: history
hist_gandhi_epic_fast_1932.detail: 20 September 1932 — Gandhi's fast-unto-death in Yeravada Jail protesting separate electorates for Depressed Classes under Communal Award. "Untouchables remain untouchables in perpetuity" if separated. Massive emotional response — temples, wells thrown open to Depressed Classes across India. Tagore's telegram. Resolved 24 September by Poona Pact negotiated by Malaviya, M.C. Rajah, Ambedkar. Gandhi broke fast 26 September.

hist_harijan_sewak_sangh.label: Harijan Sewak Sangh (1932)
hist_harijan_sewak_sangh.subject: history
hist_harijan_sewak_sangh.detail: Founded September 1932 by Gandhi, with Ghanshyam Das Birla as president and Amritlal Thakkar as secretary, for anti-untouchability work. Gandhi renamed Depressed Classes as "Harijans" ("people of God"). Funds for uplift, temple-entry campaigns, Harijan education. Gandhi's 1933-34 Harijan Tour raised funds for the Sangh.

hist_harijan_tour_1933.label: Gandhi's Harijan Tour (1933-34)
hist_harijan_tour_1933.subject: history
hist_harijan_tour_1933.detail: November 7, 1933 to July 29, 1934 — Gandhi's nine-month "Harijan tour" starting from Wardha. Travelled 20,000+ km by train, car, bullock cart, foot. Collected funds for Harijan Sewak Sangh, propagated removal of untouchability, urged social workers to go to villages for Harijan uplift. Undertook two fasts (8 May, 16 Aug 1933). Attacked by orthodox — bomb thrown 25 June 1934 at Poona on a car believed to carry Gandhi. Temple Entry Bill defeated in Central Legislature Aug 1934.

hist_wardha_ashram.label: Satyagraha Ashram, Wardha
hist_wardha_ashram.subject: history
hist_wardha_ashram.detail: Gandhi's base from 1933 after abandoning Sabarmati Ashram (he vowed in 1930 not to return till Swaraj was won). Also called Sevagram from 1936. Hub of Harijan campaign, constructive programme, nationwide Gandhian network. Gandhi's principal residence until independence.

hist_poona_bomb_1934.label: Poona Bomb Attempt on Gandhi (June 1934)
hist_poona_bomb_1934.subject: history
hist_poona_bomb_1934.detail: 25 June 1934 — bomb thrown on a car believed to be carrying Gandhi during his Harijan tour at Poona; seven people injured but Gandhi unharmed. Orthodox Sanatani Hindus reportedly behind attack; opposed his anti-untouchability campaign. Orthodox accused him of "attacking Hinduism", burned his portraits, published scurrilous leaflets.

hist_temple_entry_bill_1934.label: Temple Entry Bill Defeated (Aug 1934)
hist_temple_entry_bill_1934.subject: history
hist_temple_entry_bill_1934.detail: August 1934 — private member's Temple Entry Bill defeated in Central Legislative Assembly. Orthodox Sanatani Hindus had offered the Government full support against Congress in exchange for blocking this bill — government obliged. Showed limits of Gandhi's anti-untouchability campaign in formal politics and how communalism could be deployed against nationalism.

hist_vanar_sena.label: Vanar Senas + Manjari Senas (1930-31)
hist_vanar_sena.subject: history
hist_vanar_sena.detail: "Monkey armies" — children organised in bands during CD 1930-31 for propaganda, protests, picketing. At one place, girls insisted on their own separate "Manjari Sena" (cat army). Indira Nehru (later Gandhi) led a Vanar Sena in Allahabad. Illustrates mass penetration of CD movement into even the youngest strata of society.

hist_second_cd_withdrawal_1934.label: Second CD Withdrawal (April 1934)
hist_second_cd_withdrawal_1934.subject: history
hist_second_cd_withdrawal_1934.detail: 7 April 1934 — Gandhi announced withdrawal of second Civil Disobedience Movement; Congress Working Committee endorsed. Shifted focus to constructive programme, Harijan work, and preparing for 1935 Act implementation. Critics (Bose, Vithalbhai Patel) called for new leader. Gandhi said "I have no sense of defeat in me... the nation has got energy of which you have no conception".

hist_cpi_founding_kanpur_1925.label: Communist Party of India (Kanpur 1925)
hist_cpi_founding_kanpur_1925.subject: history
hist_cpi_founding_kanpur_1925.detail: Several left-wing and communist groups came together at Kanpur in December 1925 and founded an all-India Communist Party of India (CPI). S.V. Ghate emerged as General Secretary. Called on all members to enroll in Congress, form a strong left-wing, and make the Congress "a more radical mass-based organization". Distinct from the earlier M.N. Roy-led Tashkent CPI (Oct 1920).

hist_tashkent_cpi_1920.label: Tashkent Communist Party of India (Oct 1920)
hist_tashkent_cpi_1920.subject: history
hist_tashkent_cpi_1920.detail: October 1920 — M.N. Roy and six other Indian revolutionaries in exile met at Tashkent and formed a Communist Party of India. Linked to the Communist International. M.N. Roy co-authored the Comintern's policy towards colonies with Lenin. Predecessor (though independent) of the Kanpur CPI 1925.

hist_mn_roy.label: M.N. Roy
hist_mn_roy.subject: history
hist_mn_roy.detail: Manabendra Nath Roy (1887-1954). Founding member of Mexican CP and of Tashkent CPI 1920. Co-formulated Comintern's colonial theses with Lenin. Expelled from Comintern 1929. Returned to India 1930, organised Royist group, then founded Radical Democratic Party (1940). Opposed Quit India, supported war effort against fascism. Later shifted to Radical Humanism.

hist_kanpur_bolshevik_case_1924.label: Kanpur Bolshevik Conspiracy Case (1924)
hist_kanpur_bolshevik_case_1924.subject: history
hist_kanpur_bolshevik_case_1924.detail: 1924 — government trial of early Communists S.A. Dange, Muzaffar Ahmed, Nalini Gupta and Shaukat Usmani for conspiring with Soviet Comintern to overthrow British rule. All four sentenced to four years imprisonment. First major colonial strike at the nascent communist movement (preceded the larger Meerut Conspiracy Case 1929).

hist_peshawar_conspiracy_cases.label: Peshawar Conspiracy Cases (1922-24)
hist_peshawar_conspiracy_cases.subject: history
hist_peshawar_conspiracy_cases.detail: 1922-24 — series of prosecutions against Indian revolutionaries ("Muhajirs") returning from Soviet Union and Comintern training at Tashkent Communist University of the Toilers of the East. Five trials, long prison sentences. Aimed to prevent Soviet-trained Communists from organising in India.

hist_dutt_bradley_thesis.label: Dutt-Bradley Thesis (1936)
hist_dutt_bradley_thesis.subject: history
hist_dutt_bradley_thesis.detail: Early 1936 — theoretical and political document by R.P. Dutt and Ben Bradley laying basis for Indian Communists' renewed engagement with Congress following Seventh Comintern Congress (Aug 1935). Held that National Congress could play "a great part and a foremost part in the work of realising the anti-imperialist people's front". Triggered CPI's abandonment of sectarian "bourgeois betrayal" line and re-entry into Congress.

hist_congress_socialist_party.label: Congress Socialist Party (Oct 1934)
hist_congress_socialist_party.subject: history
hist_congress_socialist_party.detail: Formed October 1934 at Bombay during AICC meeting. Leaders: Jayaprakash Narayan (General Secretary), Acharya Narendra Dev (President), Minoo Masani, Achyut Patwardhan, Ashok Mehta, Yusuf Meherally, Sampurnanand. Four propositions: nationalism was necessary stage toward socialism, socialists must work within Congress, they must give national movement a socialist direction, and must organise workers and peasants in class organisations. Played key role in Forward Bloc (1939) and later RSP.

hist_jayaprakash_narayan.label: Jayaprakash Narayan
hist_jayaprakash_narayan.subject: history
hist_jayaprakash_narayan.detail: Founding General Secretary of Congress Socialist Party (Oct 1934). Studied Marxism in the US. Jailed during CD 1932-34. Sensational escape from Hazaribagh jail with comrades in 1942 — went underground during Quit India, organising armed resistance. One of main leaders of 1942 underground. Post-independence: Bhoodan/Sarvodaya leader (1950s-60s), 1974 JP Movement against Indira Gandhi.

hist_acharya_narendra_dev.label: Acharya Narendra Dev
hist_acharya_narendra_dev.subject: history
hist_acharya_narendra_dev.detail: Founding President of Congress Socialist Party (1934). Sanskrit scholar and Buddhist. Principal of Kashi Vidyapith. Pragmatic Marxist; coined the socialist mantra of working within national mainstream: "It would be a suicidal policy for us to cut ourselves off from the national movement that the Congress undoubtedly represents."

hist_minoo_masani.label: Minoo Masani
hist_minoo_masani.subject: history
hist_minoo_masani.detail: Founding member of Congress Socialist Party 1934. Parsi liberal socialist, prolific writer (Our India, Our Growing Human Family). Jailed during CD and Quit India. Later drifted away from socialism; founded Swatantra Party 1959 with Rajaji as right-liberal opposition to Nehruvian socialism.

hist_forward_bloc_1939.label: Forward Bloc (1939)
hist_forward_bloc_1939.subject: history
hist_forward_bloc_1939.detail: Founded 3 May 1939 by Subhas Chandra Bose after he was forced to resign from Congress presidency (following Tripuri crisis). Left bloc within Congress pushing for uncompromising radicalism. Bose became Forward Bloc's first president. Later grew into independent party outside Congress; Bose's exit from India (Jan 1941) to organise INA left the Bloc under Indian leadership (R.S. Ruikar, Aruna Asaf Ali).

hist_whither_india.label: "Whither India?" (Nehru 1933)
hist_whither_india.subject: history
hist_whither_india.detail: October 1933 — Nehru's influential essay answering the question "Where is India headed?" Answered: "to the great human goal of social and economic equality, to the ending of all exploitation of nation by nation and class by class". Marked Nehru's explicit turn to socialism as the direction of the Indian independence struggle.

hist_lucknow_session_1936.label: Lucknow Congress Session (April 1936)
hist_lucknow_session_1936.subject: history
hist_lucknow_session_1936.detail: Nehru presided. Famous Presidential Address committed Congress to socialism: "I am convinced that the only key... lies in socialism... ending of private property... replacement of the profit system". Set tone for Left's attempt to redirect Congress strategy but also began "Struggle vs S-T-S" debate with Gandhian Right wing. Backed by Gandhi despite contrary pressure from C. Rajagopalachari.

hist_faizpur_session_1936.label: Faizpur Congress Session (Dec 1936)
hist_faizpur_session_1936.subject: history
hist_faizpur_session_1936.detail: Annual INC Dec 1936 — first Congress session held in a rural location (Faizpur, Maharashtra). Nehru presided again. Adopted detailed Agrarian Programme. Decision on office acceptance deferred to post-election period. Marked Congress's conscious reach into rural areas.

hist_national_planning_committee.label: National Planning Committee (1938)
hist_national_planning_committee.subject: history
hist_national_planning_committee.detail: Set up in 1938 by Subhas Bose during his Congress presidency (Haripura). Nehru chaired. Drew up plans for post-independence industrialisation and social reconstruction. Included industrialists, scientists, economists. Basis of later Planning Commission (1950). Reflected Left's influence on Congress.

hist_aispc_1936.label: All India States Peoples Conference (Founded 1927; Bombay 1936)
hist_aispc_1936.subject: history
hist_aispc_1936.detail: Founded December 1927 at Bombay to coordinate nationalism in princely states. Reactivated in mid-1930s as major mass organ in states. Nehru presided over Ludhiana session 1939. Led struggles for democratic reforms and accession to independent India. Integrated Indian states' peoples movements with national freedom movement.

hist_aisf_1936.label: All India Students' Federation (1936)
hist_aisf_1936.subject: history
hist_aisf_1936.detail: Founded 12 August 1936 at Lucknow under Nehru's inspiration. First all-India student body spanning the anti-imperialist movement. Led by M.L. Shah. Active in anti-Simon, anti-imperialist agitation, Quit India. Split in 1939 between Left wing (later AISF-CPI affiliated) and Right wing.

hist_progressive_writers_1936.label: All India Progressive Writers' Association (April 1936)
hist_progressive_writers_1936.subject: history
hist_progressive_writers_1936.detail: Founded 9-10 April 1936 at Lucknow. First president: Munshi Premchand. Mulk Raj Anand, Sajjad Zaheer, Ahmed Ali and others were founders. Manifesto drafted in London at Nanking Hotel 1935. Aimed at literature committed to social realism, opposing imperialism and feudalism. Published Urdu-Hindi-English writings. Major force in politicising Indian literature. PWA affiliation overlapped with IPTA and CPI.

hist_swami_sahajanand.label: Swami Sahajanand Saraswati
hist_swami_sahajanand.subject: history
hist_swami_sahajanand.detail: Founding president of All India Kisan Sabha (Lucknow 1936). Bihari saint-revolutionary. Organised Bihar peasantry against zamindari oppression. Wrote extensively on agrarian economics. Aligned with Left. Independent of Congress wings; brought peasant mass politics into the national movement.

hist_ng_ranga.label: Professor N.G. Ranga
hist_ng_ranga.subject: history
hist_ng_ranga.detail: Gogineni Ranga Nayukulu (1900-1995). Peasant leader from Andhra. Co-organiser of All India Kisan Sabha (Lucknow 1936) with Sahajanand. Founding General Secretary. Oxford-educated economist, parliamentarian, prolific writer on agrarian economics. Post-independence: founded Swatantra Party with Rajaji (1959).

hist_1934_legislature_election.label: 1934 Central Legislative Assembly Elections
hist_1934_legislature_election.subject: history
hist_1934_legislature_election.detail: November 1934 — first elections after CD withdrawal. Congress (reverting to Swarajist line under Ansari, Asaf Ali, Satyamurthy, Bhulabhai Desai, B.C. Roy, Rajagopalachari) captured 45 of 75 elected Indian seats in the Central Legislative Assembly. Viceroy Willingdon called it "singularly unfortunate; a great triumph for little Gandhi". Revived Congress-in-legislature as wing of anti-imperialist strategy.

hist_sts_strategy.label: Struggle-Truce-Struggle (S-T-S') Strategy
hist_sts_strategy.subject: history
hist_sts_strategy.detail: Gandhian strategic framework articulated 1934-37. Phases of mass movement alternate with phases of truce/constructive work/constitutional work. Movement phases confront colonial authority; non-confrontational phases work concessions, build cadres, politicise masses. Spirals upward till power transfer. Opposed by Nehru's Struggle-Victory (S-V) alternative of permanent confrontation. S-T-S' was Congress's operating strategy through 1947.

hist_1937_provincial_elections.label: 1937 Provincial Elections
hist_1937_provincial_elections.subject: history
hist_1937_provincial_elections.detail: February 1937 — first elections under Government of India Act 1935 provincial autonomy. Nehru led historic 80,000-km campaign tour addressing 10+ million people. Congress won 716 of 1,161 seats contested. Majority in six provinces: Madras, Bombay, Central Provinces, Orissa, Bihar, UP. Plurality but not majority in Bengal, Assam, NWFP. Massive rejection of 1935 Act's federal side. Prestige of Congress as alternative state soared.

hist_office_acceptance_debate.label: Office Acceptance Debate (1936-37)
hist_office_acceptance_debate.subject: history
hist_office_acceptance_debate.detail: 1936-37 Congress internal debate on whether to form ministries under 1935 Act after election victory. Nehru, Bose, CSP, Communists opposed — called it surrender, co-option. Right wing (Patel, Rajendra Prasad, Rajagopalachari) favoured acceptance as tactical use of colonial framework. Gandhi initially reluctant, warmed up by early 1936. Working Committee ultimately accepted July 1937. Congress formed ministries in 6+2 provinces.

hist_congress_ministries_1937.label: Congress Ministries (July 1937 - Oct 1939)
hist_congress_ministries_1937.subject: history
hist_congress_ministries_1937.detail: Formed July 1937 in Madras, Bombay, CP, Orissa, Bihar, UP; later NWFP and Assam. Lasted 28 months till resignation in October 1939 (over WWII declaration without consultation). Parliamentary Sub-Committee (Patel, Maulana Azad, Rajendra Prasad) coordinated. Ministers reduced own salaries Rs 2000→500. Restored civil liberties, repealed emergency laws, released prisoners, ended press restrictions. Major achievements in agrarian reform, Harijan uplift, prohibition, education.

hist_parliamentary_subcommittee.label: Parliamentary Sub-Committee (1937)
hist_parliamentary_subcommittee.subject: history
hist_parliamentary_subcommittee.detail: Central control board formed by CWC July 1937 to coordinate Congress provincial ministries and prevent British strategy of "provincializing" the Congress. Members: Sardar Patel, Maulana Abul Kalam Azad, Rajendra Prasad. Ensured Congress Ministries remained answerable to the all-India Working Committee, not to provincial legislatures alone.

hist_congress_election_manifesto_1936.label: Congress Election Manifesto (1936)
hist_congress_election_manifesto_1936.subject: history
hist_congress_election_manifesto_1936.detail: Issued 1936 ahead of 1937 elections. Reaffirmed total rejection of 1935 Act. Promised: restoration of civil liberties, release of political prisoners, removal of disabilities on sex and untouchability, radical agrarian transformation, substantial rent/revenue reduction, rural debt scaling-down, cheap credit, right to form trade unions and strike. Left imprint on manifesto reflected in pro-worker/pro-peasant programme.

hist_cpi_ban_1934.label: CPI Banned (July 1934)
hist_cpi_ban_1934.subject: history
hist_cpi_ban_1934.detail: July 1934 — Government of India declared the Communist Party of India illegal under the Criminal Law Amendment Act. Followed the Meerut Conspiracy Case convictions and CPI's sectarian post-1928 turn. Ban remained during Congress Provincial Ministry era (1937-39) since it was a Central Government order; Congress provinces could not lift it but allowed CPI members to function openly. Legalised only in 1942 (during war alliance with USSR).

hist_independence_india_league_1928.label: Independence for India League (1928)
hist_independence_india_league_1928.subject: history
hist_independence_india_league_1928.detail: Founded 1928 by Jawaharlal Nehru and Subhas Bose — pressed for complete independence and "a socialist revision of the economic structure of society". Worked within Congress. Helped build momentum toward 1929 Lahore Purna Swaraj resolution. Forerunner of later Left consolidation in Congress.

hist_all_india_kisan_sabha.label: All India Kisan Sabha (April 1936)
hist_all_india_kisan_sabha.subject: history
hist_all_india_kisan_sabha.detail: Originally founded as All-India Kisan Congress at Lucknow April 1936, later renamed AIKS. President: Swami Sahajanand Saraswati (founder of Bihar Provincial Kisan Sabha 1929). General Secretary: N.G. Ranga. Adopted Kisan Manifesto which influenced Congress Faizpur Programme 1936. Zamindari abolition slogan adopted 1935. Key leaders: Ram Manohar Lohia, Sohan Singh Josh, Indulal Yagnik, Jayaprakash Narayan. CPI-aligned after 1935 led to split in 1943 (over People's War line).

hist_bihar_provincial_kisan_sabha.label: Bihar Provincial Kisan Sabha (1929)
hist_bihar_provincial_kisan_sabha.subject: history
hist_bihar_provincial_kisan_sabha.detail: Founded 1929 by Swami Sahajanand Saraswati. First organised peasant body in Bihar. Focus: zamindari abolition, Bakasht lands restoration, end illegal levies. Led major Bakasht land struggles 1938-39. Key leaders: Karyanand Sharma, Rahul Sankritayan, Yadunandan Sharma, Panchanan Sharma. Precursor of AIKS (1936).

hist_bakasht_lands_struggle.label: Bakasht Lands Struggle (Bihar 1938-39)
hist_bakasht_lands_struggle.subject: history
hist_bakasht_lands_struggle.detail: Bakasht lands = tenant lands lost to zamindars during Depression 1929-32 for non-payment, cultivated as share-croppers. Major flashpoint 1938-39 between Bihar Provincial Kisan Sabha and Congress Ministry. Yadunandan Sharma won 850/1000 bighas back at Reora, Gaya; Karyanand Sharma led Barahiya-tal Monghyr struggle; Jamuna Karjee Saran; Rahul Sankritayan Annawari. August 1939: ~600 activists arrested. Struggle continued till zamindari abolition.

hist_tebhaga_movement.label: Tebhaga Movement (Bengal 1946-47)
hist_tebhaga_movement.subject: history
hist_tebhaga_movement.detail: Late 1946 — Bengal share-croppers (bargadars) demanded tebhaga (two-thirds share) of crop instead of half paid to jotedars; crops to be stored in bargadar khamars. Led by Bengal Provincial Kisan Sabha. Floud Commission had already recommended this. Boosted by Muslim League Suhrawardy Ministry's Bargadars Temporary Regulation Bill (Jan 22, 1947) but the Bill was not pursued. Major clashes, 20 peasants killed at Khanpur. Crushed by Feb 1947. Finally addressed by Congress's Bargadars Act 1950. Centres: Dinajpur, Rangpur, Jalpaiguri, Mymensingh, Midnapore, 24-Parganas. Rajbansi Kshatriya base; spread to Muslims, Hajongs, Santhals, Oraons.

hist_punnapra_vayalar.label: Punnapra-Vayalar Uprising (Oct 1946)
hist_punnapra_vayalar.subject: history
hist_punnapra_vayalar.detail: October 1946 — workers and peasants uprising in coir industry regions of Punnapra and Vayalar, Travancore State. Communist-led. Rose against Dewan Sir C.P. Ramaswamy Aiyar's proposed "American Model" plan for Travancore independence + labour repression. Police shot at workers in Punnapra (22 Oct); Vayalar workers followed (27 Oct). Thousands killed by Travancore State forces. Contributed to Travancore eventually acceding to Indian Union.

hist_telangana_rebellion.label: Telangana Rebellion (1946-51)
hist_telangana_rebellion.subject: history
hist_telangana_rebellion.detail: July 1946 — Communist-led peasant uprising in Telangana districts of Hyderabad State against Nizam's rule and feudal landlords (doras), bonded labour (vetti), and forced food procurement. Armed struggle in 4,000 villages; redistributed land, abolished vetti, set up peasant committees. Continued resisting Nizam's Razakars. Indian Army's Hyderabad Police Action (Sept 1948) merged struggle against Nizam with Indian integration. CPI called off armed struggle 1951.

hist_bengal_famine_1943.label: Bengal Famine (1943)
hist_bengal_famine_1943.subject: history
hist_bengal_famine_1943.detail: Great Bengal Famine of 1943 killed 2-3 million through starvation, disease and malnutrition. Caused by wartime rice hoarding, Burma rice imports stopping, scorched-earth policy, British diversion of food to war effort, boat-denial policy, and Churchill's refusal to divert Commonwealth shipping. Massive relief work by Kisan Sabha and Communist rank-and-file. Major political scar for last years of British rule. Amartya Sen's "Poverty and Famines" (1981) analysed it as an entitlement failure.

hist_praja_mandals.label: Praja Mandals (States Peoples Conferences)
hist_praja_mandals.subject: history
hist_praja_mandals.detail: States Peoples Conferences/Associations in princely states modelled on the INC. Emerged after 1920 Non-Cooperation impact. Examples: Mysore, Hyderabad, Baroda, Kathiawad States, Deccan States, Jamnagar, Indore, Nawanagar. Culminated in All India States People's Conference December 1927. Demanded responsible government, civil liberties, abolition of feudal levies in states. Nehru presided over Ludhiana AISPC 1939.

hist_rajkot_satyagraha.label: Rajkot Satyagraha (1938-39)
hist_rajkot_satyagraha.subject: history
hist_rajkot_satyagraha.detail: Rajkot (Kathiawad) — protest against Thakore Dharmendrasinhji's misrule and Dewan Virawala's monopolies (on matches, sugar, rice, cinema licences). Lapse of Praja Pratinidhi Sabha and increased taxes provoked mass agitation. Gandhi's personal intervention — his birthplace. Kasturba Gandhi was arrested. Chief Justice Maurice Gwyer arbitrated but Virawala reneged. Became national issue showing Gandhi's direct engagement with princely state politics.

hist_hyderabad_state_congress.label: Hyderabad State Congress (1938)
hist_hyderabad_state_congress.subject: history
hist_hyderabad_state_congress.detail: Founded 1938 — demanded responsible government in Hyderabad under Nizam Osman Ali Khan. Banned soon after. Leaders like Swami Ramananda Tirtha, Govindbhai Shroff led movement. Majlis-e-Ittehadul Muslimeen (formed 1927) grew into Razakars under Qasim Razvi, organized communal violence against Hindus + anti-integration. Hyderabad refused accession in 1947; Operation Polo (Indian Police Action, 13-17 Sept 1948) integrated the state.

hist_kashmir_quit_kashmir.label: Quit Kashmir Movement (May 1946)
hist_kashmir_quit_kashmir.subject: history
hist_kashmir_quit_kashmir.detail: May 1946 — Sheikh Abdullah's National Conference (renamed from Muslim Conference 1939) launched "Quit Kashmir" against Maharaja Hari Singh, inspired by Congress's Quit India. Sheikh Abdullah arrested. Nehru tried to go to Srinagar to defend him, was arrested at border. Shaped the drama of Kashmir accession in Oct 1947 when Pakistani tribal invasion forced Maharaja to sign Instrument of Accession.

hist_sheikh_abdullah.label: Sheikh Mohammad Abdullah
hist_sheikh_abdullah.subject: history
hist_sheikh_abdullah.detail: "Sher-e-Kashmir". Founded All Jammu and Kashmir Muslim Conference 1932 against Maharaja Hari Singh's autocracy; renamed National Conference 1939 to widen base. Led Quit Kashmir 1946. Friend of Nehru. Became first PM of Jammu & Kashmir (Oct 1947); later deposed (1953) and jailed for decades.

hist_ficci.label: FICCI — Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce & Industry (1927)
hist_ficci.subject: history
hist_ficci.detail: Founded 1927 by G.D. Birla, Purshottamdas Thakurdas and others as national apex of Indian commercial/industrial/financial interests. Saw itself as "national guardians of trade, commerce and industry" performing in the economic sphere what a national government would. Consistently supported Congress (not Liberal Party); boycotted First RTC 1930; pushed for tariff protection, lower sterling ratio, economic autonomy. Later drafted Bombay Plan 1944.

hist_gd_birla.label: Ghanshyam Das Birla
hist_gd_birla.subject: history
hist_gd_birla.detail: Industrialist, Marwari. Co-founder of FICCI (1927). Financial supporter of Congress and Gandhi (Sevagram Ashram built on land he provided). Pushed capitalist support for nationalism while ideologically opposing communism. Negotiated Congress-British compromises in 1930s-40s. Signatory of Bombay Plan 1944. Founder of House of Birla (Hindustan Motors, Grasim, Birla Brothers).

hist_purshottamdas_thakurdas.label: Purshottamdas Thakurdas
hist_purshottamdas_thakurdas.subject: history
hist_purshottamdas_thakurdas.detail: Cotton merchant and financier. Co-founder of FICCI (first President 1927-28). Central architect of Indian capitalist class's political strategy. Co-signatory of Bombay Plan 1944. Moderate but consistent Indian nationalist; rejected Public Safety Bill 1928. Influenced Gandhi-Irwin negotiations 1931.

hist_jrd_tata.label: J.R.D. Tata
hist_jrd_tata.subject: history
hist_jrd_tata.detail: Jehangir Ratanji Dadabhoy Tata. Chairman of Tata Sons 1938-1988. First licensed pilot of India 1929, founded Tata Airlines (1932) → Air India. Signatory of Bombay Plan 1944. Modernising industrialist. Aug 1942 — co-signed with Purshottamdas and Birla letter to Viceroy urging political freedom as only solution before Quit India.

hist_league_against_imperialism.label: League Against Imperialism (Feb 1927)
hist_league_against_imperialism.subject: history
hist_league_against_imperialism.detail: Founded February 1927 at Brussels — anti-colonial international. Congress affiliated as associated member; Nehru elected to Executive Council. Other honorary presidents: Albert Einstein, Romain Rolland, Madame Sun Yat-Sen, George Lansbury. Marked Congress's foreign-policy framework of solidarity with anti-colonial struggles worldwide. Nehru's exposure here shaped his anti-imperialist internationalism.

hist_congress_foreign_dept.label: Congress Foreign Department (1927)
hist_congress_foreign_dept.subject: history
hist_congress_foreign_dept.detail: Opened at INC Calcutta session December 1927 after Nehru's Brussels participation. Developed contacts with foreign anti-imperialist movements. Precursor of Ministry of External Affairs. Built relationships with Ireland, Egypt, China, Burma, Palestine, Soviet Union.

hist_dr_kotnis.label: Dr Dwarkanath Kotnis
hist_dr_kotnis.subject: history
hist_dr_kotnis.detail: Member of Congress medical mission to China (sent 1938 under Dr. M. Atal). Worked with Eighth Route Army under Mao Zedong's command against Japanese invasion. Married Chinese nurse Guo Qinglan. Died 1942 in China. Symbol of India-China anti-imperialist solidarity. V. Shantaram's film "Dr Kotnis Ki Amar Kahani" (1946) popularised his story.

hist_china_day.label: China Day (June 12) + Ethiopia Day (May 9)
hist_china_day.subject: history
hist_china_day.detail: Congress-observed anti-fascist solidarity days: 9 May 1936 as Ethiopia Day (Italian fascist invasion of Ethiopia 1935); 27 September 1936 as Palestine Day (Arab-Jewish British-mandate crisis); 12 June 1938 as China Day (Japanese invasion of China 1937). Pan-colonial solidarity hallmark of Congress foreign policy 1936-39 under Nehru.

hist_spanish_civil_war_support.label: Indian Support for Spanish Republic (1936-39)
hist_spanish_civil_war_support.subject: history
hist_spanish_civil_war_support.detail: Congress strongly supported Spanish Republican government against Franco/fascism. Faizpur Congress Dec 1936 (Nehru presidential address): "our battles are being fought (in Spain)". Nehru with V.K. Krishna Menon visited Republican Spain June 1938, spent 5 days in bombed Barcelona. Gandhi sent message to Juan Negrin. First Indian engagement with European anti-fascist war.

hist_haripura_session_1938.label: Haripura Congress Session (Feb 1938)
hist_haripura_session_1938.subject: history
hist_haripura_session_1938.detail: Feb 1938 — Subhas Chandra Bose elected Congress President for first time. Bose proposed resolution condemning Japanese aggression in China, British approach in Palestine, fascist attacks on Ethiopia/Spain/Czechoslovakia. Set up National Planning Committee under Nehru. Famous "Haripura Panels" by Nandalal Bose — Santiniketan school paintings of Indian rural life for session decor.

hist_tripuri_crisis_1939.label: Tripuri Crisis (March 1939)
hist_tripuri_crisis_1939.subject: history
hist_tripuri_crisis_1939.detail: March 1939 at Tripuri Congress — Subhas Bose re-elected President defeating Gandhi's candidate Pattabhi Sitaramayya (1580 vs 1377). Gandhi called it "my defeat". But at Tripuri session, G.B. Pant's resolution (backed by Gandhi) effectively curtailed Bose's powers by requiring him to run the Working Committee as per Gandhi's wishes. Socialists refused to back Bose; CSP abstained. Bose resigned April 1939, founded Forward Bloc 3 May 1939. Key rupture in the Left-Right dynamic.

hist_vk_krishna_menon.label: V.K. Krishna Menon
hist_vk_krishna_menon.subject: history
hist_vk_krishna_menon.detail: Kerala-born intellectual, lawyer, Marxist. Secretary of India League London from 1930. Key propagandist of Indian independence in Britain. Edited Pelican Books. Close friend of Nehru; accompanied Nehru to Republican Spain June 1938. Post-independence: Defence Minister (1957-62), resigned after 1962 India-China war.

hist_munich_agreement.label: Munich Agreement & Congress Response (Sept 1938)
hist_munich_agreement.subject: history
hist_munich_agreement.detail: 29-30 September 1938 — Britain and France abandoned Czechoslovakia to Nazi Germany. CWC (in Nehru's absence) passed resolution of grave concern. Gandhi in Harijan: "working committee wrung itself with pain while their doom was being decided". Nehru (then in Europe) refused to visit Germany as state guest, went to Prague instead. Called Munich "the rape of Czechoslovakia with England and France holding her forcibly down". At Tripuri 1939, Congress officially dissociated from British foreign policy. Triggered Congress's anti-fascist + anti-imperialist stance before WWII.

hist_communalism_definition.label: Communalism (Definition & Three Stages)
hist_communalism_definition.subject: history
hist_communalism_definition.detail: Bipin Chandra's analytical framework: Communal ideology has three stages. (1) Belief that people following the same religion have common secular (political/economic/social) interests; (2) Belief that their interests differ from those of other religious communities; (3) Belief that their interests are mutually hostile and antagonistic. Each stage leads to the next unless actively countered. Jinnah's trajectory from "Ambassador of Hindu-Muslim Unity" to Pakistan demand illustrates this sliding logic.

hist_extreme_communalism_1937.label: Extreme Communalism (1937 onwards)
hist_extreme_communalism_1937.subject: history
hist_extreme_communalism_1937.detail: Post-1937 fascist-style phase of communalism. Motifs of domination/suppression/extermination became mainstream propaganda. Fear-and-hatred based; targeted co-religionists among nationalists. Mass-mobilizing unlike earlier elite/liberal phase. Drivers: Congress 1937 electoral dominance pushed landlords/zamindars to communal parties; Congress 1937 expelled communalists from its membership; fascist mass-politics model became available. WWII (Sept 1939) allowed colonial rulers to recognise League as sole spokesperson for Muslims.

hist_muslim_mass_contact.label: Muslim Mass Contact Programme (1937)
hist_muslim_mass_contact.subject: history
hist_muslim_mass_contact.detail: Launched by Nehru and the Congress in 1937 after the party's huge election victory. Aimed to take Congress's secular nationalist programme directly to Muslim masses, bypassing Muslim League. Alarmed Jinnah and accelerated League's shift to extreme communalism and separatism. Programme itself was undermined by WWII and Congress ministries' resignation Oct 1939.

hist_muslim_league_revival_1936.label: Muslim League Revival under Jinnah (1936)
hist_muslim_league_revival_1936.subject: history
hist_muslim_league_revival_1936.detail: Jinnah returned from London 1935 and revived the moribund Muslim League. Initially attempted liberal-communal line — stressed Indian nationalism and Hindu-Muslim cooperation. League fought 1937 elections on semi-nationalist Congress-type programme (only Muslim demands: Urdu/script protection, amelioration of Muslim conditions). Won only 109 of 482 reserved Muslim seats (4.8% of Muslim vote). Post-defeat pivot to mass communal politics.

hist_hindu_mahasabha.label: Hindu Mahasabha
hist_hindu_mahasabha.subject: history
hist_hindu_mahasabha.detail: Founded 1915 by Madan Mohan Malaviya and Lala Lajpat Rai at Haridwar; revived 1923. Key liberal-communal Hindu platform in 1920s. Fared poorly in 1937 elections. Under V.D. Savarkar's presidency (1937-42), shifted to fascist-style extreme communalism — "Hindus are already reduced to veritable helots throughout our land". Key arena for Hindu communal politics in 1930s-40s.

hist_hindutva_1923.label: Hindutva (Savarkar, 1923)
hist_hindutva_1923.subject: history
hist_hindutva_1923.detail: Concept articulated by V.D. Savarkar in his 1923 book "Essentials of Hindutva" (later published as "Hindutva: Who is a Hindu?"). Defined Hindu as anyone with pitribhu (fatherland) and punyabhu (holy land) both in India — excluding Muslims and Christians whose punyabhu lay in Arabia/Palestine. Foundational text of Hindu nationalism. Distinguished "Hindutva" (Hindu-ness, cultural) from "Hinduism" (religion).

hist_rss_1925.label: Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS, 1925)
hist_rss_1925.subject: history
hist_rss_1925.detail: Founded Vijayadashami 27 September 1925 at Nagpur by Keshav Baliram Hedgewar. Cadre-based Hindu nationalist organisation on fascist-inspired organisational lines (daily shakhas, paramilitary drills, uniform). Maharashtra base until 1930s, branched out under M.S. Golwalkar. Role during Partition: organised Hindu-Sikh resistance in Punjab. Banned briefly after Gandhi's assassination Jan 1948 — Nathuram Godse was an ex-member.

hist_kb_hedgewar.label: K.B. Hedgewar
hist_kb_hedgewar.subject: history
hist_kb_hedgewar.detail: Keshav Baliram Hedgewar (1889-1940). Nagpur-based physician. Active in Tilak's Home Rule League and INC in 1920s (participated in Non-Cooperation). Founded RSS on Vijayadashami 27 September 1925. Emphasised character-building, physical drills, Hindu cultural unity. Died 21 June 1940 in Nagpur; Golwalkar succeeded him.

hist_ms_golwalkar.label: M.S. Golwalkar (Guruji)
hist_ms_golwalkar.subject: history
hist_ms_golwalkar.detail: Madhav Sadashiv Golwalkar (1906-1973). Second Sarsanghchalak (supreme chief) of RSS from 1940 till 1973. Codified RSS ideology in his 1939 booklet "We, or Our Nationhood Defined". Articulated supremacist Hindu nationalism — non-Hindu peoples must adopt Hindu culture or live "wholly subordinated to the Hindu nation, claiming nothing, deserving no privileges". Praised Nazi Germany's "race spirit" resurgence.

hist_we_or_our_nationhood.label: "We, Or Our Nationhood Defined" (Golwalkar, 1939)
hist_we_or_our_nationhood.subject: history
hist_we_or_our_nationhood.detail: 1939 booklet by M.S. Golwalkar codifying extreme Hindu nationalism. Advocated: non-Hindus must adopt Hindu culture/language/religion or stay "wholly subordinated to the Hindu nation, claiming nothing, deserving no privileges, far less any preferential treatment — not even citizen's rights". Praised Italy and Germany for their "race spirit" revival. Foundational doctrine of RSS extremism in 1940s.

hist_maulana_azad.label: Maulana Abul Kalam Azad
hist_maulana_azad.subject: history
hist_maulana_azad.detail: Islamic scholar, journalist (Al-Hilal, Al-Balagh), nationalist. Prominent Khilafat leader. Youngest Congress President at 35 (1923), and its longest-serving (Congress President Sept 1939 to Feb 1946 — through Quit India, Simla Conference, Cabinet Mission). Consistent opponent of Partition and Muslim separatism. Branded by League propaganda as Congress's "show boy". Post-independence first Education Minister.

hist_calcutta_killings_1946.label: Great Calcutta Killing (Aug 1946)
hist_calcutta_killings_1946.subject: history
hist_calcutta_killings_1946.detail: 16-19 August 1946 — communal violence after Muslim League's Direct Action Day call. ~4,000-5,000 killed in 72-96 hours in Calcutta. Rioting started Muslims attacking Hindus, Hindus retaliating. Fazl-ul-Huq's successor Suhrawardy's Muslim League Ministry refused to contain violence. Broke civil-political unity that had held 1920-46. Cascade effect — Noakhali riots (Oct), Bihar (Oct-Nov), UP/Punjab 1947. Final push toward Partition.

hist_bihar_riots_1946.label: Bihar Communal Riots (Oct-Nov 1946)
hist_bihar_riots_1946.subject: history
hist_bihar_riots_1946.detail: October-November 1946 — large-scale massacre of Muslims in Chhapra, Saran, Patna in retaliation for Noakhali violence. Estimated 5,000-8,000 dead (far higher than Noakhali deaths). Gandhi reached Bihar early Nov and began his walking mission to restore peace. Turned Gandhi's full focus to intercommunal violence at precisely the moment partition politics was being negotiated.

hist_fazl_ul_huq.label: A.K. Fazlul Huq
hist_fazl_ul_huq.subject: history
hist_fazl_ul_huq.detail: Abul Kasem Fazlul Huq — Bengali politician. Krishak Praja Party leader. Premier of Bengal 1937-43 in coalition. Moved the Lahore Resolution 23 March 1940. Later distanced from Jinnah, formed progressive coalition 1941. Rejoined League, removed as Premier 1943 during Bengal Famine. Shifted to parliamentary politics after independence (Pakistan, then East Pakistan).

hist_unionist_party_punjab.label: Unionist Party (Punjab)
hist_unionist_party_punjab.subject: history
hist_unionist_party_punjab.detail: Non-communal cross-community agrarian party of Punjab big landlords, formed 1923 by Fazl-e-Hussain. Ruled Punjab through 1937 and 1946 elections. Multi-confessional alliance of Muslim Unionists + Jat Sikhs + Hindu Jats. Declined 1946 as Muslim landlords switched to Muslim League under pressure. Broke during Partition. Model of non-communal provincial politics before 1946.

hist_muhammad_iqbal.label: Muhammad Iqbal
hist_muhammad_iqbal.subject: history
hist_muhammad_iqbal.detail: Allama Iqbal (1877-1938). Urdu-Persian poet-philosopher. President of Muslim League Allahabad session Dec 1930 — pioneered idea of a separate Muslim-majority homeland in North-West India (later developed into Pakistan demand). Wrote "Saare Jahan Se Achha" (1904) before his ideological shift. Spiritual influence on Jinnah's later communal politics. Died April 1938 before formal Pakistan Resolution.

hist_iqbal_allahabad_1930.label: Iqbal's Allahabad Address (Dec 1930)
hist_iqbal_allahabad_1930.subject: history
hist_iqbal_allahabad_1930.detail: 29 December 1930 — Muhammad Iqbal's presidential address at Allahabad Muslim League session. First authoritative call for consolidating "the North-West Indian Muslims into a single State" (Punjab, NWFP, Sindh, Balochistan). Framed as self-determination within or outside British Empire. Early intellectual foundation of what became the Pakistan demand (1940 Lahore Resolution).

hist_choudhry_rahmat_ali.label: Choudhry Rahmat Ali & Pakistan Name (1933)
hist_choudhry_rahmat_ali.subject: history
hist_choudhry_rahmat_ali.detail: Cambridge student who coined the acronym "Pakistan" in his 1933 pamphlet "Now or Never: Are We to Live or Perish Forever?" (later expanded 1935). P = Punjab, A = Afghania (NWFP), K = Kashmir, I = Iran-imperial?, S = Sindh, tan = Balochistan. Separately invented on ideological grounds, only later adopted by Muslim League after Lahore Resolution 1940.

hist_lahore_pakistan_resolution.label: Lahore (Pakistan) Resolution (23 March 1940)
hist_lahore_pakistan_resolution.subject: history
hist_lahore_pakistan_resolution.detail: Annual Muslim League session at Minto Park, Lahore, 22-24 March 1940. Resolution moved by A.K. Fazlul Huq on 23 March — demanded that "geographically contiguous units" where Muslims were in majority be grouped to constitute "independent states" with autonomous sovereign units. Adopted by majority League delegates. Foundational demand of Pakistan. 23 March commemorated in Pakistan as Pakistan Day / Resolution Day. Hist_lahore_resolution_1940 already in working set with broader framing.

hist_direct_action_day_call.label: Direct Action Day Call (July 1946)
hist_direct_action_day_call.subject: history
hist_direct_action_day_call.detail: 29 July 1946 — Muslim League Council rejected Cabinet Mission Plan and announced Direct Action to achieve Pakistan. Jinnah: "We bid good-bye to constitutional methods... Today we have also forged a pistol and are in a position to use it." 16 August 1946 declared Direct Action Day. Triggered Calcutta Killings 16-19 Aug 1946.

hist_congress_ministries_resignation.label: Congress Ministries Resignation (Oct-Nov 1939)
hist_congress_ministries_resignation.subject: history
hist_congress_ministries_resignation.detail: Oct-Nov 1939 — Viceroy Linlithgow's 17 October statement refused to define British war aims or commit to Indian freedom. Exploited Hindu-Muslim differences, recognised Muslim League as Congress counterweight. Congress Working Committee (23 October) rejected Viceregal statement and ordered Congress provincial ministries to resign. Ended 28-month experiment of Congress Raj. League's Jinnah celebrated 22 December 1939 as "Deliverance Day" — Muslims celebrated release from "tyranny" of Congress rule.

hist_ramgarh_session_1940.label: Ramgarh Congress Session (March 1940)
hist_ramgarh_session_1940.subject: history
hist_ramgarh_session_1940.detail: March 1940 — Maulana Azad presided. Resolution confirmed "complete independence" as only acceptable goal. Deferred civil disobedience to "when Congress organisation is considered fit enough for the purpose". Bose (Forward Bloc) held parallel "Anti-Compromise Conference" at Ramgarh demanding immediate struggle. Marked Congress-Forward Bloc ideological split.

hist_august_offer_1940.label: August Offer (Aug 1940)
hist_august_offer_1940.subject: history
hist_august_offer_1940.detail: 8 August 1940 — Linlithgow's offer: promise of Dominion Status after war, expansion of Executive Council with more Indians, War Advisory Council. Crucially gave Muslim League the veto — "no constitutional change without consent of minorities". Congress rejected (AICC September 1940). League welcomed effective veto. Congress responded with Individual Satyagraha.

hist_individual_satyagraha_1940.label: Individual Satyagraha (Oct 1940 - Dec 1941)
hist_individual_satyagraha_1940.subject: history
hist_individual_satyagraha_1940.detail: Launched 17 October 1940. Non-mass, selective protest: designated Satyagrahis publicly declared anti-war stance ("It is wrong to help British war effort with men or money") and informed District Magistrate of speech. Vinoba Bhave was first satyagrahi; Nehru the second (3 days rigorous imprisonment, later extended). Later "Delhi Chalo" trek. By May 1941 over 25,000 convicted. Dual purpose: express anti-war feeling and give British another chance to concede; also prepare Congress organisation for bigger struggle.

hist_vinoba_bhave.label: Vinoba Bhave
hist_vinoba_bhave.subject: history
hist_vinoba_bhave.detail: Gandhian disciple (1895-1982). Led Bhoodan (1951) and Gramdan movements. First Bharat Ratna recipient 1983 (posthumous). 'Acharya' status. Also supported Emergency ('anushasan parv' — time of discipline).

hist_cripps_mission_detailed.label: Cripps Mission Details (March-April 1942)
hist_cripps_mission_detailed.subject: history
hist_cripps_mission_detailed.detail: March 1942 — under US/Chinese/Labour pressure after Japanese invasion of Burma (Rangoon fell March 1942), Churchill sent Stafford Cripps to Delhi. Draft Declaration offered: Dominion Status after war, constitution-making body elected by provincial legislatures + nominated by princes, right of any province not accepting to sign separate agreement (first time Pakistan option implicit), interim British control of Defence. Congress rejected — Dominion Status not independence, Pakistan implicit, no real power transfer. Viceroy Linlithgow, Churchill, Amery all sabotaged Cripps. Gandhi called it a "post-dated cheque on a crashing bank".

hist_stafford_cripps.label: Sir Stafford Cripps
hist_stafford_cripps.subject: history
hist_stafford_cripps.detail: British Labour Party leader. Former friend of Nehru (since Brussels 1927). Sent by Churchill March 1942 to negotiate with Congress (Cripps Mission). Failed. Returned to India as part of Cabinet Mission 1946. Later held Chancellor of Exchequer in Attlee government.

hist_gowalia_tank_1942.label: Gowalia Tank (AICC Aug 1942)
hist_gowalia_tank_1942.subject: history
hist_gowalia_tank_1942.detail: AICC at Gowalia Tank Maidan, Bombay, 7-8 August 1942. Passed Quit India Resolution 8 August. Gandhi's famous "Do or Die" speech: "The mantra is Do or Die. We shall either free India or die in the attempt; we shall not live to see the perpetuation of our slavery". Specific instructions: government servants to declare allegiance to Congress but not resign; soldiers to refuse firing on compatriots; princes to accept their people's sovereignty. Next day (9 Aug) all Congress leaders arrested. Aruna Asaf Ali hoisted Congress flag at the Tank on 9 August 1942. The ground became August Kranti Maidan.

hist_aruna_asaf_ali.label: Aruna Asaf Ali
hist_aruna_asaf_ali.subject: history
hist_aruna_asaf_ali.detail: "Grand Old Lady of Independence Movement". Hoisted the Congress flag at Gowalia Tank on 9 August 1942 after leaders' arrests. Went underground during Quit India, edited Inquilab journal. Jailed for 7 years. Leader of 1942 underground with Achyut Patwardhan, Ram Manohar Lohia, Sucheta Kripalani. Married Asaf Ali, Congress lawyer.

hist_ram_manohar_lohia.label: Ram Manohar Lohia
hist_ram_manohar_lohia.subject: history
hist_ram_manohar_lohia.detail: Congress Socialist leader, jail escapee with Jayaprakash Narayan (Hazaribagh Nov 1942). Led Congress Radio broadcasts from underground. Later founded Samyukta Socialist Party. Intellectual architect of non-Congress socialism post-1947.

hist_sucheta_kripalani.label: Sucheta Kripalani
hist_sucheta_kripalani.subject: history
hist_sucheta_kripalani.detail: Underground leader of Quit India in Delhi and elsewhere. Member Constituent Assembly. Sang "Vande Mataram" and "Sare Jahan Se Achha" at the Constituent Assembly's midnight session on 14-15 August 1947. Later Chief Minister of UP (1963-67) — India's first female CM.

hist_usha_mehta_radio.label: Congress Radio (Usha Mehta, 1942)
hist_usha_mehta_radio.subject: history
hist_usha_mehta_radio.detail: Clandestine Congress Radio operated by 22-year-old Usha Mehta and others (including Vithaldas Khakhar, Chandrakant Jhaveri, Vithalbhai Jhaveri) during Quit India. Broadcasts began 27 August 1942 from Bombay; ran till November 1942 when police seized the equipment. Range reached Madras. Read out news, Congress bulletins, Gandhi's messages. Ram Manohar Lohia regularly broadcast. Usha Mehta imprisoned 4 years.

hist_parallel_govts.label: Parallel Governments of 1942
hist_parallel_govts.subject: history
hist_parallel_govts.detail: Three major "swaraj" parallel governments emerged during Quit India: (1) Ballia (East UP, August 1942) under Chittu Pande — forced collector to hand over power, released arrested Congressmen; crushed within a week; (2) Tamluk Jatiya Sarkar (Midnapore Bengal, 17 Dec 1942 - Sept 1944) — cyclone relief, schools, arbitration courts, Vidyut Vahini armed wing, paddy redistribution; (3) Satara Prati Sarkar (Maharashtra, 1943-45) under Nana Patil — longest-lasting, effective parallel authority for nearly 2 years.

hist_nana_patil.label: Nana Patil + Satara Prati Sarkar
hist_nana_patil.subject: history
hist_nana_patil.detail: Leader of Satara (Maharashtra) Prati Sarkar 1943-45. Kranti Simha ("Revolution Lion") nickname. Organised Tufani Sena and nyayadan mandals (people's courts). Anti-moneylender peasant politics. Provided parallel governance for 2 years during Quit India underground. Later joined CPI; elected to Lok Sabha 1957.

hist_gandhi_21day_fast.label: Gandhi's 21-Day Fast (Feb-March 1943)
hist_gandhi_21day_fast.subject: history
hist_gandhi_21day_fast.detail: 10 February - 3 March 1943 — Gandhi's 21-day fast in Aga Khan Palace Poona against government's demand that he condemn Quit India violence. Gandhi refused, held government responsible for "leonine violence". Three Indian members of Viceroy's Executive Council (M.S. Aney, N.R. Sarkar, H.P. Mody) resigned. Wavell refused release, made plans for Gandhi's funeral. Gandhi survived. International solidarity from US, British Communist Party, Women's International League, Australian Council of Trade Unions. Moral defeat for the Raj.

hist_mohan_singh_ina1.label: Mohan Singh + First INA (1942)
hist_mohan_singh_ina1.subject: history
hist_mohan_singh_ina1.detail: Captain Mohan Singh (1909-1989). Captured by Japanese at Singapore Feb 1942; became first Commander of INA formed from Indian POWs Sept 1942. Disagreed with Japanese over INA's role; arrested by Japanese Dec 1942, INA disbanded. Second INA revived under S.C. Bose 1943. Post-independence joined Congress, elected to Rajya Sabha.

hist_azad_hind_govt.label: Azad Hind Government (Oct 1943)
hist_azad_hind_govt.subject: history
hist_azad_hind_govt.detail: 21 October 1943 — S.C. Bose proclaimed the Provisional Government of Azad Hind (Free India) at Singapore. Cabinet: Bose (Head of State, PM, Minister of War and Foreign Affairs), Captain Lakshmi Sahgal (Minister of Women's Organisation), A.C. Chatterjee (Finance), S.A. Ayer (Publicity). Recognised by Japan, Germany, Italy, Thailand, Burma, Croatia, Manchukuo, Philippines (Japanese satellites). Headquarters moved to Rangoon. Declared war on Britain and US.

hist_rani_jhansi_regiment.label: Rani of Jhansi Regiment
hist_rani_jhansi_regiment.subject: history
hist_rani_jhansi_regiment.detail: Women's armed regiment of INA formed 1943 at Singapore, named after Rani Lakshmibai. Commanded by Captain Lakshmi Sahgal (Lakshmi Swaminathan). Drew recruits from Tamil, Malayali, Bengali Indian diaspora in Malaya-Singapore. Deployed in Burma Imphal-Kohima campaigns. Rare instance of women's armed combat in modern Indian history.

hist_lakshmi_sahgal.label: Captain Lakshmi Sahgal
hist_lakshmi_sahgal.subject: history
hist_lakshmi_sahgal.detail: Dr Lakshmi Swaminathan (Lakshmi Sahgal, 1914-2012). Recruited as doctor in Singapore 1940. Joined INA 1943 on Bose's arrival. Commander of Rani of Jhansi Regiment. Minister for Women in Azad Hind Government. Captured May 1945, released 1946. Later CPM, ran for President of India 2002.

hist_imphal_kohima_1944.label: Battles of Imphal-Kohima (March-July 1944)
hist_imphal_kohima_1944.subject: history
hist_imphal_kohima_1944.detail: March-July 1944 — INA + Japanese attempted to march on Imphal and Kohima into British India. Slogan "Chalo Delhi". Bose hoisted Azad Hind flag on Indian soil at Moirang, Manipur in April 1944. British-Indian 14th Army under Slim held and then repulsed; INA suffered heavy losses from disease, hunger, British air superiority. Turning point after which INA retreated. Marked the limit of Axis eastward advance.

hist_red_fort_trials_details.label: INA Red Fort Trials (Nov 1945-Jan 1946)
hist_red_fort_trials_details.subject: history
hist_red_fort_trials_details.detail: First trial (from 5 November 1945) at Red Fort of the three senior-most captured INA officers: Shah Nawaz Khan (Muslim), Prem Kumar Sahgal (Hindu), and Gurbaksh Singh Dhillon (Sikh). Cross-communal composition turned trial into pan-Indian symbol of unity. Defence team: Bhulabhai Desai (lead), Tej Bahadur Sapru, K.N. Katju, Nehru, Asaf Ali. All three found guilty of "waging war against the King"; sentenced to transportation for life but sentences commuted by Auchinleck under political pressure and released. Sparked INA Day (12 Nov 1945), INA Week (5-11 Nov), massive popular sympathy.

hist_shah_nawaz_khan.label: Shah Nawaz Khan
hist_shah_nawaz_khan.subject: history
hist_shah_nawaz_khan.detail: Major General in INA; led INA Division into Imphal campaign. One of three tried at Red Fort Nov 1945. Post-independence joined Congress, elected to Lok Sabha (four terms), Union Minister.

hist_prem_sahgal.label: Prem Kumar Sahgal
hist_prem_sahgal.subject: history
hist_prem_sahgal.detail: Military Secretary to Subhas Bose in Azad Hind Government. One of three tried at Red Fort Nov 1945. Married Captain Lakshmi Sahgal (commander of Rani of Jhansi Regiment).

hist_gurbaksh_dhillon.label: Gurbaksh Singh Dhillon
hist_gurbaksh_dhillon.subject: history
hist_gurbaksh_dhillon.detail: INA officer, one of three tried at Red Fort Nov 1945. Represented Sikhs in the cross-communal INA Trials trinity (with Muslim Shah Nawaz Khan and Hindu P.K. Sahgal).

hist_bhulabhai_desai.label: Bhulabhai Desai + Liaqat-Desai Pact
hist_bhulabhai_desai.subject: history
hist_bhulabhai_desai.detail: Congress lawyer. Led defence at INA Red Fort Trials Nov 1945. Negotiated Liaqat-Desai Pact 1945 with Muslim League's Liaqat Ali Khan — proposed equal Hindu-Muslim representation in interim government + 20% for minorities. Congress leaders (in jail) repudiated it. Precursor to later Cabinet Mission negotiations.

hist_wavell_plan_1945.label: Wavell Plan + Simla Conference (June 1945)
hist_wavell_plan_1945.subject: history
hist_wavell_plan_1945.detail: June 1945 — Viceroy Wavell's plan for reconstituted Executive Council with equal Hindu and Muslim representation (excluding Viceroy and C-in-C). Simla Conference 25 June - 14 July 1945 brought 21 Indian leaders together including the released Congress Working Committee and Muslim League. Failed over Jinnah's insistence that only the League could nominate Muslims (Congress insisted on nominating nationalist Muslims like Azad). Conference collapsed July 1945. First major post-war political initiative and first major failure at Congress-League unity.

hist_194546_elections.label: 1945-46 Central + Provincial Elections
hist_194546_elections.subject: history
hist_194546_elections.detail: Dec 1945 Central Legislative Assembly elections + Feb 1946 Provincial Assembly elections. Congress won 57 of 102 Central seats contested and swept non-Muslim seats (91.3%). Muslim League won all 30 Muslim seats at Centre and 427 of 509 Muslim provincial seats (hence claimed sole Muslim representation). Congress took majority in 8 of 11 provinces. INA agitation and 1942 repression were key campaign issues. Established League's electoral credential and hardened communal lines. Basis for subsequent Cabinet Mission invitation.

hist_rin_mutiny_details.label: Royal Indian Navy Mutiny (Feb 1946)
hist_rin_mutiny_details.subject: history
hist_rin_mutiny_details.detail: 18-23 February 1946 — revolt of RIN ratings against racial discrimination, bad food, after arrest of B.C. Dutt for scrawling "Quit India" on HMIS Talwar. Spread from HMIS Talwar Bombay to Castle & Fort Barracks, then HMIS Hindustan Karachi and 77 other ships/shore establishments (20,000 ratings, 78 ships). Congress flags hoisted with League and CPI flags briefly. Bombay hartal by 200,000-300,000 workers Feb 22, barricades, 228 civilians killed in police/army action, 1046 injured. Patel and Jinnah separately advised ratings to surrender. Revolt ended Feb 23. Liberating effect on anti-British sentiment but demonstrated colonial state could still repress.

hist_ina_day.label: INA Day + INA Week (Nov 1945)
hist_ina_day.subject: history
hist_ina_day.detail: 12 November 1945 observed as INA Day. 5-11 November 1945 as INA Week. Massive nationwide mobilisation for release of INA prisoners during Red Fort Trial. Deshapriya Park Calcutta mass rally drew 200,000-500,000. INA Relief & Enquiry Committee formed under Congress. Sarat Chandra Bose (SC Bose's brother) led public campaign. Communal unity rare — Gurdwara donations, film stars, municipal funds, Calcutta tongawallas all contributed.

hist_cabinet_mission_plan.label: Cabinet Mission Plan (May 1946)
hist_cabinet_mission_plan.subject: history
hist_cabinet_mission_plan.detail: Cabinet Mission (Stafford Cripps, Pethick-Lawrence, A.V. Alexander) arrived Delhi 24 March 1946. Plan announced 16 May 1946. Rejected Pakistan demand but proposed three-tier federal structure: (1) Union Centre handling Defence/External Affairs/Communications; (2) Three groups — A (Hindu-majority), B (Muslim-majority NW), C (Bengal+Assam); (3) Provinces with residuary powers. Provinces could opt out of groups after first election. Interim government envisaged. League accepted 6 June. Congress accepted with reservations on grouping compulsion. Nehru's Bombay press conference 10 July made the mission unraveled. League withdrew and called Direct Action Day.

hist_interim_govt_details.label: Interim Government (Sept 1946)
hist_interim_govt_details.subject: history
hist_interim_govt_details.detail: Constituted 2 September 1946 with Nehru as de facto Prime Minister (Vice President of Executive Council). Initially Congress-only; League joined 26 October 1946 after Direct Action Day violence. Liaqat Ali Khan as Finance Minister obstructed — "budget of revenge" Feb 1947 targeted capitalists; unworkable coalition. League repeatedly undermined governmental functioning from within. Persuaded Congress that only Partition would permit functional government.

hist_attlee_statement_feb1947.label: Attlee's February 1947 Statement
hist_attlee_statement_feb1947.subject: history
hist_attlee_statement_feb1947.detail: 20 February 1947 — British PM Clement Attlee announced in House of Commons that the British would transfer power "not later than June 1948" and Lord Louis Mountbatten would replace Wavell as Viceroy. Definite deadline concentrated minds. Radically changed the dynamics — forced Congress to decide between partition and chaos. Mountbatten arrived India 22 March 1947.

hist_indian_independence_act.label: Indian Independence Act (July 1947)
hist_indian_independence_act.subject: history
hist_indian_independence_act.detail: 18 July 1947 — British Parliament passed the Act. Provided for partition of British India into two Dominions: India and Pakistan, effective 15 August 1947. Each Dominion would have its own Constituent Assembly with full sovereign powers. British paramountcy over princely states to lapse (states free to accede to either Dominion). Governor-General for each Dominion (Mountbatten became first GG of India; Jinnah of Pakistan). 1935 Act to apply in modified form until new constitutions framed. Legal basis of Partition.

hist_radcliffe_commission.label: Radcliffe Boundary Commission (July 1947)
hist_radcliffe_commission.subject: history
hist_radcliffe_commission.detail: Set up 30 June 1947 under Sir Cyril Radcliffe (London barrister who had never visited India) to demarcate Punjab and Bengal partition lines. Had six-week mandate, never set foot outside of Delhi simla estate. Radcliffe Award published 17 August 1947 (two days after Independence). Lines split villages, homes, irrigation systems. Responsible for chaos of 14-15 million refugee flows and 1-2 million killings of Partition.

hist_tryst_with_destiny.label: Tryst with Destiny (Aug 14-15, 1947)
hist_tryst_with_destiny.subject: history
hist_tryst_with_destiny.detail: At midnight 14-15 August 1947 — Jawaharlal Nehru's address to Constituent Assembly declaring independence: "Long years ago we made a tryst with destiny, and now the time comes when we shall redeem our pledge... At the stroke of the midnight hour, when the world sleeps, India will awake to life and freedom." Among foundational speeches of the Republic. Sucheta Kripalani sang "Vande Mataram" and "Sare Jahan Se Achha". Gandhi was in Calcutta leading peace walks, not present at celebrations.

hist_gandhis_peace_walks.label: Gandhi's Peace Walks (Oct 1946 - Jan 1948)
hist_gandhis_peace_walks.subject: history
hist_gandhis_peace_walks.detail: November 1946 - March 1947 — Gandhi walked through Noakhali villages after October 1946 riots, barefoot, for months, restoring Muslim-Hindu confidence. Then walked through Bihar after Oct-Nov 1946 Hindu mobs massacred Muslims. Stayed in Calcutta Aug 1947 during communal tensions — his one-man peace work was more effective than multiple army brigades. Assassinated 30 January 1948 at Birla House Delhi by Nathuram Godse over Gandhi's stand on communal reconciliation.

hist_bengal_school_of_art.label: Bengal School of Art
hist_bengal_school_of_art.subject: history
hist_bengal_school_of_art.detail: Anti-academic, swadeshi-era art movement founded by Abanindranath Tagore (student of Ernest Binfield Havell). Rejected Western academic realism in favour of "revival" of Mughal/Rajput miniature traditions, Pahari, Ajanta frescoes. Centred in Calcutta's Government School of Art and from 1918 expanded to Santiniketan Kala Bhavan. Major figures: Nandalal Bose, Asit Kumar Haldar, Kshitindranath Majumdar, Jamini Roy, Mukul Dey. Famous works: Abanindranath's "Bharat Mata" 1905, "Passing of Shah Jahan", "Ganesh Janani", "Veena Player". Shaped era-9 visual nationalism.

hist_jamini_roy.label: Jamini Roy
hist_jamini_roy.subject: history
hist_jamini_roy.detail: (1887-1972). Student of Abanindranath Tagore at Government College of Art. Pioneered Indian modern art rooted in Kalighat patua, Bengal folk and tribal art traditions. "Mother and Child", "Krishna and Radha Dancing", "Makara". Awarded Padma Bhushan 1955. His anti-elitist mass-marketed affordable paintings democratised art.

hist_santiniketan_kala_bhavan.label: Kala Bhavan, Santiniketan (1919)
hist_santiniketan_kala_bhavan.subject: history
hist_santiniketan_kala_bhavan.detail: Art school founded 1919 at Rabindranath Tagore's Santiniketan Ashram in Bolpur, Bengal. Led by Nandalal Bose (Principal 1922-51). Focus on indigenous traditions, outdoor sketching, integration with nature, folk-art immersion. Shaped the Bengal School's second generation. Rabindranath's educational-artistic vision — precursor to Visva-Bharati University 1921.

hist_visva_bharati.label: Visva-Bharati University (1921)
hist_visva_bharati.subject: history
hist_visva_bharati.detail: Founded 23 December 1921 by Rabindranath Tagore at Santiniketan. Universalist, anti-colonial educational vision: "Yatra Visvam Bhavatyekanidam" (Where the world makes a home in a single nest). International faculty. Rural-reconstruction wing at Sriniketan (1922). Declared a central university by Act of Parliament 1951. Unique pedagogy of open-air classes, tree-shade teaching, folk-craft integration.

hist_chhayavad_poetry.label: Chhayavad Movement in Hindi Poetry (1918-1937)
hist_chhayavad_poetry.subject: history
hist_chhayavad_poetry.detail: Romantic-spiritual movement in modern Hindi poetry, 1918-1937. Four pillars ("Chhayavad ke Stambh"): Jaishankar Prasad, Suryakant Tripathi "Nirala", Sumitranandan Pant, Mahadevi Verma. Responded against objectivity of Dwivedi era with subjective lyricism, romantic idealism, nationalist undercurrents, liberation of women and the self. Prasad's "Kamayani" epic, Nirala's "Ram ki Shakti Puja", Mahadevi's "Yama" — foundational modern Hindi texts.

hist_jaishankar_prasad.label: Jaishankar Prasad
hist_jaishankar_prasad.subject: history
hist_jaishankar_prasad.detail: (1889-1937). Hindi poet, playwright, novelist. One of the "Four Pillars of Chhayavad". Epic "Kamayani" (1936) — major modern Hindi poem. Plays: Chandragupta, Skandagupta, Dhruvaswamini. Novels: Kankal, Titli, Irawati. Shaped modern Hindi literary imagination.

hist_suryakant_nirala.label: Suryakant Tripathi "Nirala"
hist_suryakant_nirala.subject: history
