hist_suryakant_nirala.detail: (1896-1961). Chhayavad poet. "Ram ki Shakti Puja", "Saroj Smriti" (elegy for his daughter) are landmarks. Combined Sanskrit tradition with Bengali Vaishnav mysticism and Hindi folk. Introduced free verse (chhand-mukta) in Hindi poetry. Lifelong poverty. Influential on post-independence Hindi modernism.

hist_sumitranandan_pant.label: Sumitranandan Pant
hist_sumitranandan_pant.subject: history
hist_sumitranandan_pant.detail: (1900-1977). Chhayavad pillar. Nature poetry ("Prakritivaad") — "Veena" (1927), "Pallav" (1928). Later shift to Aurobindonian spiritualism and social realism. Jnanpith Award 1968 for "Chidambara". His early Hindi free-verse shaped modern style.

hist_mahadevi_verma.label: Mahadevi Verma
hist_mahadevi_verma.subject: history
hist_mahadevi_verma.detail: (1907-1987). Chhayavad poetess, "Modern Mirabai". "Yama" (Jnanpith winner), "Neer Bhari Dukh ki Badli" — mystical, melancholic poetry. Principal of Prayag Mahila Vidyapith. Active in Progressive Writers' Association. Padma Vibhushan 1988. Central woman voice of modern Hindi literature.

hist_alam_ara_1931.label: Alam Ara (First Indian Talkie, 1931)
hist_alam_ara_1931.subject: history
hist_alam_ara_1931.detail: 14 March 1931 — India's first sound film, screened at Majestic Cinema, Bombay. Produced by Imperial Film Company, directed by Ardeshir Irani. Urdu-Hindi dialogue. W.M. Khan sang India's first recorded film song "De de khuda ke naam par" (Wazir Mohammed Khan). Revolutionised Indian cinema overnight; silent films extinct within two years.

hist_prabhat_films.label: Prabhat Film Company (1929)
hist_prabhat_films.subject: history
hist_prabhat_films.detail: Major Indian film studio founded 1929 at Kolhapur by V. Shantaram, V.G. Damle, K.R. Dhaiber, S. Fattelal and S.B. Kulkarni. Moved to Pune 1933. Known for socially conscious subjects. Made "Sairandhri" (1933) — first Indian colour film (processed in Germany), "Amrit Manthan", "Sant Tukaram" (first Indian film at Venice Film Festival 1937), "Duniya Na Mane", "Aadmi". V. Shantaram's hallmark social-reformist cinema.

hist_bombay_talkies.label: Bombay Talkies (1934)
hist_bombay_talkies.subject: history
hist_bombay_talkies.detail: Founded 1934 by Himansu Rai and Devika Rani at Malad, Bombay. Major early studio. "Achhut Kanya" (1936) — landmark anti-untouchability film. Trained generation of actors (Ashok Kumar, Leela Chitnis, Dilip Kumar — screen debut) and directors. Franz Osten (German) was chief director. Collapsed after Himansu Rai's death 1940 and Rai-Rani estrangement.

hist_new_theatres.label: New Theatres (1931)
hist_new_theatres.subject: history
hist_new_theatres.detail: Calcutta-based film studio founded 1931 by B.N. Sircar. Centre of Bengali and Hindi cinema pioneering. Made P.C. Barua's "Devdas" (1935) — first Indian film using Studio System; "Street Singer" (1938) starring K.L. Saigal; "Mukti" (1937). Gave birth to playback singing (R.C. Boral). Training ground for directors Bimal Roy, Nitin Bose.

hist_v_shantaram.label: V. Shantaram
hist_v_shantaram.subject: history
hist_v_shantaram.detail: (1901-1990). Rajaram Vankudre Shantaram — filmmaker, co-founded Prabhat (1929). Founded Rajkamal Kalamandir (1942). Socially committed cinema: "Amar Jyoti" (women's emancipation), "Duniya Na Mane" (widow remarriage), "Aadmi" (prostitution), later "Do Aankhen Barah Haath" (1957). Dadasaheb Phalke Award 1985. Shaped Indian social-realist film aesthetic.

hist_himansu_rai_devika_rani.label: Himansu Rai & Devika Rani
hist_himansu_rai_devika_rani.subject: history
hist_himansu_rai_devika_rani.detail: Himansu Rai (1892-1940) — pioneer producer-director; Indo-German collaborations "A Throw of Dice" (1929), "Prem Sanyas/Light of Asia" (1925). Co-founded Bombay Talkies 1934. Devika Rani (1908-1994) — great-grandniece of Rabindranath Tagore; first major female Indian film star. "Karma" (1933), "Achhut Kanya" (1936). Received first Dadasaheb Phalke Award 1969.

hist_ipta_1943.label: Indian People's Theatre Association (IPTA, 1943)
hist_ipta_1943.subject: history
hist_ipta_1943.detail: Founded 25 May 1943 at Bombay as cultural wing of Communist Party of India. First President: Prof. Hiren Mukherjee; General Secretary: Anil de Silva. Response to Bengal Famine 1943, wartime misery, fascist threat. Plays on Bengal Famine (Bijon Bhattacharya's "Nabanna"), labour struggles, anti-communalism. Key figures: Prithviraj Kapoor, Balraj Sahni, Bijon Bhattacharya, Ritwik Ghatak, Utpal Dutt, Shombhu Mitra, K.A. Abbas. Made "Dharti Ke Lal" (1946) — first major left-wing Indian film.

hist_dharti_ke_lal.label: "Dharti Ke Lal" (1946)
hist_dharti_ke_lal.subject: history
hist_dharti_ke_lal.detail: K.A. Abbas's 1946 film on Bengal Famine 1943, produced by IPTA. Based on Bijon Bhattacharya's play "Nabanna" and Krishan Chander's story "Annadata". First major socially realist Indian film. Distributed to Soviet Union — international exposure. Influenced Indian parallel cinema.

hist_ka_abbas.label: K.A. Abbas
hist_ka_abbas.subject: history
hist_ka_abbas.detail: Khwaja Ahmad Abbas (1914-1987). Urdu-English journalist, filmmaker, columnist. IPTA founder. Directed "Dharti Ke Lal" (1946), "Munna" (1954). Scripted Raj Kapoor's films ("Awaara", "Shree 420", "Mera Naam Joker"). Weekly column "Last Page" in Blitz 1935-87 (longest-running column in Indian journalism).

hist_prithvi_theatre.label: Prithvi Theatre (1944)
hist_prithvi_theatre.subject: history
hist_prithvi_theatre.detail: Founded 15 January 1944 by Prithviraj Kapoor. Travelling Hindi theatre group that toured across India with nationalist-themed plays: "Shakuntala", "Paisa", "Ahuti", "Deewar", "Pathan", "Gaddar". Plays promoted Hindu-Muslim unity and anti-colonial themes. Closed 1960 after Prithviraj's decline. Revived as permanent theatre at Juhu, Mumbai in 1978 by Shashi Kapoor and Jennifer Kendal Kapoor.

hist_bengal_famine_film_ipta.label: Bengal Famine & Cultural Response (1943-47)
hist_bengal_famine_film_ipta.subject: history
hist_bengal_famine_film_ipta.detail: Cultural mobilisation around Bengal Famine of 1943 and late-war hardship. Central to IPTA's founding (1943). Bijon Bhattacharya's "Nabanna" (The New Harvest) 1944 depicted rural starvation. Zainul Abedin's unsparing sketches of Bengal famine victims (1943-44) — internationally recognised. PWA writers (Ismat Chughtai, Saadat Hasan Manto, Krishan Chander) wrote famine/Partition stories. Galvanised post-war Left cultural politics.

hist_saadat_hasan_manto.label: Saadat Hasan Manto
hist_saadat_hasan_manto.subject: history
hist_saadat_hasan_manto.detail: (1912-1955). Urdu short-story master. Associated with Progressive Writers' Association. Wrote for All India Radio (1937-41). Scripted Bombay Talkies films. Partition stories: "Toba Tek Singh", "Khol Do", "Thanda Gosht", "Kali Shalwar" — seared images of 1947 trauma. Migrated to Lahore 1948, alcoholic, died 1955. Along with Ismat Chughtai, faced obscenity trials by colonial state for "Bu" and "Lihaaf".

hist_ismat_chughtai.label: Ismat Chughtai
hist_ismat_chughtai.subject: history
hist_ismat_chughtai.detail: (1915-1991). Urdu feminist writer. Progressive Writers' Association leader. "Lihaaf" (The Quilt, 1942) faced obscenity trial in Lahore High Court 1945 for lesbian-themed content — acquitted. "Terhi Lakeer" (semi-autobiography) 1944. Her bold treatment of female sexuality made her a landmark figure of Indian feminist literature.

hist_faiz_ahmad_faiz.label: Faiz Ahmad Faiz
hist_faiz_ahmad_faiz.subject: history
hist_faiz_ahmad_faiz.detail: (1911-1984). Urdu-Punjabi revolutionary poet. Member of Progressive Writers' Movement from 1936. "Naqsh-e-Faryaadi" (1941). Served in British Indian Army during WWII (anti-fascist). Post-partition moved to Pakistan; jailed in Rawalpindi Conspiracy Case 1951-55. "Hum Dekhenge" became anthem of South Asian resistance. Lenin Peace Prize 1962. Nominated for Nobel posthumously.

hist_mahavir_prasad_dwivedi.label: Mahavir Prasad Dwivedi
hist_mahavir_prasad_dwivedi.subject: history
hist_mahavir_prasad_dwivedi.detail: (1864-1938). Hindi editor of Saraswati magazine (1903-1920). Standardiser of modern Hindi prose. "Dwivedi Yug" (1893-1918) of Hindi literature named after him. Rigorous editorial rules shaped modern Hindi grammar and prose. Key figure in Hindi-Hindustani pre-era-9 transition.

hist_qazi_nazrul_islam.label: Kazi Nazrul Islam
hist_qazi_nazrul_islam.subject: history
hist_qazi_nazrul_islam.detail: (1899-1976). "Rebel Poet" (Bidrohi Kobi) of Bengal. Bilingual Bengali-Urdu poet. "Bidrohi" (1922) — seminal anti-colonial poem. Edited Dhumketu (1922). Imprisoned by British 1923 for sedition. Co-founded Workers' and Peasants' Party. Close friend of Surya Sen. Symbol of Hindu-Muslim unity. Later national poet of Bangladesh. Published Langal (Bengali Marxist weekly) with Muzaffar Ahmed.

hist_harivansh_rai_bachchan.label: Harivansh Rai Bachchan
hist_harivansh_rai_bachchan.subject: history
hist_harivansh_rai_bachchan.detail: (1907-2003). Hindi poet. "Madhushala" (The House of Wine, 1935) — romantic-ruminative classic. Part of Chhayavadottar period transitioning into Pragativad (progressivism). Post-indep Sahitya Akademi award, Padma Bhushan. Father of actor Amitabh Bachchan.

hist_dramatic_national_theatre.label: Indian People's Theatre + Communist Cultural Politics
hist_dramatic_national_theatre.subject: history
hist_dramatic_national_theatre.detail: IPTA + PWA consolidation under Communist cultural umbrella 1936-47 produced the first sustained anti-imperialist mass-cultural movement in modern India. Merged Bengali nabanna theatre tradition with new Marxist politics. Covered labour strikes, famine, partition. Talents later flowered into post-1947 "parallel cinema" (Ritwik Ghatak, Bimal Roy, Kaifi Azmi, Shombhu Mitra). Left's major lasting cultural legacy.

hist_goi_act_1919.label: Government of India Act 1919 (Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms)
hist_goi_act_1919.subject: history
hist_goi_act_1919.detail: Passed by British Parliament, came into force 1921. Named after Edwin Montagu (Secretary of State for India) and Lord Chelmsford (Viceroy). Key provisions: (1) Demarcated central vs provincial subjects and legislatures; (2) Introduced "Dyarchy" in provinces — transferred subjects under ministers responsible to legislature, reserved subjects under Governor's Executive Council; (3) Introduced bicameralism at Centre — Council of State (upper) + Legislative Assembly (lower); (4) Extended separate electorates to Sikhs, Christians, Anglo-Indians, Europeans; (5) Limited franchise based on property/tax/education; (6) Created High Commissioner for India in London; (7) Required 3 of 6 Viceroy's Executive Council members to be Indian; (8) Set up Public Service Commission (established 1926); (9) Separated provincial budgets; (10) Provided for statutory commission review after 10 years (which became Simon Commission 1927). Dyarchy largely failed in practice.

hist_dyarchy.label: Dyarchy (1919 Provincial Government)
hist_dyarchy.subject: history
hist_dyarchy.detail: Dual-rule (Greek "di-arche") scheme introduced by GoI Act 1919 for provincial governance 1921-1937. Divided provincial subjects into "Transferred" (education, public health, local self-government, agriculture — under Indian ministers responsible to legislature) and "Reserved" (law & order, finance, revenue, labour, irrigation — under Governor and his Executive Council, not responsible to legislature). Widely unsuccessful: ministers had no control over finance, Governors retained veto, communal electorates undercut unity. Abolished by GoI Act 1935 in favour of Provincial Autonomy.

hist_cls_bicameralism_1919.label: Council of State + Legislative Assembly (1919)
hist_cls_bicameralism_1919.subject: history
hist_cls_bicameralism_1919.detail: First bicameral central legislature established under GoI Act 1919, functional 1921. Upper House: Council of State (60 members, 6-year term) — designed as conservative check, narrow franchise. Lower House: Central Legislative Assembly (145 members, 3-year term) — majority directly elected. Replaced the earlier Imperial Legislative Council. Swarajists used the Assembly to create deadlocks (Motilal Nehru, Vithalbhai Patel). Both Houses continued till 1947. Precursor to Rajya Sabha and Lok Sabha.

hist_central_psc_1926.label: Central Public Service Commission (1926)
hist_central_psc_1926.subject: history
hist_central_psc_1926.detail: Established 1926 under GoI Act 1919 provisions (Section 96C) to recruit civil servants by open competition. Chaired by Ross Barker (first Chairman). Precursor to Federal Public Service Commission (1935) and post-independence Union Public Service Commission (UPSC, 1950). Significant Indianisation mechanism — diluted European monopoly on ICS recruitment.

hist_goi_act_1935_detailed.label: Government of India Act 1935 — Detailed Features
hist_goi_act_1935_detailed.subject: history
hist_goi_act_1935_detailed.detail: Longest British Act of Parliament with 321 sections, 10 schedules. Key features: (1) Provided for All-India Federation of provinces + princely states (never came into being — princes did not join); (2) Three Lists — Federal (59 items), Provincial (54), Concurrent (36); residuary powers to Viceroy; (3) Abolished dyarchy in provinces, introduced "Provincial Autonomy" (1937-39); (4) Dyarchy at Centre (never operationalised); (5) Bicameralism extended to 6 provinces: Bengal, Bombay, Madras, Bihar, Assam, UP; (6) Communal electorates extended to SCs, women, labour; (7) Abolished 1858 Council of India; (8) Extended franchise to ~10% of population; (9) Provided for Reserve Bank of India (est. 1935); (10) Federal Court (est. 1937, precursor of Supreme Court); (11) Federal + Provincial + Joint Public Service Commissions. Basis of Indian Constitution 1950 — major constitutional scaffolding.

hist_provincial_autonomy_1937.label: Provincial Autonomy (1937)
hist_provincial_autonomy_1937.subject: history
hist_provincial_autonomy_1937.detail: Introduced by GoI Act 1935, operational April 1937. Replaced dyarchy. Provinces became autonomous units administered by elected Ministers responsible to provincial Legislative Assembly. Governor retained special powers (discretionary, of individual judgement) over minorities, civil servants, law & order, British business interests. Could take over administration indefinitely. Congress formed ministries in 8 provinces (July 1937). Discontinued when Congress Ministries resigned October 1939 over WWII declaration.

hist_federal_court_1937.label: Federal Court of India (1937)
hist_federal_court_1937.subject: history
hist_federal_court_1937.detail: Established 1 October 1937 under GoI Act 1935 provisions. Supreme judicial body for British India + princely states. First Chief Justice: Sir Maurice Gwyer. Sat in Delhi. Had limited appellate jurisdiction; Privy Council in London remained final court. Replaced 26 January 1950 by Supreme Court of India.

hist_rbi_1935.label: Reserve Bank of India (1935)
hist_rbi_1935.subject: history
hist_rbi_1935.detail: Established 1 April 1935 under GoI Act 1935 and RBI Act 1934 to regulate issue of currency and credit. Originally privately owned; nationalised January 1949. First Governor: Sir Osborne Smith (1935-37). First Indian Governor: C.D. Deshmukh (1943-49). Replaced earlier Imperial Bank of India currency-issuing function. Recommended by 1926 Hilton-Young Commission.

hist_sinha_temp_president_ca.label: Dr Sachchidananda Sinha (CA Temporary President)
hist_sinha_temp_president_ca.subject: history
hist_sinha_temp_president_ca.detail: Oldest member of Constituent Assembly (84). Elected temporary President at first CA meeting on 9 December 1946, following French practice of seating the oldest member as chairman. Dr Rajendra Prasad subsequently elected permanent President on 11 December 1946.

hist_rajendra_prasad_ca_pres.label: Rajendra Prasad elected CA President (Dec 1946)
hist_rajendra_prasad_ca_pres.subject: history
hist_rajendra_prasad_ca_pres.detail: 11 December 1946 — Dr Rajendra Prasad elected permanent President of the Constituent Assembly. H.C. Mukherjee and V.T. Krishnamachari elected Vice-Presidents. Rajendra Prasad chaired the CA when functioning as constitution-making body; G.V. Mavalankar chaired it when functioning as legislative/dominion parliament post-1947. After Constitution came into force 26 Jan 1950, Rajendra Prasad elected first President of Republic of India.

hist_ca_composition.label: Constituent Assembly Composition (1946-49)
hist_ca_composition.subject: history
hist_ca_composition.detail: Originally 389 seats under Cabinet Mission Plan (296 British India + 93 princely states). Indirectly elected by provincial assemblies (July-Aug 1946). INC won 208 of 296 seats; Muslim League 73; small groups/independents 15. Princely-state seats filled gradually after Mountbatten Plan (June 1947). Post-Partition (15 Aug 1947): strength reduced to 299 (229 provinces + 70 princely states) after Muslim League Pakistan members withdrew. Representation: Hindus, Muslims, Sikhs, Parsis, Anglo-Indians, Christians, SCs, STs, women. Notable exception: Mahatma Gandhi was not a member. Limited franchise (only 11-15% of adults voted for provincial assemblies).

hist_ca_major_committees.label: Eight Major Committees of Constituent Assembly
hist_ca_major_committees.subject: history
hist_ca_major_committees.detail: Union Powers Committee (Nehru); Union Constitution Committee (Nehru); Provincial Constitution Committee (Patel); Drafting Committee (Ambedkar); Advisory Committee on Fundamental Rights, Minorities, Tribal Areas (Patel — had 5 sub-committees including J.B. Kripalani on FR, H.C. Mukherjee on Minorities, A.V. Thakkar on Excluded Areas, Gopinath Bardoloi on NE Tribal); Rules of Procedure Committee (Rajendra Prasad); States Committee for Negotiations (Nehru); Steering Committee (Rajendra Prasad). Plus 13 minor committees. Structure underpinned the three-year constitution-making process.

hist_drafting_committee_members.label: Drafting Committee — Seven Members (Aug 1947)
hist_drafting_committee_members.subject: history
hist_drafting_committee_members.detail: Set up 29 August 1947. Chairman: Dr B.R. Ambedkar. Members: N. Gopalaswamy Ayyangar, Alladi Krishnaswamy Ayyar, Dr K.M. Munshi, Syed Mohammad Saadullah, N. Madhava Rau (replacing B.L. Mitter who resigned), T.T. Krishnamachari (replacing D.P. Khaitan who died 1948). Drafted Constitution in 141 sitting days over less than 6 months. First Draft published Feb 1948; eight months public consultation; Second Draft Oct 1948. Third reading began 14 Nov 1949; passed 26 Nov 1949 (Constitution Day).

hist_bn_rau_advisor.label: B.N. Rau (Constitutional Advisor)
hist_bn_rau_advisor.subject: history
hist_bn_rau_advisor.detail: Benegal Narsing Rau (1887-1953). Constitutional Advisor to Constituent Assembly. Prepared the initial draft of the Constitution October 1947 (studied constitutions of 60+ countries). Rau's draft was the foundation that the Drafting Committee (Ambedkar) worked on. Later India's representative at UN and Judge of International Court of Justice.

hist_mn_roy_ca_idea_1934.label: M.N. Roy's Idea of Constituent Assembly (1934)
hist_mn_roy_ca_idea_1934.subject: history
hist_mn_roy_ca_idea_1934.detail: 1934 — M.N. Roy first articulated the idea of a Constituent Assembly for India. INC officially demanded one in 1935. Nehru declared (1938) that the Constitution of free India "must be framed, without outside interference, by a Constituent Assembly elected on the basis of adult franchise". Accepted in principle by August Offer 1940. Cripps Proposals 1942 elaborated. Cabinet Mission Plan 1946 formulated the scheme actually adopted.

hist_cabinet_mission_composition.label: Cabinet Mission — Three-Member Composition (March 1946)
hist_cabinet_mission_composition.subject: history
hist_cabinet_mission_composition.detail: Three British Cabinet Ministers sent by Attlee government to negotiate Indian constitutional settlement: (1) Lord Pethick-Lawrence (Secretary of State for India — leader); (2) Sir Stafford Cripps (President of Board of Trade); (3) A.V. Alexander (First Lord of Admiralty). Arrived Delhi 24 March 1946. Plan announced 16 May 1946 — rejected Pakistan demand but proposed three-tier federal structure with Union, three provincial Groups (A: Hindu-majority; B: NW Muslim-majority; C: Bengal+Assam), and provinces. Interim Government formed Sept 1946.

hist_objectives_resolution_details.label: Objectives Resolution — Text & Adoption
hist_objectives_resolution_details.subject: history
hist_objectives_resolution_details.detail: Moved by Nehru on 13 December 1946. Declared: India shall be an Independent Sovereign Republic; territories organised as Union with autonomous units + residuary powers; all power derived from the people; guaranteed justice, equality, freedom of thought/expression/belief/worship; safeguards for minorities and backward classes; integrity of national territory. Unanimously adopted 22 January 1947. Forms basis of the Constitution's Preamble. Marked the philosophical foundation of the new Republic.

hist_august_offer_ca_accept.label: August Offer Accepts Constituent Assembly (1940)
hist_august_offer_ca_accept.subject: history
hist_august_offer_ca_accept.detail: 8 August 1940 — Linlithgow's August Offer to get Indian cooperation in WWII. Though rejected by Congress over concrete demands, it represented the first British acceptance in principle of Indian demand for a Constituent Assembly to frame a new Constitution. Elaborated later in Cripps Proposals 1942 and Cabinet Mission Plan 1946.

hist_three_tier_cabinet_mission.label: Cabinet Mission Plan Three-Tier Federation
hist_three_tier_cabinet_mission.subject: history
hist_three_tier_cabinet_mission.detail: Key innovation of Cabinet Mission Plan May 1946: (1) Union Centre handling only Defence, Foreign Affairs, Communications; (2) Three Groups of Provinces — Group A (Hindu-majority: Madras, Bombay, UP, CP, Bihar, Orissa); Group B (Muslim-majority NW: Punjab, NWFP, Sind); Group C (Bengal + Assam); (3) Provinces with residual powers, could opt out of Groups after first general election. Princes could federate or stay. Accepted by Muslim League 6 June; Congress accepted with reservations. Collapsed after Nehru's 10 July press conference and League's Direct Action call.

hist_mountbatten_ca_sovereign.label: Indian Independence Act — CA Sovereign Changes (1947)
hist_mountbatten_ca_sovereign.subject: history
hist_mountbatten_ca_sovereign.detail: 15 August 1947 — Indian Independence Act made three changes to Constituent Assembly: (1) Made it a fully sovereign body — could abrogate/alter any British law on India; (2) Assembly also became a legislative body (Dominion Parliament) — separate days for two functions; Rajendra Prasad chaired constitution-making; G.V. Mavalankar chaired legislative sessions; (3) Muslim League members from Pakistan areas withdrew — strength reduced from 389 to 299 (229 provinces + 70 states). CA held 11 sessions over 2 years, 11 months, 18 days. Final Constitution adopted 26 November 1949, came into force 26 January 1950.

hist_preamble_26nov_1949.label: Constitution Adopted (26 November 1949)
hist_preamble_26nov_1949.subject: history
hist_preamble_26nov_1949.detail: 26 November 1949 — Constituent Assembly adopted the Constitution of India. Ambedkar moved the motion: "the Constitution as settled by the Assembly be passed". 284 of 299 members signed. Preamble declares "We, the people of India... do hereby adopt, enact and give to ourselves this Constitution". Observed as Constitution Day from 2015. Some articles (citizenship, elections, provisional Parliament) came into immediate effect; rest came into force 26 January 1950 (Republic Day, echoing 1930 Poorna Swaraj pledge).

period_noncooperation_khilafat.label: Non-Cooperation + Khilafat (1920-22)
period_noncooperation_khilafat.subject: history
period_noncooperation_khilafat.detail: Gandhi's first all-India mass mobilisation. Khilafat triggers, Calcutta Special Session Sept 1920 accepts NCM, Nagpur Dec 1920 changes Congress creed. Congress Volunteer Corps, boycott of schools/courts/foreign cloth, Tilak Swaraj Fund (Rs 1 crore oversubscribed). Ali Brothers nationwide tour. Prince of Wales visit riots Nov 1921. Chauri Chaura 5 Feb 1922 → withdrawal 12 Feb 1922. Ended with Gandhi's 6-year jail sentence March 1922. Peasant spillover (Avadh Kisan Sabha, Eka), Moplah Rebellion Aug 1921 in Malabar.

period_stagnation_swarajists.label: Swarajists vs No-Changers (1922-27)
period_stagnation_swarajists.subject: history
period_stagnation_swarajists.detail: Post-NCM Congress crisis. Gaya Session Dec 1922 defeated council-entry 1748-890. C.R. Das + Motilal formed Swaraj Party Jan 1923. Delhi Special Session Sept 1923 compromised. 1923 Elections — Swarajists won 42/101. Vithalbhai Patel CLA President 1925. C.R. Das death June 1925. Belgaum Dec 1924 reunification under Gandhi. Kaliparaj/Raniparaj uplift work. Bardoli Satyagraha 1928 — Patel earns "Sardar" title. Constructive programme (ashrams, khadi, Hindu-Muslim unity, anti-untouchability).

period_revolutionary_terrorism.label: Revolutionary Terrorists (1922-34)
period_revolutionary_terrorism.subject: history
period_revolutionary_terrorism.detail: HRA founded at Kanpur Oct 1924 (Bismil, Chatterjea, Sanyal) — Kakori Robbery Aug 1925 → Kakori Conspiracy Case → Ashfaqulla, Bismil, Roshan Singh, Rajendra Lahiri hanged 1927. Reorganised as HSRA at Ferozeshah Kotla Sept 1928. Lajpat Rai death Nov 1928 → Saunders Assassination Dec 1928. Assembly Bomb 8 April 1929. Jatin Das hunger-strike death Sept 1929. Philosophy of the Bomb (1930). Lahore Conspiracy Case → Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev, Rajguru hanged 23 March 1931. Chandrashekhar Azad shoots self at Alfred Park Feb 1931. Surya Sen's Chittagong Armoury Raid 18 April 1930 → Jalalabad battle 22 April → 3-year guerrilla → Surya Sen hanged Jan 1934. Female revolutionaries: Pritilata Waddedar, Kalpana Dutt, Bina Das, Santi Ghosh, Suniti Chowdhury.

period_gathering_storm_cd.label: Gathering Storm + Civil Disobedience (1927-31)
period_gathering_storm_cd.subject: history
period_gathering_storm_cd.detail: Simon Commission announcement Nov 1927, boycott from Feb 3 1928. Madras Session Dec 1927 snap Purna Swaraj resolution. All-Parties Conference 1928 → Nehru Report. Jinnah's 14 Points March 1929. Irwin Declaration Oct 1929 + Delhi Manifesto Nov 1929. Lahore Session Dec 1929 — Purna Swaraj. Independence Day Pledge 26 Jan 1930. Gandhi's 11-point ultimatum Jan 31 1930. Dandi March 12 March - 6 April 1930. Khudai Khidmatgars + Peshawar uprising April 1930. Sholapur Uprising May 1930. Dharasana Salt Raid 21 May 1930 (Sarojini Naidu). First Round Table Conference Nov 1930. Gandhi-Irwin Pact 5 March 1931. Chowkidara Tax Refusal, no-rent UP, forest law defiance, chunks of women's participation.

period_karachi_wardha_phase.label: Karachi to Wardha (1931-34)
period_karachi_wardha_phase.subject: history
period_karachi_wardha_phase.detail: Karachi Session March 1931 — Fundamental Rights + National Economic Programme resolutions. Second RTC Aug-Dec 1931. Gandhi's "last cup of poison" journey, return empty-handed. Willingdon Viceroy. 4 Jan 1932 pre-emptive crackdown → CD Round 2 1932-34 → crushed by mid-1932. Communal Award 16 Aug 1932. Gandhi's Epic Fast 20 Sept 1932 → Poona Pact 24 Sept 1932. Harijan Sewak Sangh Sept 1932. Harijan Tour Nov 1933 - July 1934 (20,000 km). Poona bomb on Gandhi June 1934. Second CD withdrawal April 1934. Third RTC 1932.

period_left_consolidation.label: Rise of the Left Wing (1925-39)
period_left_consolidation.subject: history
period_left_consolidation.detail: Indian socialist+communist formation. Tashkent CPI 1920 (M.N. Roy). Kanpur Bolshevik Case 1924. CPI founded Kanpur Dec 1925. Workers+Peasants' Parties 1927. Meerut Conspiracy 1929-33. Bhagat Singh's Marxist turn 1929-31. CPI banned 1934. CSP founded at Bombay Oct 1934 (JP Narayan, Narendra Dev, Minoo Masani, Achyut Patwardhan). Dutt-Bradley Thesis 1936 → CPI re-enters Congress. Nehru presided Lucknow 1936 (socialist presidential address) + Faizpur Dec 1936 (first rural session). National Planning Committee 1938. Forward Bloc 1939 (Bose). Royists. Left bloc fights 1936-37 office-acceptance debate.

period_working_class_movement.label: Working Class + Trade Unionism (1918-47)
period_working_class_movement.subject: history
period_working_class_movement.detail: Ahmedabad TLA founded by Gandhi 1918. AITUC 1920 (Lala Lajpat Rai first president, Dewan Chaman Lal Gen Sec). 1919-22 railway strikes, Prince of Wales boycott involving 1.4 lakh Bombay workers. 1928 Jharia AITUC Communist dominance + Bombay Textile Strike April-Sept 1928. Girni Kamgar Union. Sholapur Uprising May 1930. 1929 Public Safety Bill + Trade Disputes Act + Meerut Case. Royal Commission on Labour 1929 (Whitley). Post-1937 Congress Ministries — rise in unions. WWII: Bombay anti-war strike Oct 1939 (90,000 workers). CPI People's War line from Dec 1941. 1942 Tata Steel 13-day strike, Ahmedabad textile 3.5-month strike. INA trials solidarity. RIN Mutiny Feb 1946. All India P&T Strike 1946.

period_peasant_movements.label: Peasant Movements (1918-47)
period_peasant_movements.subject: history
period_peasant_movements.detail: UP Kisan Sabha 1918. Oudh Kisan Sabha Oct 1920 (Baba Ramchandra, Nehru). Eka Movement 1921-22. Moplah Rebellion Aug-Dec 1921 (Ali Musaliar, Kunhammed Haji). Bardoli Satyagraha 1928 (Sardar Patel). Bihar Provincial Kisan Sabha 1929 (Sahajanand). Chowkidara Tax Refusal 1930. All India Kisan Sabha founded Lucknow April 1936. Karshaka Sangham (Kerala). N.G. Ranga's Indian Peasants Institute Andhra 1933. Andhra Long March 1938 (2,000 kisans, 1,500 miles). Bakasht Lands Struggle (Bihar 1938-39). Punjab Kisan Committee 1937 → Lahore Kisan Morcha 1939. Bengal Famine 1943 relief. Tebhaga Movement 1946-47. Punnapra-Vayalar 1946. Telangana Rebellion 1946-51.

period_princely_states_struggle.label: Princely States Freedom Struggle (1927-48)
period_princely_states_struggle.subject: history
period_princely_states_struggle.detail: Praja Mandals (States Peoples' associations) from 1920. All India States' Peoples Conference founded Dec 1927 (Baiwantrai Mehta, Manikial Kothari, G.R. Abhayankar). Congress 1920 Nagpur Resolution on states. Tripuri 1939 resolution identifying Congress with states peoples. Nehru President AISPC Ludhiana 1939. Rajkot Satyagraha 1938-39 (Gandhi + Kasturba). Hyderabad State Congress 1938 (Swami Ramananda Tirtha). Kashmir Quit Kashmir May 1946 (Sheikh Abdullah). Travancore (C.P. Ramaswamy Aiyar), Jaipur, Mysore, Patiala struggles. Integration of Princely States Aug-Oct 1947 (Patel + V.P. Menon). Instrument of Accession. Operation Polo Sept 1948 (Hyderabad).

period_capitalists_national_movement.label: Indian Capitalists + National Movement (1927-47)
period_capitalists_national_movement.subject: history
period_capitalists_national_movement.detail: FICCI founded 1927 (G.D. Birla, Purshottamdas Thakurdas). Boycotted First RTC 1930 for lack of Congress participation. Opposed Public Safety Bill 1928 (capitalists+Congress united). 1930 CD support but with warnings against "disastrous after-effects". GD Birla's mediation in Gandhi-Irwin Pact 1931. Capitalist pushback on Left radicalisation 1935-36. Indian capitalists' 5 Aug 1942 letter urging "granting political freedom" to avert Quit India. Bombay Plan 1944 (Thakurdas, JRD Tata, Birla, Ardeshir Dalal, Sri Ram, Kasturbhai Lalbhai, A.D. Shroff, John Mathai). Post-War Economic Development Committee 1942.

period_congress_ministries_1937_39.label: 28 Months of Congress Rule (1937-39)
period_congress_ministries_1937_39.subject: history
period_congress_ministries_1937_39.detail: 1937 Provincial Elections — Congress won 716/1161, majority in 6+2 provinces. Parliamentary Sub-Committee (Patel, Azad, Rajendra Prasad) coordinated ministries. Civil liberties restored. Congress Election Manifesto 1936 implemented partially. Haripura Session Feb 1938 (Bose first presidency) + Haripura Panels by Nandalal Bose. Tripuri Crisis March 1939 — Bose re-elected vs Sitaramayya 1580-1377, forced to resign. Forward Bloc 3 May 1939. WWII outbreak 1 Sept 1939 — Linlithgow declared India at war without consultation. Congress Ministries resigned Oct-Nov 1939. Muslim League "Deliverance Day" 22 Dec 1939.

period_wwii_satyagraha.label: WWII + Individual Satyagraha (1939-42)
period_wwii_satyagraha.subject: history
period_wwii_satyagraha.detail: Ministries resignation Oct 1939. Ramgarh March 1940. August Offer 8 Aug 1940 (Linlithgow). Individual Satyagraha from 17 Oct 1940 — Vinoba Bhave first, Nehru second. 25,000 convicted by May 1941. Pearl Harbor 7 Dec 1941. Japan overruns SE Asia, occupies Rangoon March 1942. CWC Dec 1941 offers cooperation; Gandhi designates Nehru as successor Jan 1942. Cripps Mission March-April 1942 — Dominion Status + provincial opt-out (implicit Pakistan) + no real transfer. Congress rejection; Gandhi "post-dated cheque".

period_quit_india_ina.label: Quit India + INA (1942-45)
period_quit_india_ina.subject: history
period_quit_india_ina.detail: AICC Gowalia Tank 8 Aug 1942 — Quit India Resolution + "Do or Die" speech. 9 Aug arrests. Aruna Asaf Ali hoists flag. Underground movement: Patwardhan, Aruna, Lohia, Sucheta, JP (escaped Nov 1942), Biju Patnaik. Usha Mehta's Congress Radio Aug-Nov 1942. Parallel governments: Ballia (Chittu Pande), Tamluk Jatiya Sarkar Dec 1942, Satara Prati Sarkar 1943-45 (Nana Patil). Gandhi's 21-Day Fast Feb-March 1943. Rash Behari Bose + Indian Independence League Tokyo 1942. First INA (Mohan Singh) Sept 1942. Bose takes charge July 1943. Azad Hind Government 21 Oct 1943 Singapore. Rani of Jhansi Regiment (Lakshmi Sahgal). Imphal-Kohima campaign 1944. Chalo Delhi, Moirang flag-hoisting.

period_endgame_partition.label: Post-War Upsurge to Partition (1945-47)
period_endgame_partition.subject: history
period_endgame_partition.detail: Labour govt elected UK July 1945. Indian leaders released June 1945. Simla Conference + Wavell Plan June-July 1945 — failed. INA Red Fort Trials Nov 1945 (Shah Nawaz, Sahgal, Dhillon) with Bhulabhai Desai leading defence. INA Day 12 Nov, INA Week 5-11 Nov 1945. Upsurges: Calcutta 21 Nov 1945, Rashid Ali Feb 1946, RIN Mutiny 18-23 Feb 1946 (HMIS Talwar, B.C. Dutt, Karachi). 1945-46 Elections (Congress 91% general, League 100% Muslim). Cabinet Mission announced 22 Jan 1946, arrived Delhi 24 March 1946. Plan 16 May 1946 (three-tier federation). Congress accepted with reservations; League accepted 6 June, withdrew July. Direct Action Day 16 Aug 1946 + Great Calcutta Killing. Noakhali Oct 1946. Bihar riots. Gandhi's peace walks. Interim Government 2 Sept 1946. League joined 26 Oct. Attlee statement 20 Feb 1947. Mountbatten arrived 22 March 1947. Mountbatten Plan 3 June 1947. Radcliffe Commission. Indian Independence Act 18 July 1947. 14-15 Aug 1947 midnight — Tryst with Destiny, Partition, Independence.

period_constitution_making.label: Constitution Making (1946-49)
period_constitution_making.subject: history
period_constitution_making.detail: M.N. Roy idea 1934. CA demand in INC from 1935, Cripps 1942. Cabinet Mission Plan May 1946 framework. CA elections July-Aug 1946 (INC 208, League 73, independents 15). CA first meeting 9 Dec 1946 — Sachchidananda Sinha temp president; Rajendra Prasad elected 11 Dec; HC Mukherjee + VT Krishnamachari VPs. Objectives Resolution by Nehru 13 Dec 1946, adopted 22 Jan 1947. Independence Act changes Aug 1947 — CA became sovereign + Dominion legislature; Muslim League Pakistan withdrawal; strength 299. 8 major committees; Drafting Committee 29 Aug 1947 (Ambedkar + 6 others). B.N. Rau constitutional advisor. First draft Feb 1948, second Oct 1948. 7,653 amendments. Constitution adopted 26 Nov 1949, effective 26 Jan 1950.

period_communalism_rise.label: Rise of Communalism (1920-47)
period_communalism_rise.subject: history
period_communalism_rise.detail: Communalism three stages framework. Liberal → Extreme after 1937. Muslim League revival by Jinnah 1936. League 1937 poor performance (4.8% Muslim vote) → shift to mass communal politics. Hindu Mahasabha under Savarkar 1937-42 (Hindutva, 1923 text). RSS founded Vijayadashami 1925 by K.B. Hedgewar Nagpur. M.S. Golwalkar took over 1940 — "We, or Our Nationhood Defined" (1939). Iqbal's Allahabad Address Dec 1930. Rahmat Ali's "Pakistan" acronym 1933. Lahore (Pakistan) Resolution 23 March 1940 (moved by Fazlul Huq). Two-Nation Theory. Jinnah's 14 Points, "Caste Hindu Fascist Congress" rhetoric. Muslim Mass Contact Programme 1937 (Nehru). Unionist Party Punjab. Direct Action Day call 29 July 1946 → Calcutta Killings Aug 1946 → Noakhali, Bihar, Punjab, UP violence 1946-47. Gandhi's assassination 30 Jan 1948.

period_nationalist_foreign_policy.label: Nationalist Foreign Policy (1920-47)
period_nationalist_foreign_policy.subject: history
period_nationalist_foreign_policy.detail: Roots 1878-1914: opposition to Afghan War 1878, Egypt 1882, Burma annexation 1885, Tibet 1903, NWF "forward policy". INC 1920 support for Turkey, 1921 Burma independence. Brussels Congress Feb 1927 — League Against Imperialism (Nehru elected to Exec Council, with Einstein, Rolland, Madame Sun Yat-Sen, Lansbury). Congress Foreign Department 1927. Madras 1927 + Calcutta 1928: support for Egypt, Syria, Palestine, Iraq, Afghanistan. 1936 active phase: Ethiopia Day May 9, Palestine Day Sept 27. Spanish Civil War support — Nehru+Krishna Menon visit Republican Spain June 1938. Haripura Congress Feb 1938 anti-Japan resolution. China Day June 12 1938. Medical mission to China (Dr M. Atal, Dr Dwarkanath Kotnis). Czechoslovakia/Munich Sept 1938 condemnation. Pro-Soviet sentiment (Nehru 1927 visit), concern for China and USSR during WWII.

period_visual_arts_bengal_school.label: Visual Arts + Bengal School (1907-47)
period_visual_arts_bengal_school.subject: history
period_visual_arts_bengal_school.detail: Bengal School of Art: Abanindranath Tagore's "Bharat Mata" 1905 (era-8 tail), taught Nandalal Bose + Jamini Roy at Govt College of Art. Indian Society of Oriental Art 1907 (era 8). Kala Bhavan, Santiniketan 1919. Visva-Bharati University 1921. Nandalal Bose principal of Kala Bhavan 1922-51; painted Haripura Panels 1938; designed Constitution manuscript illustrations. Jamini Roy — Bengal folk + Kalighat-inspired modernism. Santiniketan as pan-Indian cultural centre. Asit Kumar Haldar, Kshitindranath Majumdar, Mukul Dey. Zainul Abedin's Bengal famine sketches 1943-44.

period_literature_chhayavad_pwa.label: Literature — Chhayavad + PWA (1918-47)
period_literature_chhayavad_pwa.subject: history
period_literature_chhayavad_pwa.detail: Chhayavad Movement 1918-1937 in Hindi poetry — four pillars: Jaishankar Prasad (Kamayani 1936), Suryakant Tripathi Nirala (Ram ki Shakti Puja), Sumitranandan Pant, Mahadevi Verma (Yama). Harivansh Rai Bachchan's Madhushala 1935. Premchand's Godan 1936 — already in ws. Urdu: Iqbal (Allahabad Address 1930), Faiz Ahmad Faiz (PWA), Saadat Hasan Manto, Ismat Chughtai (Lihaaf 1942 obscenity trial). Kazi Nazrul Islam — Bidrohi 1922 + Langal 1925 + Workers-Peasants Party. All India Progressive Writers' Association April 1936 Lucknow (President Premchand; founders Mulk Raj Anand, Sajjad Zaheer, Ahmed Ali). Mahavir Prasad Dwivedi's Saraswati magazine.

period_cinema_theatre.label: Cinema + Theatre (1920-47)
period_cinema_theatre.subject: history
period_cinema_theatre.detail: Silent era through 1930: V. Shantaram, Baburao Painter, Suchet Singh, Madan, Ardeshir Irani. Alam Ara 14 March 1931 at Majestic Bombay — first Indian talkie (Imperial, Ardeshir Irani). Prabhat Film Company 1929 — Sairandhri 1933 first colour film, Sant Tukaram 1937 Venice. New Theatres Calcutta 1931 — P.C. Barua's Devdas 1935 first studio-system film. Bombay Talkies 1934 (Himansu Rai + Devika Rani) — Achhut Kanya 1936. IPTA 25 May 1943 Bombay — Bijon Bhattacharya's Nabanna on Bengal Famine, Dharti Ke Lal 1946 (K.A. Abbas). Prithvi Theatre 1944 (Prithviraj Kapoor). Kisan Kanya 1937 first indigenous colour. All India Radio. Early stars: Devika Rani, K.L. Saigal, Prithviraj Kapoor.

period_temporal_polity.label: Temporal Polity — Constitutional Scaffolding (1919-49)
period_temporal_polity.subject: history
period_temporal_polity.detail: NEW STREAM (per architecture decision). GoI Act 1919 (Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms) — Dyarchy + bicameralism + Council of State + Legislative Assembly. Central PSC 1926. GoI Act 1935 — Federation, Three Lists, Provincial Autonomy, Federal Court 1937, RBI 1935. Communal Award Aug 1932 → Poona Pact Sept 1932. August Offer 1940 accepting CA demand. Cripps Proposals 1942 + opt-out. Cabinet Mission Plan three-tier federation May 1946. Indian Independence Act 18 July 1947. CA composition, major committees (8), Drafting Committee 7 members, B.N. Rau, Objectives Resolution, draft readings, 26 Nov 1949 adoption. Constitutional scaffolding running parallel to the mass-movement stream.

period_parallel_europe_fascism_wwii.label: Parallel — Europe, Fascism & WWII (1919-45)
period_parallel_europe_fascism_wwii.subject: history
period_parallel_europe_fascism_wwii.detail: Treaty of Sèvres May 1920 → Khilafat trigger. Weimar Germany, German Hyperinflation 1923. Nazi Party, Hitler Chancellor 1933, Enabling Act 1933, Nazi Racial Ideology, Gestapo+SS, Nuremberg Laws 1935. Great Depression 1929-1939. Holocaust begins 1941. World War II Europe Sept 1939-1945. Munich Agreement Sept 1938. Bretton Woods Conference 1944.

period_parallel_soviet_stalinism.label: Parallel — Soviet Stalinism (1922-45)
period_parallel_soviet_stalinism.subject: history
period_parallel_soviet_stalinism.detail: Formation of USSR 1922. Stalin's rise late 1920s, Collectivisation 1929, Five Year Plans 1927 onwards. Great Purge 1930s. WWII Eastern Front 1941-45 (Nazi attack on USSR 22 June 1941 — triggered CPI's "People's War" shift from Dec 1941).

period_parallel_asia_anticolonial.label: Parallel — Asian Anti-Colonial Nationalism (1919-47)
period_parallel_asia_anticolonial.subject: history
period_parallel_asia_anticolonial.detail: China: Long March 1934-35, Japanese Invasion 1937-45 (China Day June 12 in India). Japan: Pearl Harbor Dec 1941, overrun of SE Asia 1942, Rangoon fallen March 1942. Vietnam: Hoa Hao 1939, Ho Chi Minh + Viet Minh 1941, Vietnamese Independence Sept 1945. Indonesia: Sukarno, independence 1945. Bandung emergence.

period_s01.label: 1991 Watershed & Rao Era (1991-1996)
period_s01.subject: history
period_s01.detail: Five years that turned India inside out. Rajiv assassinated 21 May 1991; Chandra Shekhar caretaker until June. Narasimha Rao + Manmohan Singh launch LPG reforms (24 July 1991 budget): industrial licence raj abolished, rupee devalued, MRTP cap removed, FDI opened. Babri demolished 6 Dec 1992; communal riots; 1993 Mumbai blasts. Indra Sawhney upholds 27% OBC reservation. 73rd-74th Amendments constitutionalise local government. WTO accession 1995. End of one-party dominance.

period_s02.label: Coalition Instability: United Front (1996-1998)
period_s02.subject: history
period_s02.detail: Two years of fragile centre. 1996 election produces hung parliament. BJP's 13-day Vajpayee government falls. United Front (Janata Dal + 12 regional parties + Left, supported by Congress) governs under Deve Gowda (June 1996 - April 1997), then I.K. Gujral (April 1997 - March 1998). Gujral Doctrine on neighbours. Congress withdraws support over CBI/DMK; March 1998 mid-term polls.

period_s03.label: Vajpayee NDA & Nuclear India (1998-2004)
period_s03.subject: history
period_s03.detail: BJP-led NDA full term — 13 months 1998-99 then 1999-2004. Pokhran-II (11-13 May 1998) declares India nuclear weapons state; US/Japan sanctions. Lahore Bus Yatra Feb 1999 → Kargil War May-July 1999. IC-814 hijacking Dec 1999. Parliament attack 13 Dec 2001; Operation Parakram 2001-02. Gujarat riots Feb-Mar 2002. Golden Quadrilateral, Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan, POTA 2002, RTE Article 21A (86th Amendment). India Shining 2004 ad campaign loses.

period_s04.label: UPA-I: Reform with Human Face (2004-2009)
period_s04.subject: history
period_s04.detail: UPA-I governs with Left Front external support. Sonia Gandhi declines PM, names Manmohan Singh. National Advisory Council drives rights-based architecture. RTI Act 2005, NREGA 2005, Forest Rights Act 2006, Domestic Violence Act 2005, Hindu Succession Amendment 2005, Sachar Committee 2006, Ministry of Minority Affairs 2006. POTA repealed; UAPA expanded. Indo-US Civil Nuclear Deal 2005-08; NSG waiver 6 Sept 2008; trust vote 22 July 2008. 26/11 Mumbai attacks Nov 2008. NIA created.

period_s05.label: UPA-II & Anti-Corruption Wave (2009-2014)
period_s05.subject: history
period_s05.detail: UPA-II (Manmohan PM 2009-14) battered by scams: 2G, CWG 2010, Coalgate. Anna Hazare anti-corruption movement Aug 2011 → Lokpal Act 2013. Aam Aadmi Party born. Nirbhaya Dec 2012 → Criminal Law Amendment 2013. Aadhaar enrolment, DBT pilot. Food Security Act 2013, Land Acquisition Act 2013. NJAC enacted 2014 (struck down 2015). Modi wave: 2014 election, BJP 282 seats — first single-party majority since 1984.

period_s06.label: Modi-I: Flagship Rollouts (GST, Demonetisation) (2014-2019)
period_s06.subject: history
period_s06.detail: Modi I — flagship rollouts. Jan Dhan (Aug 2014), Swachh Bharat (Oct 2014), Make in India (Sept 2014), Mudra (April 2015), NITI Aayog (Jan 2015 replaces Planning Commission). Demonetisation 8 Nov 2016 voids 86% currency. GST live 1 July 2017 (101st Amendment). RBI MPC + inflation targeting 2016. AQR 2015 → IBC 2016 → bank mergers. Surgical Strikes Sept 2016 + Balakot Feb 2019. Triple Talaq (SC 2017, Act 2019). Ayushman Bharat Sept 2018.

period_s07.label: Modi-II: Art 370, CAA, COVID, Farm Laws (2019-2024)
period_s07.stage: Modi-II: Art 370, CAA, COVID, Farm Laws
period_s07.subject: history
period_s07.detail: Modi II returns with 303 seats. Article 370 abrogated 5 Aug 2019 + J&K bifurcated. CAA 2019 + Shaheen Bagh protests. COVID-19 lockdown 25 March 2020 + migrant crisis. Atmanirbhar Bharat May 2020. Vaccine rollout 16 Jan 2021 — Covaxin/Covishield. Farm Laws Sept 2020 → 13-month protests → repealed Nov 2021. Pegasus, electoral bonds debate. PLI schemes. G20 Presidency Dec 2022-Nov 2023; Delhi Declaration. Chandrayaan-3 lunar landing 23 Aug 2023. New criminal laws (BNS/BNSS/BSA) 2023. Women's Reservation Act 2023. Article 370 SC verdict Dec 2023. 2024 election: NDA 293, BJP 240 (lost majority).

period_s08.label: Modi-III & Current Affairs (2024-2026)
period_s08.subject: history
period_s08.detail: Modi III — coalition dependence renewed. Ram Mandir consecration 22 Jan 2024 (pre-election). Waqf Amendment Act 2024. Bangladesh regime change Aug 2024 (Sheikh Hasina ouster). Maharashtra/Jharkhand polls; Delhi Assembly BJP win Feb 2025. Mahakumbh 2025 (~66 crore footfall). Aviation/manufacturing PLI scaled. Current affairs to UPSC May 2026.

period_s09.label: Kashmir & Punjab Crises (1989-2019)
period_s09.subject: history
period_s09.detail: Two parallel internal-security theatres. Kashmir Insurgency from 1989 (JKLF, Hizbul Mujahideen); Pandit exodus Jan-Mar 1990. Governor's rule under Jagmohan. ~80,000 killed by 2010. Punjab militancy ended early 1990s by KPS Gill-led police. Beant Singh CM 1992, assassinated 1995. Article 370 abrogated 2019; J&K reorganised; SC upholds 2023.

period_s10.label: Terrorism: Parliament, 26/11, Pulwama (2001-2019)
period_s10.subject: history
period_s10.detail: Era of mega-attacks. Parliament attack 13 Dec 2001 → Operation Parakram. 26/11 Mumbai 2008 (Lashkar). Pune German Bakery 2010, Delhi blasts. Pathankot Jan 2016. Uri attack Sept 2016 → surgical strikes. Pulwama 14 Feb 2019 (40 CRPF) → Balakot air strike 26 Feb 2019. NIA Act 2008/2019 expansion. UAPA amendments 2008/2012/2019. Counterterror architecture matures.

period_s11.label: Constitutional Amendments 65-106 (1990-2023)
period_s11.subject: history
period_s11.detail: 33 amendments in 33 years (1990-2023). 65th creates NCSC/NCST combined commission. 69th gives Delhi NCT special status. 71st/92nd add 4+4 languages to 8th Schedule. 73rd/74th constitutionalise PRIs/ULBs. 76th-95th cycle of reservation extensions, delimitation freezes. 86th adds Article 21A. 91st caps CoM at 15% + closes anti-defection loopholes. 99th NJAC struck down. 100th India-Bangladesh land swap. 101st GST. 102nd-105th NCBC + state OBC tussle. 103rd 10% EWS. 106th Women's Reservation 2023.

period_s12.label: Landmark SC Cases (1994-2024) (1994-2024)
period_s12.subject: history
period_s12.detail: Era of basic-structure refinement. S.R. Bommai 1994 — federalism, secularism, judicial review of Article 356. Vishaka 1997 — workplace harassment. L. Chandra Kumar 1997 — judicial review of tribunals. M. Nagaraj 2006 — promotion reservation conditions. I.R. Coelho 2007 — 9th Schedule open to review post-1973. NJAC 2015 — collegium revived. Puttaswamy 2017 — privacy fundamental right. Triple Talaq, Aadhaar, Section 377 (Navtej), Section 497 (Joseph Shine), Sabarimala — all 2017-18. Article 370 case 2023. Electoral Bonds 2024.

period_s13.label: Constitutional & Statutory Institutions (1992-2023)
period_s13.subject: history
period_s13.detail: Two waves of institution-building. Wave I (1990s-2000s): NCW 1992, NHRC 1993, NCBC 1993, CIC 2005, NCST 2004, NCPCR 2007, NIA 2008, UIDAI 2009. Wave II (2010s-2020s): NGT 2010, Lokpal Act 2013/Lokpal 2014, NITI Aayog Jan 2015 (replaces Planning Commission), GST Council 2016, NCLT/NCLAT 2016, NFRA 2018, CDS Jan 2020. State counterparts: SHRCs, SECs, SFCs.

period_s14.label: Electoral & Criminal Law Reforms (1993-2024)
period_s14.subject: history
period_s14.detail: Multi-member EC 1993 (Seshan era). NOTA 2013, VVPAT 2013 → universal 2019. Aadhaar Act 2016 (Money Bill). Electoral Bonds 2017 → struck down 2024. CEC Appointment Act 2023 replaces SC's Anoop Baranwal mechanism. POTA 2002 → repealed 2004 → UAPA expansion. Three new criminal laws 2023 (BNS, BNSS, BSA) replace IPC, CrPC, Evidence Act 1872 — effective 1 July 2024.

period_s15.label: Economic Reforms I: LPG Architecture (1991-99) (1991-1999)
period_s15.subject: history
period_s15.detail: First-generation reforms 1991-99. Industrial Policy 24 July 1991 abolishes licence raj for most sectors. Rupee devalued 20%. MRTP modified. SEBI made statutory 1992. Capital Issues (Control) Act repealed 1992. FII access 1992. NSE launched 1994. WTO accession 1 Jan 1995. Navaratnas 1997, Mini Ratnas 1997. FEMA 1999 replaces FERA. 8th-9th Five-Year Plans average 6.94% then 5.5% growth. Chelliah Tax Reform Committee.

period_s16.label: Economic Reforms II: New Millennium (2000-13) (2000-2013)
period_s16.subject: history
period_s16.detail: Reform consolidation 2000-13. QR removal April 2001 (WTO compliance). SEZ Act 2005, MGNREGA 2005, RTI 2005. FRBMA 2003. Competition Act 2002, CCI operational 2009. Maharatnas 2010. NFSA 2013, Land Acquisition Act 2013. DBT pilot 2013. 10th-12th Five-Year Plans average 7.6%-7.9%-6.7%. Taper tantrum 2013 — Raghuram Rajan takes RBI charge. Twelfth Plan is the last (post-2017 NITI Aayog 3-year action agendas).

period_s17.label: Economic Reforms III: Modi Era (2014-25) (2014-2026)
period_s17.subject: history
period_s17.detail: Modi-era reforms. Planning Commission abolished 2014; NITI Aayog Jan 2015. Sovereign Gold Bonds 2015. Make in India, Skill India, Digital India 2015. UDAY 2015 (DISCOM debt). Demonetisation Nov 2016. GST Jul 2017. PLI launched 2020 (14 sectors). Atmanirbhar Bharat May 2020 (Rs 20L cr). PMGKAY 2020 + COVID stimulus. PM Gati Shakti 2021. National Logistics Policy 2022. Ease of Doing Business 142→63. Indian economy: 5th largest by 2024 ($3.7T).

period_s18.label: Banking & Financial Sector Reforms (1991-2023)
period_s18.subject: history
period_s18.detail: Banking architecture transformed. Narasimham I 1991 + II 1998 reports drive financial-sector reform. Private bank licences 1993 (HDFC/ICICI/Axis/IndusInd). MPC 2016 — 6 members vote on repo. Flexible inflation targeting (CPI 4±2%) RBI Act amendment 2016. AQR July 2015 — NPA crisis revealed. IBC 2016 + IBBI. PSB mega-mergers 2017-2020 — 27 banks → 12. Bank recapitalisation rounds. Raghuram Rajan, Urjit Patel, Shaktikanta Das.

period_s19.label: Social Justice & Reservation (1990-2023)
period_s19.subject: history
period_s19.detail: Mandal-era reservation politics. Mandal Commission report 1980; implementation Aug 1990 → Indra Sawhney 1992 (50% cap, creamy layer). 77th, 81st, 85th Amendments + 117th Bill on promotion reservation. 27% OBC in higher education from 2007 (93rd Amendment 2005, Ashoka Thakur 2008). 103rd Amendment 2019 — 10% EWS. 102nd/105th NCBC + state OBC powers. SC/ST Atrocities Act 1989. Forest Rights Act 2006 (tribal land). BSP/Kanshi Ram → Mayawati. Dalit identity politics.

period_s20.label: Women's Rights & Gender (1992-2023)
period_s20.subject: history
period_s20.detail: Post-Shah Bano framework. Muslim Women Act 1986 → Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Marriage) Act 2019 (triple talaq). Vishaka 1997 → POSH Act 2013. Domestic Violence Act 2005. Hindu Succession Amendment 2005 — daughters equal coparceners. Beti Bachao Beti Padhao 2015 (declining sex ratio). Nirbhaya Dec 2012 → Criminal Law Amendment 2013 (acid attack, voyeurism, stalking new offences). 33% Women's Reservation Act 2023 (post-delimitation effect).

period_s21.label: Foreign Policy & Diplomacy (1991-2024)
period_s21.subject: history
period_s21.detail: Multi-aligned diplomacy. End of Soviet Union forced reset 1991. Look East Policy 1991 (PV Narasimha Rao) → Act East 2014 (Modi). India-US: Clinton visit March 2000 — first since Carter. Indo-Russian Strategic Agreement 2000. Civil Nuclear Deal 2005-08. India-Israel established 1992; Indo-Pacific framework. SAARC, BIMSTEC, BRICS (2006), SCO (2017). G20 Presidency 2022-23. Permanent UNSC seat bid (G4). Israel-Hamas, Russia-Ukraine balancing 2022+.

period_s22.label: Environment & Climate (1992-2024)
period_s22.subject: history
period_s22.detail: Climate framework era. Earth Summit Rio 1992 → UNFCCC + CBD. Kyoto 1997. India INDC Oct 2015 (Paris). India Updated NDC Aug 2022 — 50% non-fossil capacity, 45% emissions intensity cut by 2030, Net Zero 2070 (Panchamrit). ISA launched 2015 with France. NAPCC 2008 (8 missions: Solar, EE, Habitat, Water, Himalayan, Green India, Agriculture, Knowledge). Biological Diversity Act 2002, NGT 2010, CAMPA 2016, Namami Gange 2014. India 80+ Ramsar sites by 2024.

period_s23.label: Science, Technology & Space (1998-2026)
period_s23.subject: history
period_s23.detail: Pokhran-II 1998 ends nuclear ambiguity. Indo-US Nuclear Deal 2008. ISRO milestones: Chandrayaan-1 (2008, water on Moon), Mangalyaan (2014, Mars first try), Chandrayaan-2 (2019, lander failed), Chandrayaan-3 (Aug 2023, south-pole landing first), Aditya-L1 (2023, Sun observation). National Space Day 23 Aug. National Quantum Mission 2023. Gaganyaan crewed 2026. Private space sector opened 2020 (Skyroot, Pixxel, Agnikul). National Space Policy 2023.

period_s24.label: Digital India & Payments (2008-2024)
period_s24.subject: history
period_s24.detail: Digital revolution. Aadhaar from 2010 onwards. NPCI 2008 → IMPS, RuPay (2012), UPI (2016 → 14B+ monthly transactions by 2024). Digital India 2015 — DigiLocker, MyGov, BharatNet. JAM trinity (Jan Dhan + Aadhaar + Mobile) — DBT backbone for Rs 34L cr. 5G rollout from October 2022 — fastest globally. UPI internationalisation (Singapore, France, UAE). India's Digital Public Infrastructure as G20 export 2023.

period_s25.label: Culture & Heritage (UNESCO) (1993-2024)
period_s25.subject: history
period_s25.detail: UNESCO recognition era. World Heritage Sites: Qutb Minar + Humayun's Tomb (1993), Bhimbetka (2003), CST (2004), Red Fort (2007), Western Ghats (2012), Hill Forts of Rajasthan (2013), Rani ki Vav (2014), Nalanda + Le Corbusier Chandigarh (2016), Ahmedabad first Indian city (2017), Jaipur city (2019), Dholavira + Kakatiya (2021), Santiniketan + Hoysala temples (2023), Charaideo Moidams (2024). UNESCO ICH inscriptions 2008-2023: Kutiyattam, Ramlila, Vedic chanting, Yoga (2016), Kumbh Mela (2017), Durga Puja Kolkata (2021), Garba (2023). GI Act 1999.

pol_linguistic_states.label: Linguistic States
pol_linguistic_states.subject: polity
pol_linguistic_states.detail: Reorganisation of Indian states on the basis of language, primarily after 1956. Initially feared to cause disintegration, but actually made the country more united and administration easier. Some states created on basis of culture, ethnicity, or geography (Nagaland, Jharkhand).

pol_language_policy_india.label: Language Policy of India
pol_language_policy_india.subject: polity
pol_language_policy_india.detail: No national language; Hindi is official language but mother tongue of only 40% Indians. 22 Scheduled Languages recognised. States have own official languages. Government exams can be taken in any scheduled language. Anti-Hindi agitation in Tamil Nadu (1965) led to continued use of English.

pol_civil_rights_movement_us.label: Civil Rights Movement (USA)
pol_civil_rights_movement_us.subject: polity
pol_civil_rights_movement_us.detail: Movement from 1954-1968 aimed at abolishing legal racial discrimination against African-Americans. Led by Martin Luther King Jr., practiced non-violent civil disobedience. Succeeded in gaining equal legal rights. Tommie Smith and John Carlos raised Black Power fists at 1968 Olympics.

pol_black_power_movement.label: Black Power Movement
pol_black_power_movement.subject: polity
pol_black_power_movement.detail: More militant anti-racist movement (1966-1975) advocating even violence if necessary to end racism in the US. Emerged alongside the Civil Rights Movement when progress was seen as too slow.

pol_northern_ireland_conflict.label: Northern Ireland Conflict
pol_northern_ireland_conflict.subject: polity
pol_northern_ireland_conflict.detail: Conflict between Nationalists (mostly Catholics wanting unification with Ireland) and Unionists (mostly Protestants wanting to remain in UK). Example of overlapping social differences (religion, class, nationality) leading to violent civil conflict.

pol_yugoslavia_disintegration.label: Yugoslavia Disintegration
pol_yugoslavia_disintegration.subject: polity
pol_yugoslavia_disintegration.detail: Political leaders in Yugoslavia mobilised populations based on religious and ethnic identity, creating mutual hostility. Demands for separate nation-states led to disintegration of the country and a civil war. Shows how politics of social division can destroy national unity.

pol_bjp.label: Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)
pol_bjp.subject: polity
pol_bjp.detail: Founded in 1980 from former Bharatiya Jana Sangh. Ideology: cultural nationalism, Hindutva. Came to power at centre in 1998 as NDA leader. Became single largest party in India's multi-party system. Support base spread across North and West India.

pol_anti_defection_law.label: Anti-Defection Law
pol_anti_defection_law.subject: polity
pol_anti_defection_law.detail: 52nd Amendment (1985) introduced Tenth Schedule to prevent elected members from switching parties after elections. If a member defects, he/she loses seat. Aimed at reducing political instability and horse-trading. Has reduced but not eliminated defections.

pol_ambedkar.label: Dr B.R. Ambedkar
pol_ambedkar.subject: polity
pol_ambedkar.detail: Chairman of the Drafting Committee of the Constitution. Played a decisive role in shaping the document. Advocated for parliamentary system, fundamental rights for marginalized. Called the 'Father of Indian Constitution'.

pol_adoption_date.label: Adoption of Constitution
pol_adoption_date.subject: polity
pol_adoption_date.detail: Constitution adopted on November 26, 1949 (now celebrated as Constitution Day). Came into effect on January 26, 1950 (Republic Day), chosen to commemorate the Purna Swaraj declaration of 1930.

pol_42nd_amendment.label: 42nd Amendment (1976)
pol_42nd_amendment.subject: polity
pol_42nd_amendment.detail: Called 'Mini-Constitution' due to sweeping changes. Added 'Socialist', 'Secular', 'Integrity' to Preamble. Added Fundamental Duties. Curtailed judicial review. Many provisions reversed by 43rd and 44th Amendments.

pol_election_commission.label: Election Commission of India
pol_election_commission.subject: polity
pol_election_commission.detail: Independent constitutional body under Article 324. Supervises, directs and controls elections. Currently has CEC + 2 ECs. CEC can only be removed by impeachment (same as SC judge). Prepares electoral rolls, monitors model code of conduct.

pol_supreme_court.label: Supreme Court of India
pol_supreme_court.subject: polity
pol_supreme_court.detail: Apex court of the Indian judicial system established under Part V, Chapter IV of the Constitution. Has original, appellate, advisory, and writ jurisdictions. Its decisions are binding on all courts in India. Can review its own judgments under Article 137. All authorities must act in aid of the Supreme Court under Article 144.

pol_high_courts.label: High Courts
pol_high_courts.subject: polity
pol_high_courts.detail: Each state or group of states has a High Court. High Courts can issue writs under Article 226 (wider scope than SC as they cover any other purpose beyond fundamental rights). Exercise superintendence over all subordinate courts. Hear appeals from district courts.

pol_hussainara_khatoon.label: Hussainara Khatoon vs. Bihar (1979)
pol_hussainara_khatoon.subject: polity
pol_hussainara_khatoon.detail: One of the earliest PILs. Filed on behalf of under-trial prisoners in Bihar who had spent more time in jail than the maximum punishment for their alleged offences. Established right to speedy trial as a fundamental right under Article 21.

pol_kesavananda_bharati.label: Kesavananda Bharati Case (1973)
pol_kesavananda_bharati.subject: polity
pol_kesavananda_bharati.detail: Landmark 13-judge bench case that established the Basic Structure Doctrine. Ruled that Parliament can amend any part of Constitution but cannot destroy its basic structure. Right to property was held not part of basic structure. Court reserved to itself the right to decide what constitutes basic structure. Most important case in Indian constitutional law.

pol_district_courts.label: District and Subordinate Courts
pol_district_courts.subject: polity
pol_district_courts.detail: Lowest level in the judicial hierarchy. District courts deal with cases arising in the district, consider appeals from subordinate courts, and decide serious criminal offences. Subordinate courts handle civil and criminal cases at the lowest level. Function under superintendence and control of the High Court.

pol_bandhua_mukti_morcha.label: Bandhua Mukti Morcha vs. Union of India (1984)
pol_bandhua_mukti_morcha.subject: polity
pol_bandhua_mukti_morcha.detail: Important PIL case decided by Justice Bhagwati. Addressed the issue of bonded labour. Court held that problems of the poor need a different kind of judicial approach and strict adversarial procedure would prevent them from enforcing fundamental rights. Expanded locus standi for public interest cases.

pol_sunil_batra.label: Sunil Batra vs. Delhi Administration (1980)
pol_sunil_batra.subject: polity
pol_sunil_batra.detail: Pioneer PIL case. A Tihar jail inmate sent a scribbled letter to Justice Krishna Iyer about physical torture of prisoners. The judge got it converted into a petition. Established that even a letter can be treated as a writ petition if it concerns violation of fundamental rights.

pol_sarkaria_commission.label: Sarkaria Commission Report (1988)
pol_sarkaria_commission.subject: polity
pol_sarkaria_commission.detail: Commission on Centre-State Relations set up 1983, submitted report 1988. Chaired by former SC Justice R.S. Sarkaria. 247 recommendations on legislative, financial, administrative relations. Key: restrain Article 356, strengthen Inter-State Council, residuary powers. Many implemented gradually.

pol_states_reorganisation_commission.label: States Reorganisation Commission (1954)
pol_states_reorganisation_commission.subject: polity
pol_states_reorganisation_commission.detail: Set up in 1954 to examine the question of reorganisation of states. Recommended creation of linguistic states at least for major linguistic groups. Led to the States Reorganisation Act, 1956. Marked the beginning of the process of creating states on linguistic basis.

pol_armed_forces_special_powers.label: Armed Forces Special Powers Act (AFSPA)
pol_armed_forces_special_powers.subject: polity
pol_armed_forces_special_powers.detail: Made on the basis of Articles 33 and 34 which authorize Parliament to protect persons in service of union or state for actions during martial law. Has created tensions between people and armed forces in some regions. A manifestation of Union powers that can override normal federal arrangements in areas of conflict.

pol_pk_thungon_committee.label: P.K. Thungon Committee (1989)
pol_pk_thungon_committee.subject: polity
pol_pk_thungon_committee.detail: Recommended constitutional recognition for local government bodies in 1989. Advocated periodic elections to local bodies and enlistment of appropriate functions along with funds. Its recommendations formed the basis for the 73rd and 74th Constitutional Amendment bills introduced in 1989.

pol_community_development_1952.label: Community Development Programme (1952)
pol_community_development_1952.subject: polity
pol_community_development_1952.detail: Launched in 1952 to promote people participation in local development across a range of activities. Led to the recommendation of a three-tier Panchayati Raj system for rural areas. First systematic attempt at involving local communities in development planning in independent India.

pol_43rd_44th_amendments.label: 43rd and 44th Amendments (1977-78)
pol_43rd_44th_amendments.subject: polity
pol_43rd_44th_amendments.detail: Passed after Janata Party came to power in 1977. Cancelled most controversial changes made by the 38th, 39th and 42nd amendments. Restored constitutional balance. 44th Amendment specifically: restored Lok Sabha term to 5 years, removed right to property from fundamental rights (made it legal right under Art 300A), strengthened safeguards against misuse of emergency provisions.

pol_52nd_amendment.label: 52nd Amendment -- Anti-Defection (1985)
pol_52nd_amendment.subject: polity
pol_52nd_amendment.detail: Added the Tenth Schedule to the Constitution dealing with disqualification of members on grounds of defection. A member who voluntarily gives up membership of the party or votes against party whip is disqualified. Decision rests with the Speaker/Chairman. Later modified by 91st Amendment (2003). Example of amendment through political consensus.

pol_minerva_mills_case.label: Minerva Mills Case (1980)
pol_minerva_mills_case.subject: polity
pol_minerva_mills_case.detail: Supreme Court reaffirmed the basic structure doctrine from Kesavananda Bharati. Struck down provisions of the 42nd Amendment that attempted to override judicial review. Held that the balance between fundamental rights and directive principles is itself part of the basic structure. Established that limited amending power is a basic feature of the Constitution.

pol_article_74_amendment.label: Amendment on Binding Nature of Council of Ministers Advice
pol_article_74_amendment.subject: polity
pol_article_74_amendment.detail: Article 74(1) was amended to clarify that the advice of the Council of Ministers will be binding on the President (President shall act in accordance with the advice). In reality, this was already the practice in parliamentary government. The amendment was only by way of explanation, making explicit what was implicit in the original Constitution.

pol_38th_39th_amendments.label: 38th and 39th Amendments (1975)
pol_38th_39th_amendments.subject: polity
pol_38th_39th_amendments.detail: Controversial amendments passed during the Emergency period. The 38th Amendment made the declaration of Emergency non-justiciable. The 39th Amendment placed the election of the President, Vice President, Prime Minister and Speaker beyond judicial scrutiny. Both were later largely reversed by the 43rd and 44th Amendments after the Emergency ended.

pol_udhr.label: Universal Declaration of Human Rights
pol_udhr.subject: polity
pol_udhr.detail: Adopted by UN General Assembly in 1948. 30 articles covering civil, political, economic, social, and cultural rights. Not legally binding but morally authoritative. Inspired national constitutions and international covenants.

pol_cuban_missile_crisis.label: Cuban Missile Crisis
pol_cuban_missile_crisis.subject: polity
pol_cuban_missile_crisis.detail: In 1962, the USSR placed nuclear missiles in Cuba, putting the US mainland under threat from close range. President Kennedy ordered a naval blockade. The crisis was the closest the Cold War came to nuclear war. Soviet ships turned back, averting catastrophe.

pol_nato.label: North Atlantic Treaty Organisation (NATO)
pol_nato.subject: polity
pol_nato.detail: Western military alliance formed in April 1949 with 12 member states. An armed attack on any member in Europe or North America was regarded as an attack on all. Led by the US. Continues to exist post-Cold War.

pol_warsaw_pact.label: Warsaw Pact
pol_warsaw_pact.subject: polity
pol_warsaw_pact.detail: Eastern military alliance led by the Soviet Union, created in 1955 to counter NATO forces in Europe. Included most East European communist states. Dissolved after the Cold War ended.

pol_seato.label: Southeast Asian Treaty Organisation (SEATO)
pol_seato.subject: polity
pol_seato.detail: US-led alliance in Southeast Asia, formed in 1954 as part of Cold War containment strategy. Aimed to prevent the spread of communism. Less effective than NATO, dissolved in 1977.

pol_cento.label: Central Treaty Organisation (CENTO)
pol_cento.subject: polity
pol_cento.detail: Originally the Baghdad Pact (1955), a US-backed alliance in West Asia. Included UK, Turkey, Iran, Iraq, and Pakistan. Dissolved in 1979 after the Iranian Revolution.

pol_nam.label: Non-Aligned Movement (NAM)
pol_nam.subject: polity
pol_nam.detail: Movement of newly decolonised countries choosing not to join either Cold War bloc. First summit in Belgrade 1961 with 25 members. Founded by Tito, Nehru, Nasser, Sukarno, and Nkrumah. Not isolationism or neutrality but active involvement in world affairs. Had 116 members by 2006.

pol_tito.label: Josip Broz Tito
pol_tito.subject: polity
pol_tito.detail: President of Yugoslavia (1945-80). One of five founders of NAM. Communist leader who maintained independence from the Soviet Union. Key meeting with Nehru and Nasser in 1956 led to NAM.

pol_nasser.label: Gamal Abdel Nasser
pol_nasser.subject: polity
pol_nasser.detail: Ruler of Egypt (1952-70). One of five founders of NAM. Championed Arab nationalism, socialism, and anti-imperialism. Nationalised the Suez Canal in 1956.

pol_nkrumah.label: Kwame Nkrumah
pol_nkrumah.subject: polity
pol_nkrumah.detail: First Prime Minister of Ghana (1952-66). One of five founders of NAM. Advocated socialism and African unity. Opposed neo-colonialism. Removed in a military coup.

pol_unctad.label: UNCTAD
pol_unctad.subject: polity
pol_unctad.detail: UN Conference on Trade and Development. Published 1972 report proposing reforms to make global trade beneficial for poorer countries. Institutional basis for NIEO demands.

pol_ltbt.label: Limited Test Ban Treaty (LTBT)
pol_ltbt.subject: polity
pol_ltbt.detail: Signed in 1963 by US, UK, and USSR. Banned nuclear weapon tests in the atmosphere, outer space, and under water. One of the first major arms control agreements of the Cold War.

pol_npt.label: Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty (NPT)
pol_npt.subject: polity
pol_npt.detail: Signed 1968, in force 1970. Only five states that tested before 1967 may keep nuclear weapons. Extended indefinitely in 1995. India has not signed, considering it discriminatory.

pol_abm_treaty.label: Anti-Ballistic Missile (ABM) Treaty
pol_abm_treaty.subject: polity
pol_abm_treaty.detail: Part of SALT-I, signed 1972. Limited deployment of ABM systems, preventing their use as defensive shield to launch nuclear attacks. Maintained strategic stability.

pol_korean_war.label: Korean War
pol_korean_war.subject: polity
pol_korean_war.detail: War 1950-53 between North Korea (backed by USSR and China) and South Korea (backed by US-led UN forces). Ended with division along 38th Parallel. Nehru played key mediating role.

pol_gorbachev.label: Mikhail Gorbachev
pol_gorbachev.subject: polity
pol_gorbachev.detail: Last leader of the Soviet Union (1985-91). Introduced perestroika (restructuring) and glasnost (openness). Stopped the arms race with the US, withdrew troops from Afghanistan. His reforms inadvertently accelerated the disintegration of the USSR.

pol_perestroika.label: Perestroika and Glasnost
pol_perestroika.subject: polity
pol_perestroika.detail: Reform policies introduced by Gorbachev. Perestroika meant economic restructuring to modernise the Soviet economy. Glasnost meant political openness allowing freedom of expression. Together they loosened the system but set in motion forces that led to the USSR's collapse.

pol_berlin_wall_fall.label: Fall of the Berlin Wall (9 November 1989)
pol_berlin_wall_fall.stage: Parallel — End of Cold War & Post-Soviet Russia
pol_berlin_wall_fall.subject: polity
pol_berlin_wall_fall.detail: Berlin Wall (built 1961) opened 9 November 1989 after East German government announced free travel to West Germany. Symbolic end of Cold War and division of Europe. Led to German reunification (3 October 1990) and collapse of communist regimes in Eastern Europe.

pol_baltic_independence.label: Baltic States Independence
pol_baltic_independence.subject: polity
pol_baltic_independence.detail: Estonia, Latvia, and Lithuania were the first Soviet republics to declare independence. Lithuania declared independence in March 1990. All three became UN members in September 1991 and later joined NATO in 2004 and the EU.

pol_asean.label: Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN)
pol_asean.subject: polity
pol_asean.detail: Established in 1967 by Indonesia, Malaysia, Philippines, Singapore, and Thailand (Bangkok Declaration). Later joined by Brunei, Vietnam, Laos, Myanmar, and Cambodia (10 members). Follows the ASEAN Way: informal, non-confrontationist, cooperative. Established ASEAN Regional Forum (ARF) in 1994.

pol_china_sez.label: China's Special Economic Zones (SEZs)
pol_china_sez.subject: polity
pol_china_sez.detail: Zones where trade barriers were eliminated and foreign investors could set up enterprises. State played central role in setting up market economy. Led to phenomenal rise in foreign trade and FDI. China has 6 SEZs compared to India's 200+ approved SEZs.

pol_four_modernisations.label: Four Modernisations
pol_four_modernisations.subject: polity
pol_four_modernisations.detail: Proposed by Premier Zhou Enlai in 1973: modernisation of agriculture, industry, science and technology, and military. Laid the groundwork for Deng Xiaoping's subsequent economic reforms.

pol_india_china_relations.label: India-China Relations
pol_india_china_relations.subject: polity
pol_india_china_relations.detail: Border conflict in 1962 over Arunachal Pradesh and Aksai Chin had long-term implications. Relations improved after Rajiv Gandhi's 1988 visit. Bilateral trade grew from $338 million (1992) to $18 billion (2006). Both view themselves as rising powers. Boundary talks continue.

pol_japan_power.label: Japan as Economic Power
pol_japan_power.subject: polity
pol_japan_power.detail: Second largest economy in the world. Only Asian member of G-8. Second largest contributor to UN budget (nearly 20%). Security alliance with US since 1951. Article 9 of constitution renounces war. Despite low military spending (1% of GDP), fourth largest military expenditure globally.

pol_us_china_relations_1972.label: US-China Relations (1972)
pol_us_china_relations_1972.subject: polity
pol_us_china_relations_1972.detail: China ended political and economic isolation by establishing relations with the US in 1972 when President Nixon visited China. This was a major shift in Cold War dynamics and preceded China's economic reforms.

pol_indus_waters_treaty.label: Indus Waters Treaty
pol_indus_waters_treaty.subject: polity
pol_indus_waters_treaty.detail: Signed in 1960 between India and Pakistan with World Bank mediation. Governs sharing of rivers of the Indus basin. Has survived all military conflicts between the two countries. Minor differences on interpretation remain.

pol_saarc.label: South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC)
pol_saarc.subject: polity
pol_saarc.detail: Regional cooperation initiative begun in 1985, headquartered in Kathmandu. Has not had much success due to persisting political differences, especially India-Pakistan tensions. Members signed SAFTA agreement for free trade zone.

pol_india_bangladesh_relations.label: India-Bangladesh Relations
pol_india_bangladesh_relations.subject: polity
pol_india_bangladesh_relations.detail: Differences over Ganga and Brahmaputra water sharing, illegal immigration, and Bangladesh's refusal to allow Indian troop transit to northeast. Farakka Treaty signed in 1996. Bangladesh part of India's Look East policy. Cooperation on disaster management improved.

pol_india_sri_lanka_relations.label: India-Sri Lanka Relations
pol_india_sri_lanka_relations.subject: polity
pol_india_sri_lanka_relations.detail: Tensions over Tamil ethnic conflict. India sent IPKF in 1987 (withdrew 1989). Adopted policy of disengagement after IPKF failure. Free trade agreement signed. India's post-tsunami reconstruction aid improved ties.

pol_shimla_agreement.label: Shimla Agreement
pol_shimla_agreement.subject: polity
pol_shimla_agreement.detail: Signed in 1972 between India and Pakistan after the 1971 war. Established that all issues between the two countries would be resolved bilaterally through peaceful means. Established the Line of Control in Kashmir.

pol_ipkf.label: Indian Peace Keeping Force (IPKF)
pol_ipkf.subject: polity
pol_ipkf.detail: Indian troops sent to Sri Lanka in 1987 under an Indo-Sri Lanka accord to stabilise Tamil-Sinhala relations. Got into conflict with LTTE. Sri Lankans saw it as interference. Withdrew in 1989-90 without achieving objectives.

pol_maldives_1988.label: India's Intervention in Maldives
pol_maldives_1988.subject: polity
pol_maldives_1988.detail: In November 1988, Tamil mercenaries from Sri Lanka attacked the Maldives. Indian air force and navy responded quickly to Maldives' request, stopping the invasion. India has contributed to the island's economic development.

pol_1971_bangladesh_war.label: Bangladesh Liberation War
pol_1971_bangladesh_war.subject: polity
pol_1971_bangladesh_war.detail: In 1971, East Pakistan's demand for autonomy under Sheikh Mujib was crushed by Pakistani military. India supported independence movement financially and militarily. War in December 1971 ended with Pakistani surrender and creation of Bangladesh.

pol_iaea.label: International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA)
pol_iaea.subject: polity
pol_iaea.detail: Established in 1957 to implement US President Eisenhower's Atoms for Peace proposal. Promotes peaceful use of nuclear energy and prevents military use. Teams regularly inspect nuclear facilities worldwide.

pol_bwc.label: Biological Weapons Convention (BWC)
pol_bwc.subject: polity
pol_bwc.detail: Signed in 1972. Banned the production and possession of biological weapons. Over 155 states acceded. Included all great powers. One of the key disarmament treaties alongside CWC.

pol_montreal_protocol.label: Montreal Protocol
pol_montreal_protocol.subject: polity
