pol_montreal_protocol.detail: 1987 path-breaking agreement to protect the ozone layer by phasing out ozone-depleting substances like CFCs. Discovery of ozone hole over Antarctica in mid-1980s provided urgency. Considered one of the most successful environmental agreements.

pol_hyderabad_integration.label: Integration of Hyderabad
pol_hyderabad_integration.subject: polity
pol_hyderabad_integration.detail: The Nizam of Hyderabad wanted independent status. After a peoples movement in the Telangana region and the Nizam refusal to accede, Indian army conducted Operation Polo in September 1948 to integrate the state.

pol_junagadh_integration.label: Integration of Junagadh
pol_junagadh_integration.subject: polity
pol_junagadh_integration.detail: Junagadh was a small state in Gujarat whose Muslim ruler acceded to Pakistan despite having an overwhelmingly Hindu population. India conducted a plebiscite in which people voted to join India.

pol_manipur_integration.label: Integration of Manipur
pol_manipur_integration.subject: polity
pol_manipur_integration.detail: Manipur Maharaja Bodhchandra Singh signed the Instrument of Accession under pressure in 1949. The state had a democratically elected legislature which was not consulted, generating resentment among the people.

pol_states_reorganisation.label: States Reorganisation Act (1956)
pol_states_reorganisation.subject: polity
pol_states_reorganisation.detail: Following the States Reorganisation Commission (SRC) report of 1955, India reorganised its internal boundaries along linguistic lines in 1956. Preceded by formation of Andhra Pradesh in 1953 after Potti Sriramulu death. Created the modern map of Indian states.

pol_gandhi_assassination.label: Assassination of Mahatma Gandhi
pol_gandhi_assassination.subject: polity
pol_gandhi_assassination.detail: Mahatma Gandhi was assassinated on 30 January 1948 by Nathuram Godse, a Hindu extremist opposed to Gandhi pursuit of Hindu-Muslim unity. Gandhi death had a dramatic effect -- communal violence subsided, RSS was briefly banned, and communal politics lost appeal.

pol_rss_ban_1948.label: RSS Ban (1948)
pol_rss_ban_1948.subject: polity
pol_rss_ban_1948.detail: After Gandhi assassination, the Government cracked down on organisations spreading communal hatred. The RSS was banned for some time. Part of the broader effort to contain communal politics after Partition violence.

pol_first_general_election.label: First General Election (1952)
pol_first_general_election.subject: polity
pol_first_general_election.detail: India's first general election held October 1951 to February 1952 was the biggest gamble in democratic history. 17 crore eligible voters (only 15% literate) elected 489 Lok Sabha MPs and 3200+ MLAs. Election Commission under Sukumar Sen conducted it. Over half the eligible voters turned out, proving democracy could work in a poor nation.

pol_socialist_party.label: Socialist Party
pol_socialist_party.subject: polity
pol_socialist_party.detail: Originated from Congress Socialist Party (CSP) formed in 1934. Forced to separate in 1948 when Congress banned dual membership. Leaders included Jayaprakash Narayan, Rammanohar Lohia, Acharya Narendra Dev, Asoka Mehta. Advocated democratic socialism but faced a dilemma when Congress declared socialist pattern as its goal in 1955.

pol_cpi.label: Communist Party of India (CPI)
pol_cpi.subject: polity
pol_cpi.detail: Emerged in 1920s inspired by Bolshevik revolution. Won 16 seats in 1952, becoming largest opposition party. In 1957, CPI-led government in Kerala became the world's first democratically elected Communist government. Split in 1964 into CPI and CPI(M) following the Sino-Soviet rift.

pol_kerala_communist_govt.label: Communist Government in Kerala (1957)
pol_kerala_communist_govt.subject: polity
pol_kerala_communist_govt.detail: E.M.S. Namboodiripad led CPI to victory in Kerala in 1957 -- the world's first democratically elected Communist government. Won 60 of 126 seats. Congress launched a 'liberation struggle' against it. In 1959, central government dismissed it under Article 356 -- widely cited as first misuse of emergency powers.

pol_bharatiya_jana_sangh.label: Bharatiya Jana Sangh
pol_bharatiya_jana_sangh.subject: polity
pol_bharatiya_jana_sangh.detail: Founded in 1951 by Shyama Prasad Mukherjee. Drew ideological inspiration from RSS. Emphasised one country, one culture, one nation and called for a uniform civil code. Initially limited to Hindi-speaking states and urban areas. Later merged into Janata Party in 1977 and its members formed BJP in 1980.

pol_swatantra_party.label: Swatantra Party
pol_swatantra_party.subject: polity
pol_swatantra_party.detail: Founded in 1959 by C. Rajagopalachari (Rajaji). First explicitly right-wing party, advocating free enterprise, opposing state intervention, planning and nationalisation. Drew support from former princes, landlords and industrialists.

pol_shyama_prasad_mukherjee.label: Shyama Prasad Mukherjee
pol_shyama_prasad_mukherjee.subject: polity
pol_shyama_prasad_mukherjee.detail: Founder of Bharatiya Jana Sangh in 1951. Member of Nehru's first cabinet, resigned over the Nehru-Liaquat Pact. Opposed Article 370 granting special status to J&K. Died in 1953 while in detention in Kashmir.

pol_cpi_split_1964.label: CPI Split (1964)
pol_cpi_split_1964.subject: polity
pol_cpi_split_1964.detail: The Communist Party of India split in 1964 following the Sino-Soviet ideological rift and the India-China war of 1962. The pro-USSR faction remained as CPI. The pro-China faction formed CPI(M). Many CPI(M) leaders were arrested as pro-China.

pol_ems_namboodiripad.label: E.M.S. Namboodiripad
pol_ems_namboodiripad.subject: polity
pol_ems_namboodiripad.detail: Leader of the Communist Party in Kerala who became Chief Minister in 1957, heading the world's first democratically elected Communist government. Initiated radical land reforms. His government was dismissed under Article 356 in 1959.

pol_sukumar_sen.label: Sukumar Sen
pol_sukumar_sen.subject: polity
pol_sukumar_sen.detail: First Chief Election Commissioner of India appointed in January 1950. Organised the mammoth first general election of 1952 with 17 crore voters. Trained over 3 lakh officers and devised the ballot-box-per-candidate system for largely illiterate voters.

pol_rajagopalachari.label: C. Rajagopalachari (Rajaji)
pol_rajagopalachari.subject: polity
pol_rajagopalachari.detail: Last Governor-General of India, senior Congress leader, and founder of the Swatantra Party in 1959. Opposed Congress socialist policies, especially state controls and the License Raj. Advocated free enterprise as the path to prosperity.

pol_avadi_resolution.label: Avadi Resolution (1955)
pol_avadi_resolution.subject: polity
pol_avadi_resolution.detail: At its session in Avadi near Madras, Congress passed a resolution declaring socialist pattern of society as its goal. Reflected in the Second Five Year Plan. Made it difficult for the Socialist Party to differentiate itself from Congress.

pol_public_sector.label: Public Sector Development
pol_public_sector.subject: polity
pol_public_sector.detail: State controlled key heavy industries -- steel plants, oil refineries, defence production, railways, electricity. Created commanding heights of the economy. Critics said it bred inefficiency, corruption through license-permit raj, and created a privileged middle class.

pol_import_substitution.label: Import Substitution Strategy
pol_import_substitution.subject: polity
pol_import_substitution.detail: India's development strategy emphasised producing domestically what was being imported. Substantial tariffs imposed on imports to protect domestic industries. Limited India's economic interaction with the outside world but helped domestic industries grow.

pol_kn_raj.label: K.N. Raj
pol_kn_raj.subject: polity
pol_kn_raj.detail: Young economist involved in drafting the First Five Year Plan. Argued that India should hasten slowly for the first two decades as fast development might endanger democracy.

pol_charan_singh.label: Chaudhary Charan Singh
pol_charan_singh.subject: polity
pol_charan_singh.detail: Congress leader who later broke away to form Bharatiya Lok Dal. Forcefully articulated the case for agriculture-centred planning. Argued planning created urban-industrial prosperity at the expense of farmers. Later became PM briefly in 1979.

pol_jc_kumarappa.label: J.C. Kumarappa
pol_jc_kumarappa.subject: polity
pol_jc_kumarappa.detail: Gandhian economist who proposed an alternative blueprint emphasising rural industrialisation. Author of Economy of Permanence. Member of the Planning Commission but his views represented the minority position.

pol_panchsheel.label: Panchsheel (Five Principles of Peaceful Coexistence)
pol_panchsheel.subject: polity
pol_panchsheel.detail: Five principles enunciated jointly by PM Nehru and Chinese Premier Zhou Enlai on 29 April 1954: mutual respect for territorial integrity, mutual non-aggression, mutual non-interference, equality and mutual benefit, and peaceful coexistence. Ironically preceded the India-China border conflict.

pol_india_china_war_1962.label: India-China War (1962)
pol_india_china_war_1962.subject: polity
pol_india_china_war_1962.detail: China launched a massive invasion in October 1962 on both Aksai-chin (Ladakh) and NEFA (Arunachal Pradesh). India suffered a humiliating defeat. Led to V.K. Krishna Menon's resignation as Defence Minister, a no-confidence motion against Nehru, and the CPI split. India approached US and UK for military help.

pol_bandung_conference.label: Bandung Conference (1955)
pol_bandung_conference.subject: polity
pol_bandung_conference.detail: Afro-Asian conference held in Bandung, Indonesia in 1955. Marked the zenith of India's engagement with newly independent Asian and African nations. Later led to the establishment of the Non-Aligned Movement. India was a key participant under Nehru's leadership.

pol_indo_pak_war_1965.label: Indo-Pakistan War (1965)
pol_indo_pak_war_1965.subject: polity
pol_indo_pak_war_1965.detail: Pakistan launched armed attacks in Rann of Kutch (April 1965) followed by a bigger offensive in J&K (August-September). PM Shastri ordered counter-offensive on Punjab border; Indian army reached close to Lahore. Ended with Tashkent Agreement brokered by USSR in January 1966.

pol_bangladesh_war_1971.label: Bangladesh War (1971)
pol_bangladesh_war_1971.subject: polity
pol_bangladesh_war_1971.detail: India intervened in East Pakistan after Pakistani army's crackdown on Bengali population. About 80 lakh refugees fled to India. India signed Treaty of Peace and Friendship with USSR. War lasted 13 days; 90,000 Pakistani soldiers surrendered. Bangladesh was created. Shimla Agreement signed July 1972.

pol_tashkent_agreement.label: Tashkent Agreement (1966)
pol_tashkent_agreement.subject: polity
pol_tashkent_agreement.detail: Peace agreement between India (PM Shastri) and Pakistan (Gen Ayub Khan) brokered by Soviet Union to end the 1965 war. Signed in January 1966. PM Shastri died in Tashkent immediately after signing the agreement, leading to the second succession crisis in India.

pol_nuclear_test_1974.label: India's First Nuclear Test (1974)
pol_nuclear_test_1974.subject: polity
pol_nuclear_test_1974.detail: India conducted its first nuclear explosion in May 1974 at Pokhran, termed a 'peaceful explosion'. India's nuclear programme was initiated in the late 1940s under Homi J. Bhabha. India opposed the NPT of 1968 as discriminatory. The test came during a period of domestic economic crisis.

pol_tibet_issue.label: Tibet and Dalai Lama
pol_tibet_issue.subject: polity
pol_tibet_issue.detail: China took control of Tibet in 1950. India conceded China's claim over Tibet through Panchsheel (1954). In 1959, after armed uprising against Chinese occupation, the Dalai Lama fled to India and was granted asylum. This strained India-China relations and contributed to the 1962 war.

pol_indo_soviet_treaty.label: Indo-Soviet Treaty of Friendship (1971)
pol_indo_soviet_treaty.subject: polity
pol_indo_soviet_treaty.detail: 20-year Treaty of Peace and Friendship signed with the Soviet Union in August 1971, to counter the US-Pakistan-China axis before the Bangladesh war. Assured India of Soviet support against attack. Questioned India's non-aligned credentials but was seen as strategic necessity.

pol_shastri_pm.label: Lal Bahadur Shastri as PM
pol_shastri_pm.subject: polity
pol_shastri_pm.detail: PM from 1964 to 1966 after Nehru's death. Known for simplicity and principles -- had earlier resigned as Railway Minister accepting moral responsibility for a railway accident. Coined the slogan 'Jai Jawan Jai Kisan'. Led India through the 1965 war with Pakistan. Died in Tashkent in January 1966.

pol_indira_gandhi_rise.label: Rise of Indira Gandhi
pol_indira_gandhi_rise.subject: polity
pol_indira_gandhi_rise.detail: Became PM in 1966 after defeating Morarji Desai in a secret ballot among Congress MPs. Daughter of Nehru but initially seen as a political novice. Senior leaders (the Syndicate) backed her expecting she would be pliable. She gradually asserted independence and sidelined the old guard.

pol_1967_elections.label: Fourth General Elections (1967)
pol_1967_elections.subject: polity
pol_1967_elections.detail: A landmark election described as a 'political earthquake'. Congress won Lok Sabha with its lowest tally since 1952. Lost power in 9 states including UP, Bihar, Punjab, West Bengal, Kerala. DMK won Tamil Nadu with a clear majority -- first non-Congress party to do so. Marked the beginning of coalition politics.

pol_congress_split_1969.label: Congress Split (1969)
pol_congress_split_1969.subject: polity
pol_congress_split_1969.detail: Indira Gandhi's conflict with the Syndicate came to a head during the 1969 Presidential election. Indira supported V.V. Giri against the Syndicate's candidate Sanjeeva Reddy. Congress split into Congress(R) led by Indira and Congress(O) led by the Syndicate. Indira projected it as a socialist vs conservative divide.

pol_1971_election.label: 1971 Lok Sabha Election
pol_1971_election.subject: polity
pol_1971_election.detail: Congress(R)-CPI alliance won 375 seats (Congress(R) alone won 352) with 48.4% votes. The Grand Alliance of opposition parties (SSP, PSP, Jana Sangh, Swatantra, BKD) was a grand failure with less than 40 seats combined. Congress(O) won only 16 seats. Restored Congress dominance under Indira.

pol_bank_nationalisation.label: Bank Nationalisation (1969)
pol_bank_nationalisation.subject: polity
pol_bank_nationalisation.detail: Indira Gandhi nationalised 14 leading private banks in July 1969 as part of her Left-oriented policy push. This was a popular move that gave the government control over credit allocation. It was part of her strategy to build independence from the Syndicate and demonstrate socialist credentials.

pol_privy_purse_abolition.label: Abolition of Privy Purse
pol_privy_purse_abolition.subject: polity
pol_privy_purse_abolition.detail: Privy purse was the government allowance given to former princely rulers after integration. Indira Gandhi pushed for abolition as it contradicted constitutional principles of equality. First attempt failed in Rajya Sabha and was struck down by Supreme Court. Succeeded through constitutional amendment after 1971 election victory.

pol_devaluation_1966.label: Rupee Devaluation (1966)
pol_devaluation_1966.subject: polity
pol_devaluation_1966.detail: One of Indira Gandhi's first decisions as PM was to devalue the Indian rupee under pressure from the US. Dollar price went from less than Rs 5 to more than Rs 7. Added to economic difficulties and public resentment. Was a politically unpopular move.

pol_kamraj.label: K. Kamraj
pol_kamraj.subject: polity
pol_kamraj.detail: Congress President and former Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu. Leader of the Syndicate. Proposed the 'Kamraj Plan' in 1963 where senior Congressmen should resign from office to make way for younger workers. Played kingmaker role in choosing both Shastri and Indira as PM.

pol_morarji_desai.label: Morarji Desai
pol_morarji_desai.subject: polity
pol_morarji_desai.detail: Former Chief Minister of Bombay state and Indira's main rival. Deputy PM and Finance Minister but left after differences over bank nationalisation. Led Congress(O) after the split. Later became PM heading the Janata Party government in 1977.

pol_ten_point_programme.label: Ten Point Programme (1967)
pol_ten_point_programme.subject: polity
pol_ten_point_programme.detail: Adopted by the Congress Working Committee in May 1967 at Indira Gandhi's initiative. Included social control of banks, nationalisation of general insurance, ceiling on urban property and income, public distribution of food grains, land reforms. Gave government policy a Left orientation.

pol_emergency_1975.label: Emergency (1975-77)
pol_emergency_1975.subject: polity
pol_emergency_1975.detail: On 25 June 1975, PM Indira Gandhi declared internal Emergency under Article 352 on grounds of internal disturbances. Fundamental Rights suspended, press censored, opposition leaders arrested, RSS and Jamaat-e-Islami banned. About 1 lakh 11 thousand arrested under preventive detention. Lasted 18 months.

pol_jp_movement.label: JP Movement (Total Revolution)
pol_jp_movement.subject: polity
pol_jp_movement.detail: In 1974, students in Bihar invited Jayaprakash Narayan to lead their movement against rising prices, corruption and unemployment. JP demanded dismissal of Bihar government and called for 'Total Revolution' (Sampoorna Kranti). In 1975, he led a massive peoples march to Parliament and asked army/police to disobey illegal orders.

pol_jayaprakash_narayan.label: Jayaprakash Narayan (JP)
pol_jayaprakash_narayan.subject: polity
pol_jayaprakash_narayan.detail: Marxist in youth, founder of Congress Socialist Party, hero of 1942 Quit India movement. Declined to join Nehru's cabinet. After 1955, became Gandhian involved in Bhoodan movement. Led Bihar movement in 1974, became symbol of opposition to Emergency, and was the moving force behind the Janata Party.

pol_allahabad_hc_verdict.label: Allahabad High Court Verdict (1975)
pol_allahabad_hc_verdict.subject: polity
pol_allahabad_hc_verdict.detail: On 12 June 1975, Justice Jagmohan Lal Sinha declared Indira Gandhi's election to Lok Sabha invalid on a petition by Raj Narain. She was found to have used government servants in her campaign. Supreme Court granted partial stay. This verdict was the immediate trigger for the declaration of Emergency.

pol_naxalite_movement.label: Naxalite Movement
pol_naxalite_movement.subject: polity
pol_naxalite_movement.detail: Began in 1967 with peasant uprising in Naxalbari (Darjeeling, West Bengal). CPI(ML) formed in 1969 under Charu Majumdar. Argued Indian democracy was a sham and adopted strategy of protracted guerrilla warfare. Spread to many states. About 75 districts in 9 states affected by Naxalite violence.

pol_railway_strike_1974.label: Railway Strike (1974)
pol_railway_strike_1974.subject: polity
pol_railway_strike_1974.detail: National strike by railway employees led by George Fernandes demanding bonus and better service conditions. Government declared it illegal, arrested leaders, deployed territorial army. Strike called off after 20 days without settlement. Added to atmosphere of labour unrest before Emergency.

pol_gujarat_movement.label: Gujarat Movement (1974)
pol_gujarat_movement.subject: polity
pol_gujarat_movement.detail: Student agitation in January 1974 against rising prices of food and cooking oil, and corruption. Joined by opposition parties. Led to President's Rule in Gujarat. Morarji Desai went on indefinite fast demanding fresh elections. Congress was defeated in the subsequent Gujarat election in June 1975.

pol_janata_party.label: Janata Party
pol_janata_party.subject: polity
pol_janata_party.detail: Formed in 1977 by merging opposition parties (Congress(O), Jana Sangh, BLD, Socialist Party) under JP's leadership for the post-Emergency elections. Won 330 seats in 1977 election, defeating Congress (154 seats). Morarji Desai became PM. Government collapsed in 1979 due to internal contradictions.

pol_1977_election.label: 1977 Lok Sabha Election
pol_1977_election.subject: polity
pol_1977_election.detail: First election after Emergency, treated as a referendum on Emergency. Janata Party won decisively. Congress party defeated for the first time since independence -- won only 154 seats with less than 35% vote share. Indira Gandhi herself lost her seat. Demonstrated that anti-democratic governments will be punished by voters.

pol_shah_commission.label: Shah Commission of Inquiry
pol_shah_commission.subject: polity
pol_shah_commission.detail: Appointed by Janata government in May 1977 under Justice J.C. Shah (retired CJI) to inquire into excesses during Emergency. Found widespread abuse of authority. Indira Gandhi appeared but refused to answer questions. Reports were tabled in Parliament.

pol_press_censorship.label: Press Censorship During Emergency
pol_press_censorship.subject: polity
pol_press_censorship.detail: Government disconnected electricity to newspaper offices, imposed prior approval for all publications. Indian Express and Statesman protested by leaving blank spaces. Magazines Seminar and Mainstream chose to shut down. Many journalists arrested. Kannada writer Karanth and Hindi writer Renu returned Padma awards in protest.

pol_habeas_corpus_case.label: ADM Jabalpur Case (Habeas Corpus)
pol_habeas_corpus_case.subject: polity
pol_habeas_corpus_case.detail: In April 1976, the Supreme Court constitution bench overruled High Courts and accepted the government's plea that during Emergency, courts cannot entertain habeas corpus petitions. Meant government could take away right to life and liberty. Regarded as one of the most controversial SC judgments.

pol_44th_amendment.label: 44th Constitutional Amendment (1978)
pol_44th_amendment.subject: polity
pol_44th_amendment.detail: Passed by Janata government to undo Emergency-era changes. Internal Emergency can now be proclaimed only on grounds of 'armed rebellion' (not internal disturbances). Advice to President must be given in writing by Cabinet. Right to life and liberty cannot be suspended even during Emergency.

pol_forced_sterilisation.label: Forced Sterilisation and Demolitions
pol_forced_sterilisation.subject: polity
pol_forced_sterilisation.detail: During Emergency, Sanjay Gandhi (PM's son, holding no official position) allegedly controlled administration. Over-enthusiasm about population control led to compulsory sterilisation. Turkman Gate area in Delhi saw forced demolitions and sterilisations. These excesses became symbols of Emergency abuse.

pol_chipko_movement.label: Chipko Movement
pol_chipko_movement.subject: polity
pol_chipko_movement.detail: Environmental movement that began in 1973 in Uttarakhand when villagers hugged trees to prevent commercial logging. Started when forest dept refused villagers ash trees for tools but allotted the same land to a sports manufacturer. Led to a 15-year ban on felling trees in the Himalayan regions. Women's active participation was a novel aspect.

pol_dalit_panthers.label: Dalit Panthers
pol_dalit_panthers.subject: polity
pol_dalit_panthers.detail: Militant organisation of Dalit youth formed in Maharashtra in 1972. Fought against caste-based inequalities and atrocities despite constitutional guarantees. Broader agenda was to destroy caste system and unite all oppressed sections. Contributed to the passage of a comprehensive law against Dalit atrocities in 1989.

pol_bku.label: Bharatiya Kisan Union (BKU)
pol_bku.subject: polity
pol_bku.detail: Farmers organisation from western UP and Haryana. In January 1988, 20,000 farmers gathered in Meerut protesting electricity rate hike. Demanded higher floor prices for sugarcane and wheat, abolition of restrictions on farm produce movement, loan waivers, and pensions. Used caste panchayat networks for mobilisation.

pol_narmada_bachao.label: Narmada Bachao Andolan
pol_narmada_bachao.subject: polity
pol_narmada_bachao.detail: Movement against the Sardar Sarovar Dam on river Narmada, led by Medha Patkar. Raised fundamental questions about large dam projects, displacement of tribal communities, environmental destruction and the meaning of development. Became a symbol of peoples resistance against state-driven development.

pol_bamcef.label: BAMCEF
pol_bamcef.subject: polity
pol_bamcef.detail: Backward and Minority Communities Employees Federation formed in 1978. Not an ordinary trade union -- took strong position in favour of political power to the 'bahujan' (SC, ST, OBC and minorities). Led by Kanshi Ram. Precursor organisation to the Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP).

pol_right_to_information.label: Right to Information Movement
pol_right_to_information.subject: polity
pol_right_to_information.detail: Movement demanding transparency in governance. Mazdoor Kisan Shakti Sangathan (MKSS) in Rajasthan pioneered the demand for the right to information about government expenditure. Eventually led to the Right to Information Act, 2005.

pol_shetkari_sanghatana.label: Shetkari Sanghatana
pol_shetkari_sanghatana.subject: polity
pol_shetkari_sanghatana.detail: Maharashtra-based farmers organisation that declared the farmers movement as a war of Bharat (rural, agrarian sector) against India (urban, industrial sector). Along with BKU, represented the farmers movement of the 1980s against liberalisation policies.

pol_atrocities_act_1989.label: SC/ST Prevention of Atrocities Act (1989)
pol_atrocities_act_1989.subject: polity
pol_atrocities_act_1989.detail: Comprehensive law passed in 1989 providing rigorous punishment for atrocities against Dalits. Result of sustained agitations by Dalit Panthers and other organisations. Despite constitutional abolition of untouchability, social discrimination and violence against Dalits continued to necessitate this law.

pol_telangana_peasant_movement.label: Telangana Peasant Movement
pol_telangana_peasant_movement.subject: polity
pol_telangana_peasant_movement.detail: Massive agitations by peasants in the Telangana region of Andhra Pradesh under Communist party leadership in the early years of independence. Demanded redistribution of land to cultivators. One of the earliest post-independence social movements linking land reforms to political power.

pol_medha_patkar.label: Medha Patkar
pol_medha_patkar.subject: polity
pol_medha_patkar.detail: Social activist who led the Narmada Bachao Andolan against the Sardar Sarovar Dam. Raised issues of displacement, rehabilitation of tribals, and environmental sustainability. Became a prominent face of peoples movements challenging the dominant development model.

pol_sheikh_abdullah.label: Sheikh Abdullah
pol_sheikh_abdullah.subject: polity
pol_sheikh_abdullah.detail: Leader of National Conference and key figure in Kashmir politics. Became PM of J&K in 1948. Initiated land reforms but dismissed in 1953 over differences with Centre on Kashmir's status and detained for years. Reached agreement with Indira Gandhi in 1974 and became Chief Minister.

pol_kashmir_insurgency.label: Kashmir Insurgency (1989)
pol_kashmir_insurgency.subject: polity
pol_kashmir_insurgency.detail: By 1989, militant movement mobilised around separate Kashmiri nation. Triggered by rigged 1987 elections and growing resentment against Centre's interference. Insurgents got support from Pakistan. State under President's rule and armed forces control through the 1990s. Assembly elections held only in 1996.

pol_punjab_crisis.label: Punjab Crisis
pol_punjab_crisis.subject: polity
pol_punjab_crisis.detail: In the 1980s, demand for Sikh political autonomy escalated from the Anandpur Sahib Resolution (1973) to extremist demands for Khalistan. Militants made headquarters in Golden Temple. Led to Operation Blue Star, Indira Gandhi's assassination, anti-Sikh riots, and a decade of militancy.

pol_anandpur_sahib_resolution.label: Anandpur Sahib Resolution (1973)
pol_anandpur_sahib_resolution.subject: polity
pol_anandpur_sahib_resolution.detail: Resolution passed at Akali Dal conference asserting regional autonomy and redefining centre-state relations. Spoke of aspirations of the Sikh qaum and declared goal of attaining 'bolbala' (dominance). Could be interpreted as plea for federalism or for separate Sikh nation.

pol_operation_blue_star.label: Operation Blue Star (1984)
pol_operation_blue_star.subject: polity
pol_operation_blue_star.detail: Army action in the Golden Temple, Amritsar in June 1984 to flush out militants. Government successfully removed militants but damaged the historic temple, deeply hurting Sikh sentiments. A large proportion of Sikhs saw it as an attack on their faith. Gave further impetus to extremism.

pol_indira_assassination.label: Assassination of Indira Gandhi (1984)
pol_indira_assassination.subject: polity
pol_indira_assassination.detail: PM Indira Gandhi was assassinated on 31 October 1984 by her Sikh bodyguards wanting revenge for Operation Blue Star. Followed by organised anti-Sikh violence -- over 2000 Sikhs killed in Delhi alone, hundreds in other parts of India. PM Manmohan Singh apologised in Parliament in 2005.

pol_rajiv_longowal_accord.label: Punjab Accord (Rajiv-Longowal, 1985)
pol_rajiv_longowal_accord.subject: polity
pol_rajiv_longowal_accord.detail: Agreement between PM Rajiv Gandhi and Akali Dal president Harchand Singh Longowal in July 1985. Chandigarh to be transferred to Punjab, commission for border dispute, tribunal for river water sharing, compensation for militancy victims, withdrawal of AFSPA. Longowal was assassinated shortly after.

pol_dravidian_movement.label: Dravidian Movement
pol_dravidian_movement.subject: polity
pol_dravidian_movement.detail: One of the first regional movements in Indian politics. Led to formation of Dravida Kazhagam (DK) under E.V. Ramasami Periyar. Opposed Brahmin dominance and north Indian cultural domination. DMK formed as political offshoot, came to power in 1967. Split into DMK and AIADMK. Good example of compatibility of regionalism and nationalism.

pol_anti_hindi_agitation.label: Anti-Hindi Agitation
pol_anti_hindi_agitation.subject: polity
pol_anti_hindi_agitation.detail: Protests in Tamil Nadu against making Hindi the official national language, especially intense in 1965. Led by DMK and students. Added greatly to DMK's popularity and contributed to its victory in 1967 elections. Forced the central government to continue English alongside Hindi.

pol_mizo_accord.label: Mizo Accord (1986)
pol_mizo_accord.subject: polity
pol_mizo_accord.detail: Peace accord signed between PM Rajiv Gandhi and MNF leader Laldenga in 1986. Mizoram became a full state in 1987. The MNF came to power through democratic elections. Regarded as one of the most successful peace accords in Indian history. Ended two decades of insurgency.

pol_assam_movement.label: Assam Movement (1979-85)
pol_assam_movement.subject: polity
pol_assam_movement.detail: Anti-foreigners movement led by All Assam Students Union (AASU) demanding identification and deportation of illegal immigrants, mainly from Bangladesh. Led to Assam Accord of 1985 with PM Rajiv Gandhi. AASU leaders formed Asom Gana Parishad and won state elections.

pol_mandal_commission.label: Mandal Commission (1978-80)
pol_mandal_commission.subject: polity
pol_mandal_commission.detail: Second Backward Classes Commission, chaired by B.P. Mandal. Set up 1978 by Janata government, submitted report 1980. Recommended 27% reservation for OBCs in central government jobs and educational institutions, based on caste-based social and educational backwardness. Report shelved until 1990.

pol_mandal_implementation.label: Implementation of Mandal Commission (1990)
pol_mandal_implementation.subject: polity
pol_mandal_implementation.detail: National Front government under PM V.P. Singh decided in August 1990 to implement Mandal Commission recommendations for OBC reservations. Triggered violent protests, self-immolations. Supreme Court upheld in the Indira Sawhney case (1992). All major parties now support OBC reservations. Reshaped Indian politics around caste identity.

pol_shah_bano_case.label: Shah Bano Case (1985)
pol_shah_bano_case.subject: polity
pol_shah_bano_case.detail: 62-year-old divorced Muslim woman sought maintenance from former husband. Supreme Court (1985) ruled in her favour under Section 125 CrPC. Orthodox Muslims protested judicial 'interference' in Personal Law. Rajiv Gandhi government passed Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Divorce) Act 1986 to override the ruling. Fueled BJP critique of 'appeasement' and Hindutva rise.

pol_bsp.label: Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP)
pol_bsp.subject: polity
pol_bsp.detail: Founded by Kanshi Ram in 1984 out of BAMCEF and DS-4. Envisaged as organisation based on pragmatic politics for bahujans (SC, ST, OBC and minorities). First major breakthrough in UP in 1989-91 elections. Under Mayawati, governed UP multiple times. First party primarily supported by Dalit voters to achieve such political success.

pol_vp_singh.label: V.P. Singh
pol_vp_singh.subject: polity
pol_vp_singh.detail: PM from 1989-90 heading the National Front government with outside support from BJP and Left. Former Congress leader who broke away. His decision to implement Mandal Commission recommendations transformed Indian politics. Government fell when BJP withdrew support over the Ayodhya issue.

pol_kanshi_ram.label: Kanshi Ram (1934-2006)
pol_kanshi_ram.subject: polity
pol_kanshi_ram.detail: Dalit politician, founder of BAMCEF (1978), DS-4 (1981), and Bahujan Samaj Party (1984). Mentor of Mayawati. Credited with Dalit political mobilisation in North India. Advocated 'Bahujan' coalition of SC/ST/OBC/minorities.

pol_courts.label: Courts
pol_courts.subject: polity
pol_courts.detail: Part of the government that resolves disputes and handles crimes. If a person feels that laws are not being followed (e.g., denied a job due to religion or caste), they can approach the court, which can give orders about what should be done.

pol_hindu_succession_amendment.label: Hindu Succession Amendment Act 2005
pol_hindu_succession_amendment.subject: polity
pol_hindu_succession_amendment.detail: A law that gave Hindu women equal right to inherit family agricultural land. Previously, in some states, only sons inherited agricultural property. Under the new law, sons, daughters, and mothers get equal shares. Applies to all states and union territories.

pol_judiciary.label: Indian Judiciary
pol_judiciary.subject: polity
pol_judiciary.detail: The system of courts enforcing rule of law, resolving disputes, conducting judicial review, and protecting Fundamental Rights. An independent organ of government and key feature of Indian democracy. Serves as check on legislature and executive.

pol_subordinate_courts.label: Subordinate/District Courts
pol_subordinate_courts.subject: polity
pol_subordinate_courts.detail: Lowest tier at district or tehsil level. Known as Trial Court, District Judge Court, Sessions Court, Magistrate Court etc. Each district presided by a District Judge. Most people interact with these courts.

pol_olga_tellis_case.label: Olga Tellis vs Bombay Municipal Corporation (1985)
pol_olga_tellis_case.subject: polity
pol_olga_tellis_case.detail: Landmark Supreme Court judgment establishing Right to Livelihood as part of Right to Life under Article 21. Court held that eviction of slum dwellers deprives them of livelihood and consequently of life. No person can live without means of living.

pol_bhopal_gas_tragedy.label: Bhopal Gas Tragedy
pol_bhopal_gas_tragedy.subject: polity
pol_bhopal_gas_tragedy.detail: The world's worst industrial tragedy on 2 December 1984. MIC gas leaked from Union Carbide's pesticide factory in Bhopal. Over 8,000 died within three days, hundreds of thousands maimed. UC had deliberately ignored safety measures to cut costs. Government filed $3 billion case but accepted only $470 million in 1989.

pol_subhash_kumar_case.label: Subhash Kumar vs State of Bihar (1991)
pol_subhash_kumar_case.subject: polity
pol_subhash_kumar_case.detail: Supreme Court held that the Right to Life under Article 21 includes the right to enjoyment of pollution-free water and air for full enjoyment of life. Government is responsible for setting up laws and procedures to check pollution and introduce heavy fines.

pol_allende_chile.label: Salvador Allende (Chile)
pol_allende_chile.subject: polity
pol_allende_chile.detail: Democratically elected socialist President of Chile (1970-1973). Implemented land redistribution, free milk for children, and education reforms. Overthrown and killed in military coup on 11 September 1973 led by General Pinochet.

pol_pinochet_dictatorship.label: Pinochet's Military Dictatorship
pol_pinochet_dictatorship.subject: polity
pol_pinochet_dictatorship.detail: General Augusto Pinochet ruled Chile from 1973-1990 after a US-supported military coup. Over 3,000 people killed, many more disappeared. Dictatorship ended after 1988 referendum where people voted no to his continued rule.

pol_solidarity_movement.label: Solidarity Movement (Poland)
pol_solidarity_movement.subject: polity
pol_solidarity_movement.detail: First independent trade union in any communist state, formed in 1980 at Gdansk shipyard. Led by Lech Walesa, grew to one crore members. Won 99 of 100 Senate seats in 1989 free elections, leading to Poland's democratic transition.

pol_lech_walesa.label: Lech Walesa
pol_lech_walesa.subject: polity
pol_lech_walesa.detail: Former electrician who led the Solidarity trade union movement in Poland. Emerged as leader of striking workers at Gdansk shipyard in 1980. Elected President of Poland in 1990 after democratic transition.

pol_decolonisation_democracy.label: Decolonisation and Democracy
pol_decolonisation_democracy.subject: polity
pol_decolonisation_democracy.detail: After World War II, many colonies gained independence and adopted democratic governments. Many countries in Asia and Africa became democratic between 1950-1975, significantly expanding democracy's global reach.

pol_constituent_assembly_india.label: Constituent Assembly of India
pol_constituent_assembly_india.subject: polity
pol_constituent_assembly_india.detail: Formed in 1946, had 299 members elected by existing provincial legislatures. Chaired by Dr. Rajendra Prasad. Drafting Committee headed by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar. Worked for 2 years 11 months 18 days. Constitution adopted on 26 November 1949, enacted on 26 January 1950.

pol_dr_ambedkar.label: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar
pol_dr_ambedkar.subject: polity
pol_dr_ambedkar.detail: Chairman of the Drafting Committee of the Indian Constitution. Champion of Dalit rights, legal luminary who studied at Columbia and London. Played the most important role in drafting the Constitution. Also India's first Law Minister.

pol_parliament_india.label: Parliament of India
pol_parliament_india.subject: polity
pol_parliament_india.detail: Supreme legislative body consisting of President and two Houses - Lok Sabha (House of the People) and Rajya Sabha (Council of States). Final authority for making laws, controls government finances, and is highest forum for public debate.

pol_president_india.label: President of India
pol_president_india.subject: polity
pol_president_india.detail: Head of state and highest formal authority. Elected indirectly by an electoral college. Exercises powers on advice of Council of Ministers. Appoints PM, gives assent to bills, can return bills for reconsideration. Nominal executive head.

pol_judiciary_india.label: Judiciary of India
pol_judiciary_india.subject: polity
pol_judiciary_india.detail: Independent branch that settles disputes and protects fundamental rights. Supreme Court at apex, High Courts at state level, subordinate courts below. Can declare laws unconstitutional (judicial review). Integrated and independent judiciary.

pol_kosovo_ethnic_massacre.label: Kosovo Ethnic Massacre
pol_kosovo_ethnic_massacre.subject: polity
pol_kosovo_ethnic_massacre.detail: In Kosovo province of Yugoslavia, Serb nationalist Milosevic's government persecuted ethnic Albanians despite being democratically elected. Thousands killed in ethnic cleansing. Shows that even elected governments can violate rights if unchecked.

pol_nhrc.label: National Human Rights Commission (NHRC)
pol_nhrc.subject: polity
pol_nhrc.detail: Statutory body established to protect and promote human rights in India. Investigates complaints of human rights violations. Can recommend compensation and action against violators. Works alongside judiciary in rights protection.

eco_consumer_movement.label: Consumer Movement in India
eco_consumer_movement.subject: economics
eco_consumer_movement.detail: Originated as a social force to protect consumers against unethical trade practices. Triggered by food shortages, hoarding, black marketing, adulteration in 1960s. Early activities: articles, exhibitions, monitoring ration shops. Led to COPRA 1986. Over 700 consumer groups in India but only 20-25 well organised.

eco_copra.label: Consumer Protection Act 1986 (COPRA)
eco_copra.subject: economics
eco_copra.detail: Enacted on 24 December 1986 (celebrated as National Consumers' Day). Major step by Indian government for consumer protection. Set up three-tier quasi-judicial machinery for consumer disputes redressal. Led to separate Consumer Affairs departments in central and state governments. India has exclusive consumer courts.

eco_un_consumer_guidelines.label: UN Guidelines for Consumer Protection
eco_un_consumer_guidelines.subject: economics
eco_un_consumer_guidelines.detail: Adopted by United Nations in 1985. A tool for nations to adopt consumer protection measures. Foundation for international consumer movement. Consumers International: umbrella body of 240 organisations from over 100 countries. India observes 24 December as National Consumers' Day.

eco_planning_commission.label: Planning Commission
eco_planning_commission.subject: economics
eco_planning_commission.detail: Set up in 1950 with the Prime Minister as Chairperson to formulate five year plans. India chose a mixed economy model combining features of socialism and capitalism. The era of five year plans became the basis for India's planned development from 1950 to 2017 when NITI Aayog replaced it.

eco_five_year_plans.label: Five Year Plans
eco_five_year_plans.subject: economics
eco_five_year_plans.detail: Borrowed from the Soviet Union, these plans specified objectives for five-year periods within a twenty-year perspective plan. The four key goals were growth (increase in GDP), modernisation (new technology adoption), self-reliance (reducing import dependence), and equity (basic needs for all).

eco_pc_mahalanobis.label: P.C. Mahalanobis
eco_pc_mahalanobis.subject: economics
eco_pc_mahalanobis.detail: Statistician regarded as the architect of Indian planning. The Second Five Year Plan was based on his ideas, emphasising heavy industry and capital goods. Founded the Indian Statistical Institute (ISI) in Calcutta and the journal Sankhya. Made Fellow of Britain's Royal Society in 1946.

eco_land_reforms.label: Land Reforms
eco_land_reforms.subject: economics
eco_land_reforms.detail: Two major components: abolition of intermediaries (zamindars, jagirdars) making tillers the owners, and land ceiling (fixing maximum land size per individual). About 200 lakh tenants came into direct contact with government. Successful in Kerala and West Bengal but largely failed elsewhere due to loopholes exploited by landlords.

eco_abolition_of_zamindari.label: Abolition of Zamindari
eco_abolition_of_zamindari.subject: economics
eco_abolition_of_zamindari.detail: Steps taken just a year after independence to abolish intermediaries and make tillers the owners of land. About 200 lakh tenants freed from zamindari exploitation. However, many zamindars used loopholes to retain land by registering in relatives' names. Poorest agricultural labourers did not benefit.

eco_land_ceiling.label: Land Ceiling
eco_land_ceiling.subject: economics
eco_land_ceiling.detail: Policy of fixing maximum size of land that could be owned by an individual to reduce concentration of land ownership. Big landlords challenged legislation in courts, used delays to register lands in relatives' names. Vast inequality in landholding continues despite this policy.

eco_green_revolution.label: Green Revolution
eco_green_revolution.subject: economics
eco_green_revolution.detail: Large increase in food grain production through High Yielding Variety (HYV) seeds, especially wheat and rice. First phase (mid-1960s to mid-1970s) limited to affluent states like Punjab, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu and mainly wheat. Second phase (mid-1970s to mid-1980s) spread wider. Made India self-sufficient in food grains.

eco_ipr_1956.label: Industrial Policy Resolution 1956
eco_ipr_1956.subject: economics
eco_ipr_1956.detail: Classified industries into three categories: exclusively state-owned (strategic), state-led with private supplementation, and private sector. Formed basis of Second Five Year Plan for socialist pattern of society. Private sector controlled through licensing system -- no new industry without government permission.

eco_small_scale_industry.label: Small-Scale Industry Policy
eco_small_scale_industry.subject: economics
eco_small_scale_industry.detail: Karve Committee (1955) recommended using small-scale industries for rural development. Defined by maximum investment on assets (Rs 5 lakh in 1950, Rs 1 crore later). More labour-intensive than large firms, generating more employment. Given concessions: reserved products, lower excise duty, subsidised bank loans.

eco_import_substitution.label: Import Substitution Policy
eco_import_substitution.subject: economics
eco_import_substitution.detail: Inward-looking trade strategy followed in the first seven plans, aiming to replace imports with domestic production. Protection through tariffs (tax on imports) and quotas (quantity restrictions on imports). Based on the notion that developing country industries cannot compete with developed economies without protection.

eco_second_five_year_plan.label: Second Five Year Plan (1956-61)
eco_second_five_year_plan.subject: economics
eco_second_five_year_plan.detail: Landmark plan based on Mahalanobis model emphasising heavy industry and building a socialist pattern of society. Classified industries into three categories through IPR 1956. Laid down the basic ideas regarding goals of Indian planning. Stressed that benefits of development must reach less privileged classes.

eco_gatt.label: General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT)
eco_gatt.subject: economics
eco_gatt.detail: Established in 1948 with 23 countries as the global trade organisation to administer multilateral trade agreements and provide equal opportunities to all countries in international markets. Succeeded by the WTO in 1995.

eco_growth_oriented_approach.label: Growth-Oriented Approach to Poverty
eco_growth_oriented_approach.subject: economics
eco_growth_oriented_approach.detail: First dimension of poverty alleviation (1950s-60s). Based on expectation that economic growth (rapid GDP increase) would trickle down to all sections. Focus on rapid industrialisation and Green Revolution. Failed because benefits did not trickle down; gap between poor and rich widened; Green Revolution exacerbated regional disparities.

eco_poverty_alleviation_programmes.label: Poverty Alleviation Programmes
eco_poverty_alleviation_programmes.subject: economics
eco_poverty_alleviation_programmes.detail: Second approach from Third Five Year Plan (1961-66). Specific programmes to raise incomes and employment for the poor through asset creation and work generation. Includes self-employment programmes (REGP, PMRY, SJSRY, SGSY) and wage employment programmes (NFWP, SGRY, NREGA-2005). Food for Work initiated in 1970s.

eco_self_employment_programmes.label: Self-Employment Programmes
eco_self_employment_programmes.subject: economics
eco_self_employment_programmes.detail: Include REGP (rural/small town self-employment via Khadi and Village Industries Commission), PMRY (educated unemployed from low-income families), SJSRY (urban employment), and SGSY (self-help group based). Since 1990s, approach shifted from individual assistance to encouraging Self-Help Groups (SHGs).

eco_basic_amenities_approach.label: Minimum Basic Amenities Approach
eco_basic_amenities_approach.subject: economics
eco_basic_amenities_approach.detail: Third approach from Fifth Five Year Plan. India pioneered public expenditure on social consumption -- subsidised food grains, education, health, water, sanitation. Key programmes: PDS, ICDS, Midday Meal Scheme, PMGSY, PMGY, Valmiki Ambedkar Awas Yojana. Aims to supplement consumption and improve health/education of the poor.

eco_pds.label: Public Distribution System (PDS)
eco_pds.subject: economics
eco_pds.detail: Major programme providing food grains at subsidised rates to the poor. One of three key programmes along with ICDS and Midday Meal aimed at improving food and nutritional status of the poor. Part of the minimum basic amenities approach to poverty alleviation.

eco_national_social_assistance.label: National Social Assistance Programme
eco_national_social_assistance.subject: economics
eco_national_social_assistance.detail: Central government social security programme providing pensions to elderly without caregivers and assistance to destitute and widowed poor women. Part of the government's variety of social security programmes targeting specific vulnerable groups.

eco_education_commission.label: Education Commission (1964-66)
eco_education_commission.subject: economics
eco_education_commission.detail: Recommended that at least 6% of GDP should be spent on education for noticeable growth in educational achievements. More than 40 years later, India's education spending was still around 4%, well short of this target. The 6% goal has been accepted as a must for coming years.

eco_nabard.label: NABARD (National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development)
eco_nabard.subject: economics
eco_nabard.detail: Set up in 1982 as apex body to coordinate activities of all institutions involved in rural financing. Green Revolution diversified rural credit portfolio towards production-oriented lending. NABARD oversees the multi-agency rural banking system comprising commercial banks, RRBs, cooperatives, and land development banks.

eco_regulated_markets.label: Regulated Markets
eco_regulated_markets.subject: economics
eco_regulated_markets.detail: First step in agricultural marketing reform: creating orderly and transparent marketing conditions. Benefited farmers and consumers. However, about 27,000 rural periodic markets still need development as regulated market places to realise the full potential of rural markets.

eco_msp_buffer_stock.label: MSP, Buffer Stock and PDS
eco_msp_buffer_stock.subject: economics
eco_msp_buffer_stock.detail: Fourth element of agricultural marketing: (i) Minimum Support Prices for 24 agricultural products protecting farmer income, (ii) Buffer stocks of wheat and rice maintained by Food Corporation of India, (iii) Distribution of food grains and sugar through PDS at subsidised rates. Despite this, private trade handles 90% of agricultural marketing.

eco_operation_flood.label: Operation Flood
eco_operation_flood.subject: economics
eco_operation_flood.detail: Launched from 1966 onwards, it created a system where farmers pool milk by quality grading, which is processed and marketed to urban centres through cooperatives. Farmers assured fair price and income. Gujarat is the success story. Milk production in India increased more than four times between 1960-2002.

eco_cpcb.label: Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB)
eco_cpcb.subject: economics
eco_cpcb.detail: Set up in 1974 to address water and air pollution. State-level boards followed. Functions: investigate and disseminate information on pollution, set standards for sewage/emissions, provide technical assistance, organise mass awareness, prepare manuals for waste disposal, assess air quality, monitor water quality in 125 rivers. Industries periodically inspected.

eco_chipko_appiko.label: Chipko and Appiko Movements
eco_chipko_appiko.subject: economics
eco_chipko_appiko.detail: Chipko Movement aimed at protecting Himalayan forests. Appiko Movement in Karnataka (1983) -- 160 people in Salkani forest, Sirsi district hugged trees to stop commercial felling, saving 12,000 trees. Spread to adjoining districts. Demonstrated how community action can protect forests from indiscriminate commercial exploitation.

eco_great_leap_forward.label: Great Leap Forward (GLF)
eco_great_leap_forward.subject: economics
eco_great_leap_forward.detail: Campaign initiated in 1958 to industrialise China on a massive scale. People encouraged to set up industries in backyards. In rural areas, communes were started for collective cultivation. Met many problems: severe drought killed about 30 million people. Russia withdrew its professionals after conflicts with China.

eco_commune_system.label: Commune System in China
eco_commune_system.subject: economics
eco_commune_system.detail: Under the Great Leap Forward, people collectively cultivated lands in communes. By 1958, there were 26,000 communes covering almost all the farm population. During 1978 reforms, commune lands were divided into small plots allocated to individual households (for use, not ownership). Households kept income after paying stipulated taxes.

eco_cultural_revolution.label: Great Proletarian Cultural Revolution
eco_cultural_revolution.subject: economics
eco_cultural_revolution.detail: Introduced by Mao in 1965, implemented 1966-76. Students and professionals were sent to work and learn from the countryside. A political movement that disrupted education and professional development in China. Pre-dated the economic reforms that began in 1978.

eco_china_1978_reforms.label: China's 1978 Economic Reforms
eco_china_1978_reforms.subject: economics
eco_china_1978_reforms.detail: Introduced in phases. First phase: agriculture (commune lands to individual households), foreign trade, and investment reforms. Later phase: industrial reforms with private sector and township/village enterprises allowed. SOEs (State Owned Enterprises) faced competition. Dual pricing system: government-fixed prices for fixed quantities, market prices for the rest.

eco_sez_china.label: Special Economic Zones (China)
eco_sez_china.subject: economics
eco_sez_china.detail: Set up to attract foreign investors as part of China's reform process. Along with township and village enterprises, SEZs became key drivers of China's export-oriented industrial growth. These zones offered special incentives and regulations different from the rest of the economy.

eco_dual_pricing_china.label: Dual Pricing System (China)
eco_dual_pricing_china.subject: economics
eco_dual_pricing_china.detail: Reform process involved fixing prices in two ways: farmers and industrial units bought/sold fixed quantities at government-set prices, with the rest at market prices. Over time, as production increased, the proportion transacted at market prices was gradually increased.

eco_pakistan_green_revolution.label: Pakistan's Green Revolution
eco_pakistan_green_revolution.subject: economics
eco_pakistan_green_revolution.detail: Led to mechanisation and increase in public investment in infrastructure in select areas, resulting in rise in food grain production. Changed the agrarian structure dramatically. Similar to India's experience but with different scale and outcomes.

eco_one_child_policy.label: China's One-Child Policy
eco_one_child_policy.subject: economics
eco_one_child_policy.detail: Introduced in late 1970s, major reason for China's low population growth rate. Led to decline in sex ratio (proportion of females per 1000 males) -- biased against females due to son-preference. Has implications for future ageing population, rising labour costs, and potential labour shortage.

eco_saarc.label: SAARC and Regional Groupings
eco_saarc.subject: economics
eco_saarc.detail: South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation. Nations form regional and global economic groupings (SAARC, EU, ASEAN, G-8, G-20) to strengthen domestic economies. Understanding neighbouring economies is essential as developing countries face competition from each other and from developed nations in limited economic space.

eco_bengal_famine.label: Bengal Famine of 1943
eco_bengal_famine.subject: economics
eco_bengal_famine.detail: Most devastating famine in India, killed 30 lakh people in Bengal. Agricultural labourers, fishermen, transport workers, and casual labourers were worst affected by dramatically rising rice prices. Led to the introduction of rationing system in India.

eco_nfsa.label: National Food Security Act (2013)
eco_nfsa.subject: economics
eco_nfsa.detail: Provides food and nutritional security at affordable prices. Covers 75% of rural population and 50% of urban population as eligible households. Entitles 5 kg per person per month at Rs 2/kg wheat, Rs 3/kg rice, Rs 1/kg coarse grains.

eco_icds.label: Integrated Child Development Services (ICDS)
eco_icds.subject: economics
eco_icds.detail: Introduced in 1975 on experimental basis as a food intervention programme. Along with PDS and Food-for-Work (1977-78), one of three major food security interventions launched in mid-1970s following high poverty levels reported by NSSO.

hist_dien_bien_phu.label: Battle of Dien Bien Phu
hist_dien_bien_phu.subject: history
hist_dien_bien_phu.detail: In 1954 French forces decisively defeated by Viet Minh at Dien Bien Phu. This ended French colonial rule in Indo-China. Led to Geneva Peace Agreement dividing Vietnam at 17th parallel.

hist_vietnam_war_us.label: Vietnam War (US Involvement)
hist_vietnam_war_us.subject: history
hist_vietnam_war_us.detail: US entered to prevent communist takeover of South Vietnam. Used napalm and Agent Orange extensively. First television war created anti-war movement in US. Peace signed in Paris 1974. Saigon fell 30 April 1975.

hist_ho_chi_minh_trail.label: Ho Chi Minh Trail
hist_ho_chi_minh_trail.subject: history
hist_ho_chi_minh_trail.detail: Network of paths through Laos and Cambodia used to transport supplies to South Vietnam. 2,195 km of strategic roads maintained by young volunteers, 70-80% women. Vital supply line despite constant US bombing.

hist_ngo_dinh_diem.label: Ngo Dinh Diem
hist_ngo_dinh_diem.subject: history
hist_ngo_dinh_diem.detail: US-backed dictator of South Vietnam. Built authoritarian government, refused land reform. His brutal suppression of Buddhists and political opponents ultimately lost US support. Overthrown and killed in 1963 coup.

hist_linguistic_states.label: Formation of Linguistic States
hist_linguistic_states.subject: history
hist_linguistic_states.detail: Potti Sriramulu's death after 58-day fast in 1952 forced creation of Andhra state in 1953. States Reorganisation Commission (1956) redrew boundaries for linguistic provinces. Bombay divided in 1960, Punjab in 1966.

hist_hindi_language_debate.label: Hindi as Official Language Debate
hist_hindi_language_debate.subject: history
hist_hindi_language_debate.detail: Many wanted Hindi to replace English as official language. T.T. Krishnamachari warned southern states would separate if Hindi imposed. Compromise: Hindi as official language with English for courts, services and inter-state communication.

hist_ambedkar_drafting_committee.label: Ambedkar as Chairman of Drafting Committee
hist_ambedkar_drafting_committee.subject: history
hist_ambedkar_drafting_committee.detail: B.R. Ambedkar chaired the Constitution's Drafting Committee. Warned that political democracy must be accompanied by economic and social democracy, as equality in politics coexists with inequality in social and economic life.

hist_potti_sriramulu.label: Potti Sriramulu
hist_potti_sriramulu.subject: history
hist_potti_sriramulu.detail: Gandhian leader who fasted unto death demanding separate state for Telugu speakers. Died on 15 December 1952 after 58 days of fasting. His death forced the creation of Andhra state on 1 October 1953.

hist_mao_zedong.label: Mao Zedong
hist_mao_zedong.subject: history
hist_mao_zedong.detail: Founded People's Republic of China 1949. Peasant-based adaptation of Marxism. Long March 1934-35. Great Leap Forward 1958-62. Cultural Revolution 1966-76.

hist_chinese_communist_revolution.label: Chinese Communist Revolution (1949)
hist_chinese_communist_revolution.subject: history
hist_chinese_communist_revolution.detail: Mao defeated KMT; PRC proclaimed 1 Oct 1949. Land redistribution, industry nationalised. Chiang retreated Taiwan.

hist_great_leap_forward.label: Great Leap Forward (1958-62)
hist_great_leap_forward.subject: history
hist_great_leap_forward.detail: Mao's collectivisation + backyard steel furnaces. Catastrophic famine 15-45M deaths. Mao temporarily lost standing.

hist_cultural_revolution.label: Cultural Revolution (1966-76)
hist_cultural_revolution.subject: history
hist_cultural_revolution.detail: Mao vs 'bourgeois' elements. Red Guards attacked intellectuals + traditional culture. Millions persecuted. Universities closed. Ended with Mao's death 1976.

hist_deng_xiaoping.label: Deng Xiaoping
hist_deng_xiaoping.subject: history
hist_deng_xiaoping.detail: Paramount leader from 1978. 'Socialism with Chinese characteristics' = market reforms, Special Economic Zones. Suppressed Tiananmen 1989.

hist_g77_nieo.label: G-77 and NIEO
hist_g77_nieo.subject: history
hist_g77_nieo.detail: Group of 77 developing countries demanded New International Economic Order: resource sovereignty, development aid, fairer commodity prices, market access.

pol_cold_war.label: Cold War
pol_cold_war.subject: polity
pol_cold_war.detail: Competition, tensions and confrontations between the US and Soviet Union from 1945 to 1991. Both a power rivalry and an ideological conflict between liberal democracy/capitalism and socialism/communism. Never escalated into direct full-scale war between the two superpowers.

pol_two_power_blocs.label: Two Power Blocs
pol_two_power_blocs.subject: polity
pol_two_power_blocs.detail: Post-WWII world divided into Western (capitalist, US-led) and Eastern (communist, Soviet-led) alliances. Smaller states joined blocs for protection, weapons, and economic aid. Division first occurred in Europe, then extended globally.

pol_sukarno.label: Sukarno
pol_sukarno.subject: polity
pol_sukarno.detail: First President of Indonesia (1945-65). One of five founders of NAM. Organised the Bandung Conference in 1955. Championed socialism and anti-imperialism. Overthrown in a military coup.

pol_india_cold_war.label: India and the Cold War
pol_india_cold_war.subject: polity
pol_india_cold_war.detail: India pursued non-alignment, staying away from both alliances while actively mediating. Served India by allowing independent decisions and balancing superpowers. Signed Treaty of Friendship with USSR in 1971 during Bangladesh crisis.

pol_arms_race.label: Arms Race
pol_arms_race.subject: polity
pol_arms_race.detail: Competitive buildup of nuclear and conventional weapons between US and USSR. Both stockpiled thousands of thermonuclear weapons. Led to arms control treaties (SALT-I, SALT-II, START-I, START-II).

pol_india_ussr_relations.label: India-USSR Relations (Cold War Era)
pol_india_ussr_relations.subject: polity
pol_india_ussr_relations.detail: Multi-dimensional relationship covering economic aid (Bhilai, Bokaro steel plants), political support (Kashmir in UN, 1971 war), military hardware supply, and cultural exchanges. USSR accepted Indian currency for trade. Led critics to call India part of the Soviet camp.

pol_marshall_plan.label: Marshall Plan
pol_marshall_plan.subject: polity
pol_marshall_plan.detail: US aid programme (1947-52) for reconstruction of Western Europe. Led to the establishment of OEEC in 1948 to channel aid. Helped European economic recovery and integration. Part of the US Cold War strategy of containment.

pol_pakistan_democracy.label: Democracy in Pakistan
pol_pakistan_democracy.subject: polity
pol_pakistan_democracy.detail: Alternated between civilian and military rule. Military coups by Ayub Khan, Yahya Khan, Zia-ul-Haq, and Pervez Musharraf. Social dominance of military, clergy, and landowners undermines democracy. Pakistan joined Cold War blocs SEATO and CENTO. Strong pro-democracy sentiment exists despite military dominance.

pol_india_pakistan_conflicts.label: India-Pakistan Conflicts
pol_india_pakistan_conflicts.subject: polity
pol_india_pakistan_conflicts.detail: Wars in 1947-48, 1965, 1971, and Kargil conflict 1999. Kashmir dispute remains central. Both conducted nuclear tests in 1998 (India at Pokhran, Pakistan at Chagai Hills). Disputes over Siachen glacier, Sir Creek, and cross-border terrorism. Indus Waters Treaty (1960) has survived all conflicts.

pol_kashmir_issue.label: Kashmir Issue
pol_kashmir_issue.subject: polity
pol_kashmir_issue.detail: Dispute since partition in 1947. Wars in 1947-48 resulted in division along Line of Control. 1971 war did not settle the issue. India blames Pakistan for supporting militants. Strategic issues include Siachen glacier control. Shimla Agreement (1972) governs bilateral resolution.

pol_united_nations.label: United Nations (UN)
pol_united_nations.subject: polity
pol_united_nations.detail: Founded in 1945 as successor to League of Nations, with 51 original members (192 by 2006). Signed at San Francisco. Objective: prevent conflict and facilitate cooperation. India joined on 30 October 1945. October 24 celebrated as UN Day.

pol_un_general_assembly.label: UN General Assembly
pol_un_general_assembly.subject: polity
pol_un_general_assembly.detail: All UN members have one vote each. Debates and discusses global issues including war, peace, and development. Overwhelming majority of members are now developing countries.

pol_un_security_council.label: UN Security Council
pol_un_security_council.subject: polity
pol_un_security_council.detail: Five permanent members (US, Russia, UK, France, China) with veto power, and ten non-permanent members serving two-year terms. Responsible for maintaining international peace and security. Permanent members selected as most powerful after WWII.

pol_un_secretary_general.label: UN Secretary-General
pol_un_secretary_general.subject: polity
pol_un_secretary_general.detail: Most visible public figure and representative head of the UN. Ban Ki-Moon (South Korea) became eighth Secretary-General on 1 January 2007. Previous holders include Dag Hammarskjold, U Thant, Kofi Annan. US has considerable influence in selection.

pol_imf.label: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
pol_imf.subject: polity
pol_imf.detail: International organisation overseeing financial institutions and regulations. 184 member countries but unequal voting: top ten countries have 55% of votes. US alone has 17.4% voting rights. G-8 members plus Saudi Arabia and China dominate decision-making.

pol_world_bank.label: World Bank
pol_world_bank.subject: polity
pol_world_bank.detail: Created in 1945, focused on developing countries. Works on education, health, agriculture, infrastructure, and governance. Provides loans with conditions, often criticised for imposing free market reforms and setting economic agendas of poorer nations.

pol_three_challenges.label: Three Challenges of Nation Building
pol_three_challenges.subject: polity
pol_three_challenges.detail: Independent India faced three broad challenges: (1) shaping a united nation accommodating diversity, (2) establishing democracy with constitutional governance, and (3) ensuring development and well-being of all sections, especially the poor and disadvantaged.

pol_non_alignment.label: Policy of Non-Alignment
pol_non_alignment.subject: polity
pol_non_alignment.detail: India's foreign policy of not joining either the US-led NATO or Soviet-led Warsaw Pact blocs during the Cold War. Advocated by Nehru to preserve sovereignty, protect territorial integrity and promote economic development. India was a co-founder of the Non-Aligned Movement (NAM) with its first summit in Belgrade (1961).

pol_cauvery_water_dispute.label: Cauvery Water Dispute
pol_cauvery_water_dispute.subject: polity
pol_cauvery_water_dispute.detail: A conflict between Karnataka and Tamil Nadu over sharing of Cauvery river water. Water from Krishna Raja Sagara dam (Karnataka) and Mettur dam (Tamil Nadu) serves different regions. The central government must step in to ensure fair distribution. An example of inter-state conflict.

pol_instrument_of_accession.label: Instrument of Accession
pol_instrument_of_accession.subject: polity
pol_instrument_of_accession.detail: The legal document through which princely states agreed to merge with India, transferring control over defence, external affairs and communications to the Government of India. Maharaja Hari Singh of Kashmir signed it in October 1947 after Pakistani tribal invasion.

hist_rajiv_gandhi.label: Rajiv Gandhi
hist_rajiv_gandhi.subject: history
hist_rajiv_gandhi.detail: Youngest PM of India (1984-89) after mother Indira's assassination 31 Oct 1984. Computer revolution beginning, telecom push (C-DOT, Sam Pitroda), Panchayati Raj initiative, Shah Bano reversal (Muslim Women Act 1986), Assam Accord 1985, Punjab Accord 1985 (Rajiv-Longowal), Mizo Accord 1986. Tarnished by Bofors scandal (1987). Assassinated 21 May 1991 in Sriperumbudur by LTTE suicide bomber.

eco_ms_swaminathan.label: M.S. Swaminathan
eco_ms_swaminathan.subject: economics
eco_ms_swaminathan.detail: Father of the Green Revolution in India. Agricultural scientist who led the HYV seed programme with Norman Borlaug's wheat varieties from Mexico/CIMMYT in the 1960s. Director of IARI. Later chair of National Commission on Farmers (2004-06).

sci_homi_bhabha.label: Homi J. Bhabha
sci_homi_bhabha.subject: science
sci_homi_bhabha.detail: Father of Indian nuclear programme. Founded Tata Institute of Fundamental Research (TIFR) 1945 and Atomic Energy Commission 1948. First chairman of AEC. Designed three-stage nuclear programme using India's thorium reserves. Died in Air India Flight 101 crash Jan 1966.

sci_vikram_sarabhai.label: Vikram Sarabhai
sci_vikram_sarabhai.subject: science
sci_vikram_sarabhai.detail: Father of Indian space programme. Founded Physical Research Laboratory (PRL) Ahmedabad 1947 and INCOSPAR 1962 (precursor to ISRO). Convinced Nehru of importance of space tech for developing country. Died 1971.

eco_c_subramaniam.label: C. Subramaniam
eco_c_subramaniam.subject: economics
eco_c_subramaniam.detail: Union Minister for Food and Agriculture (1964-67) under Shastri and Indira. Political architect of Green Revolution — pushed HYV wheat adoption, created Agricultural Prices Commission (1965) and FCI (1965). Worked with Swaminathan.

eco_verghese_kurien.label: Verghese Kurien
eco_verghese_kurien.subject: economics
eco_verghese_kurien.detail: Father of White Revolution / Operation Flood. Led Amul (Kaira District Cooperative) and National Dairy Development Board (NDDB, est. 1965). Transformed India from milk-deficit into world's largest milk producer via three-phase Operation Flood (1970-96).

pol_golaknath_case.label: Golaknath Case (1967)
pol_golaknath_case.subject: polity
pol_golaknath_case.detail: I.C. Golaknath vs State of Punjab 1967. SC held by 6-5 that Parliament cannot amend Fundamental Rights — reversed Sajjan Singh (1965) and Shankari Prasad (1951). Led to 24th Amendment (1971) explicitly reinstating Parliament's amending power over FRs. Overruled by Kesavananda Bharati 1973.

pol_maneka_gandhi_case.label: Maneka Gandhi Case (1978)
pol_maneka_gandhi_case.subject: polity
pol_maneka_gandhi_case.detail: Maneka Gandhi vs Union of India 1978. SC expanded scope of Article 21 (Right to Life and Personal Liberty) — procedure established by law must be 'just, fair, and reasonable' (due process in substance). Overruled A.K. Gopalan (1950). Foundation of expansive Article 21 jurisprudence.

sci_barc.label: Bhabha Atomic Research Centre (BARC)
sci_barc.subject: science
sci_barc.detail: India's premier nuclear research centre, Trombay Mumbai. Founded 1954 as Atomic Energy Establishment Trombay (AEET) by Homi Bhabha. Renamed BARC after his death 1967. Designed Apsara (first Asian research reactor, 1956), CIRUS, Dhruva. Core facility for Pokhran-I and II.

sci_isro.label: Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO)
sci_isro.subject: science
sci_isro.detail: Established 15 Aug 1969 by Vikram Sarabhai, replacing INCOSPAR (1962). Under Department of Space from 1972. Early milestones: Aryabhata satellite (1975, with USSR), Rohini SLV-3 (1980, India's first indigenous satellite launch), INSAT-1A (1982), Chandrayaan (2008), Mangalyaan (2013).

hist_hyderabad_police_action.label: Hyderabad Police Action (Operation Polo, Sept 1948)
hist_hyderabad_police_action.subject: history
hist_hyderabad_police_action.detail: 13-18 Sept 1948 Indian Army operation against Nizam Mir Osman Ali Khan's Hyderabad State which refused accession. Codenamed 'Operation Polo'. Triggered by Razakar militia violence. Ended in 5 days. Integrated Hyderabad into Indian Union. Major Patel achievement.

hist_junagadh_accession.label: Junagadh Accession (1947-48)
hist_junagadh_accession.subject: history
hist_junagadh_accession.detail: Junagadh Nawab (Muslim ruler, Hindu-majority population) acceded to Pakistan Aug 1947 despite geographic non-contiguity. Indian forces moved in, plebiscite held Feb 1948 — overwhelming vote for India. Integrated into Indian Union.

hist_goa_liberation.label: Goa Liberation (Operation Vijay, Dec 1961)
hist_goa_liberation.subject: history
hist_goa_liberation.detail: Indian Army operation 17-19 Dec 1961 ending 451 years of Portuguese rule over Goa, Daman and Diu. Portugal refused to negotiate transfer. Ended Portuguese colonial presence in India. Goa became UT; full statehood 1987.

sci_pokhran_1_1974.label: Pokhran-I / Smiling Buddha (1974)
sci_pokhran_1_1974.subject: science
sci_pokhran_1_1974.detail: India's first nuclear test, 18 May 1974 at Pokhran, Rajasthan. Codenamed 'Smiling Buddha'. Described officially as 'Peaceful Nuclear Explosion' (PNE). Made India sixth nuclear-weapons-capable state. Led to formation of Nuclear Suppliers Group (NSG) in 1975. Raja Ramanna led the team.

pol_hindu_code_bills.label: Hindu Code Bills (1955-56)
pol_hindu_code_bills.subject: polity
pol_hindu_code_bills.detail: Four codification acts reforming Hindu personal law: Hindu Marriage Act (1955), Hindu Succession Act (1956), Hindu Minority and Guardianship Act (1956), Hindu Adoptions and Maintenance Act (1956). Originally proposed by Ambedkar 1948-51 (led to his resignation Sept 1951 when diluted). Finally passed under Nehru. Gave Hindu women divorce rights, inheritance rights.

pol_indus_waters_treaty_1960.label: Indus Waters Treaty (1960)
pol_indus_waters_treaty_1960.subject: polity
pol_indus_waters_treaty_1960.detail: Signed 19 Sept 1960 between Nehru and Ayub Khan, brokered by World Bank. Divides Indus river system: India gets eastern rivers (Ravi, Beas, Sutlej), Pakistan gets western rivers (Indus, Jhelum, Chenab). Has survived three wars. India can use western rivers for non-consumptive purposes (hydro).

pol_shimla_agreement_1972.label: Shimla Agreement (1972)
pol_shimla_agreement_1972.subject: polity
pol_shimla_agreement_1972.detail: Signed 2 July 1972 between Indira Gandhi and Zulfikar Ali Bhutto after 1971 war. Bilateralism principle — Kashmir to be resolved bilaterally, not internationalised. Converted 1971 ceasefire line into Line of Control (LoC). Pakistan agreed to recognise Bangladesh. Return of 93,000 POWs.

pol_article_356.label: Article 356 - President's Rule
pol_article_356.subject: polity
pol_article_356.detail: Empowers President to impose central rule on a state if constitutional machinery fails. Used 100+ times 1950-1990, often for partisan purposes. Controversial misuses: Kerala 1959 (first, against EMS Namboodiripad communist govt), 1977 Janata dismissing Congress-ruled states, 1980 Indira dismissing non-Congress states. Restrained by S.R. Bommai case (1994).

pol_article_370.label: Article 370 - Special Status of J&K
pol_article_370.subject: polity
pol_article_370.detail: Gave Jammu & Kashmir special autonomous status from 1949. Emerged from Instrument of Accession (Oct 1947) limited to defence, foreign affairs, communications. Only these subjects of Union List applied to J&K without state concurrence. Abrogated 5 Aug 2019 (era 11).

eco_license_raj.label: License-Permit-Quota Raj
eco_license_raj.subject: economics
eco_license_raj.detail: Elaborate system of licenses, permits and quotas governing private industry 1951-1991. Industries (Development and Regulation) Act 1951 mandated licenses for establishment/expansion. Meant to direct investment toward Plan priorities but created corruption, delays, inefficiency. Dismantled by 1991 LPG reforms.

eco_first_plan.label: First Five Year Plan (1951-56)
eco_first_plan.subject: economics
eco_first_plan.detail: 1 April 1951 - 31 March 1956. Based on Harrod-Domar model. Focus on agriculture and irrigation post-Partition. Major dams: Bhakra Nangal, Hirakud, Damodar Valley. Target 2.1% growth, achieved 3.6%. PM Nehru, Planning Commission under Mahalanobis framework.

eco_third_plan.label: Third Five Year Plan (1961-66)
eco_third_plan.subject: economics
eco_third_plan.detail: Aimed at self-reliant economy. Disrupted by 1962 China war, 1965 Pakistan war, 1965-66 drought. Plan failed — growth only 2.8%. Followed by Plan Holiday (1966-69) with annual plans. Devaluation of rupee June 1966.

eco_plan_holiday.label: Plan Holiday (1966-69)
eco_plan_holiday.subject: economics
eco_plan_holiday.detail: Three annual plans 1966-67, 1967-68, 1968-69 instead of a five-year plan. Caused by 1965 war strain, 1965-66 drought, rupee devaluation June 1966. Green Revolution launched in this period as interim strategy.

eco_fourth_plan.label: Fourth Five Year Plan (1969-74)
eco_fourth_plan.subject: economics
eco_fourth_plan.detail: Growth with stability and progressive self-reliance. Bank nationalisation 1969 (14 banks). Garibi Hatao slogan 1971. 1971 Bangladesh war, 1973 oil shock. Achieved 3.3% vs 5.7% target. Indira Gandhi era.

eco_fifth_plan.label: Fifth Five Year Plan (1974-78)
eco_fifth_plan.subject: economics
eco_fifth_plan.detail: Poverty removal (Garibi Hatao) + self-reliance. Minimum Needs Programme. Emergency years 1975-77. Terminated one year early by Janata govt March 1978. 4.8% growth.

eco_rolling_plan.label: Rolling Plan (1978-80)
eco_rolling_plan.subject: economics
eco_rolling_plan.detail: Janata govt's Gunnar Myrdal-inspired Rolling Plan replacing Fifth Plan's final year. Abandoned when Indira returned Jan 1980.

eco_sixth_plan.label: Sixth Five Year Plan (1980-85)
eco_sixth_plan.subject: economics
eco_sixth_plan.detail: Indira II, then Rajiv from 1984. Poverty alleviation + modernisation. IRDP (Integrated Rural Development), NREP. Family planning emphasis. 5.7% growth — first to exceed target.

eco_seventh_plan.label: Seventh Five Year Plan (1985-90)
eco_seventh_plan.subject: economics
eco_seventh_plan.detail: Rajiv Gandhi era. Food, work, productivity. Jawahar Rozgar Yojana 1989. Growing fiscal deficit, BOP crisis brewing. 6% growth. Ended with BOP crisis 1990-91 that triggered liberalisation.

hist_first_general_elections_1951.label: First General Elections (1951-52)
hist_first_general_elections_1951.subject: history
