hist_first_general_elections_1951.detail: Oct 1951 - Feb 1952. 173 million voters (of whom 85% illiterate), world's largest democratic exercise. Sukumar Sen as first CEC. Congress swept with 364/489 LS seats, 45% vote share. Proved universal adult suffrage workable in mass-illiterate country.

pol_fazal_ali_commission.label: Fazal Ali Commission / States Reorganisation Commission (1953)
pol_fazal_ali_commission.subject: polity
pol_fazal_ali_commission.detail: Appointed Dec 1953 by Nehru after Potti Sriramulu's death forced Andhra's creation. Chair: Justice Fazal Ali. Members: H.N. Kunzru, K.M. Panikkar. Report submitted Sept 1955 rejected one-language-one-state principle but recommended reorganisation broadly on linguistic lines. Led to States Reorganisation Act 1956.

hist_andhra_state_1953.label: Andhra State Creation (Oct 1953)
hist_andhra_state_1953.subject: history
hist_andhra_state_1953.detail: First linguistic state formed after Potti Sriramulu's 58-day fast-unto-death (died 15 Dec 1952) galvanised Telugu demand. Separated from Madras State. Later merged with Telangana (Hyderabad State) in 1956 as Andhra Pradesh. Set precedent for linguistic reorganisation.

hist_nefa_1954.label: NEFA (North-East Frontier Agency, 1954)
hist_nefa_1954.subject: history
hist_nefa_1954.detail: Created 1954 from Assam tribal areas. Administered by Ministry of External Affairs (not Home) under special Governor-via-President arrangement. Verrier Elwin's tribal-friendly policy. Became Arunachal Pradesh UT in 1972, state in 1987.

hist_naga_hills_insurgency.label: Naga Insurgency (1950s onwards)
hist_naga_hills_insurgency.subject: history
hist_naga_hills_insurgency.detail: Led by A.Z. Phizo's Naga National Council demanding independent Nagaland. Armed rebellion from 1955. Nagaland state created 1963 (from Assam). 1975 Shillong Accord briefly held. Ongoing insurgency across decades.

pol_tribal_policy_nehru.label: Nehru's Tribal Policy (Panchsheel of Tribals)
pol_tribal_policy_nehru.subject: polity
pol_tribal_policy_nehru.detail: Five principles articulated by Nehru (influenced by Verrier Elwin): (1) develop along lines of own genius, (2) respect tribal rights in land and forests, (3) train own team of administrators, (4) not over-administer or introduce too many outside schemes, (5) judge results by quality of human character evolved.

pol_verrier_elwin.label: Verrier Elwin
pol_verrier_elwin.subject: polity
pol_verrier_elwin.detail: British-Indian anthropologist (1902-1964), Gandhian, tribal expert. Key advisor to Nehru on tribal policy, particularly NEFA. Advocated gradualist, protective approach to tribal integration. First Indian citizen of British origin (1954).

hist_gandhi_assassination_1948.label: Mahatma Gandhi's Assassination (30 Jan 1948)
hist_gandhi_assassination_1948.subject: history
hist_gandhi_assassination_1948.detail: Shot dead at Birla House, Delhi by Nathuram Godse, former RSS/Hindu Mahasabha worker. Three bullets fired at point-blank range. Trigger: Gandhi's fasts demanding protection of Muslims and payment of Rs 55 crore to Pakistan. Led to ban on RSS (lifted 1949 after pledge). Profoundly shifted Indian politics against communalism.

hist_rss_ban_1948.label: RSS Ban (Feb 1948 - July 1949)
hist_rss_ban_1948.subject: history
hist_rss_ban_1948.detail: Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh banned after Gandhi assassination in Feb 1948. Ban lifted July 1949 after RSS pledged loyalty to Constitution, flag, and renounced violence. Accepted written constitution with M.S. Golwalkar. Banned again during Emergency (1975) and after Babri (1992).

hist_princely_mergers.label: Princely State Mergers (Saurashtra, PEPSU, Vindhya, Madhya Bharat)
hist_princely_mergers.subject: history
hist_princely_mergers.detail: Post-1947 consolidation: Saurashtra (1948, 222 states of Kathiawar), Madhya Bharat (1948), PEPSU (Patiala and East Punjab States Union, 1948), Vindhya Pradesh (1948), Rajasthan (1948-49). Most merged into larger states by SRC 1956.

pol_avadi_session_1955.label: Avadi Session of Congress (Jan 1955)
pol_avadi_session_1955.subject: polity
pol_avadi_session_1955.detail: 61st Congress session at Avadi, near Madras. Adopted 'Socialistic Pattern of Society' as party's declared objective. Influenced Second Five Year Plan's public-sector emphasis. Followed by Nagpur Resolution 1959 on cooperative joint farming.

pol_nagpur_resolution_1959.label: Nagpur Resolution (Jan 1959)
pol_nagpur_resolution_1959.subject: polity
pol_nagpur_resolution_1959.detail: Congress Nagpur session adopted 'Cooperative Joint Farming' as agrarian objective — land to be pooled into cooperatives. Created huge backlash from landed peasants. Policy effectively abandoned. Contributed to rise of Swatantra Party (1959).

pol_swatantra_party_1959.label: Swatantra Party (1959)
pol_swatantra_party_1959.subject: polity
pol_swatantra_party_1959.detail: Founded Aug 1959 by C. Rajagopalachari with N.G. Ranga, Minoo Masani. Classical liberal, anti-socialist, anti-Congress. Peak in 1967 (44 LS seats, largest opposition). Declined by 1974, formally merged into Bharatiya Kranti Dal. Key voice against licence raj.

pol_bharatiya_jana_sangh_1951.label: Bharatiya Jana Sangh (1951)
pol_bharatiya_jana_sangh_1951.subject: polity
pol_bharatiya_jana_sangh_1951.detail: Founded Oct 1951 by Syama Prasad Mookerjee (former Hindu Mahasabha, ex-Nehru cabinet). Aligned with RSS cadre. Anti-Congress right-wing Hindu nationalist. Under Deendayal Upadhyaya's 'Integral Humanism' (1965). Merged into Janata Party 1977; re-emerged as BJP 1980.

pol_kamaraj_plan_1963.label: Kamaraj Plan (Aug 1963)
pol_kamaraj_plan_1963.subject: polity
pol_kamaraj_plan_1963.detail: Devised by K. Kamaraj, then TN CM. Senior Congress leaders (6 CMs + 6 Union ministers) resigned party/govt posts to re-dedicate themselves to party organisation. Kamaraj himself resigned and became Congress President. Meant to revitalise party and ease Nehru succession. Succeeded for Nehru but unwound by 1964.

pol_k_kamaraj.label: K. Kamaraj
pol_k_kamaraj.subject: polity
pol_k_kamaraj.detail: Dravidian-era Congressman, TN CM (1954-63). Created midday meal scheme and universal primary education in Tamil Nadu. Congress President (1964-67). 'Kingmaker' — engineered succession of Shastri (1964) and Indira (1966). Led Syndicate against Indira in 1969 split.

pol_syndicate.label: Congress Syndicate
pol_syndicate.subject: polity
pol_syndicate.detail: Informal group of old-guard Congress bosses: K. Kamaraj, S. Nijalingappa, S.K. Patil, Atulya Ghosh, N. Sanjiva Reddy. Dominant after Nehru's death. Backed Shastri (1964), then Indira (1966). Expelled Indira after Congress split 1969 (Congress-O vs Congress-R).

pol_mundhra_scandal_1957.label: Mundhra Scandal (1957-58)
pol_mundhra_scandal_1957.subject: polity
pol_mundhra_scandal_1957.detail: First major post-independence corruption scandal. LIC purchased Rs 1.26 crore shares in Haridas Mundhra's six sank companies without board approval, under T.T. Krishnamachari's (FM) alleged direction. JP Committee inquiry. Feroze Gandhi (MP) exposed. Led to TTK's resignation Feb 1958. First LIC scandal.

pol_tt_krishnamachari.label: T.T. Krishnamachari (TTK)
pol_tt_krishnamachari.subject: polity
pol_tt_krishnamachari.detail: Congress economic thinker and Union Finance Minister (1956-58, 1964-66). Resigned 1958 over Mundhra scandal, returned as FM under Shastri. Key architect of Second Plan's industrial policy. Warned of Hindi imposition on south during Constituent Assembly.

pol_krishna_menon.label: V.K. Krishna Menon
pol_krishna_menon.subject: polity
pol_krishna_menon.detail: Marxist-leaning Nehru confidant, Defence Minister (1957-62). India's rep at UN, delivered record 8-hour speech on Kashmir 1957. Architect of non-alignment rhetoric. Forced to resign after 1962 China war debacle (military unpreparedness). Controversial intellectually sharp figure.

pol_feroze_gandhi.label: Feroze Gandhi
pol_feroze_gandhi.subject: polity
pol_feroze_gandhi.detail: Congress MP (Lok Sabha 1952-60), husband of Indira. Parsi journalist-politician. Rigorous backbencher — exposed Mundhra (1957) and LIC scandals. Championed PAC reforms, parliamentary accountability. Died Sept 1960.

hist_tibet_asylum_1959.label: Dalai Lama Takes Asylum in India (March 1959)
hist_tibet_asylum_1959.subject: history
hist_tibet_asylum_1959.detail: 14th Dalai Lama fled Lhasa to India after failed Tibetan uprising March 1959, reaching Tezpur 31 March. Nehru granted asylum despite Chinese protest. Established Central Tibetan Administration in Dharamshala. Key irritant souring India-China relations pre-1962 war.

hist_mcmahon_line.label: McMahon Line
hist_mcmahon_line.subject: history
hist_mcmahon_line.detail: 1914 Simla Convention boundary between Tibet and British India along Eastern Himalayas (NEFA/Arunachal). Named after Sir Henry McMahon. China never ratified. Core of 1962 war dispute. India maintains it as legal border; China rejects.

pol_forward_policy_1961.label: Forward Policy (1961-62)
pol_forward_policy_1961.subject: polity
pol_forward_policy_1961.detail: Indian military posture under Nehru-Menon — establishing forward posts in disputed Aksai Chin and NEFA to assert sovereignty without reinforcing logistics. Provoked Chinese response. Military unprepared. Led to disastrous 1962 war.

hist_1962_aftermath.label: Aftermath of 1962 China War
hist_1962_aftermath.subject: history
hist_1962_aftermath.detail: Nehru's prestige shattered; Krishna Menon resigned. Emergency (external) proclaimed 1962. India rapidly expanded army (from 0.5M to 1M) and air force (82 to 45 squadrons target). Parliamentary 'no resolution' that India would recover every inch. Emotional blow hastened Nehru's decline; died May 1964.

hist_nehru_death_1964.label: Nehru's Death (27 May 1964)
hist_nehru_death_1964.subject: history
hist_nehru_death_1964.detail: Jawaharlal Nehru died 27 May 1964 at 74, of stroke preceded by heart attack Jan 1964. End of 17-year premiership. Kamaraj Plan (1963) had prepared but not resolved succession. Gulzarilal Nanda acting PM. Lal Bahadur Shastri elected by Syndicate as successor June 1964.

hist_nanda_acting_pm.label: Gulzarilal Nanda (Acting PM)
hist_nanda_acting_pm.subject: history
hist_nanda_acting_pm.detail: Home Minister who served as acting PM twice: after Nehru's death (27 May - 9 June 1964) and after Shastri's death (11-24 Jan 1966). Gandhian, Planning Commission member. Never a contender for full PM-ship.

hist_indira_ascent_1966.label: Indira Gandhi Becomes PM (24 Jan 1966)
hist_indira_ascent_1966.subject: history
hist_indira_ascent_1966.detail: After Shastri's death at Tashkent (11 Jan 1966), Syndicate chose Indira as compromise against Morarji Desai. Parliamentary party vote 355-169. Seen as malleable 'gungi gudiya' (dumb doll). Proved otherwise by 1969 bank nationalisation and 1971 war.

hist_rupee_devaluation_1966.label: Rupee Devaluation (June 1966)
hist_rupee_devaluation_1966.subject: history
hist_rupee_devaluation_1966.detail: 6 June 1966 — Indian rupee devalued 36.5% against USD (Rs 4.76 to Rs 7.50) under US/World Bank pressure for economic aid amid BOP crisis. Politically disastrous for Indira. Led to backlash against 'IMF dependence' and Congress election setback 1967.

hist_1967_elections.label: 1967 General Elections
hist_1967_elections.subject: history
hist_1967_elections.detail: Feb 1967 — Congress vote down to 40.8%, lost 8 states to opposition coalitions (SVDs). Ram Manohar Lohia's 'anti-Congressism' succeeded. Early collapse of Congress System. Birth of SVD (Samyukta Vidhayak Dal) coalition politics in states.

pol_vv_giri_president.label: V.V. Giri (4th President, 1969-74)
pol_vv_giri_president.subject: polity
pol_vv_giri_president.detail: Independent candidate (conscience vote) backed by Indira in 1969 presidential election against Syndicate's Sanjiva Reddy. Won by 17,366 votes. Former Labour Minister. His victory precipitated Congress split.

pol_privy_purses_abolition.label: Abolition of Privy Purses (1971)
pol_privy_purses_abolition.subject: polity
pol_privy_purses_abolition.detail: Indira's 1970 ordinance de-recognising princes failed in Supreme Court (Madhavrao Scindia case). 26th Constitutional Amendment Dec 1971 abolished privy purses and princely privileges permanently. Indira's populist move; ~Rs 4 crore/year savings but huge symbolic statement.

pol_26th_amendment.label: 26th Constitutional Amendment (1971)
pol_26th_amendment.subject: polity
pol_26th_amendment.detail: Abolished privy purses and official recognition of former princely rulers. Omitted Articles 291 and 362, inserted Article 363A. Response to SC striking down 1970 ordinance. Ratified Dec 1971.

pol_24th_amendment.label: 24th Constitutional Amendment (1971)
pol_24th_amendment.subject: polity
pol_24th_amendment.detail: Nov 1971 — Reasserted Parliament's power to amend any part of Constitution including Fundamental Rights. Response to Golaknath (1967). Amended Articles 13 and 368. Set stage for Kesavananda Bharati (1973).

pol_25th_amendment.label: 25th Constitutional Amendment (1971)
pol_25th_amendment.subject: polity
pol_25th_amendment.detail: April 1972 (passed 1971). Curtailed Right to Property (Article 31) to enable social welfare laws. Reduced compensation review. Added Article 31C giving primacy to DPSPs (Articles 39b, 39c) over FRs (14, 19, 31). Part of Indira's 1971 mandate bundle.

hist_garibi_hatao_1971.label: Garibi Hatao Slogan (1971)
hist_garibi_hatao_1971.subject: history
hist_garibi_hatao_1971.detail: Indira's election slogan for 1971 mid-term polls. Promised poverty eradication. Won landslide 352/518 LS seats. Political success, economic results disputed — poverty ratio in 1973-74 was 55%, largely unchanged.

hist_1971_elections.label: 1971 Lok Sabha Elections
hist_1971_elections.subject: history
hist_1971_elections.detail: March 1971 mid-term poll (after Congress split). Indira's Congress-R swept 352/518 seats with 43.7% vote. 'Indira hatao vs Garibi hatao' contest. Consolidated Indira's personal authority. 1971 Bangladesh War followed immediately after.

pol_kesavananda_bharati_doctrine.label: Basic Structure Doctrine (Kesavananda Bharati, 1973)
pol_kesavananda_bharati_doctrine.subject: polity
pol_kesavananda_bharati_doctrine.detail: SC ruling 24 April 1973 by 13-judge bench (7-6 majority). Established that Parliament can amend any part of Constitution but cannot alter its 'basic structure'. Chief Justice Sikri. Features: supremacy of Constitution, democratic republic, federalism, secularism, separation of powers, judicial review etc. Reaffirmed and expanded in Minerva Mills (1980).

pol_allahabad_hc_judgment_1975.label: Allahabad HC Judgment (12 June 1975)
pol_allahabad_hc_judgment_1975.subject: polity
pol_allahabad_hc_judgment_1975.detail: Justice Jagmohanlal Sinha ruled in Raj Narain vs Indira Gandhi that Indira's 1971 Rae Bareli election was corrupt (misuse of govt machinery). Declared her election void, barred her from holding office for 6 years. Triggered Emergency declaration 13 days later (25 June 1975).

pol_raj_narain.label: Raj Narain
pol_raj_narain.subject: polity
pol_raj_narain.detail: Socialist politician, losing candidate against Indira in 1971 Rae Bareli. His election petition led to Allahabad HC judgment June 1975. Defeated Indira in 1977 Rae Bareli. Later health minister in Janata govt. Eccentric, colourful figure.

pol_emergency_declaration.label: Emergency Declaration (25 June 1975)
pol_emergency_declaration.subject: polity
pol_emergency_declaration.detail: President Fakhruddin Ali Ahmed proclaimed Emergency under Article 352 on grounds of internal disturbance, at Indira's advice midnight 25 June. No cabinet consultation (ex-post ratification). Based on JP Movement, Allahabad HC judgment. Lasted 21 months till 21 March 1977.

pol_fakhruddin_ali_ahmed.label: Fakhruddin Ali Ahmed (5th President)
pol_fakhruddin_ali_ahmed.subject: polity
pol_fakhruddin_ali_ahmed.detail: President 1974-77. Signed Emergency proclamation 25 June 1975 midnight on Indira's advice. Famous/infamous for rubber-stamping ordinances 'from his bathtub'. Died Feb 1977 in office.

pol_misa.label: Maintenance of Internal Security Act (MISA)
pol_misa.subject: polity
pol_misa.detail: 1971 act allowing preventive detention without trial. Amended during Emergency (1975) to increase detention periods and bar judicial review. Used to detain opposition leaders (JP Narayan, Morarji Desai, Advani, Vajpayee, 110,000+ total). Repealed 1978 by Janata govt.

pol_adm_jabalpur_case.label: ADM Jabalpur vs Shivkant Shukla (1976)
pol_adm_jabalpur_case.subject: polity
pol_adm_jabalpur_case.detail: SC's notorious 'Habeas Corpus Case' — 4-1 majority ruling that right to life and personal liberty (Art 21) could be suspended during Emergency. Justice H.R. Khanna's lone dissent (cost him CJI). Widely considered SC's darkest hour. Overruled by Puttaswamy (2017).

pol_42nd_amendment_details.label: 42nd Amendment — 'Mini-Constitution' (1976)
pol_42nd_amendment_details.subject: polity
pol_42nd_amendment_details.detail: Swaran Singh Committee proposals enacted Dec 1976. Added Part IV-A (Fundamental Duties), inserted 'Socialist', 'Secular', 'Integrity' in Preamble, extended LS/Assembly term 5→6 years, curtailed judicial review, made DPSPs override FRs, transferred education etc. to Concurrent List. Largest amendment ever. Mostly reversed by 44th (1978).

pol_sanjay_gandhi.label: Sanjay Gandhi
pol_sanjay_gandhi.subject: polity
pol_sanjay_gandhi.detail: Indira's younger son (1946-1980). Emerged as extra-constitutional authority during Emergency. Led 5-Point Programme: family planning (forced sterilisations 8M+ done), tree planting, adult literacy, dowry ban, slum clearance (Turkman Gate demolitions). Died Jun 1980 plane crash.

pol_turkman_gate_1976.label: Turkman Gate Demolitions (April 1976)
pol_turkman_gate_1976.subject: polity
pol_turkman_gate_1976.detail: Forced slum-clearance in Old Delhi by Sanjay Gandhi's DDA. Bulldozers razed homes of poor (Muslim) residents. Police firing killed protesters. Symbol of Emergency excesses. Enduring political scar.

hist_1977_elections.label: 1977 General Elections
hist_1977_elections.subject: history
hist_1977_elections.detail: March 1977 — first non-Congress govt at Centre. Janata Party swept 298/542 seats (41%). Congress crashed to 154 (34%). Indira and Sanjay lost their seats. JP Narayan's moral leadership + anti-Emergency backlash. Morarji Desai became PM at 81.

pol_44th_amendment_details.label: 44th Amendment (1978) — Reversal
pol_44th_amendment_details.subject: polity
pol_44th_amendment_details.detail: Janata govt's landmark reversal of 42nd Amendment. Removed Right to Property from FRs (made Article 300A legal right), restored judicial review, required written cabinet advice for Emergency, narrowed Article 352 to 'armed rebellion' (from 'internal disturbance'), required written cabinet note, restored Supreme Court/HC jurisdiction.

pol_janata_split_1979.label: Janata Party Split (July 1979)
pol_janata_split_1979.subject: polity
pol_janata_split_1979.detail: Charan Singh revolted over 'dual membership' (Jana Sangh members' RSS ties). Raj Narain expelled. Morarji resigned 15 July. Charan Singh sworn in 28 July with Indira's promised support — but she withdrew, forcing fresh polls Jan 1980.

hist_1980_elections.label: 1980 General Elections
hist_1980_elections.subject: history
hist_1980_elections.detail: Jan 1980 — Indira's Congress-I returned with 353/529 LS seats (42.7%). Janata collapsed. 'Indira is India' campaign. Sanjay Gandhi emerged stronger — but died Jun 1980 in plane crash. Rajiv reluctantly entered politics.

pol_mandal_commission_1979.label: Mandal Commission (1979)
pol_mandal_commission_1979.subject: polity
pol_mandal_commission_1979.detail: Second Backward Classes Commission chaired by B.P. Mandal. Appointed Dec 1978 by Morarji govt under Article 340. Submitted report Dec 1980 — recommended 27% reservation for OBCs (in addition to 22.5% SC/ST). Shelved till VP Singh implemented 1990.

pol_bp_mandal.label: B.P. Mandal
pol_bp_mandal.subject: polity
pol_bp_mandal.detail: Former Bihar CM, chairman of Second Backward Classes Commission (1979-80). Report recommended 27% OBC reservation. Name synonymous with OBC quota. Died 1982 — didn't live to see implementation.

hist_bhopal_gas_1984.label: Bhopal Gas Tragedy (3 Dec 1984)
hist_bhopal_gas_1984.subject: history
hist_bhopal_gas_1984.detail: Union Carbide India Ltd pesticide plant leaked 40 tons methyl isocyanate (MIC). 3,787 immediate deaths; 15,000+ over time; 500,000+ affected. Warren Anderson (UCC CEO) briefly arrested, released on bail — never faced trial. Rs 715 crore settlement 1989. World's worst industrial disaster.

hist_1984_sikh_riots.label: 1984 Anti-Sikh Riots (Nov 1984)
hist_1984_sikh_riots.subject: history
hist_1984_sikh_riots.detail: After Indira's assassination 31 Oct 1984, organised mob violence against Sikhs in Delhi (2,733 killed officially, 3,000+ per unofficial) and other cities. Congress leaders implicated. Rajiv's 'when a big tree falls...' remark. Enduring trauma. Commissions: Mishra (1985), Nanavati (2000).

hist_assam_accord_1985.label: Assam Accord (14-15 Aug 1985)
hist_assam_accord_1985.subject: history
hist_assam_accord_1985.detail: Signed between Rajiv and All Assam Students' Union (AASU) / Assam Gana Sangram Parishad leaders. Set 25 March 1971 as cutoff for detection/deportation of illegal Bangladeshi immigrants. Promised protection of Assamese identity (Clause 6). Led to AGP formation 1985 and 1985 Assembly polls.

hist_mizo_accord_1986.label: Mizo Accord (30 June 1986)
hist_mizo_accord_1986.subject: history
hist_mizo_accord_1986.detail: Signed by Rajiv and Laldenga's Mizo National Front. Ended 20-year MNF insurgency. Created Mizoram statehood (1987) from UT. Laldenga became first CM. Model for peaceful insurgency resolution. Perhaps most successful accord.

hist_rajiv_longowal_accord_1985.label: Rajiv-Longowal Accord / Punjab Accord (24 July 1985)
hist_rajiv_longowal_accord_1985.subject: history
hist_rajiv_longowal_accord_1985.detail: Rajiv and Sant Harchand Singh Longowal (Akali Dal moderate) signed accord addressing Anandpur Sahib demands partially. Transfer of Chandigarh to Punjab (never happened), Ravi-Beas waters tribunal, Army deserters treatment. Longowal assassinated 20 Aug 1985 by militants. Accord largely unimplemented.

hist_jarnail_singh_bhindranwale.label: Jarnail Singh Bhindranwale
hist_jarnail_singh_bhindranwale.subject: history
hist_jarnail_singh_bhindranwale.detail: Radical Sikh preacher, leader of Damdami Taksal. Initially backed by Congress (Zail Singh, Sanjay) to undercut Akalis. Mobilised for Sikh separatism, sheltered militants. Took over Akal Takht in Golden Temple 1983. Killed in Operation Blue Star June 1984.

pol_52nd_amendment_antidefection.label: 52nd Amendment — Anti-Defection Law (1985)
pol_52nd_amendment_antidefection.subject: polity
pol_52nd_amendment_antidefection.detail: Rajiv era. Inserted Tenth Schedule. Disqualifies MPs/MLAs for voluntarily giving up party membership, voting against party whip. Provided exemption for 'split' (1/3rd defection) — removed by 91st Amendment 2003. Major cleanup of 'aya ram gaya ram' politics.

pol_shah_bano_reversal.label: Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Divorce) Act (1986)
pol_shah_bano_reversal.subject: polity
pol_shah_bano_reversal.detail: Rajiv's Parliament overturned Shah Bano SC verdict (1985) under orthodox Muslim clerical pressure. Limited maintenance to iddat period (~3 months), devolved responsibility to Waqf Board. Major political misstep — perceived minority appeasement. Followed by Shilanyas at Ayodhya 1989 (counterbalance to Hindu votes).

hist_shilanyas_1989.label: Shilanyas at Ayodhya (Nov 1989)
hist_shilanyas_1989.subject: history
hist_shilanyas_1989.detail: Nov 1989 — Rajiv govt allowed VHP to perform foundation-stone laying (shilanyas) of Ram Mandir at disputed Babri Masjid site (Ayodhya), to counterbalance Shah Bano reversal perception. Major concession to Hindu sentiment. Accelerated Ayodhya movement.

hist_bofors_scandal.label: Bofors Scandal (1987 onwards)
hist_bofors_scandal.subject: history
hist_bofors_scandal.detail: April 1987 Swedish Radio revealed kickbacks in Rs 1,437 crore Bofors 155mm howitzer deal (1986). Rs 64 crore paid to Ottavio Quattrocchi (Rajiv's friend). V.P. Singh (FM, then Defence) resigned, broke away to form Jan Morcha (1988). Defined 1989 elections — Rajiv lost. Case dragged decades.

hist_ipkf_sri_lanka.label: IPKF in Sri Lanka (1987-90)
hist_ipkf_sri_lanka.subject: history
hist_ipkf_sri_lanka.detail: Indian Peace Keeping Force deployed under Rajiv-Jayewardene Accord (29 July 1987). Meant to disarm LTTE after Indo-Sri Lanka Peace Accord. Turned into war with LTTE (80,000 troops peak, 1,200+ Indian casualties). Withdrawn March 1990. Rajiv assassinated by LTTE 21 May 1991 in revenge.

hist_ltte.label: LTTE (Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam)
hist_ltte.subject: history
hist_ltte.detail: Sri Lankan Tamil militant separatist group founded 1976 by Velupillai Prabhakaran. Initially trained in India (Tamil Nadu camps, 1980s). Fought IPKF 1987-90. Pioneered suicide-vest bombing (assassinated Rajiv 1991, Premadasa 1993). Defeated by Sri Lankan army May 2009.

hist_1989_elections.label: 1989 General Elections
hist_1989_elections.subject: history
hist_1989_elections.detail: Nov 1989 — Congress reduced to 197/529 seats. National Front (VP Singh's Janata Dal + allies, 143 seats) formed minority govt with outside support from BJP (85) and Left (52). Bofors, Shah Bano, Ayodhya shaped vote.

pol_annadurai.label: C.N. Annadurai
pol_annadurai.subject: polity
pol_annadurai.detail: Founded DMK 1949 (split from Periyar's DK). TN CM 1967-69 after DMK historic 1967 victory. Ended decade of anti-Hindi agitation. Died Feb 1969 of cancer. Succeeded by Karunanidhi. Pioneer of Dravidian political cinema.

pol_dmk.label: DMK (Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam)
pol_dmk.subject: polity
pol_dmk.detail: Founded 1949 by C.N. Annadurai splitting from Periyar's DK. Dravidian regional party. Won TN 1967 elections (ending Congress rule, never returned). Split 1972 creating AIADMK (MGR). Alternated TN govt with AIADMK ever since. Family dominance under Karunanidhi-Stalin.

pol_karunanidhi.label: M. Karunanidhi
pol_karunanidhi.subject: polity
pol_karunanidhi.detail: TN CM five terms (1969-71, 1971-76, 1989-91, 1996-2001, 2006-11). Annadurai's successor. Tamil scholar-politician. Party split in 1972 creating AIADMK. Long DMK patriarch till 2018 death.

pol_mgr_aiadmk.label: M.G. Ramachandran (MGR) & AIADMK (1972)
pol_mgr_aiadmk.subject: polity
pol_mgr_aiadmk.detail: Matinee idol who broke from DMK 1972 to found AIADMK. TN CM 1977 till death 1987. Introduced midday meal scheme 1982 (national model). Charismatic mass leader. Succeeded by Jayalalithaa.

hist_anti_hindi_agitation_1965.label: Anti-Hindi Agitation (1965)
hist_anti_hindi_agitation_1965.subject: history
hist_anti_hindi_agitation_1965.detail: Jan-Feb 1965 TN agitation against Hindi becoming sole official language from 26 Jan 1965 (15-year transition per Article 343). Student riots, self-immolations (70+ deaths). Shastri govt passed Official Languages Act 1963 then amended 1967 — guaranteed English continuation. Catapulted DMK to 1967 power.

pol_ntr_tdp_1982.label: N.T. Rama Rao & TDP (1982)
pol_ntr_tdp_1982.subject: polity
pol_ntr_tdp_1982.detail: Telugu film star founded Telugu Desam Party 29 March 1982. Won Andhra Pradesh 1983 (202/294 seats) — first non-Congress state govt in AP. 'Telugu pride' against Congress. Dismissed by Governor 1984 but reinstated after protests. 3x CM (1983-88, 1994-95). Model for regional ethno-linguistic mobilisation.

hist_left_front_wb_1977.label: Left Front Government in West Bengal (1977-2011)
hist_left_front_wb_1977.subject: history
hist_left_front_wb_1977.detail: CPI(M)-led coalition won 1977 WB elections (231/294 seats). Jyoti Basu CM till 2000, then Buddhadeb Bhattacharjee till 2011. World's longest-running democratically-elected communist govt (34 years). Operation Barga land tenancy reform 1978. Eventually lost to Mamata's TMC 2011.

pol_jyoti_basu.label: Jyoti Basu
pol_jyoti_basu.subject: polity
pol_jyoti_basu.detail: CPI(M) stalwart, WB CM 1977-2000 (23 years, longest serving). Declined PM-ship in 1996 despite United Front offer (CPI(M) Politburo veto — 'historic blunder' he later called). Barrister-turned-trade-unionist. Died 2010.

hist_naxalbari_1967.label: Naxalbari Uprising (May 1967)
hist_naxalbari_1967.subject: history
hist_naxalbari_1967.detail: May 1967 peasant uprising in Naxalbari, Darjeeling district (WB). Led by CPI(M) cadres Charu Majumdar, Kanu Sanyal, Jangal Santhal. Landlord killed; police retaliation killed 11. Spark for Naxalite movement. Broke from CPI(M), formed CPI(ML) 1969. Spread to AP, Bihar; state crushed by 1972.

pol_farooq_abdullah.label: Farooq Abdullah
pol_farooq_abdullah.subject: polity
pol_farooq_abdullah.detail: Son of Sheikh Abdullah. J&K CM 1982-84, dismissed by Jagmohan. Rajiv-Farooq Accord 1986. CM 1986-90 (resigned when Jagmohan returned as Governor amid insurgency). Later CM 1996-2002. Union Minister under UPA.

eco_industrial_policy_1948.label: Industrial Policy Resolution (1948)
eco_industrial_policy_1948.subject: economics
eco_industrial_policy_1948.detail: First IPR. Classified industries into 4 groups: (1) Central monopoly — arms, atomic energy, railways; (2) New govt undertakings — coal, iron/steel, aircraft, shipping, telegraphs; (3) 18 industries state-regulated; (4) rest private. Mixed-economy framework. Replaced by IPR 1956.

eco_feldman_mahalanobis_model.label: Feldman-Mahalanobis Model
eco_feldman_mahalanobis_model.subject: economics
eco_feldman_mahalanobis_model.detail: Economic development model emphasising heavy capital-goods industries to achieve self-reliance and growth. Borrowed from Soviet economist G.A. Feldman (1928); adapted by P.C. Mahalanobis for India's Second Plan (1956-61). Theoretical basis for public-sector heavy industry.

eco_bhakra_nangal.label: Bhakra Nangal Dam
eco_bhakra_nangal.subject: economics
eco_bhakra_nangal.detail: Multipurpose project on Sutlej (Punjab-Himachal). Conceived pre-1947, construction 1948-63 under First & Second Plans. Dedicated by Nehru 22 Oct 1963 as 'new temple of resurgent India'. Then India's highest dam (226m). Symbol of Nehruvian vision.

eco_hirakud_dam.label: Hirakud Dam
eco_hirakud_dam.subject: economics
eco_hirakud_dam.detail: On Mahanadi (Odisha). First major post-independence dam, started 1948, inaugurated by Nehru 13 Jan 1957. Then world's longest dam (26km). Flood control + irrigation + hydropower.

eco_damodar_valley.label: Damodar Valley Corporation (1948)
eco_damodar_valley.subject: economics
eco_damodar_valley.detail: Set up July 1948 — first river valley authority modelled on TVA (Tennessee Valley). Covers Damodar basin (Jharkhand-WB). Multipurpose: flood control, irrigation, power, navigation. Flagship Nehruvian public-sector institution.

eco_bhilai_rourkela_durgapur.label: Bhilai-Rourkela-Durgapur Steel Plants
eco_bhilai_rourkela_durgapur.subject: economics
eco_bhilai_rourkela_durgapur.detail: Three public-sector steel mills under Second Plan: Bhilai (1955, Soviet help), Rourkela (1955, West German), Durgapur (1956, UK). Plus expansion of Tata Iron & Steel, Hindustan Steel. Core of industrial self-reliance strategy.

eco_mrtp_act_1969.label: MRTP Act (1969)
eco_mrtp_act_1969.subject: economics
eco_mrtp_act_1969.detail: Monopolies and Restrictive Trade Practices Act 1969. Based on Mahalanobis Committee 1964 + Dutt Committee 1969 findings that Tatas/Birlas concentrated too much economic power. Required MRTP Commission approval for expansion/merger by big houses. Repealed/replaced by Competition Act 2002.

eco_fera_1973.label: FERA (Foreign Exchange Regulation Act, 1973)
eco_fera_1973.subject: economics
eco_fera_1973.detail: Indira era. Tight restrictions on foreign companies — forex controls required dilution to 40% foreign equity. IBM and Coca-Cola exited India 1977 rather than dilute. Replaced by FEMA 1999.

eco_nationalisation_coal.label: Nationalisation of Coal (1971-73)
eco_nationalisation_coal.subject: economics
eco_nationalisation_coal.detail: Coking Coal Mines Nationalisation Act 1971 + Coal Mines Nationalisation Act 1973. Coal India Limited established 1975. Indira era — extension of public-sector dominance. Preceded by 1969 bank nationalisation.

eco_nationalisation_insurance.label: Nationalisation of General Insurance (1972)
eco_nationalisation_insurance.subject: economics
eco_nationalisation_insurance.detail: General Insurance Business (Nationalisation) Act 1972 — 107 insurers nationalised into 4 subsidiaries of GIC (General Insurance Corp). Followed LIC nationalisation (1956). Reversed by 1999 IRDA Act.

eco_1966_devaluation.label: 1966 Rupee Devaluation
eco_1966_devaluation.subject: economics
eco_1966_devaluation.detail: See hist_rupee_devaluation_1966. Economics angle: broke fixed-exchange-rate peg, 36.5% devaluation. Prompted by Third Plan failures, 1965 war, drought, US aid conditionality (PL-480 'ship-to-mouth'). Failed to boost exports quickly; politically toxic.

eco_plan_targets_growth.label: Five Year Plan Growth Rates (1951-1990)
eco_plan_targets_growth.subject: economics
eco_plan_targets_growth.detail: 1st (3.6%), 2nd (4.0-4.3%), 3rd (2.8% failed), 4th (3.3%), 5th (4.8%), 6th (5.7% first to beat target), 7th (6%). Average ~3.5% 'Hindu rate of growth' through 1950-80s. Accelerated post-1980 with deregulation.

eco_hindu_rate_growth.label: Hindu Rate of Growth
eco_hindu_rate_growth.subject: economics
eco_hindu_rate_growth.detail: Term coined by Raj Krishna (1978) for India's 3.5% annual growth 1950-80, low vs East Asia's 7-10%. Derogatory — implied stagnation due to planning-era constraints. Broken by 1980s partial liberalisation (5.5%) and decisively by 1991 reforms.

eco_zamindari_abolition.label: Zamindari Abolition (1950s)
eco_zamindari_abolition.subject: economics
eco_zamindari_abolition.detail: Multiple state laws 1947-56 abolishing zamindari, jagirdari, inamdari. UP Zamindari Abolition Act 1950; Bihar 1950; West Bengal Estates Acquisition 1953. Transferred land from 'intermediaries' to actual tillers (ryots). First-phase land reform — largely successful.

eco_bhoodan_movement.label: Bhoodan Movement
eco_bhoodan_movement.subject: economics
eco_bhoodan_movement.detail: Vinoba Bhave's land-gift movement from 1951 (started Pochampalli, AP). Persuaded landlords to donate land to landless. ~4.4M acres gifted by 1960s; ~2.5M actually distributed. Extended to Gramdan (village-collective ownership). Peaceful alternative to radical land redistribution. Substantially wound down by 1970.

eco_cooperative_movement.label: Cooperative Movement in India
eco_cooperative_movement.subject: economics
eco_cooperative_movement.detail: Post-1947 expansion — AMUL (1946), cooperative credit societies, IFFCO (1967), KRIBHCO (1980). Nagpur Resolution 1959 pushed 'cooperative joint farming' (failed). Kerala/WB strong. Cooperative federalism through Vaidyanathan Committee.

eco_hyv_seeds.label: HYV (High-Yielding Variety) Seeds
eco_hyv_seeds.subject: economics
eco_hyv_seeds.detail: Dwarf wheat varieties imported from Mexico (Norman Borlaug, CIMMYT) and rice from IRRI Philippines. Mexican wheat: Sonora-64, Lerma Rojo. Adopted 1966 onwards. Wheat yield doubled. Required complementary inputs (fertiliser, irrigation, credit, MSP).

eco_fci_1965.label: Food Corporation of India (1965)
eco_fci_1965.subject: economics
eco_fci_1965.detail: Established 1965 under Food Corporations Act. Procures food grains at MSP, maintains buffer stock, distributes through PDS. Core of India's food security system. C. Subramaniam's creation.

eco_apc_cacp.label: Agricultural Prices Commission (APC, 1965)
eco_apc_cacp.subject: economics
eco_apc_cacp.detail: Set up Jan 1965 to recommend MSP for crops. Renamed CACP (Commission for Agricultural Costs & Prices) 1985. Key institution enabling Green Revolution by assuring farmers remunerative prices.

eco_msp.label: Minimum Support Price (MSP)
eco_msp.subject: economics
eco_msp.detail: Govt-guaranteed procurement floor price for key crops. Started 1966-67 for wheat, extended to 23+ crops. Recommended by APC/CACP. Backbone of Green Revolution incentive structure. Major farmer protest issue late 2010s onwards.

hist_1969_ahmedabad_riots.label: 1969 Ahmedabad Riots
hist_1969_ahmedabad_riots.subject: history
hist_1969_ahmedabad_riots.detail: 18-28 Sept 1969 Hindu-Muslim riots, ~500-2,000 deaths (disputed). First major post-independence communal violence. Trigger: cow-dispute. Reddy Commission found systematic. Set template for subsequent riots. Gandhi's birthplace irony.

hist_bhiwandi_1970.label: Bhiwandi Riots (May 1970)
hist_bhiwandi_1970.subject: history
hist_bhiwandi_1970.detail: Bhiwandi-Jalgaon-Mahad riots in Maharashtra May 1970. 200+ killed, mostly Muslim. Sparked by Shivaji Jayanti procession. Madon Commission. Indira govt called out army. Pattern of planned communal violence tied to politics.

hist_ram_janmabhoomi_1980s.label: Ram Janmabhoomi Movement (1980s)
hist_ram_janmabhoomi_1980s.subject: history
hist_ram_janmabhoomi_1980s.detail: VHP-led campaign from early 1980s to 'liberate' Babri Masjid site (claimed as Ram's birthplace). Shilanyas 1989, LK Advani's Rath Yatra Sept-Oct 1990. VP Singh govt fell blocking yatra. Mosque demolished 6 Dec 1992 (era-11 boundary).

hist_rath_yatra_1990.label: Advani's Rath Yatra (Sept-Oct 1990)
hist_rath_yatra_1990.subject: history
hist_rath_yatra_1990.detail: L.K. Advani's BJP Rath Yatra from Somnath to Ayodhya in 'Toyota chariot' — Ram temple campaign. 10,000km through 8 states. Arrested in Bihar by Lalu Yadav 23 Oct 1990. BJP withdrew support from VP Singh govt, which fell 7 Nov 1990.

pol_mandal_implementation_1990.label: Mandal Implementation (August 1990)
pol_mandal_implementation_1990.subject: polity
pol_mandal_implementation_1990.detail: V.P. Singh government decided in August 1990 to implement Mandal Commission's 27% OBC reservation in central government jobs and PSUs. Triggered violent anti-Mandal agitations in North India — students self-immolated. Reshaped politics around caste mobilisation.

pol_indra_sawhney_case.label: Indra Sawhney Case (1992)
pol_indra_sawhney_case.subject: polity
pol_indra_sawhney_case.detail: 9-judge SC bench Nov 1992. Upheld 27% OBC reservation (Mandal). Introduced: 'creamy layer' exclusion, 50% overall reservation cap, reservations only in initial appointment (not promotions — later amended by 77th Amendment 1995).

hist_towards_equality_1974.label: Towards Equality Report (1974)
hist_towards_equality_1974.subject: history
hist_towards_equality_1974.detail: First govt report on status of women in India (Dec 1974). Committee chaired by Phulrenu Guha under Education Ministry. Documented widening gender gaps post-1947 — declining sex ratio, limited gains from law. Catalyst for feminist movement of late 1970s.

hist_mathura_case_1979.label: Mathura Rape Case (1972/1979)
hist_mathura_case_1979.subject: history
hist_mathura_case_1979.detail: 14-year-old tribal girl raped 1972 in Desaiganj police station, Maharashtra. SC 1979 acquitted officers — 'no injuries' → 'consent'. Public outrage. Open letter by 4 law professors. Led to Criminal Law (Second Amendment) Act 1983 — burden-of-proof shift in custodial rape cases.

hist_chipko_movement.label: Chipko Movement (1973)
hist_chipko_movement.subject: history
hist_chipko_movement.detail: Tree-hugging environmental movement in Garhwal (Uttarakhand). Led by Chandi Prasad Bhatt, Sunderlal Bahuguna, Gaura Devi. 1973 Reni village women hugged trees to prevent felling. Spawned decentralised forest policy. Inspired global eco-movement. Forest Conservation Act 1980 partially a response.

hist_narmada_bachao.label: Narmada Bachao Andolan (1985 onwards)
hist_narmada_bachao.subject: history
hist_narmada_bachao.detail: Led by Medha Patkar from 1985 against Sardar Sarovar Dam (Narmada). Raised rehabilitation, environmental costs. World Bank withdrew 1993 after Morse Review. SC in Narmada case (2000) allowed dam at reduced height. Landmark environmental-justice movement.

hist_silent_valley.label: Silent Valley Movement (Kerala, 1970s-80s)
hist_silent_valley.subject: history
hist_silent_valley.detail: Campaign against Silent Valley hydel project in Kerala's Western Ghats. KSSP (Kerala Sasthra Sahitya Parishat) led. Indira Gandhi scrapped project Jan 1981. Silent Valley declared national park 1984. Early environmental victory.

hist_progressive_artists_group.label: Progressive Artists' Group (Bombay, 1947)
hist_progressive_artists_group.subject: history
hist_progressive_artists_group.detail: Founded Aug 1947 Bombay by F.N. Souza, K.H. Ara, S.H. Raza, M.F. Husain, S.K. Bakre, H.A. Gade. Broke from Bengal School, embraced modernism (Cubism, Expressionism). Disbanded 1956, but members became giants of Indian modern art.

hist_satyajit_ray_pather.label: Pather Panchali (1955) / Parallel Cinema
hist_satyajit_ray_pather.subject: history
hist_satyajit_ray_pather.detail: Satyajit Ray's debut, Apu Trilogy first film (1955). Launched Indian parallel/art cinema. Won best human document at Cannes 1956. Other masters: Ritwik Ghatak, Mrinal Sen, Bimal Roy. Later 1970s: Shyam Benegal, Govind Nihalani.

hist_sahitya_akademi_1954.label: Sahitya Akademi (1954)
hist_sahitya_akademi_1954.subject: history
hist_sahitya_akademi_1954.detail: National Academy of Letters. Inaugurated 12 March 1954 in Delhi. Promotes Indian literature in 24 recognised languages. Sahitya Akademi Awards annually since 1955. Autonomous under Culture Ministry.

hist_sangeet_natak_akademi.label: Sangeet Natak Akademi (1952)
hist_sangeet_natak_akademi.subject: history
hist_sangeet_natak_akademi.detail: India's first national academy for performing arts (music, dance, drama). Founded Jan 1953 (registered 1952). Autonomous body under Culture Ministry. SNA Awards, Ratna Sadasya. Based in Delhi.

hist_lalit_kala_akademi.label: Lalit Kala Akademi (1954)
hist_lalit_kala_akademi.subject: history
hist_lalit_kala_akademi.detail: National Academy of Fine Arts. Founded 5 Aug 1954. Promotes Indian fine arts, organises Triennale India, supports artists. Rashtriya Lalit Kala Ratna awards. Part of trio with Sahitya and Sangeet Natak Akademis.

pol_4th_amendment_1955.label: 4th Amendment (1955)
pol_4th_amendment_1955.subject: polity
pol_4th_amendment_1955.detail: Put compensation scale for compulsory land acquisition beyond court scrutiny. Authorised state to nationalise any trade. Added more Acts to Ninth Schedule. Extended scope of Article 31A. Response to Bela Banerjee case.

pol_9th_amendment_1960.label: 9th Amendment (1960) — Berubari
pol_9th_amendment_1960.subject: polity
pol_9th_amendment_1960.detail: Facilitated cession of Berubari Union (West Bengal) to Pakistan per Indo-Pakistan Agreement 1958 (Nehru-Noon). Passed after SC's Berubari Union case (1960) held that territorial cession requires constitutional amendment. Never actually notified for implementation.

pol_12th_amendment_1962.label: 12th Amendment (1962) — Goa, Daman, Diu
pol_12th_amendment_1962.subject: polity
pol_12th_amendment_1962.detail: Incorporated Goa, Daman and Diu into Indian Union after Dec 1961 liberation. Added to Union Territory list.

pol_13th_amendment_1962.label: 13th Amendment (1962) — Nagaland Statehood
pol_13th_amendment_1962.subject: polity
pol_13th_amendment_1962.detail: Granted statehood to Nagaland (carved from Assam) with special provisions under Article 371A. Response to Naga insurgency and 1960 Naga agreement. Nagaland became 16th state on 1 Dec 1963.

pol_14th_amendment_1962.label: 14th Amendment (1962) — Puducherry
pol_14th_amendment_1962.subject: polity
pol_14th_amendment_1962.detail: Incorporated Puducherry (then Pondicherry) into Indian Union following 1954 merger. Created legislatures for Himachal Pradesh, Manipur, Tripura, Goa Daman Diu, Puducherry (all then UTs).

pol_16th_amendment_1963.label: 16th Amendment (1963) — Sovereignty Restrictions
pol_16th_amendment_1963.subject: polity
pol_16th_amendment_1963.detail: Empowered state to restrict freedom of speech/assembly/association in interests of sovereignty and integrity of India. Added 'integrity' to oath. Response to DMK's earlier separatist rhetoric in Tamil Nadu.

pol_17th_amendment_1964.label: 17th Amendment (1964) — Ninth Schedule Expansion
pol_17th_amendment_1964.subject: polity
pol_17th_amendment_1964.detail: Required market-value compensation for land under personal cultivation. Added 44 more Acts to Ninth Schedule. Response to Karimbil Kunhikoman case (Kerala).

pol_21st_amendment_1967.label: 21st Amendment (1967) — Sindhi Added
pol_21st_amendment_1967.subject: polity
pol_21st_amendment_1967.detail: Added Sindhi as 15th language in Eighth Schedule. Response to Sindhi-speaking community's demand after Partition displacement.

pol_22nd_amendment_1969.label: 22nd Amendment (1969) — Meghalaya
pol_22nd_amendment_1969.subject: polity
pol_22nd_amendment_1969.detail: Created autonomous state of Meghalaya within Assam (Khasi, Jaintia, Garo Hills). Meghalaya became full state via 23rd Constitutional (Amendment) Act 1972 + NE Reorganisation Act 1971.

pol_31st_amendment_1972.label: 31st Amendment (1972) — Lok Sabha 525→545
pol_31st_amendment_1972.subject: polity
pol_31st_amendment_1972.detail: Increased Lok Sabha strength from 525 to 545 seats. Froze state-wise LS seat distribution based on 1971 census (further frozen 2001 till 2026 by 84th Amendment).

pol_36th_amendment_1975.label: 36th Amendment (1975) — Sikkim Statehood
pol_36th_amendment_1975.subject: polity
pol_36th_amendment_1975.detail: Made Sikkim 22nd full state of Indian Union on 26 April 1975, replacing 'associate state' status under 35th Amendment 1974. Chogyal monarchy abolished after 1975 referendum (97.5% for merger).

pol_38th_amendment_1975.label: 38th Amendment (1975) — Emergency Non-Justiciable
pol_38th_amendment_1975.subject: polity
pol_38th_amendment_1975.detail: Emergency-era amendment. Made President's proclamation of Emergency and ordinances non-justiciable. Empowered President to declare Emergency on different grounds simultaneously. Reversed by 44th Amendment 1978.

pol_39th_amendment_1975.label: 39th Amendment (1975) — Election Protection
pol_39th_amendment_1975.subject: polity
pol_39th_amendment_1975.detail: Indira's shield after Allahabad HC verdict (June 1975). Placed elections of PM, President, VP, Speaker beyond judicial review. Struck down in Indira Nehru Gandhi vs Raj Narain (1975) — SC invoked basic structure doctrine for first time.

pol_40th_amendment_1976.label: 40th Amendment (1976) — Maritime Zones
pol_40th_amendment_1976.subject: polity
pol_40th_amendment_1976.detail: Empowered Parliament to specify territorial waters, EEZ (Exclusive Economic Zone), continental shelf, maritime zones of India. Constitutional basis for Maritime Zones Act 1976.

pol_58th_amendment_1987.label: 58th Amendment (1987) — Hindi Constitution
pol_58th_amendment_1987.subject: polity
pol_58th_amendment_1987.detail: Provided authoritative text of Constitution in Hindi language, giving same legal sanctity as English version. Article 394A added.

pol_61st_amendment_1989.label: 61st Amendment (1989) — Voting Age 18
pol_61st_amendment_1989.subject: polity
pol_61st_amendment_1989.detail: Reduced voting age from 21 to 18 years for LS and Assembly elections. Article 326 amended. Rajiv Gandhi's initiative. Added ~5 crore young voters. Took effect before 1989 general elections.

pol_65th_amendment_1990.label: 65th Amendment Act (1990)
pol_65th_amendment_1990.subject: polity
pol_65th_amendment_1990.detail: Added Article 338 — established National Commission for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (combined) with constitutional status. Replaced the earlier office of Special Officer for SCs/STs. Commission bifurcated into NCSC and NCST by 89th Amendment (2003).

pol_amendments_summary.label: Constitutional Amendments 1950-1990 (Overview)
pol_amendments_summary.subject: polity
pol_amendments_summary.detail: 65 amendments passed 1951-1990, 4 themes: (1) State reorganisation — 7th, 9th, 12th-14th, 18th, 22nd, 27th, 35th, 36th, 53rd-57th; (2) SC/ST/OBC reservation extensions — 8th, 23rd, 45th, 51st, 62nd; (3) Land reform / 9th Schedule — 1st, 4th, 17th, 29th, 34th, 40th, 47th, 66th; (4) Emergency + judicial — 24-26th, 38th-42nd (authoritarian), 43rd-44th (restoration).

pol_ak_gopalan_case.label: A.K. Gopalan Case (1950)
pol_ak_gopalan_case.subject: polity
pol_ak_gopalan_case.detail: A.K. Gopalan vs State of Madras, first major post-constitution SC case. Challenged Preventive Detention Act 1950. SC held narrow interpretation — Articles 19, 21, 22 were mutually exclusive. Procedure 'established by law' literal (not due process). Overruled by Maneka Gandhi (1978).

pol_champakam_dorairajan.label: Champakam Dorairajan Case (1951)
pol_champakam_dorairajan.subject: polity
pol_champakam_dorairajan.detail: State of Madras vs Champakam Dorairajan. Madras Communal GO providing caste-based reservation struck down. Led to 1st Constitutional Amendment 1951 adding Article 15(4) authorising special provisions for socially/educationally backward classes.

pol_romesh_thappar_case.label: Romesh Thappar Case (1950)
pol_romesh_thappar_case.subject: polity
pol_romesh_thappar_case.detail: Romesh Thappar vs State of Madras 1950. Communist magazine 'Cross Roads' banned. SC struck down Madras Maintenance of Public Order Act. Expanded free speech under Article 19(1)(a). Led to 1st Amendment 1951 adding 'public order' as permissible restriction.

pol_shankari_prasad_case.label: Shankari Prasad Case (1951)
pol_shankari_prasad_case.subject: polity
pol_shankari_prasad_case.detail: Shankari Prasad Singh Deo vs Union of India 1951. Challenge to 1st Amendment. SC held Parliament can amend Fundamental Rights under Article 368; 'law' in Article 13(2) means ordinary law, not constitutional amendment. Reaffirmed in Sajjan Singh (1965), reversed by Golaknath (1967).

pol_sajjan_singh_case.label: Sajjan Singh Case (1965)
pol_sajjan_singh_case.subject: polity
pol_sajjan_singh_case.detail: Sajjan Singh vs State of Rajasthan 1965. Challenge to 17th Amendment. SC (5-judge) 3-2 reaffirmed Shankari Prasad — Parliament can amend FRs. But minority (Hidayatullah, Mudholkar) expressed doubts — seed of Golaknath.

pol_berubari_case.label: Berubari Union Case (1960)
pol_berubari_case.subject: polity
pol_berubari_case.detail: In Re: Berubari Union 1960. Presidential Reference on Nehru-Noon agreement's cession of Berubari to Pakistan. SC held territorial cession requires constitutional amendment (not just ordinary law). Also held Preamble is not part of Constitution (later reversed in Kesavananda 1973). Led to 9th Amendment 1960.

pol_indira_nehru_gandhi_case.label: Indira Nehru Gandhi vs Raj Narain (1975)
pol_indira_nehru_gandhi_case.subject: polity
pol_indira_nehru_gandhi_case.detail: SC 7 Nov 1975 struck down 39th Amendment (1975) which placed PM's election beyond judicial review. First application of basic structure doctrine post-Kesavananda. Upheld Indira's election on merits via election law changes but doctrine stood. Judges: Ray CJ, Khanna, Mathew, Beg, Chandrachud Y.V.

pol_waman_rao_case.label: Waman Rao Case (1981)
pol_waman_rao_case.subject: polity
pol_waman_rao_case.detail: SC 1981 held amendments to Ninth Schedule BEFORE 24 April 1973 (Kesavananda date) are valid; amendments AFTER that date are subject to basic structure review. 'Doctrine of prospective overruling'. Key case fencing basic structure doctrine.

pol_eci_1950.label: Election Commission of India (25 Jan 1950)
pol_eci_1950.subject: polity
pol_eci_1950.detail: Established 25 January 1950 under Article 324, one day before Constitution came into force. Single-member body (CEC) till 16 Oct 1989, then multi-member (CEC + 2 ECs) after 1991 (some flip-flops). First CEC: Sukumar Sen 1950-58. Key institution of Indian democracy.

pol_cag_1950.label: Comptroller & Auditor General (CAG, 1950)
pol_cag_1950.subject: polity
pol_cag_1950.detail: Constitutional body under Article 148. First CAG: V. Narahari Rao (1948-54). Audits Central and State govt accounts. 'Guardian of the public purse'. Submits report to President/Governor, tabled in Parliament/Assembly.

pol_upsc_1950.label: Union Public Service Commission (UPSC, 1950)
pol_upsc_1950.subject: polity
pol_upsc_1950.detail: Constitutional body under Article 315. Conducts Civil Services, Engineering Services, other All-India exams. Successor to Federal Public Service Commission (1935). First Chairman post-1950: H.K. Kripalani.

pol_finance_commission_1951.label: Finance Commission (1951)
pol_finance_commission_1951.subject: polity
pol_finance_commission_1951.detail: Constituted every 5 years under Article 280. Recommends Centre-State tax sharing, grants-in-aid. First FC: K.C. Neogy, 1951. K. Santhanam (FC-2), A.K. Chanda (FC-3), P.V. Rajamannar (FC-4), Mahavir Tyagi (FC-5), K. Brahmananda Reddy (FC-6), J.M. Shelat (FC-7), Y.B. Chavan (FC-8), N.K.P. Salve (FC-9).

pol_planning_commission_1950.label: Planning Commission (March 1950)
pol_planning_commission_1950.subject: polity
pol_planning_commission_1950.detail: Established 15 March 1950 by Cabinet resolution (extra-constitutional). Nehru chaired ex-officio. Designed Five Year Plans. G.L. Nanda, C.M. Trivedi, P.C. Mahalanobis key architects. Replaced by NITI Aayog on 1 Jan 2015.

pol_ncw_1990.label: National Commission for Women (1990)
pol_ncw_1990.subject: polity
pol_ncw_1990.detail: Statutory body under NCW Act 1990, constituted 31 Jan 1992. Recommends legal safeguards, investigates violations of women's rights. First chair: Jayanti Patnaik. Not a constitutional body (that's NCSC/ST).

pol_emergency_1962_external.label: External Emergency (1962-68)
pol_emergency_1962_external.subject: polity
pol_emergency_1962_external.detail: First national emergency under Article 352. Proclaimed 26 Oct 1962 during China war on grounds of 'external aggression'. Revoked 10 Jan 1968. Enabled DIR (Defence of India Rules), suspension of FRs.

pol_emergency_1971_external.label: External Emergency (1971-77)
pol_emergency_1971_external.subject: polity
pol_emergency_1971_external.detail: Second national emergency, 3 Dec 1971 during Bangladesh War. Continued until March 1977. Overlapped with internal Emergency (1975-77). Never properly revoked before internal emergency. Janata govt revoked both.

pol_presidents_rule_first_1959.label: First President's Rule — Kerala (1959)
pol_presidents_rule_first_1959.subject: polity
pol_presidents_rule_first_1959.detail: 31 July 1959 — Nehru dismissed first democratically elected communist state govt (E.M.S. Namboodiripad, CPI, Kerala 1957-59) under Article 356. Trigger: 'Liberation Struggle' against Education Bill. Controversial precedent for political abuse of Article 356. Used 100+ times since.

pol_ninth_schedule.label: Ninth Schedule
pol_ninth_schedule.subject: polity
pol_ninth_schedule.detail: Added by 1st Amendment 1951 to protect land reform laws from judicial review. 284 acts added by 2018. I.R. Coelho case (2007) held that post-24 April 1973 additions are subject to basic structure review. Original purpose: save zamindari abolition laws.

pol_tenth_schedule.label: Tenth Schedule — Anti-Defection
pol_tenth_schedule.subject: polity
pol_tenth_schedule.detail: Added by 52nd Amendment 1985. Provides grounds for disqualification of MPs/MLAs on defection. Originally had 'split' exemption (1/3rd), removed by 91st Amendment 2003 (only 'merger' with 2/3rd now). Speaker/Chairman decides disqualification (judicial review allowed after Kihoto Hollohan 1992).

pol_fundamental_duties_42nd.label: Fundamental Duties (Part IV-A, 1976)
pol_fundamental_duties_42nd.subject: polity
pol_fundamental_duties_42nd.detail: Added by 42nd Amendment 1976 on Swaran Singh Committee recommendation (inspired by USSR Constitution). Originally 10 duties; 11th added by 86th Amendment 2002 (parental duty to educate children 6-14). Non-justiciable, moral obligations.

pol_preamble_42nd_changes.label: Preamble Changes by 42nd Amendment (1976)
pol_preamble_42nd_changes.subject: polity
pol_preamble_42nd_changes.detail: Added three words to Preamble: 'Socialist', 'Secular', 'Integrity' (last joined 'Unity and Integrity'). Changed 'Sovereign Democratic Republic' to 'Sovereign Socialist Secular Democratic Republic'. Preamble remains part of basic structure post-Kesavananda.

pol_swaran_singh_committee.label: Swaran Singh Committee (1976)
pol_swaran_singh_committee.subject: polity
pol_swaran_singh_committee.detail: Congress-appointed 12-member committee under Sardar Swaran Singh. Recommended Fundamental Duties, Preamble changes, DPSP/FR ordering, curtailing judicial review. Report used to enact 42nd Amendment 1976. Not a constitutional commission.

pol_officially_official_language_act_196.label: Official Languages Act (1963) + 1967 Amendment
pol_officially_official_language_act_196.subject: polity
pol_officially_official_language_act_196.detail: Parliament enacted 1963 to continue English as official language alongside Hindi indefinitely (not limited to 1965 deadline of Article 343). Amended 1967 after anti-Hindi agitations — guaranteed English continuation in non-Hindi states. Basis of current language policy.

pol_citizenship_act_1955.label: Citizenship Act (1955)
pol_citizenship_act_1955.subject: polity
pol_citizenship_act_1955.detail: Defines acquisition of Indian citizenship: birth, descent, registration, naturalisation, incorporation of territory. Articles 5-11 of Constitution left details to Parliament. Amended multiple times — 1985 (Assam), 1986, 1992, 2003, 2005, 2015, 2019 (CAA).

pol_preventive_detention_act_1950.label: Preventive Detention Act (1950)
pol_preventive_detention_act_1950.subject: polity
pol_preventive_detention_act_1950.detail: Enacted Feb 1950 under Article 22 — detention without trial. Challenged in A.K. Gopalan. Lapsed 1969. Succeeded by MISA (1971), National Security Act (1980), POTA (2002, repealed 2004), UAPA (amended). Critical era-10 civil liberties backdrop.

pol_nsa_1980.label: National Security Act (1980)
pol_nsa_1980.subject: polity
pol_nsa_1980.detail: Preventive detention act passed by Indira govt 1980 to replace MISA (repealed 1978). Allows detention up to 12 months without trial on grounds of 'national security', 'public order'. Still in force. Used by Centre and states.

pol_official_secrets_act_1923.label: Official Secrets Act (1923)
pol_official_secrets_act_1923.subject: polity
pol_official_secrets_act_1923.detail: Colonial-era espionage law retained by independent India. Makes disclosure of 'secret' official information a crime (2-14 years). Widely critiqued post-RTI (2005). Covered Bofors, ISRO spy case (1994) etc. Reform recommended by 2nd ARC 2006.

pol_all_india_services.label: All India Services (IAS, IPS, IFoS)
pol_all_india_services.subject: polity
pol_all_india_services.detail: Article 312 — services common to Centre and states. Originally IAS (successor to ICS, 1947) and IPS (from IP). Indian Forest Service added 1966. All AIS officers recruited by UPSC, state-cadre allocated, serve under both Centre/state. Sardar Patel's 'steel frame'.

pol_ics_to_ias.label: ICS → IAS Transition (1947-50)
pol_ics_to_ias.subject: polity
pol_ics_to_ias.detail: Indian Civil Service (ICS, 1858) continued briefly post-1947. Recast as IAS per Article 312 + 1951 All India Services Act. Patel as Home Minister defended 'steel frame' against opposition from princes and politicians. Pathway for ICS officers + new recruits.

eco_mahalanobis_plan.label: Mahalanobis Plan (Second Plan)
eco_mahalanobis_plan.subject: economics
eco_mahalanobis_plan.detail: P.C. Mahalanobis's heavy-industry growth model for Second Plan (1956-61). Four-sector model: investment goods, consumer manufactured goods, consumer household goods, services. Emphasis on capital-goods sector investment to build industrial base. Critics: Vakil, Brahmananda favoured wage-goods first.

eco_lic_nationalisation_1956.label: LIC Nationalisation (1956)
eco_lic_nationalisation_1956.subject: economics
eco_lic_nationalisation_1956.detail: Life Insurance Corporation Act 1956 nationalised 245 private life-insurance companies into LIC on 1 Sept 1956. First major nationalisation of private financial sector. Response to several scandals in private insurance. LIC monopoly till 1999 IRDA Act.

eco_sbi_1955.label: State Bank of India (1955)
eco_sbi_1955.subject: economics
eco_sbi_1955.detail: SBI Act 1955 nationalised Imperial Bank of India (originally 1921 amalgamation of 3 presidency banks — Bengal 1806, Bombay 1840, Madras 1843) into State Bank of India on 1 July 1955. First major bank nationalisation, 14 years before 1969.

eco_bank_nationalisation_1980.label: Second Bank Nationalisation (1980)
eco_bank_nationalisation_1980.subject: economics
eco_bank_nationalisation_1980.detail: Six more private banks nationalised by Indira Gandhi on 15 April 1980: Andhra Bank, Corporation Bank, New Bank of India, Oriental Bank of Commerce, Punjab & Sind Bank, Vijaya Bank. Total 20 nationalised banks (1969 + 1980), covering 91% of deposits. Consolidation underway since 2019.

eco_rbi_1935.label: Reserve Bank of India (1935/1949)
eco_rbi_1935.subject: economics
eco_rbi_1935.detail: Established 1 April 1935 under RBI Act 1934 (era-9 boundary). Nationalised 1 Jan 1949 under RBI (Transfer to Public Ownership) Act 1948. Central bank — monetary policy, currency issue, banker to govt, regulator of banks. Key post-1947 institution.

eco_sidbi_nabard.label: NABARD (1982) & SIDBI (1990)
eco_sidbi_nabard.subject: economics
eco_sidbi_nabard.detail: NABARD: National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development, 12 July 1982, on Shivaraman Committee recommendation. Apex rural-development bank. SIDBI: Small Industries Development Bank of India, 2 April 1990, apex for small-scale industry.

eco_idbi_1964.label: IDBI (1964)
eco_idbi_1964.subject: economics
eco_idbi_1964.detail: Industrial Development Bank of India, established 1 July 1964 as RBI subsidiary. Apex development financial institution (DFI) for industry. Became independent of RBI 1976. Converted to commercial bank 2004 (IDBI Bank). Archetype of DFI era.

eco_ifci_1948.label: IFCI (1948)
eco_ifci_1948.subject: economics
eco_ifci_1948.detail: Industrial Finance Corporation of India, 1948 (first DFI). Long-term finance for industry. Became public limited company 1993. Core of Nehruvian financial architecture — direct lending to Plan priorities.

eco_icici_1955.label: ICICI (1955)
eco_icici_1955.subject: economics
eco_icici_1955.detail: Industrial Credit and Investment Corporation of India, 1955. Private-sector-oriented DFI, backed by World Bank, US, British firms, Indian private sector. Became ICICI Bank (first major reverse-merger 2002 — DFI merged into its subsidiary bank).

eco_nrega_prelude.label: Maharashtra Employment Guarantee Scheme (1972)
eco_nrega_prelude.subject: economics
eco_nrega_prelude.detail: Maharashtra's 1972-77 drought relief EGS — guaranteed manual work within 5km, minimum wage. Pioneered wage-employment-as-right concept. Model for NREGA 2005 (era 11). Designed by V.S. Page, implemented by Vasantrao Naik govt.

eco_pds_expansion.label: Public Distribution System (PDS) — Expansion
eco_pds_expansion.subject: economics
eco_pds_expansion.detail: Originated WW2 rationing (Bengal 1943 famine). Expanded post-1965 with FCI procurement + ration shops. Universal till 1997 (TPDS with APL/BPL), 2013 NFSA moved to rights-based approach (era 11). India's largest food safety net.

eco_irdp_1978.label: Integrated Rural Development Programme (IRDP, 1978)
eco_irdp_1978.subject: economics
eco_irdp_1978.detail: Launched 1978-79 by Janata, expanded nationwide 1980. Self-employment + assets scheme for rural BPL households — subsidised credit for income-generating assets. Running for 20+ years; merged into SGSY (1999).

eco_nrep_rlegp.label: NREP (1980) + RLEGP (1983)
eco_nrep_rlegp.subject: economics
eco_nrep_rlegp.detail: Wage-employment schemes: National Rural Employment Programme (1980) + Rural Landless Employment Guarantee Programme (1983). Merged 1989 into Jawahar Rozgar Yojana (JRY). Manual-labour public works. Predecessor to NREGA (2005).

eco_jawahar_rozgar_yojana.label: Jawahar Rozgar Yojana (1989)
eco_jawahar_rozgar_yojana.subject: economics
eco_jawahar_rozgar_yojana.detail: Launched 1 April 1989 by Rajiv Gandhi, merging NREP + RLEGP. Rural wage-employment with 30% for women, 30% for SC/ST. Local Panchayat implementation. Renamed JGSY 1999, absorbed into NREGA 2005.

eco_rural_banks_1975.label: Regional Rural Banks (RRBs, 1975)
eco_rural_banks_1975.subject: economics
eco_rural_banks_1975.detail: Established 2 Oct 1975 on Narasimham Committee (1975) recommendation. Joint ownership: Centre 50%, Sponsor Bank 35%, State 15%. Rural credit to small farmers, artisans, labourers. 196 RRBs at peak, consolidated to 43 by 2020.

eco_bop_crisis_buildup.label: BOP Crisis Build-up (1985-91)
eco_bop_crisis_buildup.subject: economics
eco_bop_crisis_buildup.detail: Rajiv-era fiscal deficit (8%+ of GDP), oil imports, short-term debt accumulation. 1990-91 Gulf War spiked oil. Forex reserves down to 15 days' imports by June 1991. Credit rating downgrades. IMF bailout contingent on liberalisation. Triggered 1991 reforms (era 11 opening).

eco_dutt_committee_1969.label: Dutt Committee on Industrial Licensing (1969)
eco_dutt_committee_1969.subject: economics
eco_dutt_committee_1969.detail: Subimal Dutt Committee. Found that 20 large business houses cornered 2/3 of industrial licences 1956-66. Catalyst for MRTP Act 1969. Exposed licence-permit-quota raj's capture by established players.

eco_hazari_committee_1967.label: Hazari Committee (1967)
eco_hazari_committee_1967.subject: economics
eco_hazari_committee_1967.detail: R.K. Hazari Committee. Studied industrial planning and licensing. Found large business houses exploiting licensing system. Led to Monopolies Inquiry Commission (Mahalanobis Committee) 1964 follow-up, eventually MRTP 1969.

hist_mf_husain.label: M.F. Husain
hist_mf_husain.subject: history
hist_mf_husain.detail: Modernist painter (1915-2011), 'Picasso of India'. Member Progressive Artists' Group 1947. Horses, goddesses, Bharat Mata themes. Took Qatari citizenship 2010 amid Hindu-right controversies over nudes. Padma Shri 1966, Bhushan 1973, Vibhushan 1991.

hist_sh_raza.label: S.H. Raza
hist_sh_raza.subject: history
hist_sh_raza.detail: Modernist painter (1922-2016). Progressive Artists' Group founder. Lived in France 1950-2010. 'Bindu' series iconic. Padma Shri 1981, Padma Bhushan 2007, Padma Vibhushan 2013.

hist_ritwik_ghatak.label: Ritwik Ghatak
hist_ritwik_ghatak.subject: history
hist_ritwik_ghatak.detail: Bengali filmmaker (1925-1976). Along with Satyajit Ray and Mrinal Sen, defined Indian parallel cinema. Films: Meghe Dhaka Tara (1960), Subarnarekha (1965), Titash Ekti Nadir Naam (1973). Partition-obsessed themes.

hist_mrinal_sen.label: Mrinal Sen
hist_mrinal_sen.subject: history
hist_mrinal_sen.detail: Bengali filmmaker (1923-2018). Bhuvan Shome (1969) kickstarted parallel cinema movement with FFC (Film Finance Corp) funding. Calcutta trilogy (1971-73). Padma Bhushan, Dadasaheb Phalke 2003.

hist_shyam_benegal.label: Shyam Benegal
hist_shyam_benegal.subject: history
hist_shyam_benegal.detail: Parallel cinema director from 1970s. Ankur (1974), Nishant (1975), Manthan (1976, Operation Flood film crowdfunded by dairy farmers), Bhumika (1977). Discovered Shabana Azmi, Smita Patil, Naseeruddin Shah.

hist_ncpa_1969.label: NCPA (1969)
hist_ncpa_1969.subject: history
hist_ncpa_1969.detail: National Centre for the Performing Arts, Mumbai. Founded 1969 by JRD Tata and Jamshed Bhabha. Premier performing arts venue — opera, Indian classical, theatre. Private initiative rare for culture.

hist_cciaf_icca.label: ICCR (1950)
hist_cciaf_icca.subject: history
hist_cciaf_icca.detail: Indian Council for Cultural Relations, founded 1950 by Maulana Azad (first Education Minister). External cultural diplomacy — exchange programmes, cultural centres abroad (Ichinichi 37+), scholarships for foreign students.

hist_sai_1984.label: Sports Authority of India (1984)
hist_sai_1984.subject: history
hist_sai_1984.detail: Established 1984 post-1982 Asian Games (Delhi). Apex sports body. Manages national training centres, talent identification. Under Youth Affairs and Sports Ministry.

hist_asiad_1982.label: 1982 Asian Games (Delhi)
hist_asiad_1982.subject: history
hist_asiad_1982.detail: 9th Asian Games, Delhi 19 Nov - 4 Dec 1982. India hosted after 1951. Built Nehru Stadium (Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium), new infrastructure. Colour TV launched nationwide for coverage — Doordarshan's first colour broadcast. 'Appu' elephant mascot. Political showcase for Indira.

hist_cricket_world_cup_1983.label: Cricket World Cup 1983
hist_cricket_world_cup_1983.subject: history
hist_cricket_world_cup_1983.detail: India won 3rd Prudential Cricket World Cup on 25 June 1983 at Lord's, beating West Indies by 43 runs. Kapil Dev captain. Defining sporting moment — launched Indian cricket as mass phenomenon, laid ground for BCCI economic rise.

hist_doordarshan_1959.label: Doordarshan (1959)
hist_doordarshan_1959.subject: history
hist_doordarshan_1959.detail: Launched 15 Sept 1959 as experimental TV service from Delhi. UNESCO assistance. Regular service 1965. Colour broadcasting from 1982 (Asian Games). National channel 1984. Monopoly till 1991 satellite TV.

hist_akashvani_air.label: All India Radio (AIR)
hist_akashvani_air.subject: history
hist_akashvani_air.detail: Successor to Indian State Broadcasting Service (1930). Named 'All India Radio' 1936; 'Akashvani' 1957. Vividh Bharati 1957 (popular music/entertainment). FM services from 1977. Originally under Ministry of I&B, autonomous Prasar Bharati since 1997.

pol_objectives_resolution_text.label: Objectives Resolution (13 Dec 1946)
pol_objectives_resolution_text.subject: polity
pol_objectives_resolution_text.detail: Moved by Nehru 13 Dec 1946, adopted 22 Jan 1947. Declared India as independent sovereign republic with justice-liberty-equality-fraternity. Became basis for Preamble. 8 clauses covering sovereign character, federal unit structure, guaranteed fundamental rights, minorities/backward classes/tribal areas protection, territorial integrity, world peace.

pol_article_1.label: Article 1 — Name and Territory
pol_article_1.subject: polity
pol_article_1.detail: 'India, that is Bharat, shall be a Union of States.' Asserts indestructible Union (vs destructible states). Berubari case (1960) held cession requires constitutional amendment. Territory = states + UTs + acquired territories. 'Union' preferred over 'Federation'.

pol_radhakrishnan.label: S. Radhakrishnan (2nd President, 1962-67)
pol_radhakrishnan.subject: polity
pol_radhakrishnan.detail: Philosopher-statesman. First VP 1952-62 under Rajendra Prasad. 2nd President 13 May 1962 - 13 May 1967. Birthday 5 Sept celebrated as Teachers' Day. Oxford Spalding Professor. Author of 'The Hindu View of Life'.

pol_zakir_husain.label: Zakir Husain (3rd President, 1967-69)
pol_zakir_husain.subject: polity
pol_zakir_husain.detail: First Muslim President of India, 13 May 1967 - died in office 3 May 1969. Educationist, founded Jamia Millia Islamia. Gandhian. First Indian President to die in office. Succeeded by V.V. Giri (as acting, then elected).

pol_sanjiva_reddy.label: Neelam Sanjiva Reddy (6th President, 1977-82)
pol_sanjiva_reddy.subject: polity
pol_sanjiva_reddy.detail: Only President elected unopposed (21 July 1977). Earlier defeated by V.V. Giri in 1969 (Congress Syndicate's candidate). Previous Speaker of LS, Andhra CM. Janata-backed. Presided over Janata collapse and Indira's 1980 return.

pol_zail_singh.label: Giani Zail Singh (7th President, 1982-87)
pol_zail_singh.subject: polity
pol_zail_singh.detail: First Sikh President. 25 July 1982 - 25 July 1987. Punjab CM 1972-77. Home Minister 1980-82. Controversially signed Operation Blue Star order despite reservations. Used pocket veto on Postal Bill 1986. Swore in Rajiv Gandhi hours after Indira's assassination.

pol_r_venkataraman.label: R. Venkataraman (8th President, 1987-92)
pol_r_venkataraman.subject: polity
pol_r_venkataraman.detail: 25 July 1987 - 25 July 1992. Presided over four PMs (Rajiv, VP Singh, Chandra Shekhar, Narasimha Rao) — political instability era. Appointed Chandra Shekhar PM Nov 1990. Authored 'My Presidential Years'.

pol_cbi_1963.label: Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI, 1963)
pol_cbi_1963.subject: polity
pol_cbi_1963.detail: Established 1 April 1963 by Home Ministry resolution (not by act). Successor to Delhi Special Police Establishment (DSPE) 1941. Santhanam Committee (1962) recommended its creation. India's premier investigating agency. Controversial 'caged parrot' (SC 2013).

pol_cvc_1964.label: Central Vigilance Commission (CVC, 1964)
pol_cvc_1964.subject: polity
pol_cvc_1964.detail: Established February 1964 on Santhanam Committee (1962) recommendation to combat corruption. Initially executive body; given statutory status by CVC Act 2003. Head: Central Vigilance Commissioner. Oversees vigilance administration in Central govt.

pol_santhanam_committee.label: Santhanam Committee on Prevention of Corruption (1962)
pol_santhanam_committee.subject: polity
pol_santhanam_committee.detail: K. Santhanam chaired. Submitted report 1964. Recommended CVC (est. 1964) + CBI (est. 1963). Identified corruption in government as serious concern. Led to Prevention of Corruption Act framework.

pol_arc_1_1966.label: Administrative Reforms Commission I (1966-70)
pol_arc_1_1966.subject: polity
pol_arc_1_1966.detail: Set up 5 Jan 1966 under Morarji Desai (later K. Hanumanthaiah). Submitted 20 reports 1966-70 with 537 recommendations. Recommended Lokpal/Lokayukta, civil service reform, district administration overhaul, removal of delays. Most not implemented.

pol_kaka_kalelkar_1953.label: Kaka Kalelkar Commission (1953)
pol_kaka_kalelkar_1953.subject: polity
pol_kaka_kalelkar_1953.detail: First Backward Classes Commission, appointed Jan 1953 under Article 340. Chair: Kaka Kalelkar. Submitted report March 1955 identifying 2,399 backward communities. Report rejected by Central govt due to internal disagreements + no consensus on criteria. Led to Mandal Commission (1979).

pol_ndc_1952.label: National Development Council (NDC, 1952)
pol_ndc_1952.subject: polity
pol_ndc_1952.detail: Established 6 Aug 1952 by Cabinet resolution (extra-constitutional, non-statutory). Apex body for plan approval. Members: PM (chair), all CMs, Union Cabinet ministers, Planning Commission. Reviewed plans before adoption. Effectively dormant since NITI Aayog (2015).

pol_inter_state_council.label: Inter-State Council (Article 263)
pol_inter_state_council.subject: polity
pol_inter_state_council.detail: Constitutional body under Article 263, but first established only 28 May 1990 by Presidential order (on Sarkaria Commission 1988 recommendation). PM heads, includes CMs, Union Ministers. Meets rarely. Unlike NDC, advisory on Centre-State disputes.

pol_zonal_councils_1957.label: Zonal Councils (1957)
pol_zonal_councils_1957.subject: polity
pol_zonal_councils_1957.detail: Established by States Reorganisation Act 1956 (Part III), constituted 1957. Five councils: Northern, Southern, Eastern, Western, Central. North-Eastern Council added 1971 (separate Act). Advisory bodies for inter-state cooperation. PM suggested by Nehru.

pol_cat_1985.label: Central Administrative Tribunal (CAT, 1985)
pol_cat_1985.subject: polity
pol_cat_1985.detail: Established 1 November 1985 under Administrative Tribunals Act 1985 (basis: Article 323-A added by 42nd Amendment 1976). Adjudicates disputes of central govt employees. Initially no appeal to HC (struck down by L. Chandra Kumar 1997). Statutory body.

pol_first_law_commission_1955.label: First Law Commission (1955)
pol_first_law_commission_1955.subject: polity
pol_first_law_commission_1955.detail: Established 5 Aug 1955 under M.C. Setalvad (first Attorney General). Executive body (not statutory). Predecessor: British-era Law Commissions (4 between 1834-1879). Law Commissions from 1955 onwards advise on legal reform. Each Commission has 3-year tenure.

eco_ipr_1977.label: Industrial Policy 1977 (Janata)
eco_ipr_1977.subject: economics
eco_ipr_1977.detail: Janata govt's IPR (Dec 1977) under George Fernandes (Industry Minister). Emphasised small-scale, cottage, village industries. Prime sectors reserved for small units. Decentralised industrial pattern. Reversed some Indira-era heavy-industry focus. Coca-Cola + IBM exited India under FERA dilution.

eco_ipr_1980.label: Industrial Policy 1980 (Indira)
eco_ipr_1980.subject: economics
eco_ipr_1980.detail: Indira's IPR (July 1980) after return to power. 'Promotion of competition', economic federalism. De-licensing of certain industries, automatic expansion up to 25% capacity. First liberal nudge. Set stage for Rajiv-era technocratic liberalisation 1984-89.

eco_essential_commodities_1955.label: Essential Commodities Act (1955)
eco_essential_commodities_1955.subject: economics
eco_essential_commodities_1955.detail: Enacted 1 April 1955. Empowers Centre to control production, supply, distribution and price of essential commodities. List amended repeatedly. Used for food grains, edible oils, petroleum, pharmaceuticals. Core of post-1947 state control over commodities. Reformed 2020 (era-11).

pol_operation_barga_1978.label: Operation Barga (1978-85, West Bengal)
pol_operation_barga_1978.subject: polity
pol_operation_barga_1978.detail: Left Front's flagship land-tenancy reform in West Bengal from 1978. Registered 1.5M bargadars (sharecroppers) giving them legal security + 75% crop share. Boosted Left Front's rural base. Model referenced nationally. Credited as WB's only successful land reform.

pol_ulfa_1979.label: ULFA (United Liberation Front of Asom, 1979)
pol_ulfa_1979.subject: polity
pol_ulfa_1979.detail: Founded 7 April 1979 at Rang Ghar, Sibsagar during Assam Movement. Demanded 'Swadhin Asom' (sovereign Assam). Went underground 1990 after ban. Operation Bajrang 1990, Operation Rhino 1991. Paresh Baruah (military) + Arabinda Rajkhowa (political). Peace talks 2011 onwards.

sci_aryabhata_1975.label: Aryabhata (India's First Satellite, 1975)
sci_aryabhata_1975.subject: science
sci_aryabhata_1975.detail: India's first indigenous satellite, launched 19 April 1975 from Kapustin Yar, USSR on Soviet Kosmos-3M rocket (India had no launch vehicle yet). Built by ISRO at Peenya, Bangalore under U.R. Rao. 360 kg, named after 5th-century astronomer Aryabhata. Studied X-ray astronomy and aeronomy.

sci_rohini_slv3_1980.label: Rohini / SLV-3 (First Indigenous Launch, 1980)
sci_rohini_slv3_1980.subject: science
sci_rohini_slv3_1980.detail: India's first successful indigenous satellite launch, 18 July 1980 from Sriharikota. SLV-3 (Satellite Launch Vehicle) developed by ISRO under APJ Abdul Kalam (project director). Placed Rohini RS-1 (35 kg) into orbit. Made India sixth nation with launch capability.

sci_insat_1_1982.label: INSAT-1A (1982)
sci_insat_1_1982.subject: science
sci_insat_1_1982.detail: India's first multipurpose geostationary communications satellite, launched 10 April 1982 on US Delta rocket. Started Indian National Satellite System (INSAT). Used for TV broadcasting (1982 Asian Games colour telecast), telephony, meteorology. INSAT series backbone of Indian broadcasting.

sci_apj_abdul_kalam.label: A.P.J. Abdul Kalam
sci_apj_abdul_kalam.subject: science
sci_apj_abdul_kalam.detail: Aerospace engineer (1931-2015). SLV-3 project director (first indigenous launch 1980).
