DRDO scientific advisor — Agni + Prithvi missiles (Integrated Guided Missile Development Programme 1983-2008). Pokhran-II 1998 (era 11) coordinator. 11th President of India 2002-07. 'Missile Man of India'.

sci_drdo_1958.label: DRDO (Defence Research and Development Organisation, 1958)
sci_drdo_1958.subject: science
sci_drdo_1958.detail: Established 1958 by merger of Defence Science Organisation + Technical Development Establishment. Under Ministry of Defence. Apex military R&D body. Key programmes: IGMDP (1983-08, Kalam), Light Combat Aircraft (Tejas), Arjun MBT, Akash, BrahMos.

sci_csir.label: CSIR (Council of Scientific and Industrial Research)
sci_csir.subject: science
sci_csir.detail: Established 26 Sept 1942 (pre-independence) but rapidly expanded post-1947 under S.S. Bhatnagar (first DG 1943-54). Network of 37+ national labs. CSIR Bhatnagar Award. PM is President ex-officio. Core of India's civilian scientific establishment.

sci_raja_ramanna.label: Raja Ramanna
sci_raja_ramanna.subject: science
sci_raja_ramanna.detail: Nuclear physicist (1925-2004). Director BARC 1972-83. Led Pokhran-I team (18 May 1974 'Smiling Buddha'). Member Planning Commission, Rajya Sabha MP. Bharata Natyam dancer-musician as well. Padma Vibhushan 1975.

pol_rajiv_jayewardene_accord.label: Rajiv-Jayewardene Accord (29 July 1987)
pol_rajiv_jayewardene_accord.subject: polity
pol_rajiv_jayewardene_accord.detail: Indo-Sri Lanka Peace Accord signed 29 July 1987 by Rajiv Gandhi + J.R. Jayewardene. Provisions: devolve power to Tamil provinces, IPKF deployment to disarm militants, Tamil as official language. LTTE initially surrendered arms then resumed war. IPKF 1987-90 costly failure. Led to Rajiv's LTTE assassination 1991.

hist_mncs_globalisation.label: MNCs and Modern Globalisation
hist_mncs_globalisation.subject: history
hist_mncs_globalisation.detail: MNCs first 1920s. Spread 1950s-60s. Late-1970s shifted production to low-wage Asia. China's post-1979 opening transformed global economy.

hist_rajiv_assassination_1991.label: Rajiv Gandhi Assassination (21 May 1991)
hist_rajiv_assassination_1991.subject: history
hist_rajiv_assassination_1991.detail: Assassinated 21 May 1991 at Sriperumbudur, Tamil Nadu during 1991 campaign. LTTE suicide bomber Thenmozhi Rajaratnam ('Dhanu') detonated RDX vest during garland presentation. Revenge for IPKF 1987-90. Led to Congress sympathy wave, Narasimha Rao became PM 21 June 1991. Jain Commission investigated.

hist_chandra_shekhar_pm.label: Chandra Shekhar (Interim PM, Nov 1990 - Jun 1991)
hist_chandra_shekhar_pm.subject: history
hist_chandra_shekhar_pm.detail: 8th PM of India, 10 Nov 1990 - 21 Jun 1991. Janata Dal (S) leader, 64 MPs with Congress outside support. Bhrought during Mandal-Rath Yatra crisis. Authorised gold-pledge to BOP crisis (47 tons to Bank of England May 1991). Lost when Congress withdrew support March 1991. Caretaker till Rao.

hist_babri_demolition_1992.label: Babri Masjid Demolition (6 Dec 1992)
hist_babri_demolition_1992.subject: history
hist_babri_demolition_1992.detail: 16th-century mosque demolished by VHP/Bajrang Dal kar sevaks at Ayodhya on 6 Dec 1992. Built 1528 under Mir Baqi (Babur's commander). Kar Seva organised by VHP-BJP after Dec 1990 suspension of kar seva. Kalyan Singh UP CM (BJP) resigned. Riots across India (~2,000 killed). 1993 Mumbai blasts retaliation. 2019 SC verdict awarded site for Ram temple.

pol_narasimha_rao_pm.label: P.V. Narasimha Rao (PM 1991-96)
pol_narasimha_rao_pm.subject: polity
pol_narasimha_rao_pm.detail: 9th PM, 21 June 1991 - 16 May 1996. Congress. Presided over LPG reforms (Manmohan Singh FM). Handled Babri demolition Dec 1992 + 1993 Mumbai blasts. Look East Policy 1992. Issued Panchayati Raj 73rd + 74th Amendments April 1993. First PM outside Nehru-Gandhi family to serve full 5-year term.

pol_lok_sabha_1991_polls.label: 1991 Lok Sabha Elections
pol_lok_sabha_1991_polls.subject: polity
pol_lok_sabha_1991_polls.detail: Held May-June 1991, disrupted by Rajiv's assassination 21 May. Congress (I) 232 seats under sympathy wave (pre-assassination estimate was 120-130). BJP 120 (up from 85), National Front 59, Left 49, Janata Dal 59. Narasimha Rao PM 21 June 1991. First minority Congress govt survived full term via internal coalitions.

pol_73rd_74th_amendments.label: 73rd and 74th Constitutional Amendments
pol_73rd_74th_amendments.subject: polity
pol_73rd_74th_amendments.detail: Passed in 1992 to constitutionalise local self-government. Made regular elections to local bodies mandatory. Reserved one-third seats for women. Created State Election Commission for local elections. Gave constitutional status to panchayats and municipalities.

pol_dalit_rights_movement.label: Dalit Rights Movement
pol_dalit_rights_movement.subject: polity
pol_dalit_rights_movement.detail: Movement for rights and dignity of Dalits (formerly called untouchables) in India. Seeks to end caste discrimination. Some groups sought international attention by raising caste at UN Conference Against Racism in Durban (2001). Political expression has led to reservations and anti-discrimination laws.

pol_nepal_democracy_movement.label: Nepal's Movement for Democracy (2006)
pol_nepal_democracy_movement.subject: polity
pol_nepal_democracy_movement.detail: King Gyanendra dismissed PM and dissolved Parliament in February 2005. Seven Party Alliance (SPA) called indefinite strike in April 2006, joined by Maoists. 3-5 lakh protesters. King forced to concede: restored Parliament, all-party government, new Constituent Assembly. SPA chose Girija Prasad Koirala as PM.

pol_bolivia_water_war.label: Bolivia's Water War (2000)
pol_bolivia_water_war.subject: polity
pol_bolivia_water_war.detail: World Bank pressured Bolivia to privatise water supply. MNC raised prices 4 times in Cochabamba. FEDECOR-led alliance of workers, farmers, students organised strikes. Government imposed martial law. People forced MNC to flee, contract cancelled, water restored to municipality at old rates.

pol_narmada_bachao_andolan.label: Narmada Bachao Andolan
pol_narmada_bachao_andolan.subject: polity
pol_narmada_bachao_andolan.detail: Movement opposing the Sardar Sarovar Dam on river Narmada. Led by Medha Patkar. Raised issues of displacement, environmental destruction, and rehabilitation. Example of a movement group that combines environmental concerns with social justice. Influenced dam height and rehabilitation policies.

pol_rti_movement.label: Right to Information Movement
pol_rti_movement.subject: polity
pol_rti_movement.detail: Movement for citizens' right to access government information. Led to enactment of Right to Information Act (RTI Act, 2005). MKSS (Mazdoor Kisan Shakti Sangathan) in Rajasthan was a key organisation. RTI became a powerful tool for transparency and accountability.

pol_seven_party_alliance.label: Seven Party Alliance (Nepal)
pol_seven_party_alliance.subject: polity
pol_seven_party_alliance.detail: Alliance of major political parties in Nepal's Parliament that led the 2006 democracy movement. Joined by Maoists, labour unions, indigenous peoples' organisations, teachers, lawyers, and human rights groups. Showed how diverse organisations unite for democratic goals.

pol_fedecor.label: FEDECOR (Bolivia)
pol_fedecor.subject: polity
pol_fedecor.detail: Organisation of local professionals (engineers, environmentalists) that led Bolivia's water war. Supported by farmers' federation, factory workers' unions, university students, and homeless children. Socialist Party also supported the movement, later came to power in 2006.

pol_article_21.label: Article 21 - Right to Life
pol_article_21.subject: polity
pol_article_21.detail: No person shall be deprived of life or personal liberty except according to procedure established by law. Expanded by SC to include right to livelihood, education, health, clean environment, privacy, dignity. Most expansively interpreted article.

pol_indra_sawhney.label: Indra Sawhney Case (1992)
pol_indra_sawhney.subject: polity
pol_indra_sawhney.detail: Mandal Commission case. SC upheld 27% OBC reservation but capped total reservation at 50%. Introduced 'creamy layer' concept — economically advanced sections of backward classes excluded from reservation.

pol_91st_amendment.label: 91st Amendment (2003)
pol_91st_amendment.subject: polity
pol_91st_amendment.detail: Limited size of Council of Ministers to 15% of total Lok Sabha/Assembly strength. Also strengthened anti-defection provisions. Aimed at preventing oversized ministries used as patronage.

pol_justice_ramaswamy_case.label: Justice Ramaswamy Impeachment (1993)
pol_justice_ramaswamy_case.subject: polity
pol_justice_ramaswamy_case.detail: First and only impeachment motion against a Supreme Court judge. Justice V. Ramaswamy was accused of misappropriating funds as Chief Justice of Punjab and Haryana HC. Inquiry commission found him guilty. Motion got required two-thirds of those voting but failed because Congress abstained, so it did not get majority of total strength of the House.

pol_creation_new_states_2000.label: Creation of New States (2000)
pol_creation_new_states_2000.subject: polity
pol_creation_new_states_2000.detail: In the 1990s, larger states were divided for administrative efficiency and to meet demands for separate statehood. Bihar divided to create Jharkhand, UP to create Uttaranchal (now Uttarakhand), Madhya Pradesh to create Chhattisgarh. All three new states created in November 2000.

pol_73rd_amendment.label: 73rd Constitutional Amendment (1992)
pol_73rd_amendment.subject: polity
pol_73rd_amendment.detail: Passed in 1992, came into force in 1993. Provides constitutional status to Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs). Creates uniform three-tier structure: Gram Panchayat, Block/Mandal Panchayat, Zilla Panchayat. Mandates direct elections, 5-year term, one-third reservation for women, reservations for SC/ST, Gram Sabha, State Election Commissioner, and State Finance Commission. Added Eleventh Schedule with 29 subjects.

pol_74th_amendment.label: 74th Constitutional Amendment (1992)
pol_74th_amendment.subject: polity
pol_74th_amendment.detail: Passed in 1992, came into force in 1993. Provides constitutional status to urban local bodies (Nagarpalikas). Mirrors provisions of 73rd amendment for urban areas: direct elections, reservations, State Election Commission, State Finance Commission. Added Twelfth Schedule listing functions of municipalities. Applies to Nagar Panchayats, Municipal Councils, and Municipal Corporations.

pol_reservation_women_local.label: Reservation for Women in Local Bodies
pol_reservation_women_local.subject: polity
pol_reservation_women_local.detail: One-third of all positions in panchayat institutions reserved for women. Applies not just to ordinary members but also to positions of Chairpersons/Adhyakshas at all three levels. Reservation within reserved categories too -- a seat may be reserved for both woman and SC/ST simultaneously. Over 10 lakh women elected to local bodies. Over 80,000 women Sarpanchas.

pol_reservation_sc_st_local.label: Reservation for SC/ST in Local Bodies
pol_reservation_sc_st_local.subject: polity
pol_reservation_sc_st_local.detail: Reservations for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes at all three levels of Panchayati Raj in proportion to their population. Applies to positions of Chairpersons also. States can additionally provide for OBC reservations. About 6.6 lakh elected members from SC/ST communities in urban and local bodies. Has significantly altered social profile of local bodies.

pol_eleventh_schedule.label: Eleventh Schedule
pol_eleventh_schedule.subject: polity
pol_eleventh_schedule.detail: Added by the 73rd Amendment. Lists 29 subjects to be transferred to Panchayati Raj institutions from the State List. Includes agriculture, minor irrigation, rural housing, drinking water, roads, rural electrification, poverty alleviation, education, health and sanitation, family welfare, women and child development, public distribution system. Actual transfer depends on state legislation.

pol_twelfth_schedule.label: Twelfth Schedule
pol_twelfth_schedule.subject: polity
pol_twelfth_schedule.detail: Added by the 74th Amendment. Lists 18 functions to be transferred to urban local bodies (Nagarpalikas). Includes urban planning, regulation of land use, public health, water supply, fire services, urban forestry, slum improvement, urban poverty alleviation, provision of urban amenities. Actual devolution depends on state legislation.

pol_state_election_commissioner.label: State Election Commissioner
pol_state_election_commissioner.subject: polity
pol_state_election_commissioner.detail: State government required to appoint a State Election Commissioner responsible for conducting elections to Panchayati Raj institutions and urban local bodies. Office is autonomous like the Election Commission of India. However, SEC is an independent officer not linked to or under the control of ECI. Ensures regular and fair elections to local bodies.

pol_state_finance_commission.label: State Finance Commission
pol_state_finance_commission.subject: polity
pol_state_finance_commission.detail: State government required to appoint a State Finance Commission every five years. Examines financial position of local governments. Reviews distribution of revenues between state and local governments, and between rural and urban local governments. Ensures allocation of funds to local bodies is not merely a political matter. Recommends principles for tax sharing with panchayats.

pol_panchayat_five_year_term.label: Five-Year Term for Panchayats
pol_panchayat_five_year_term.subject: polity
pol_panchayat_five_year_term.detail: Each Panchayat body has a fixed term of five years. If dissolved before completing its term, fresh elections must be held within six months. This is a crucial provision ensuring continuous existence of elected local bodies. Before the 73rd amendment, elections were often postponed indefinitely in many states.

pol_pesa_act_1996.label: PESA Act (1996)
pol_pesa_act_1996.subject: polity
pol_pesa_act_1996.detail: Panchayats (Extension to Scheduled Areas) Act, 1996. Extended provisions of Panchayat system to Adivasi/tribal areas. Protects rights of tribal communities to manage common resources (forests, water reservoirs) in ways acceptable to them. Gives more powers to Gram Sabhas in these areas. Elected panchayats must get Gram Sabha consent. Balances modern elected bodies with local traditions of self-government.

pol_ussr_disintegration.label: Disintegration of the USSR
pol_ussr_disintegration.stage: Parallel — End of Cold War & Post-Soviet Russia
pol_ussr_disintegration.subject: polity
pol_ussr_disintegration.detail: In December 1991, Russia, Ukraine, and Belarus declared the Soviet Union disbanded under Yeltsin's leadership. Communist Party was banned. Caused by economic stagnation, Gorbachev's reforms, nationalist movements in republics, and the failed 1991 coup.

pol_cis.label: Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS)
pol_cis.stage: Parallel — End of Cold War & Post-Soviet Russia
pol_cis.subject: polity
pol_cis.detail: Formed in December 1991 after the USSR's dissolution by Russia, Ukraine, and Belarus. Central Asian republics were later made founding members. Russia accepted as successor state of the USSR, inheriting the UN Security Council seat.

pol_shock_therapy.label: Shock Therapy
pol_shock_therapy.stage: Parallel — End of Cold War & Post-Soviet Russia
pol_shock_therapy.subject: polity
pol_shock_therapy.detail: Model of transition from socialism to capitalism in post-Soviet states, influenced by World Bank and IMF. Involved rapid privatisation, free trade, currency convertibility, and FDI. Led to economic ruin, massive inequality, rise of mafia, collapse of industries, and loss of social welfare.

pol_india_russia_relations.label: India-Russia Relations
pol_india_russia_relations.subject: polity
pol_india_russia_relations.detail: Built on Cold War-era trust. Over 80 bilateral agreements under the Indo-Russian Strategic Agreement of 2001. Russia is India's major arms supplier and supports India on Kashmir. Cooperation in energy, space technology, and nuclear energy. Both advocate multipolar world order.

pol_balkan_conflict.label: Yugoslav Breakup and Balkan Conflicts
pol_balkan_conflict.stage: Parallel — End of Cold War & Post-Soviet Russia
pol_balkan_conflict.subject: polity
pol_balkan_conflict.detail: After 1991, Yugoslavia broke apart with Croatia, Slovenia, and Bosnia declaring independence. Ethnic Serbs opposed this, leading to massacres of non-Serb Bosnians. NATO intervened with bombing of Yugoslavia. Most severe post-Cold War European conflict.

pol_first_gulf_war.label: First Gulf War (Operation Desert Storm)
pol_first_gulf_war.stage: Parallel — End of Cold War & Post-Soviet Russia
pol_first_gulf_war.subject: polity
pol_first_gulf_war.detail: In 1990, Iraq invaded Kuwait. A UN-mandated coalition of 660,000 troops from 34 countries, led by the US (75% of forces), defeated Iraq in 1991. Revealed the vast technological gap in US military capability. Called a 'computer war' for use of smart bombs.

pol_911_attacks.label: 9/11 Attacks
pol_911_attacks.subject: polity
pol_911_attacks.detail: On 11 September 2001, 19 hijackers flew planes into the World Trade Centre in New York and the Pentagon. Nearly 3,000 killed. Most severe attack on US soil since 1776. Led to the Global War on Terror, invasion of Afghanistan and Iraq.

pol_war_on_terror.label: Global War on Terror
pol_war_on_terror.subject: polity
pol_war_on_terror.detail: US response to 9/11 under President George W. Bush. Included Operation Enduring Freedom against Al-Qaeda and Taliban in Afghanistan, secret prisons, Guantanamo Bay detentions, and the Iraq invasion. Bypassed international law and UN provisions.

pol_iraq_invasion.label: Iraq Invasion (Operation Iraqi Freedom)
pol_iraq_invasion.subject: polity
pol_iraq_invasion.detail: US invaded Iraq on 19 March 2003 with a coalition of the willing after UN refused mandate. Ostensible reason was preventing WMDs, but none were found. Saddam Hussein's government fell swiftly, but a full insurgency followed. Widely seen as a military and political failure.

pol_al_qaeda.label: Al-Qaeda
pol_al_qaeda.subject: polity
pol_al_qaeda.detail: Terrorist organisation influenced by extremist Islamist ideas. Bombed US embassies in Kenya and Tanzania in 1998. Carried out 9/11 attacks. Led by Osama bin Laden. US launched operations against Al-Qaeda in Sudan, Afghanistan, and globally.

pol_taliban.label: Taliban
pol_taliban.subject: polity
pol_taliban.detail: Islamic fundamentalist regime in Afghanistan that harboured Al-Qaeda. Overthrown by US-led Operation Enduring Freedom after 9/11. Remnants continued as potent force launching terrorist attacks against Western targets.

pol_india_us_relations.label: India-US Relations
pol_india_us_relations.subject: polity
pol_india_us_relations.detail: India was on the opposite side during the Cold War but relations improved after 1991 economic liberalisation. New factors: technology sector (65% of India's software exports to US, 35% of Boeing's technical staff of Indian origin) and the Indian-American diaspora. Three strategic options debated in India.

pol_clinton_years.label: Clinton Presidency
pol_clinton_years.subject: polity
pol_clinton_years.detail: Bill Clinton was US President 1993-2001. Focused on soft issues: democracy promotion, climate change, world trade. Used military force in Kosovo (1999 NATO bombing of Yugoslavia) and against Al-Qaeda in Sudan and Afghanistan (Operation Infinite Reach 1998).

pol_eu.label: European Union (EU)
pol_eu.stage: Parallel — End of Cold War & Post-Soviet Russia
pol_eu.subject: polity
pol_eu.detail: Established in 1992 by Treaty of Maastricht. Evolved from EEC (1957). World's biggest economy (GDP over $12 trillion in 2005). Has its own flag, anthem, currency (euro), common foreign and security policy. Two members (UK, France) hold UNSC permanent seats. Combined armed forces second largest globally.

pol_arf.label: ASEAN Regional Forum (ARF)
pol_arf.subject: polity
pol_arf.detail: Established in 1994. Coordinates security and foreign policy for ASEAN. Only regional association in Asia providing a political forum where Asian countries and major powers discuss security concerns.

pol_look_east_policy.label: India's Look East Policy
pol_look_east_policy.subject: polity
pol_look_east_policy.detail: India's policy since 1991 to strengthen ties with ASEAN and East Asian nations. India signed FTAs with Singapore and Thailand. Seeks FTA with ASEAN itself. Led to greater economic interaction with ASEAN, China, Japan, and South Korea.

pol_maastricht_treaty.label: Treaty of Maastricht
pol_maastricht_treaty.subject: polity
pol_maastricht_treaty.detail: Signed on 7 February 1992, establishing the European Union. Laid foundation for common foreign and security policy, cooperation on justice and home affairs, and creation of single currency. Denmark and Sweden resisted some provisions.

pol_nuclear_tests_1998.label: Nuclear Tests 1998
pol_nuclear_tests_1998.subject: polity
pol_nuclear_tests_1998.detail: India conducted nuclear tests at Pokhran in May 1998 (first test was in 1974). Pakistan responded within days with tests at Chagai Hills. Both states became declared nuclear powers. Changed the military relationship with possibility of direct full-scale war declining.

pol_safta.label: South Asian Free Trade Agreement (SAFTA)
pol_safta.subject: polity
pol_safta.detail: Signed at the 12th SAARC Summit in Islamabad in 2004, effective from January 2006. Aims to lower trade tariffs by 20% by 2007. Smaller neighbours fear Indian market domination. India argues economic benefits for all from freer trade.

pol_india_nepal_relations.label: India-Nepal Relations
pol_india_nepal_relations.subject: polity
pol_india_nepal_relations.detail: Special relationship allowing citizens to travel and work without visas. Disputes over trade, Nepal's ties with China, and Indian interference. India concerned about Maoist movement spreading. Relations held together by trade, electricity cooperation, and water management.

pol_india_unsc_bid.label: India's UNSC Permanent Membership Bid
pol_india_unsc_bid.subject: polity
pol_india_unsc_bid.detail: India argues for permanent membership based on: second most populous country, largest democracy, participated in virtually all UN initiatives, long peacekeeping record, growing economic power, regular financial contributor. Opposed by Pakistan and some others over nuclear weapons and regional conflicts.

pol_cwc.label: Chemical Weapons Convention (CWC)
pol_cwc.stage: Parallel — End of Cold War & Post-Soviet Russia
pol_cwc.subject: polity
pol_cwc.detail: Signed in 1992. Banned the production and possession of chemical weapons. 181 states acceded. Included all great powers. India is a signatory. Frequently tested in UPSC.

pol_earth_summit.label: Earth Summit (Rio 1992)
pol_earth_summit.subject: polity
pol_earth_summit.detail: UN Conference on Environment and Development held in Rio de Janeiro, June 1992. Attended by 170 states, thousands of NGOs, and MNCs. Produced conventions on climate change, biodiversity, forestry, and Agenda 21. Established principle of common but differentiated responsibilities.

pol_unfccc.label: UN Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC)
pol_unfccc.subject: polity
pol_unfccc.detail: 1992 convention providing that parties should act on basis of equity and common but differentiated responsibilities. Acknowledged that largest share of historical greenhouse gas emissions originated in developed countries. Per capita emissions in developing countries still relatively low.

pol_kyoto_protocol.label: Kyoto Protocol
pol_kyoto_protocol.subject: polity
pol_kyoto_protocol.detail: 1997 international agreement setting targets for industrialised countries to cut greenhouse gas emissions (CO2, methane, hydrofluorocarbons). Based on UNFCCC principles. India and China exempted. India signed and ratified in August 2002. Some major countries did not sign.

pol_india_environment_stand.label: India's Stand on Environmental Issues
pol_india_environment_stand.subject: polity
pol_india_environment_stand.detail: Signed and ratified Kyoto Protocol in 2002. Position based on historical responsibility principle from UNFCCC. Per capita emissions far below world average (0.9 tonnes in 2000 vs 3.8 world average). National Auto-fuel Policy, Energy Conservation Act 2001, Electricity Act 2003, renewable energy programmes.

pol_india_globalisation.label: India and Globalisation
pol_india_globalisation.subject: polity
pol_india_globalisation.detail: After independence, India adopted protectionism. In 1991, responding to financial crisis, India embarked on economic reforms including de-regulation of trade and foreign investment. Previously sluggish growth rate improved. Challenge is ensuring benefits of growth are shared.

pol_wto_seattle.label: WTO Seattle Protests (1999)
pol_wto_seattle.subject: polity
pol_wto_seattle.detail: Widespread protests at the 1999 WTO Ministerial Meeting in Seattle alleging unfair trading practices by economically powerful states. Argued that developing world interests were insufficiently represented in evolving global economic system.

pol_world_social_forum.label: World Social Forum (WSF)
pol_world_social_forum.subject: polity
pol_world_social_forum.detail: Global platform bringing together human rights activists, environmentalists, labour, youth, and women activists opposed to neo-liberal globalisation. First meeting in Porto Alegre, Brazil in 2001. Fourth meeting in Mumbai 2004. Seventh in Nairobi, Kenya 2007.

pol_kargil_conflict.label: Kargil Conflict (1999)
pol_kargil_conflict.subject: polity
pol_kargil_conflict.detail: In early 1999, forces claiming to be Mujahideens occupied Indian positions along the LoC in Kargil sector. India recovered control by 26 July 1999. Significant because both India and Pakistan had attained nuclear capability in 1998. Led to the fall of PM Nawaz Sharif's government in Pakistan.

pol_anti_arrack_movement.label: Anti-Arrack Movement
pol_anti_arrack_movement.subject: polity
pol_anti_arrack_movement.detail: Spontaneous mobilisation of rural women in Andhra Pradesh in 1992 demanding ban on sale of arrack (locally brewed alcohol). Started in Nellore district through adult literacy classes. Women of about 5000 villages passed prohibition resolutions. Connected to broader issues of domestic violence, rural indebtedness and criminalisation of politics.

pol_national_fish_workers_forum.label: National Fish Workers Forum (NFF)
pol_national_fish_workers_forum.subject: polity
pol_national_fish_workers_forum.detail: Platform for fishworkers formed to fight against mechanised trawlers and bottom trawling threatening traditional livelihoods. In 1991, successfully fought a legal battle against the government's deep sea fishing policy that opened India's waters to multinational companies. Called nationwide strike in 2002.

pol_ayodhya_demolition.label: Babri Masjid Demolition (1992)
pol_ayodhya_demolition.subject: polity
pol_ayodhya_demolition.detail: On 6 December 1992, thousands gathered at Ayodhya and demolished the 16th century Babri Masjid despite Supreme Court orders. Triggered Hindu-Muslim clashes across the country. BJP-ruled state governments dismissed. BJP expressed regret. Raised fundamental questions about secularism and Indian nationalism.

pol_new_economic_policy.label: New Economic Policy / LPG Reforms
pol_new_economic_policy.subject: polity
pol_new_economic_policy.detail: Structural adjustment programme initiated by Rajiv Gandhi and made visible in 1991 under PM Narasimha Rao and FM Manmohan Singh. Marked Liberalisation, Privatisation and Globalisation. Radically changed India's economic direction from the Nehruvian mixed economy model. Widely criticised by movements and organisations but continued by all governments.

pol_rajiv_gandhi_assassination.label: Assassination of Rajiv Gandhi (1991)
pol_rajiv_gandhi_assassination.subject: polity
pol_rajiv_gandhi_assassination.detail: PM Rajiv Gandhi was assassinated in May 1991 by a Sri Lankan Tamil linked to the LTTE during an election campaign in Tamil Nadu. Led to change in Congress leadership. Narasimha Rao became PM. Congress won 1991 elections as the single largest party.

pol_gujarat_riots_2002.label: Gujarat Violence (2002)
pol_gujarat_riots_2002.subject: polity
pol_gujarat_riots_2002.detail: In February-March 2002, large-scale violence against Muslims in Gujarat after Godhra train burning incident (57 karsevaks killed). Nearly 1100 persons, mostly Muslims, killed. NHRC criticised Gujarat government. Election Commission postponed assembly elections. PM Vajpayee urged Gujarat CM to follow 'raj dharma'.

pol_african_national_congress.label: African National Congress
pol_african_national_congress.subject: polity
pol_african_national_congress.detail: A group of people who led the struggle against apartheid in South Africa. Along with Nelson Mandela, the ANC fought for racial equality and eventually succeeded in establishing democracy in South Africa in 1994.

pol_surat_plague.label: Surat Plague Scare 1994
pol_surat_plague.subject: polity
pol_surat_plague.detail: In 1994, Surat had a plague scare due to being one of the dirtiest cities in India. Houses and restaurants dumped garbage into drains and streets, and the Municipal Corporation failed in garbage collection. Several people died and over 300,000 fled. After this, Surat became one of the cleanest cities.

pol_swachh_bharat.label: Swachh Bharat Mission
pol_swachh_bharat.subject: polity
pol_swachh_bharat.detail: Launched by the Government of India on 2 October 2014 to promote cleanliness in both rural and urban areas. Includes the Swachh Bharat Swachh Vidyalaya campaign for sanitation awareness in schools. Implemented by municipalities and panchayats.

pol_midday_meal_scheme.label: Mid-Day Meal Scheme
pol_midday_meal_scheme.subject: polity
pol_midday_meal_scheme.detail: Government programme providing cooked lunch in all government elementary schools. Tamil Nadu was the first state to introduce it. In 2001, the Supreme Court directed all states to implement it within six months. It improved school enrollment, attendance, and helped reduce caste prejudices.

pol_govt_equality_programmes.label: Government Programmes for Equality
pol_govt_equality_programmes.subject: polity
pol_govt_equality_programmes.detail: The government implements equality through two methods: laws that protect equal treatment, and schemes or programmes to help disadvantaged communities gain greater opportunities. These target communities treated unequally for centuries.

pol_hakim_seikh_case.label: Hakim Seikh Case
pol_hakim_seikh_case.subject: polity
pol_hakim_seikh_case.detail: Hakim Seikh, an agricultural labourer in West Bengal, was denied treatment at eight government hospitals after a train accident in 1992. The court ruled the government must provide emergency medical treatment and that denial violates the Right to Life. State was ordered to reimburse his expenses.

pol_kerala_health_model.label: Kerala Health Model
pol_kerala_health_model.subject: polity
pol_kerala_health_model.detail: In 1996, the Kerala government allocated 40 percent of the state budget to panchayats for local planning of water, food, education, and health. This decentralised approach improved health centres, school functioning, and water supply schemes.

pol_dowry_deaths_campaign.label: Campaign Against Dowry Deaths
pol_dowry_deaths_campaign.subject: polity
pol_dowry_deaths_campaign.detail: In the 1980s, womens groups across India spoke out against cases of young brides being murdered by in-laws or husbands for more dowry. Through street protests, court approaches, and information sharing, they made it a public issue and dowry laws were strengthened.

pol_domestic_violence_law.label: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act 2005
pol_domestic_violence_law.subject: polity
pol_domestic_violence_law.detail: Law made in 2006 (enacted 2005) to give women who face physical and mental violence within their homes legal protection. A key achievement of the womens movement in getting legislation to address violence within the private sphere of the family.

pol_sexual_harassment_guidelines.label: Supreme Court Guidelines on Sexual Harassment
pol_sexual_harassment_guidelines.subject: polity
pol_sexual_harassment_guidelines.detail: In 1997, the Supreme Court formulated guidelines (Vishaka guidelines) to protect women against sexual harassment at the workplace and within educational institutions. This was a result of efforts by the womens movement and was later codified into law.

pol_beti_bachao_beti_padhao.label: Beti Bachao Beti Padhao
pol_beti_bachao_beti_padhao.subject: polity
pol_beti_bachao_beti_padhao.detail: Campaign launched in 2014 to address declining child sex ratio and promote education of the girl child. Represents government recognition that gender equality requires both protection and empowerment of women through education.

pol_tawa_matsya_sangh.label: Tawa Matsya Sangh (TMS)
pol_tawa_matsya_sangh.subject: polity
pol_tawa_matsya_sangh.detail: Federation of fisherworker cooperatives in Madhya Pradesh fighting for rights of displaced forest dwellers of Satpura forest. After Tawa dam displaced them, government gave fishing rights to private contractors. TMS organised protests and in 1996 won fishing rights. Members now earn three times more through cooperative marketing.

pol_sachar_committee.label: Sachar Committee Report
pol_sachar_committee.subject: polity
pol_sachar_committee.detail: A high-level committee chaired by Justice Rajindar Sachar set up in 2005 to examine social, economic, and educational status of Muslims. Found Muslim community's situation comparable to SCs and STs on many indicators. Debunked myths like preference for madrasas (only 4% attend). Average years of schooling for Muslim children much lower.

pol_niyamgiri.label: Niyamgiri Hill - Adivasi Resistance
pol_niyamgiri.subject: polity
pol_niyamgiri.detail: Niyamgiri in Kalahandi, Odisha, is the sacred mountain of Dongarria Konds (Adivasi community). A major aluminium company planned a mine and refinery here, threatening displacement. The community strongly resisted, joined by environmentalists. A case was pending in the Supreme Court.

pol_sc_st_poa_act.label: SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989
pol_sc_st_poa_act.subject: polity
pol_sc_st_poa_act.detail: Framed in response to demands by Dalits for government action against everyday ill-treatment and violence. Lists various levels of crimes: physical humiliation, dispossession of resources, forced slave labour, and crimes against Dalit/tribal women. Prescribes stringent punishments. Also used by Adivasis to defend land rights.

pol_manual_scavenging_act_1993.label: Manual Scavengers Prohibition Act 1993
pol_manual_scavenging_act_1993.subject: polity
pol_manual_scavenging_act_1993.detail: Prohibited employment of manual scavengers and construction of dry latrines. Despite the law, manual scavenging persisted. Safai Karamchari Andolan filed PIL in Supreme Court in 2003. The 2013 Act replaced it with stronger provisions for prohibition and rehabilitation.

pol_forest_rights_act_2006.label: Forest Rights Act 2006
pol_forest_rights_act_2006.subject: polity
pol_forest_rights_act_2006.detail: The Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act, 2006. Meant to undo historical injustices to forest-dwelling populations. Recognises rights to homestead, cultivable and grazing land, and non-timber forest produce. Also recognises forest dwellers' role in conservation.

pol_safai_karamchari_andolan.label: Safai Karamchari Andolan
pol_safai_karamchari_andolan.subject: polity
pol_safai_karamchari_andolan.detail: An Andhra Pradesh-based organisation working with manual scavengers. Filed PIL in Supreme Court in 2003 with 13 other organisations and 7 scavengers. Complained that manual scavenging persisted despite 1993 Act. Supreme Court directed governments to verify and take time-bound rehabilitation action.

pol_environment_laws.label: Environmental Protection Laws
pol_environment_laws.subject: polity
pol_environment_laws.detail: After Bhopal, India introduced new environmental laws. The polluter is held accountable for environmental damage. In Subhash Kumar vs State of Bihar (1991), Supreme Court held Right to Life includes right to pollution-free water and air. Government must check pollution, clean rivers, and impose heavy fines.

pol_child_labour_law.label: Child Labour Laws
pol_child_labour_law.subject: polity
pol_child_labour_law.detail: The Child Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act, 1986, amended in 2016, bans employment of children below 14 in all occupations and adolescents (14-18) in hazardous work. Violation is a cognizable offence with jail term of 6 months to 2 years and/or fine of Rs 20,000-50,000. PENCIL portal launched in 2017.

pol_cng_order.label: CNG Order by Supreme Court
pol_cng_order.subject: polity
pol_cng_order.detail: In a series of rulings from 1998 onwards, the Supreme Court ordered all public transport vehicles using diesel in Delhi to switch to Compressed Natural Gas (CNG). This significantly reduced air pollution. But diesel cars and increased vehicle numbers continued to cause pollution concerns.

pol_end_of_cold_war_democracy.label: End of Cold War and Democracy
pol_end_of_cold_war_democracy.stage: Parallel — End of Cold War & Post-Soviet Russia
pol_end_of_cold_war_democracy.subject: polity
pol_end_of_cold_war_democracy.detail: Collapse of the Soviet Union in 1991 led to democratisation in Eastern Europe and Central Asia. Many former communist countries transitioned to multi-party democracies. Democracy became the dominant form globally.

pol_pakistan_musharraf.label: Pakistan under Musharraf
pol_pakistan_musharraf.subject: polity
pol_pakistan_musharraf.detail: General Pervez Musharraf led military coup in October 1999. Amended constitution via Legal Framework Order (2002) giving President power to dismiss assemblies. National Security Council dominated by military. Elections held but real power with army, not elected reps.

pol_china_single_party.label: China's Single Party System
pol_china_single_party.subject: polity
pol_china_single_party.detail: China holds elections every five years for National People's Congress (nearly 3,000 members). But candidates need Communist Party approval. Only CCP and eight allied parties allowed. Government always formed by Communist Party. Not a democracy by any definition.

pol_zimbabwe_mugabe.label: Zimbabwe under Mugabe
pol_zimbabwe_mugabe.subject: polity
pol_zimbabwe_mugabe.detail: Robert Mugabe ruled since independence in 1980. Won elections but used unfair practices. Changed constitution to increase presidential powers. Opposition harassed, protests declared illegal, press freedom curtailed, judiciary pressurised. Forced out in 2017.

pol_south_africa_constitution.label: South African Constitution
pol_south_africa_constitution.subject: polity
pol_south_africa_constitution.detail: Drafted after two years of negotiations between oppressor and oppressed groups. Gave citizens most extensive rights available. Based on principles of equality, democratic values, social justice and human rights. Model for democracies worldwide.

eco_lpg_reforms_1991.label: LPG Reforms (July 1991)
eco_lpg_reforms_1991.subject: economics
eco_lpg_reforms_1991.detail: Liberalisation + Privatisation + Globalisation reforms launched 24 July 1991 by FM Manmohan Singh under PM Narasimha Rao. Triggered by BOP crisis (forex <15 days imports) + IMF conditionality. Rupee devalued 2x (July 1-3). Industrial Policy 24 July abolished licence raj for most industries. FERA liberalised. Landmark moment ending Nehruvian planning era.

eco_manmohan_singh_fm_1991.label: Manmohan Singh (FM 1991-96)
eco_manmohan_singh_fm_1991.subject: economics
eco_manmohan_singh_fm_1991.detail: Finance Minister 21 June 1991 - 16 May 1996 under Narasimha Rao. Architect of 1991 reforms budget (24 July 1991). Earlier: Economic Advisor, RBI Governor 1982-85, Planning Commission. PM 2004-2014. Delivered 'No power on earth can stop an idea whose time has come'.

eco_nrega_2005.label: NREGA 2005 (Right to Work)
eco_nrega_2005.subject: economics
eco_nrega_2005.detail: National Rural Employment Guarantee Act 2005. Guarantees 100 days of employment per year to those able and in need. Government must provide unemployment allowance if it fails. Preference for work that increases future land productivity. Initially covered 200 districts.

eco_liberalisation.label: Liberalisation
eco_liberalisation.subject: economics
eco_liberalisation.detail: Removing barriers or restrictions set by government on foreign trade and investment. India began liberalising around 1991 -- allowing freer imports, exports, and foreign companies to set up operations. Post-independence, India had protective trade barriers for domestic producers. Decision supported by powerful international organisations.

eco_1991_reforms.label: 1991 Economic Reforms
eco_1991_reforms.subject: economics
eco_1991_reforms.detail: Far-reaching policy changes in India around 1991. Government decided Indian producers should compete globally. Barriers on foreign trade and investment were significantly removed. Goods could be imported and exported more freely. Foreign companies allowed to set up factories and offices in India.

eco_rti_act.label: Right to Information Act (RTI), 2005
eco_rti_act.subject: economics
eco_rti_act.detail: Enacted October 2005 by Government of India. Ensures citizens can access information about functions of government departments. Expands the right to information beyond consumer goods to government services. Empowers citizens to question government and seek accountability.

eco_bop_crisis_1991.label: Balance of Payments Crisis 1991
eco_bop_crisis_1991.subject: economics
eco_bop_crisis_1991.detail: India faced an external debt crisis -- government could not repay foreign borrowings, forex reserves fell to less than two weeks of imports. Rising prices of essential goods compounded the crisis. Root cause: inefficient economic management in the 1980s with expenditure exceeding revenue, profligate spending of borrowed forex on consumption.

eco_new_economic_policy.label: New Economic Policy (NEP) 1991
eco_new_economic_policy.subject: economics
eco_new_economic_policy.detail: Wide-ranging reforms announced after India received $7 billion loan from World Bank and IMF. Consisted of stabilisation measures (short-term: forex reserves, inflation control) and structural reforms (long-term: efficiency, international competitiveness). Three pillars: Liberalisation, Privatisation, and Globalisation.

eco_industrial_deregulation.label: Deregulation of Industrial Sector
eco_industrial_deregulation.subject: economics
eco_industrial_deregulation.detail: Industrial licensing abolished for almost all products except alcohol, cigarettes, hazardous chemicals, industrial explosives, electronics, aerospace, and drugs/pharmaceuticals. Only defence equipment, atomic energy, and railway transport reserved for public sector. Small-scale industry reservations were dereserved. Market-determined pricing allowed.

eco_financial_sector_reforms.label: Financial Sector Reforms
eco_financial_sector_reforms.subject: economics
eco_financial_sector_reforms.detail: Aimed at reducing RBI's role from regulator to facilitator. Private sector banks (Indian and foreign) allowed. Foreign investment limit in banks raised to 50%. Banks given freedom to set up branches without RBI approval. Foreign Institutional Investors (FIIs) including merchant bankers, mutual funds, pension funds allowed to invest.

eco_tax_reforms.label: Tax Reforms Post-1991
eco_tax_reforms.subject: economics
eco_tax_reforms.detail: Continuous reduction in income tax rates to encourage savings and voluntary disclosure (high rates had caused evasion). Corporation tax gradually reduced. Indirect taxes reformed to facilitate a common national market. Procedures simplified and rates substantially lowered for better compliance.

eco_forex_reforms.label: Foreign Exchange Reforms
eco_forex_reforms.subject: economics
eco_forex_reforms.detail: Rupee was devalued against foreign currencies in 1991 as immediate crisis measure, increasing foreign exchange inflow. Market-determined exchange rates replaced government-controlled rates. This freed the determination of rupee value based on demand and supply of foreign exchange.

eco_trade_investment_reforms.label: Trade and Investment Policy Reforms
eco_trade_investment_reforms.subject: economics
eco_trade_investment_reforms.detail: Dismantling of quantitative restrictions on imports and exports, reduction of tariff rates, removal of import licensing (except hazardous/environmentally sensitive industries). Quantitative restrictions on manufactured consumer goods and agricultural products fully removed from April 2001. Export duties removed for international competitiveness.

eco_privatisation.label: Privatisation
eco_privatisation.subject: economics
eco_privatisation.detail: Shedding of government ownership or management of enterprises. Two methods: withdrawal from ownership/management, or outright sale. Purpose: improve financial discipline, facilitate modernisation, attract FDI, and utilise private capital and managerial capabilities. Some PSUs given autonomy as Navaratnas and Miniratnas instead of being sold.

eco_disinvestment.label: Disinvestment
eco_disinvestment.subject: economics
eco_disinvestment.detail: Selling off part of equity of Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs) to the public. Critics argue PSU assets were undervalued and sold cheaply. Proceeds were used to offset revenue shortfalls rather than developing PSUs or building social infrastructure. Annual targets set by government, sometimes exceeded.

eco_navaratna_psu.label: Navaratna PSUs
eco_navaratna_psu.subject: economics
eco_navaratna_psu.detail: In 1996, nine PSUs were given greater managerial and operational autonomy to improve efficiency and compete globally. Original nine included IOC, BPCL, HPCL, ONGC, SAIL, IPCL, BHEL, NTPC, VSNL. Later GAIL and MTNL added. Also 97 profit-making PSUs designated as Miniratnas. Better performance resulted from this status.

eco_stabilisation_measures.label: Stabilisation Measures
eco_stabilisation_measures.subject: economics
eco_stabilisation_measures.detail: Short-term measures to correct weaknesses in balance of payments and control inflation. Included maintaining sufficient foreign exchange reserves and controlling rising prices. Part of the NEP alongside long-term structural reforms.

eco_structural_reforms.label: Structural Reform Measures
eco_structural_reforms.subject: economics
eco_structural_reforms.detail: Long-term measures to improve efficiency and increase international competitiveness by removing rigidities in the economy. Encompassed liberalisation (industrial, financial, trade), privatisation, and policies that led to globalisation. Aimed at creating a more competitive economic environment.

eco_rupee_devaluation.label: Rupee Devaluation 1991
eco_rupee_devaluation.subject: economics
eco_rupee_devaluation.detail: As an immediate measure to resolve the balance of payments crisis, the rupee was devalued against foreign currencies in 1991. This increased inflow of foreign exchange and set the tone for market-determined exchange rates, moving away from government-controlled currency valuation.

eco_86th_amendment.label: 86th Constitutional Amendment (Right to Education)
eco_86th_amendment.subject: economics
eco_86th_amendment.detail: In December 2002, made free and compulsory education a fundamental right for all children aged 6-14 years. The Constitution's Directive Principles originally set a target of achieving this within 10 years (by 1960). Tapas Majumdar Committee (1998) estimated Rs 1.37 lakh crore needed over 10 years to achieve this.

eco_golden_revolution.label: Golden Revolution (Horticulture)
eco_golden_revolution.subject: economics
eco_golden_revolution.detail: Period 1991-2003 called Golden Revolution when planned investment in horticulture became highly productive. India emerged as world leader in mangoes, bananas, coconuts, cashew nuts, and spices; second largest producer of fruits and vegetables. Provides employment to 19% of total labour force. Flower harvesting and food processing are remunerative for rural women.

eco_kudumbashree.label: Kudumbashree
eco_kudumbashree.subject: economics
eco_kudumbashree.detail: Women-oriented community-based poverty reduction programme in Kerala. Started in 1995 as thrift and credit society for poor women. Mobilised Rs 1 crore as thrift savings. Acclaimed as the largest informal bank in Asia in terms of participation and savings mobilised. Functions like mini banks through micro-credit system.

eco_inflation_targeting.label: Inflation Targeting
eco_inflation_targeting.subject: economics
eco_inflation_targeting.detail: A monetary policy framework where the central bank commits to keeping inflation at a specified target. In India, the inflation target is 4% CPI with a tolerance band of +/- 2% (2-6%). RBI uses CPI (not WPI) as the key measure for inflation targeting since 2016. If inflation exceeds 6% for three consecutive quarters, MPC must explain to the government.

eco_gst.label: Goods and Services Tax (GST)
eco_gst.subject: economics
eco_gst.detail: A comprehensive indirect tax on manufacture, sale, and consumption of goods and services. Replaced multiple taxes to create a single national market. Dual GST model: CGST (Centre) + SGST (State) for intra-state; IGST for inter-state. Implemented from July 1, 2017 via 101st Constitutional Amendment. GST Council determines rates.

eco_frbma.label: Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act (FRBMA)
eco_frbma.subject: economics
eco_frbma.detail: Enacted in 2003 to institutionalize fiscal discipline. Targets: elimination of revenue deficit and reduction of fiscal deficit. Mandates the Finance Minister to present the Macro Economic Framework Statement before Parliament. Restricts RBI from buying government securities in primary market (no monetization). FRBM Review Committee recommended 60% debt-to-GDP ratio.

eco_mgnrega.label: MGNREGA (2005)
eco_mgnrega.subject: economics
eco_mgnrega.detail: Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act guarantees 100 days of wage employment per household per year. Aims at livelihood security in rural areas and sustainable development. One-third jobs reserved for women. Provided employment to 4.78 crore households.

eco_pmry.label: Prime Minister Rozgar Yojana (PMRY)
eco_pmry.subject: economics
eco_pmry.detail: Started in 1993 to create self-employment opportunities for educated unemployed youth in rural areas and small towns. Helps in setting up small business and industries.

eco_sgsy.label: Swarnajayanti Gram Swarozgar Yojana (SGSY)
eco_sgsy.subject: economics
eco_sgsy.detail: Launched in 1999 to bring assisted poor families above the poverty line by organising them into self-help groups (SHGs). Uses a mix of bank credit and government subsidy for self-employment generation.

eco_aay.label: Antyodaya Anna Yojana (AAY)
eco_aay.subject: economics
eco_aay.detail: Launched December 2000 for the poorest among BPL families. Initially 1 crore families, expanded to 2 crore. Provides 35 kg of foodgrains at Rs 2/kg (wheat) and Rs 3/kg (rice). Identified through BPL surveys by state rural development departments.

eco_production_across_countries.label: Spreading Production Across Countries
eco_production_across_countries.subject: economics
eco_production_across_countries.detail: MNCs divide production into small parts spread globally. Example: design in US, components in China, assembly in Mexico/Eastern Europe, customer care in India -- saving 50-60% costs. Methods: joint ventures with local companies, using local suppliers, buying local companies, placing orders with small producers.

pol_1989_general_elections.label: 1989 General Elections
pol_1989_general_elections.subject: polity
pol_1989_general_elections.detail: Ninth Lok Sabha elections, December 1989. Congress reduced from 415 (1984) to 197 seats — end of the 'Congress system'. Coalition era begins. National Front (Janata Dal + regional parties) formed government under V.P. Singh, supported by BJP and Left Front from outside.

pol_vp_singh_pm.label: V.P. Singh (PM 1989-90)
pol_vp_singh_pm.subject: polity
pol_vp_singh_pm.detail: Prime Minister, December 1989 to November 1990. Led National Front government. Implemented Mandal Commission recommendations in August 1990. Government fell after BJP withdrew support over Advani's Rath Yatra arrest.

pol_national_front_government.label: National Front Government (1989-90)
pol_national_front_government.subject: polity
pol_national_front_government.detail: Coalition government under V.P. Singh, 1989-90. Alliance of Janata Dal + regional parties. Supported from outside by BJP (right) and Left Front. First major non-Congress non-emergency coalition era government.

pol_muslim_women_act_1986.label: Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Divorce) Act 1986
pol_muslim_women_act_1986.subject: polity
pol_muslim_women_act_1986.detail: Passed by Rajiv Gandhi government to nullify the Shah Bano Supreme Court judgment. Made Muslim personal law applicable to maintenance disputes between divorced Muslim couples. Widely criticised as minority 'appeasement'. Basis for BJP's critique of pseudo-secularism.

pol_indra_sawhney_1992.label: Indra Sawhney Case (Mandal, 1992)
pol_indra_sawhney_1992.subject: polity
pol_indra_sawhney_1992.detail: Supreme Court 9-judge bench (1992) upheld 27% OBC reservation but capped total reservation at 50%. Introduced 'creamy layer' exclusion from OBC benefits. Held that reservation in promotions not permissible. Foundational case for reservation jurisprudence.

pol_rath_yatra_1990.label: Advani's Rath Yatra (1990)
pol_rath_yatra_1990.subject: polity
pol_rath_yatra_1990.detail: L.K. Advani led a 10,000-km Rath Yatra from Somnath (Gujarat) to Ayodhya in September-October 1990 to mobilise Hindus for Ram Janmabhoomi temple construction. Advani arrested in Bihar by CM Lalu Yadav. BJP withdrew support from V.P. Singh government, causing its fall.

pol_chandra_shekhar_pm.label: Chandra Shekhar (PM 1990-91)
pol_chandra_shekhar_pm.subject: polity
pol_chandra_shekhar_pm.detail: Prime Minister, 10 November 1990 to 21 June 1991. Led breakaway Samajwadi Janata Party with Congress external support. Handled the 1991 BoP crisis, pledging gold to IMF. Resigned when Congress withdrew support in March 1991.

pol_anti_sikh_riots_1984.label: Anti-Sikh Riots (November 1984)
pol_anti_sikh_riots_1984.subject: polity
pol_anti_sikh_riots_1984.detail: Mass communal violence against Sikhs following Indira Gandhi's assassination (31 October 1984). ~3,000 Sikhs killed, mostly in Delhi. Nanavati Commission (2005) indicted several Congress leaders. Chronic impunity issue for Indian secularism.

pol_1993_mumbai_blasts.label: 1993 Mumbai Serial Blasts (12 March 1993)
pol_1993_mumbai_blasts.subject: polity
pol_1993_mumbai_blasts.detail: Thirteen coordinated bomb blasts in Mumbai, 12 March 1993; killed 257 and injured 713. Retaliation for Babri demolition and communal riots. Planned by Dawood Ibrahim's D-Company with ISI facilitation. Yakub Memon hanged 2015.

pol_bjp_formation.label: Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP, 1980)
pol_bjp_formation.subject: polity
pol_bjp_formation.detail: Political party formed 6 April 1980 by former Jana Sangh members after Janata Party split. Initially adopted 'Gandhian Socialism'; shifted to Hindutva from mid-1980s under Advani. Rose via Ram Janmabhoomi movement (1989 → 85 MPs; 1991 → 120; 1996 → 161 largest).

pol_hindutva_politics.label: Hindutva Politics
pol_hindutva_politics.subject: polity
pol_hindutva_politics.detail: Political ideology defined by V.D. Savarkar (1923) as the basis of Indian nationhood — acceptance of India as pitrubhu (fatherland) and punyabhu (holy land). Adopted by BJP from mid-1980s as mobilising strategy. Became central to BJP's electoral rise via Ram Janmabhoomi movement.

pol_ayodhya_unlocking_1986.label: Ayodhya Dispute — Faizabad Court Unlocking (February 1986)
pol_ayodhya_unlocking_1986.subject: polity
pol_ayodhya_unlocking_1986.detail: Faizabad district court ordered Babri Masjid premises unlocked in February 1986 for Hindu darshan. Triggered mobilisation by VHP/RSS/BJP around Ram Janmabhoomi claim and counter-mobilisation by Muslim organisations. Converted local dispute into national communal flashpoint.

pol_vhp.label: Vishva Hindu Parishad (VHP)
pol_vhp.subject: polity
pol_vhp.detail: Hindu nationalist organisation formed 1964, became prominent in Ram Janmabhoomi agitation 1984 onwards. Spearheaded shila pujan (1989), kar seva programmes. Part of RSS-led Sangh Parivar along with BJP, Bajrang Dal, ABVP.

pol_godhra_train_burning.label: Godhra Train Burning (27 February 2002)
pol_godhra_train_burning.subject: polity
pol_godhra_train_burning.detail: Coach S-6 of Sabarmati Express set on fire at Godhra railway station, 27 February 2002; 59 kar sevaks returning from Ayodhya killed. Triggered large-scale Gujarat riots. SIT investigation (2011) convicted 31 people; Gujarat HC upheld 11 death sentences (commuted to life by SC in 2017).

pol_bahujan_samaj_party.label: Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP, 1984)
pol_bahujan_samaj_party.subject: polity
pol_bahujan_samaj_party.detail: Political party founded 14 April 1984 by Kanshi Ram, representing Bahujans (SC/ST/OBC/minorities). Major force in UP from 1990s. Mayawati CM four times (1995, 1997, 2002-03, 2007-12). Peaked 2007 with absolute majority in UP.

pol_united_front_government.label: United Front Government (1996-98)
pol_united_front_government.subject: polity
pol_united_front_government.detail: Coalition of 13 parties (Janata Dal, DMK, Samajwadi Party, TDP, AGP, Left Front) that governed 1996-98 with Congress external support. Two PMs: H.D. Deve Gowda (June 1996 - April 1997) and I.K. Gujral (April 1997 - March 1998). Congress withdrew support over CBI investigation of DMK.

pol_deve_gowda_pm.label: H.D. Deve Gowda (PM 1996-97)
pol_deve_gowda_pm.subject: polity
pol_deve_gowda_pm.detail: Prime Minister, 1 June 1996 to 21 April 1997. Janata Dal leader, former Karnataka CM. Led United Front coalition with Congress outside support. Replaced by Gujral after Congress demanded leadership change.

pol_gujral_pm.label: I.K. Gujral (PM 1997-98)
pol_gujral_pm.subject: polity
pol_gujral_pm.detail: Prime Minister, 21 April 1997 to 19 March 1998. Janata Dal leader, former External Affairs Minister. Formulated the Gujral Doctrine of non-reciprocal concessions to South Asian neighbours. Government fell over Jain Commission report on Rajiv Gandhi assassination and DMK.

pol_gujral_doctrine.label: Gujral Doctrine (1996-97)
pol_gujral_doctrine.subject: polity
pol_gujral_doctrine.detail: Five-point foreign policy articulated by I.K. Gujral for India's relations with South Asian neighbours: non-reciprocal concessions to smaller neighbours, no interference in internal affairs, respect for territorial integrity, dispute resolution via peaceful bilateral negotiations, no use of territory against another South Asian country.

pol_vajpayee_pm.label: Atal Bihari Vajpayee (PM, full term 1999-2004)
pol_vajpayee_pm.subject: polity
pol_vajpayee_pm.detail: BJP leader, three-time PM: 13 days (May 1996), 13 months (March 1998 - April 1999), full term (October 1999 - May 2004). Led NDA government. Oversaw Pokhran-II (1998), Kargil War (1999), Lahore Bus Yatra, Golden Quadrilateral, SSA, Privatisation push.

pol_nda_1998.label: National Democratic Alliance (NDA, 1998)
pol_nda_1998.subject: polity
pol_nda_1998.detail: BJP-led coalition formed 1998. Initial constituents: BJP, Shiv Sena, Samata Party, BJD, TDP (outside support), AIADMK (briefly). Vajpayee PM 1998-99, 1999-2004. Modi PM 2014-, 2019-, 2024-. Replaced Hindutva ideological thrust with common governance programme (National Agenda).

pol_upa_2004.label: United Progressive Alliance (UPA, 2004)
pol_upa_2004.subject: polity
pol_upa_2004.detail: Congress-led coalition formed May 2004 after 2004 Lok Sabha elections. Initial constituents: Congress, DMK, NCP, RJD, JMM, LJP etc. with Left Front outside support. Manmohan Singh PM 2004-14 (UPA-I and UPA-II).

pol_2004_general_elections.label: 2004 General Elections (UPA-I)
pol_2004_general_elections.subject: polity
pol_2004_general_elections.detail: 14th Lok Sabha elections, April-May 2004. BJP-led NDA's 'India Shining' campaign failed. Congress 145, BJP 138. UPA formed with Left support. Sonia Gandhi declined PM; Manmohan Singh sworn in 22 May 2004.

pol_nhrc_1993.label: National Human Rights Commission (NHRC, 1993)
pol_nhrc_1993.subject: polity
pol_nhrc_1993.detail: Statutory body established under Protection of Human Rights Act 1993. Chairperson + members investigate human rights violations. Played key role criticising Gujarat 2002 riots response. Members: former CJI (chairperson), former SC/HC judges, human rights experts.

eco_industrial_policy_1991.label: Industrial Policy Statement 24 July 1991
eco_industrial_policy_1991.subject: economics
eco_industrial_policy_1991.detail: New Industrial Policy announced 24 July 1991 alongside Manmohan Singh's budget. Abolished industrial licensing except for 18 industries (later reduced to 6); abolished MRTP asset threshold; allowed 51% FDI in 34 high-priority industries; ended public sector monopoly in most areas; provided for disinvestment of loss-making PSUs. End of licence raj.

eco_imf_bailout_1991.label: IMF Bailout 1991 ($7bn Loan)
eco_imf_bailout_1991.subject: economics
eco_imf_bailout_1991.detail: India approached IMF/World Bank (IBRD) in 1991 during the BoP crisis, receiving ~$7 billion loan. Conditionalities required liberalisation, opening to private sector, reduced government role, trade deregulation. Accepted by Chandra Shekhar government (emergency gold pledge) and Narasimha Rao government (NEP).

eco_gold_pledge_1991.label: Gold Pledge to Bank of England/Switzerland (1991)
eco_gold_pledge_1991.subject: economics
eco_gold_pledge_1991.detail: Chandra Shekhar government airlifted 46.91 tonnes of gold to Bank of England and Union Bank of Switzerland in May-June 1991 against a loan of $405 million, to meet forex obligations. Symbol of the BoP crisis depth. Repaid by November 1991.

eco_navaratnas_1997.label: Navaratnas Status (1997)
eco_navaratnas_1997.subject: economics
eco_navaratnas_1997.detail: Greater financial and operational autonomy granted to 9 profit-making PSUs in 1997: IOC, BPCL, HPCL, ONGC, SAIL, IPCL, BHEL, NTPC, VSNL. Later GAIL and MTNL added. Enables investments up to Rs 1,000 crore without government approval. Precursor to Maharatna scheme (2010).

eco_mini_ratnas.label: Mini Ratnas (Category I and II)
eco_mini_ratnas.subject: economics
eco_mini_ratnas.detail: Classification of profit-making PSUs introduced 1997. Category I (Rs 300 cr pre-tax profit, 3 consecutive years) can invest up to Rs 500 cr; Category II up to Rs 300 cr. ~70 Mini Ratnas as of 2024. Provides operational autonomy to second-tier PSUs.

eco_maharatnas_2010.label: Maharatnas (2010 scheme)
eco_maharatnas_2010.subject: economics
eco_maharatnas_2010.detail: Top tier of PSUs with ≥Rs 5,000 cr avg annual turnover and ≥Rs 25,000 cr avg annual net worth (3 yrs). Can invest up to 15% of net worth (capped at Rs 5,000 cr) without government approval. Initial: CIL, IOC, NTPC, ONGC, SAIL; expanded to 14 including BHEL, GAIL, HPCL, BPCL, PowerGrid, HAL etc.

eco_wto_accession_1995.label: WTO Accession (1 January 1995)
eco_wto_accession_1995.subject: economics
eco_wto_accession_1995.detail: India joined World Trade Organisation as founding member, 1 January 1995. WTO succeeded GATT (established 1948). India committed to dismantling QRs, tariff reduction, TRIPS compliance. QRs on manufactured consumer goods and agricultural products fully removed from April 2001.

eco_gatt_to_wto.label: GATT to WTO Transition (Uruguay Round)
eco_gatt_to_wto.subject: economics
eco_gatt_to_wto.detail: General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (1948, 23 countries) replaced by World Trade Organisation on 1 January 1995 after Uruguay Round (1986-94). Marrakesh Agreement signed 1994. WTO covers goods, services (GATS), IPR (TRIPS), dispute settlement mechanism.

eco_qr_removal_2001.label: Removal of Quantitative Restrictions (April 2001)
eco_qr_removal_2001.subject: economics
eco_qr_removal_2001.detail: India removed QRs on imports of all manufactured consumer goods and agricultural products from 1 April 2001, fulfilling WTO commitments. Final step of trade liberalisation started in 1991. Triggered debate on farmer competitiveness against subsidised imports.

eco_outsourcing_bpo.label: Outsourcing / BPO Industry
eco_outsourcing_bpo.subject: economics
eco_outsourcing_bpo.detail: Business Process Outsourcing — Indian IT-enabled services (call centres, back-office, transcription, accounting) for developed country firms. Exploded post-2000 on low wages + skilled English-speaking manpower + telecom revolution. India became global BPO hub by mid-2000s.

eco_fii_introduction.label: Foreign Institutional Investors (FIIs, 1992)
eco_fii_introduction.subject: economics
eco_fii_introduction.detail: FII investment in Indian financial markets permitted from 1992 under SEBI regulations. Merchant bankers, mutual funds, pension funds allowed to invest in Indian equity and debt. Triggered sustained portfolio flows; today FPIs hold ~16% of Indian equity market.

eco_sez_act_2005.label: Special Economic Zones (SEZ) Act 2005
eco_sez_act_2005.subject: economics
eco_sez_act_2005.detail: SEZ Act passed 2005, operational April 2006. Duty-free enclaves with simplified procedures, tax holidays, single-window clearances to attract FDI and boost exports. Controversial over land acquisition (Nandigram, Singur, POSCO protests). 378+ approved SEZs as of 2024.

eco_fema_1999.label: Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA) 1999
eco_fema_1999.subject: economics
eco_fema_1999.detail: Passed 1999, operational 1 June 2000. Replaced draconian Foreign Exchange Regulation Act (FERA) 1973. Facilitated external trade and payments, promoted orderly forex market development. Civil rather than criminal offences. RBI as regulator.

pol_soviet_disintegration_1991.label: Soviet Union Disintegration (December 1991)
pol_soviet_disintegration_1991.stage: Parallel — End of Cold War & Post-Soviet Russia
pol_soviet_disintegration_1991.subject: polity
pol_soviet_disintegration_1991.detail: USSR dissolved 26 December 1991. Gorbachev resigned 25 December. Triggered by nationalist movements in Baltic states (1988-90), August 1991 coup attempt against Gorbachev by hardliners, and Belavezha Accords (8 Dec 1991) signed by Russia/Ukraine/Belarus. 15 successor states formed.

pol_gorbachev_reforms.label: Gorbachev's Perestroika & Glasnost (1985-91)
pol_gorbachev_reforms.stage: Parallel — End of Cold War & Post-Soviet Russia
pol_gorbachev_reforms.subject: polity
pol_gorbachev_reforms.detail: Mikhail Gorbachev (General Secretary 1985) launched perestroika (economic restructuring) and glasnost (openness) reforms. Loosened central planning, liberalised political speech, reduced Cold War confrontation. Unintentionally triggered nationalist movements in republics; USSR collapsed 1991.

pol_boris_yeltsin.label: Boris Yeltsin (President of Russia 1991-99)
pol_boris_yeltsin.stage: Parallel — End of Cold War & Post-Soviet Russia
pol_boris_yeltsin.subject: polity
pol_boris_yeltsin.detail: First elected President of Russian Federation (1991-99). Led opposition to August 1991 coup against Gorbachev. Dissolved USSR via Belavezha Accords with Ukraine/Belarus. Oversaw shock therapy transition. Resigned 31 December 1999, handed over to Putin.

pol_indo_russian_strategic_2001.label: Indo-Russian Strategic Agreement (October 2001)
pol_indo_russian_strategic_2001.subject: polity
pol_indo_russian_strategic_2001.detail: Declaration on Strategic Partnership signed by PM Vajpayee and President Putin in Delhi, 4 October 2000 (not 2001 as sometimes cited). Over 80 bilateral agreements under this framework. Areas: defence, nuclear energy, space, counter-terrorism, shared vision of multipolar world.

pol_george_w_bush.label: George W. Bush (US President 2001-09)
pol_george_w_bush.subject: polity
pol_george_w_bush.detail: 43rd US President (20 January 2001 - 20 January 2009). Launched War on Terror post-9/11: Afghanistan (Oct 2001) and Iraq (March 2003). Signed Indo-US Nuclear Deal (2008). NDA relations with India deepened under his tenure — Bush/Vajpayee/Manmohan Singh era.

pol_george_hw_bush.label: George H.W. Bush (US President 1989-93)
pol_george_hw_bush.subject: polity
pol_george_hw_bush.detail: 41st US President (January 1989 - January 1993). Presided over end of Cold War, German reunification, First Gulf War (Operation Desert Storm, 1991). Lost 1992 election to Clinton amid recession.

pol_operation_enduring_freedom.label: Operation Enduring Freedom (Afghanistan, Oct 2001)
pol_operation_enduring_freedom.subject: polity
pol_operation_enduring_freedom.detail: US-led military campaign in Afghanistan launched 7 October 2001 in response to 9/11. Toppled Taliban regime by December 2001; Hamid Karzai became interim leader. Transitioned to NATO-led ISAF (2003). US withdrew August 2021, Taliban returned.

pol_hegemony_post_cold_war.label: US Hegemony / Unipolar Moment (1991-2008)
pol_hegemony_post_cold_war.stage: Parallel — End of Cold War & Post-Soviet Russia
pol_hegemony_post_cold_war.subject: polity
pol_hegemony_post_cold_war.detail: Post-Cold War period of sole US superpower status, 1991-2008. Military (all-domain dominance), economic (dollar hegemony, WTO/IMF/World Bank), structural (cultural/institutional/ideological). Challenged post-2008 by China's rise, Russia resurgence, BRICS, 2008 financial crisis.

pol_bofors_scandal.label: Bofors Scandal (1987)
pol_bofors_scandal.subject: polity
pol_bofors_scandal.detail: Alleged kickbacks of Rs 64 crore paid by Swedish arms firm AB Bofors to Indian officials and politicians for the 1986 contract to supply 155mm howitzer guns. Triggered V.P. Singh's resignation from Rajiv Gandhi cabinet in 1987. Became central election issue in 1989. Supreme Court quashed charges in 2004; acquittals of accused.

pol_jan_morcha_1987.label: Jan Morcha (People's Front, 1987)
pol_jan_morcha_1987.subject: polity
pol_jan_morcha_1987.detail: Political grouping formed 2 October 1987 by V.P. Singh, Arif Mohammad Khan, Arun Nehru, and other Congress dissidents after their expulsion/resignation from Congress. Core of the anti-Rajiv opposition. Merged with Lok Dal, Janata, Congress(S) to form Janata Dal on 11 October 1988.

pol_janata_dal_formation.label: Janata Dal Formation (11 October 1988)
pol_janata_dal_formation.subject: polity
pol_janata_dal_formation.detail: Janata Dal formed 11 October 1988 (J.P. Narayan's birthday) by merging Jan Morcha, Lok Dal, Janata Party, and Congress(S). V.P. Singh elected president. Became principal non-Congress opposition party. Led the National Front in 1989 and United Front in 1996-98.

pol_allahabad_byelection_1988.label: Allahabad By-election (June 1988)
pol_allahabad_byelection_1988.subject: polity
pol_allahabad_byelection_1988.detail: V.P. Singh won the Allahabad Lok Sabha by-election in June 1988 against Congress with Bofors gun as campaign symbol. Convinced Left and BJP that he was viable anti-Congress candidate. Led to National Front formation on 6 August 1988.

pol_kargil_war_1999.label: Kargil War (May-July 1999)
pol_kargil_war_1999.subject: polity
pol_kargil_war_1999.detail: Indo-Pakistani armed conflict in Kargil district of Kashmir, 3 May - 26 July 1999. Pakistan's regular army (Northern Light Infantry) and Mujahideen infiltrated across LoC and occupied heights. India launched Operation Vijay to evict them. Capture of Tololing and Tiger Hill. ~527 Indian soldiers killed. PM Vajpayee, Army Chief V.P. Malik.

pol_pokhran_ii_1998.label: Pokhran-II / Operation Shakti (11-13 May 1998)
pol_pokhran_ii_1998.subject: polity
pol_pokhran_ii_1998.detail: Five nuclear tests conducted at Pokhran range, Rajasthan, 11-13 May 1998: 3 on 11 May (one thermonuclear/hydrogen bomb, 45 kiloton yield), 2 on 13 May (sub-kiloton). PM Vajpayee declared India a nuclear weapons state. Team led by Dr A.P.J. Abdul Kalam (DRDO) and R. Chidambaram (DAE). Triggered US/Japan/Western sanctions.

pol_lahore_bus_yatra_1999.label: Lahore Bus Yatra / Lahore Declaration (February 1999)
pol_lahore_bus_yatra_1999.subject: polity
pol_lahore_bus_yatra_1999.detail: Vajpayee took inaugural Delhi-Lahore bus service on 19 February 1999. Met Pakistan PM Nawaz Sharif at Lahore. Signed Lahore Declaration 21 Feb 1999 — confidence-building measures, bilateral dispute resolution, nuclear risk reduction. Kargil War 3 months later undermined the initiative.

pol_kandahar_hijacking.label: IC-814 Kandahar Hijacking (December 1999)
pol_kandahar_hijacking.subject: polity
pol_kandahar_hijacking.detail: Indian Airlines flight IC-814 (Kathmandu-Delhi) hijacked on Christmas Eve 1999 by Harkat-ul-Mujahideen. Diverted through Amritsar, Lahore, Dubai to Kandahar (Taliban-controlled). One passenger killed. Ended 31 Dec 1999 with India releasing Maulana Masood Azhar, Omar Sheikh, Mushtaq Zargar. Jaswant Singh escorted prisoners.

pol_parliament_attack_2001.label: Parliament Attack (13 December 2001)
pol_parliament_attack_2001.subject: polity
pol_parliament_attack_2001.detail: Five Lashkar-e-Taiba/Jaish-e-Mohammed terrorists attacked Indian Parliament complex, 13 December 2001. 9 security personnel and a gardener killed; all 5 terrorists killed. Triggered Operation Parakram — massive 10-month Indian military mobilisation on Pakistan border. Afzal Guru hanged 2013.

pol_operation_parakram.label: Operation Parakram (2001-02)
pol_operation_parakram.subject: polity
pol_operation_parakram.detail: Largest Indian military mobilisation since 1971, launched after 13 December 2001 Parliament attack. 500,000 Indian troops deployed on Pakistan border, December 2001 to October 2002. Stood down without war but led to significant casualties via mine accidents. US/UK diplomatic pressure defused crisis.

pol_agra_summit_2001.label: Agra Summit (July 2001)
pol_agra_summit_2001.subject: polity
pol_agra_summit_2001.detail: Vajpayee-Musharraf summit at Agra, 14-16 July 2001. Collapsed without joint statement due to disagreement over terminology (Kashmir as 'core issue' vs 'cross-border terrorism'). Musharraf's media outreach scored PR gains. Formal resumption of dialogue delayed until SAARC Islamabad 2004.

pol_tehelka_expose_2001.label: Tehelka Exposé (March 2001)
pol_tehelka_expose_2001.subject: polity
pol_tehelka_expose_2001.detail: Online news portal Tehelka aired 'Operation West End' sting, 13 March 2001 — journalists posing as arms dealers filmed BJP president Bangaru Laxman taking Rs 1 lakh cash and Samata Party president Jaya Jaitly accepting Rs 2 lakh at Defence Minister George Fernandes's residence. Laxman and Fernandes resigned. Tehelka subsequently faced harassment.

pol_india_shining_2004.label: 'India Shining' Campaign (2004)
pol_india_shining_2004.subject: polity
pol_india_shining_2004.detail: BJP-NDA's pre-election ad campaign, early 2004, extolling economic growth under Vajpayee. Rs 150 crore spend. Backfired — rural and poor voters felt excluded. Congress countered with 'Congress ka haath, aam aadmi ke saath'. NDA defeated in May 2004, biggest upset since 1977.

pol_pota_2002.label: POTA / Prevention of Terrorism Act 2002
pol_pota_2002.subject: polity
pol_pota_2002.detail: Anti-terror law enacted 28 March 2002 replacing lapsed TADA. Passed after Parliament attack. Expanded police powers, presumption of guilt. Critics alleged misuse against minorities. Repealed in 2004 by UPA government, replaced by UAPA amendment.

pol_pota_repeal_2004.label: POTA Repeal + UAPA Expansion (2004)
pol_pota_repeal_2004.subject: polity
pol_pota_repeal_2004.detail: UPA government repealed POTA in September 2004. Simultaneously amended Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA) 1967 to incorporate anti-terror provisions. UAPA further expanded 2008, 2012, 2019. Critics note UAPA more draconian than POTA in bail/evidence provisions.

pol_national_advisory_council.label: National Advisory Council (NAC, 2004)
pol_national_advisory_council.subject: polity
pol_national_advisory_council.detail: Advisory body set up June 2004 under Sonia Gandhi (chair) to advise UPA government on policy. Members: civil society activists, intellectuals (Aruna Roy, Jean Drèze etc.). Drove RTI Act, NREGA, Forest Rights Act, Food Security Act. Disbanded 2014.

pol_sachar_committee_2005.label: Sachar Committee (2005-06)
pol_sachar_committee_2005.subject: polity
pol_sachar_committee_2005.detail: High-level committee headed by Justice Rajindar Sachar to study social, economic and educational status of Muslims in India. Report submitted 17 November 2006. Found Muslims worse off than SCs/STs on many indicators. Drove Ministry of Minority Affairs and 15-Point Programme for Welfare of Minorities.

pol_ministry_minority_affairs_2006.label: Ministry of Minority Affairs (2006)
pol_ministry_minority_affairs_2006.subject: polity
pol_ministry_minority_affairs_2006.detail: Created 29 January 2006 as separate ministry (earlier part of Ministry of Social Justice). Nodal ministry for 6 notified minority communities (Muslims, Christians, Sikhs, Buddhists, Parsis, Jains added 2014). Implements Pre-Matric/Post-Matric scholarships, Maulana Azad Foundation, Waqf matters.

pol_domestic_violence_act_2005.label: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act 2005
pol_domestic_violence_act_2005.subject: polity
pol_domestic_violence_act_2005.detail: Enacted September 2005, in effect 26 October 2006. Recognised physical, sexual, emotional, verbal, and economic abuse within shared households as domestic violence. Provided civil remedies (protection orders, residence orders, monetary relief). Applicable to any woman in domestic relationship regardless of marital status.

pol_hindu_succession_amendment_2005.label: Hindu Succession (Amendment) Act 2005
pol_hindu_succession_amendment_2005.subject: polity
pol_hindu_succession_amendment_2005.detail: Amended Hindu Succession Act 1956. Made daughters equal coparceners in ancestral joint family property — same rights as sons by birth. Removed gender discrimination in Mitakshara coparcenary. Radical gender reform in inheritance law.

pol_rte_act_2009.label: Right to Education Act 2009
pol_rte_act_2009.subject: polity
pol_rte_act_2009.detail: Enacted 4 August 2009, in force 1 April 2010. Operationalised Article 21A (86th Amendment 2002) guaranteeing free and compulsory education to all children aged 6-14. 25% reservation in private unaided schools for economically weaker sections. No detention till Class 8 (repealed 2019).

pol_obc_reservation_education_2006.label: 27% OBC Reservation in Higher Education (2006)
pol_obc_reservation_education_2006.subject: polity
pol_obc_reservation_education_2006.detail: Central Educational Institutions (Reservation in Admission) Act 2006. Introduced 27% OBC reservation in central universities and IITs/IIMs from 2007. Challenged in Ashoka Kumar Thakur case; Supreme Court upheld 2008 (with creamy layer exclusion).

pol_ashoka_thakur_case_2008.label: Ashoka Kumar Thakur Case (2008)
pol_ashoka_thakur_case_2008.subject: polity
