cul_nauroz_ich_2016.detail: Persian New Year marking spring equinox. India joined 7-country (now 12) multinational UNESCO ICH inscription 2016 (originally inscribed 2009). Celebrated by Parsis and Kashmiri communities in India. Cultural links to Zoroastrian tradition.

cul_yoga_ich_2016.label: Yoga (UNESCO ICH, 2016)
cul_yoga_ich_2016.subject: history
cul_yoga_ich_2016.detail: Physical, mental, spiritual practices of ancient Indian origin. UNESCO ICH Representative List 1 December 2016. UN declared 21 June International Day of Yoga (2014, observed from 2015). India's diplomatic outreach under PM Modi.

cul_kumbh_mela_ich_2017.label: Kumbh Mela (UNESCO ICH, 2017)
cul_kumbh_mela_ich_2017.subject: history
cul_kumbh_mela_ich_2017.detail: World's largest religious gathering. UNESCO ICH Representative List December 2017. Held every 12 years at 4 sites: Prayagraj (Ganga-Yamuna-Saraswati sangam), Haridwar, Nashik, Ujjain. Ardh Kumbh every 6 years. Prayagraj 2019 drew ~24 crore pilgrims; 2025 Mahakumbh ~66+ crore.

cul_durga_puja_ich_2021.label: Durga Puja in Kolkata (UNESCO ICH, 2021)
cul_durga_puja_ich_2021.subject: history
cul_durga_puja_ich_2021.detail: Annual festival of Durga worship in Kolkata, West Bengal. Inscribed UNESCO ICH Representative List 15 December 2021. Features elaborate pandals, artistic clay idols (kumartuli), community involvement spanning religions and classes. Immersion in Hooghly on Vijaya Dashami.

cul_garba_ich_2023.label: Garba of Gujarat (UNESCO ICH, 2023)
cul_garba_ich_2023.subject: history
cul_garba_ich_2023.detail: Traditional folk dance of Gujarat performed during Navratri honouring Goddess Amba. UNESCO ICH Representative List 6 December 2023. Circular formation around a central garbi (lamp) or image. Accompanied by dholak, cymbals, songs. Popularised globally via Gujarati diaspora.

cul_whs_qutb_minar_1993.label: Qutb Minar & Monuments UNESCO Site (1993)
cul_whs_qutb_minar_1993.subject: history
cul_whs_qutb_minar_1993.detail: Qutb Minar complex in Delhi inscribed UNESCO World Heritage Site 1993. 73m tall minaret built by Qutb-ud-din Aibak (1199 onwards). Includes Quwwat-ul-Islam Mosque, Alai Darwaza, Iron Pillar of Delhi. Iconic of Delhi Sultanate architecture.

cul_whs_humayuns_tomb_1993.label: Humayun's Tomb UNESCO Site (1993)
cul_whs_humayuns_tomb_1993.subject: history
cul_whs_humayuns_tomb_1993.detail: Mughal garden tomb of Emperor Humayun in Delhi, commissioned by his widow Bega Begum 1565, completed 1572. Architect Mirak Mirza Ghiyath. UNESCO WHS 1993. Precursor to Taj Mahal in charbagh garden plan. Aga Khan Trust restoration 2003-2013.

cul_whs_darjeeling_railway_1999.label: Darjeeling Himalayan Railway UNESCO Site (1999)
cul_whs_darjeeling_railway_1999.subject: history
cul_whs_darjeeling_railway_1999.detail: Narrow-gauge mountain railway (1881) between Siliguri and Darjeeling, West Bengal. Inscribed UNESCO WHS 1999. Extended to include Nilgiri Mountain Railway (2005) and Kalka-Shimla Railway (2008) as 'Mountain Railways of India' serial site.

cul_whs_bhimbetka_2003.label: Bhimbetka Rock Shelters UNESCO Site (2003)
cul_whs_bhimbetka_2003.subject: history
cul_whs_bhimbetka_2003.detail: Paleolithic-to-Medieval rock shelters near Bhopal, Madhya Pradesh with prehistoric paintings dating back ~30,000 years (Upper Palaeolithic to Historic). Discovered by V.S. Wakankar 1957. Inscribed UNESCO WHS 2003. 750+ shelters, 400+ with paintings across 7 hills.

cul_whs_cst_2004.label: Chhatrapati Shivaji Terminus UNESCO Site (2004)
cul_whs_cst_2004.subject: history
cul_whs_cst_2004.detail: Victorian Gothic railway station in Mumbai (originally Victoria Terminus), designed by F.W. Stevens 1878-87. Inscribed UNESCO WHS 2004. Blend of Victorian-Italianate Gothic and traditional Indian architecture.

cul_whs_red_fort_2007.label: Red Fort Complex UNESCO Site (2007)
cul_whs_red_fort_2007.subject: history
cul_whs_red_fort_2007.detail: Mughal fortress-palace in Delhi built by Shah Jahan 1639-48 as capital of Shahjahanabad. UNESCO WHS 2007. PM's Independence Day address from Lahori Gate. Diwan-i-Aam, Diwan-i-Khas, Rang Mahal, Moti Masjid. Looted during 1857 revolt, again during British colonial period.

cul_whs_jantar_mantar_2010.label: Jantar Mantar Jaipur UNESCO Site (2010)
cul_whs_jantar_mantar_2010.subject: history
cul_whs_jantar_mantar_2010.detail: Astronomical observatory in Jaipur built by Sawai Jai Singh II, 1727-33. UNESCO WHS 2010. 19 monumental masonry instruments including the world's largest stone sundial. Delhi, Varanasi, Ujjain, Mathura also have Jantar Mantars.

cul_whs_western_ghats_2012.label: Western Ghats UNESCO Site (2012)
cul_whs_western_ghats_2012.subject: history
cul_whs_western_ghats_2012.detail: Serial natural WHS, inscribed 2012. 39 component sites across Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Maharashtra. One of 8 'hottest biodiversity hotspots' globally — 325 globally threatened species. Older than Himalayas. Part of UNESCO World Heritage List (Natural Criteria).

cul_whs_hill_forts_rajasthan_2013.label: Hill Forts of Rajasthan UNESCO Site (2013)
cul_whs_hill_forts_rajasthan_2013.subject: history
cul_whs_hill_forts_rajasthan_2013.detail: Serial WHS of 6 hill forts: Chittorgarh, Kumbhalgarh, Ranthambore, Amber, Jaisalmer, Gagron. Inscribed 2013. Examples of Rajput military architecture across 8th-19th centuries.

cul_whs_rani_ki_vav_2014.label: Rani ki Vav UNESCO Site (2014)
cul_whs_rani_ki_vav_2014.subject: history
cul_whs_rani_ki_vav_2014.detail: 11th-century stepwell in Patan, Gujarat, built by Queen Udayamati in memory of Solanki king Bhimdev I (c.1063). Inscribed UNESCO WHS 2014. 7 storeys, 500+ sculptures depicting Hindu mythology. Featured on Rs 100 note.

cul_whs_nalanda_2016.label: Nalanda Mahavihara UNESCO Site (2016)
cul_whs_nalanda_2016.subject: history
cul_whs_nalanda_2016.detail: Archaeological remains of ancient Buddhist mahavihara (monastic university), Bihar. Flourished 5th-12th centuries under Guptas and Palas. Inscribed UNESCO WHS 2016. Destroyed by Bakhtiyar Khilji c.1193. Modern Nalanda University established 2010.

cul_whs_le_corbusier_chandigarh_2016.label: Chandigarh Capitol (Le Corbusier) UNESCO Site (2016)
cul_whs_le_corbusier_chandigarh_2016.subject: history
cul_whs_le_corbusier_chandigarh_2016.detail: Part of transnational serial WHS 'Architectural Work of Le Corbusier' inscribed 2016 across 7 countries. Indian component: Capitol Complex Chandigarh — Assembly, Secretariat, High Court (1950s-60s). Reflects modern movement architecture.

cul_whs_ahmedabad_2017.label: Historic City of Ahmadabad UNESCO Site (2017)
cul_whs_ahmedabad_2017.subject: history
cul_whs_ahmedabad_2017.detail: Walled city founded by Sultan Ahmad Shah I 1411 on east bank of Sabarmati. Inscribed UNESCO WHS 8 July 2017 — first Indian city on the list. Heritage: pols (neighbourhoods), Jama Masjid, Sidi Saiyyed Jali, Sabarmati Ashram.

cul_whs_jaipur_city_2019.label: Jaipur City UNESCO Site (2019)
cul_whs_jaipur_city_2019.subject: history
cul_whs_jaipur_city_2019.detail: Planned city founded by Sawai Jai Singh II 1727. Inscribed UNESCO WHS 2019 — second Indian city. Planned on Vedic architectural grid (9-square). Pink colour-washed 1876 in honour of Prince Albert's visit. Heritage: Hawa Mahal, City Palace, Jantar Mantar.

cul_whs_kakatiya_temple_2021.label: Kakatiya Rudreshwara (Ramappa) Temple UNESCO Site (2021)
cul_whs_kakatiya_temple_2021.subject: history
cul_whs_kakatiya_temple_2021.detail: 13th-century Kakatiya-era Shaiva temple in Palampet, Telangana, built by Recharla Rudra under Kakatiya Ganapati Deva, 1213 CE. Sculptor Ramappa. UNESCO WHS 25 July 2021. Notable for sandbox foundation and lightweight floating bricks.

cul_whs_dholavira_2021.label: Dholavira UNESCO Site (2021)
cul_whs_dholavira_2021.subject: history
cul_whs_dholavira_2021.detail: Harappan (Indus Valley) city in Kutch, Gujarat. Excavated by R.S. Bisht 1989-2005. UNESCO WHS 27 July 2021 — 40th Indian site. Three subdivisions (citadel/middle/lower town), sophisticated water management with 16 reservoirs. Dated 3000-1500 BCE.

cul_whs_santiniketan_2023.label: Santiniketan UNESCO Site (2023)
cul_whs_santiniketan_2023.subject: history
cul_whs_santiniketan_2023.detail: Educational and cultural centre founded by Rabindranath Tagore 1901, West Bengal. Inscribed UNESCO WHS 17 September 2023. Visva-Bharati University (1921). Pedagogy of nature-based education. Tagore's 'universalism' philosophy embodied in campus architecture.

cul_whs_hoysala_temples_2023.label: Sacred Ensembles of Hoysalas UNESCO Site (2023)
cul_whs_hoysala_temples_2023.subject: history
cul_whs_hoysala_temples_2023.detail: 12th-13th century Hoysala-era temples in Karnataka: Chennakeshava Temple (Belur), Hoysaleswara Temple (Halebidu), Keshava Temple (Somanathapura). UNESCO WHS 18 September 2023. Known for intricate stone carvings, star-shaped plans.

cul_whs_charaideo_moidams_2024.label: Charaideo Moidams UNESCO Site (2024)
cul_whs_charaideo_moidams_2024.subject: history
cul_whs_charaideo_moidams_2024.detail: Ahom dynasty burial mounds (moidams) of Assam, built over 600 years (13th-19th centuries) at Charaideo. UNESCO WHS 2024 — first cultural site from North-East India. 90 moidams at site; vaulted underground chambers.

cul_gi_act_1999.label: Geographical Indications Act 1999
cul_gi_act_1999.subject: history
cul_gi_act_1999.detail: Geographical Indications of Goods (Registration and Protection) Act 1999, in force 15 September 2003. Implements TRIPS GI obligation. GI Registry in Chennai. First GI: Darjeeling Tea (2004). 600+ GIs registered by 2024 including Basmati, Mysore Silk, Kanchipuram Saree, Banarasi Saree, Banaganapalle Mangoes.

cul_national_culture_fund_1996.label: National Culture Fund (1996)
cul_national_culture_fund_1996.subject: history
cul_national_culture_fund_1996.detail: Public charitable trust set up under Charitable Endowments Act 1890, registered 28 November 1996. Enables private sector and individuals to partner in conservation/promotion of India's cultural heritage. CSR contributions eligible. Major projects: Humayun's Tomb restoration, Qutub Minar complex.

cul_international_yoga_day_2014.label: International Day of Yoga (21 June, UN 2014)
cul_international_yoga_day_2014.subject: history
cul_international_yoga_day_2014.detail: Proposed by PM Modi at UNGA 27 September 2014. Adopted unanimously by UNGA 11 December 2014 (177 co-sponsors). First observed 21 June 2015. Marks summer solstice (longest day). Common Yoga Protocol performed. India's soft-power diplomacy success.

sci_chandrayaan_1_2008.label: Chandrayaan-1 Lunar Mission (2008)
sci_chandrayaan_1_2008.subject: history
sci_chandrayaan_1_2008.detail: India's first lunar probe, launched 22 October 2008 by PSLV-C11 from Sriharikota. Operational phase November 2008 - August 2009. Major discovery: water molecules on Moon (September 2009, with NASA M3 instrument). Mission cost Rs 386 crore. Established India as 6th country to reach Moon.

sci_mangalyaan_2013.label: Mangalyaan / Mars Orbiter Mission (2013)
sci_mangalyaan_2013.subject: history
sci_mangalyaan_2013.detail: India's first interplanetary mission, launched 5 November 2013 by PSLV-C25. Achieved Mars orbit 24 September 2014. First Asian nation, fourth space agency to reach Mars. First nation to succeed in first Mars attempt. Cost Rs 450 crore — lower than Hollywood film Gravity. Operational till April 2022.

sci_chandrayaan_2_2019.label: Chandrayaan-2 Mission (2019)
sci_chandrayaan_2_2019.subject: history
sci_chandrayaan_2_2019.detail: India's second lunar mission, launched 22 July 2019 by GSLV Mk-III. Orbiter-Lander-Rover (Vikram-Pragyan). Lander crash-landed 7 September 2019 near south pole. Orbiter continues operations. Terrain Mapping Camera, Dual-Frequency Synthetic Aperture Radar instruments.

sci_chandrayaan_3_2023.label: Chandrayaan-3 Soft Landing (23 August 2023)
sci_chandrayaan_3_2023.subject: history
sci_chandrayaan_3_2023.detail: India's third lunar mission, launched 14 July 2023 by LVM3 Mk-III. Soft-landed Vikram lander + Pragyan rover near Moon's south pole, 23 August 2023 — first country to achieve south pole soft-landing; 4th to soft-land on Moon. National Space Day 23 August instituted. Confirmed presence of elements (Al, Ca, Fe, S, Ti) near south pole.

sci_aditya_l1_2023.label: Aditya-L1 Solar Mission (2023)
sci_aditya_l1_2023.subject: history
sci_aditya_l1_2023.detail: India's first solar observation mission, launched 2 September 2023 by PSLV-C57. Placed in halo orbit around Sun-Earth L1 Lagrangian point (~1.5 million km) on 6 January 2024. 7 payloads to study solar corona, chromosphere, solar wind.

sci_quantum_mission_2023.label: National Quantum Mission (2023)
sci_quantum_mission_2023.subject: history
sci_quantum_mission_2023.detail: Approved by Union Cabinet 19 April 2023. Rs 6,003 crore outlay (2023-31). Targets: develop quantum computers (50-1000 physical qubits), quantum communication, quantum sensing, quantum materials. DST nodal. 4 T-Hubs at IIT Bombay, IISc, IIT Madras, IIT Delhi.

sci_gaganyaan.label: Gaganyaan (Indian Human Spaceflight Programme)
sci_gaganyaan.subject: history
sci_gaganyaan.detail: India's human spaceflight programme, announced 15 August 2018 by PM Modi. First crewed mission targeted 2026. Test flights: Gaganyaan-1 (uncrewed, TV-D1 test October 2023), G-1, G-2 before crewed G-3. 3-member crew, LEO mission. Budget Rs 10,000+ crore expanded to Rs 20,000 crore.

period_s26.label: Parallel — End of Cold War & Post-Soviet Russia (1989-2000)
period_s26.stage: Parallel — End of Cold War & Post-Soviet Russia
period_s26.subject: history
period_s26.detail: Berlin Wall falls 9 Nov 1989 → 1990 unification. USSR dissolves 26 Dec 1991. Gorbachev's perestroika/glasnost (1985-91) trigger nationalist surge. Yeltsin shock therapy. CIS formed Dec 1991. Yugoslavia breaks up; Bosnian war. EU formed Maastricht 1992. First Gulf War 1991. Chemical Weapons Convention 1992. Russia-NATO uneasy peace. India loses Soviet ally; pivots to multipolar diplomacy.

period_s27.label: Parallel — 9/11 & War on Terror (2001-2012)
period_s27.subject: history
period_s27.detail: 9/11 attacks 11 Sept 2001 reshape world order. US launches Operation Enduring Freedom (Afghanistan) Oct 2001 → Taliban falls Dec 2001. Al-Qaeda hunted. Operation Iraqi Freedom March 2003 — toppled Saddam, no WMDs found. Musharraf coup Pakistan Oct 1999; ally in War on Terror. Kosovo crisis 1999. India-US engagement deepens via War on Terror frame. Bin Laden killed May 2011 in Abbottabad raid.

period_s28.label: Parallel — 2008 Global Financial Crisis (2007-2010)
period_s28.subject: history
period_s28.detail: Lehman Brothers collapse 15 Sept 2008 triggers global recession. Credit freeze, bank failures across US/Europe. India weathers via insulated banking, domestic demand. RBI cuts repo from 9% to 4.75% (Oct 2008-Apr 2009). Three fiscal stimulus packages Dec 2008-Feb 2009. GDP slows 9.3%→6.7% but rebounds. Foundation of expansionary trend that turned into 2013 taper tantrum and twin balance sheet problem.

period_s29.label: Parallel — COVID-19 Pandemic (2019-2023)
period_s29.subject: history
period_s29.detail: COVID-19 declared pandemic 11 Mar 2020. India lockdown 25 March 2020 — strictest globally. Migrant labour reverse-migration. PMGKAY food relief. Delta wave April-June 2021 (Kumbh + WB elections super-spreaders). Vaccination drive 16 Jan 2021 — Covaxin (indigenous), Covishield (SII-AstraZeneca). 220 crore+ doses by 2023. Co-WIN platform. Economic contraction FY21 (-6.6%, first since 1979). India world's pharmacy: 'vaccine maitri' diplomacy. Atmanirbhar Bharat response.

pol_president_shankar_dayal.label: Shankar Dayal Sharma (President 1992-97)
pol_president_shankar_dayal.subject: polity
pol_president_shankar_dayal.detail: 9th President of India (25 July 1992 - 25 July 1997). Former Vice President (1987-92). Imposed President's Rule on BJP state governments after Babri demolition. Oversaw coalition governments' swearing-in (Narasimha Rao, Deve Gowda).

pol_president_kr_narayanan.label: K.R. Narayanan (President 1997-2002)
pol_president_kr_narayanan.subject: polity
pol_president_kr_narayanan.detail: 10th President of India (25 July 1997 - 25 July 2002). First Dalit President. Dismissed Gujarat government's advice on President's Rule 1998. Broke convention by publicly warning PM during Gujarat 2002 riots. Former diplomat, VP.

pol_president_kalam.label: A.P.J. Abdul Kalam (President 2002-07)
pol_president_kalam.subject: polity
pol_president_kalam.detail: 11th President of India (25 July 2002 - 25 July 2007). Eminent aerospace scientist, 'Missile Man of India'. Led Pokhran-II team as DRDO head. Authored 'Wings of Fire', 'India 2020'. Died 27 July 2015. Bharat Ratna 1997.

pol_president_pratibha_patil.label: Pratibha Patil (President 2007-12)
pol_president_pratibha_patil.subject: polity
pol_president_pratibha_patil.detail: 12th President of India (25 July 2007 - 25 July 2012). First woman President. Former Rajasthan Governor. Commuted death sentences of 35 convicts (most by any President). Approved Lokpal referral.

pol_president_pranab_mukherjee.label: Pranab Mukherjee (President 2012-17)
pol_president_pranab_mukherjee.subject: polity
pol_president_pranab_mukherjee.detail: 13th President of India (25 July 2012 - 25 July 2017). Former Finance Minister (UPA-I and UPA-II), Congress stalwart. Known as 'the best PM India never had'. Bharat Ratna 2019. Died 31 August 2020.

pol_president_kovind.label: Ram Nath Kovind (President 2017-22)
pol_president_kovind.subject: polity
pol_president_kovind.detail: 14th President of India (25 July 2017 - 25 July 2022). Second Dalit President. Former Bihar Governor. Signed Article 370 abrogation order 5 Aug 2019 and Farm Laws 2020.

pol_president_murmu.label: Droupadi Murmu (President 2022-present)
pol_president_murmu.subject: polity
pol_president_murmu.detail: 15th President of India (25 July 2022 -). First tribal (Santhal) President, youngest ever (64). Former Jharkhand Governor (2015-21). Signed Women's Reservation Act 2023, new criminal laws 2023.

eco_pmay_2015.label: Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (PMAY, 2015)
eco_pmay_2015.subject: economics
eco_pmay_2015.detail: Housing for All scheme launched June 2015. PMAY-Urban (25 June) + PMAY-Gramin (November). Targets pucca houses with water/electricity/LPG/toilets. Central assistance Rs 1.2-2.5 lakh/unit. 4+ crore houses built by 2024. Target extended to 2024-29 with 3 crore more houses.

eco_smart_cities_2015.label: Smart Cities Mission (2015)
eco_smart_cities_2015.subject: economics
eco_smart_cities_2015.detail: Urban renewal mission launched 25 June 2015. 100 cities selected competitively. Core infrastructure + area-based development + technology solutions. Special Purpose Vehicles (SPVs). Central outlay Rs 48,000 crore. Extended to March 2025 and beyond.

eco_amrut_2015.label: AMRUT Mission (2015)
eco_amrut_2015.subject: economics
eco_amrut_2015.detail: Atal Mission for Rejuvenation and Urban Transformation launched 25 June 2015. 500 cities with population >1 lakh. Water supply, sewerage, urban transport, green spaces. AMRUT 2.0 launched October 2021 for water and sewage in all urban areas.

eco_bharatmala_2017.label: Bharatmala Pariyojana (2017)
eco_bharatmala_2017.subject: economics
eco_bharatmala_2017.detail: Umbrella highway programme approved October 2017. Rs 5.35 lakh crore outlay (Phase I). Target 34,800 km of highways: economic corridors, inter-corridor/feeder routes, national corridors efficiency, border roads, coastal/port connectivity, expressways. Slowed rollout; partially subsumed under Gati Shakti.

eco_sagarmala_2015.label: Sagarmala Programme (2015)
eco_sagarmala_2015.subject: economics
eco_sagarmala_2015.detail: Port-led development programme approved March 2015. 6 Mega Ports, modernise existing ports, port-rail/road connectivity, coastal shipping, coastal community development. Aimed to reduce logistics cost for EXIM/domestic cargo. 802 projects worth Rs 5.5 lakh crore identified.

eco_pm_kisan_2018.label: PM-KISAN (2018)
eco_pm_kisan_2018.stage: Modi-II: Art 370, CAA, COVID, Farm Laws
eco_pm_kisan_2018.subject: economics
eco_pm_kisan_2018.detail: PM Kisan Samman Nidhi launched 24 February 2019 (announced Feb 2018 Interim Budget). Rs 6,000/year DBT to all landholding farmers (earlier only small/marginal). 11+ crore beneficiaries. Rs 3.24 lakh crore disbursed by 2024 over 17 installments.

eco_saubhagya_2017.label: Saubhagya Scheme (2017)
eco_saubhagya_2017.subject: economics
eco_saubhagya_2017.detail: Pradhan Mantri Sahaj Bijli Har Ghar Yojana, launched 25 September 2017. Universal household electrification — all remaining non-electrified rural + urban households. 2.86+ crore households electrified; India declared 100% village electrification 28 April 2018.

eco_atal_pension_2015.label: Atal Pension Yojana (APY, 2015)
eco_atal_pension_2015.subject: economics
eco_atal_pension_2015.detail: Pension scheme for unorganised sector workers, launched 1 June 2015 by PFRDA. Guaranteed monthly pension Rs 1,000-5,000 from age 60. Open to 18-40 years. 6+ crore subscribers by 2024. Complements NPS.

eco_vande_bharat_2019.label: Vande Bharat Express Trains (2019)
eco_vande_bharat_2019.stage: Modi-II: Art 370, CAA, COVID, Farm Laws
eco_vande_bharat_2019.subject: economics
eco_vande_bharat_2019.detail: Indigenous semi-high-speed trains by ICF Chennai. First Vande Bharat (Delhi-Varanasi) launched 15 February 2019 by PM Modi. Integrated Coach Factory indigenously manufactured. 160 km/h speeds. 50+ services by 2024 connecting major cities. Part of Indian Railways modernisation.

eco_nep_2020.label: National Education Policy 2020 (NEP)
eco_nep_2020.stage: Modi-II: Art 370, CAA, COVID, Farm Laws
eco_nep_2020.subject: polity
eco_nep_2020.detail: Approved by Union Cabinet 29 July 2020, replaced 1986 NEP. Structural reform 5+3+3+4 (replacing 10+2). Mother tongue instruction till Class 5. Multidisciplinary higher education with multiple entry-exit points. Target: 6% GDP public education spend. National Research Foundation. PM SHRI schools scheme.

eco_nmm_2020.label: New Labour Codes (2019-20)
eco_nmm_2020.stage: Modi-II: Art 370, CAA, COVID, Farm Laws
eco_nmm_2020.subject: economics
eco_nmm_2020.detail: Four labour codes consolidating 29 central laws: Code on Wages 2019, Industrial Relations Code 2020, Code on Social Security 2020, Occupational Safety Health and Working Conditions Code 2020. Universal minimum wage, inter-state migrants covered, gratuity portability. Implementation rules pending by states.

eco_aspirational_districts.label: Aspirational Districts Programme (2018)
eco_aspirational_districts.stage: Modi-II: Art 370, CAA, COVID, Farm Laws
eco_aspirational_districts.subject: economics
eco_aspirational_districts.detail: Launched January 2018 by NITI Aayog. 112 most underdeveloped districts identified across 28 states. Real-time monitoring of health/nutrition, education, agriculture/water, financial inclusion, skill development, basic infrastructure via Champions of Change portal. Extended to Aspirational Blocks Programme January 2023 (500 blocks).

pol_look_east_act_east.label: Look East → Act East Policy
pol_look_east_act_east.subject: polity
pol_look_east_act_east.detail: Look East Policy launched 1991 by PM Narasimha Rao to engage ASEAN + Japan + South Korea + Australia. Upgraded to Act East Policy 2014 by PM Modi — expanded to South Pacific, strategic partnerships. India-ASEAN FTA 2009 (goods), 2014 (services/investments). East Asia Summit participation.

pol_quad_2017.label: Quad (Quadrilateral Security Dialogue)
pol_quad_2017.subject: polity
pol_quad_2017.detail: India-US-Japan-Australia grouping. Originated 2007 (tsunami relief), paused 2008, revived November 2017 at ASEAN Summit. First Leaders' Summit 12 March 2021 (virtual). In-person summits 2021 DC, 2022 Tokyo, 2023 Sydney/Hiroshima, 2024 Wilmington. Focus: Indo-Pacific, supply chains, vaccines, climate, critical tech.

pol_i2u2_2022.label: I2U2 (India-Israel-UAE-USA)
pol_i2u2_2022.subject: polity
pol_i2u2_2022.detail: Minilateral grouping launched July 2022 at first Leaders' Summit. Focus: food security, water, energy, transportation, space, health, technology. UAE committed $2bn for integrated food parks in India. Pragmatic bloc bridging West Asia-South Asia.

pol_imec_2023.label: IMEC (India-Middle East-Europe Corridor, 2023)
pol_imec_2023.subject: polity
pol_imec_2023.detail: India-Middle East-Europe Economic Corridor announced at G20 Delhi Summit 9 September 2023. India-UAE-Saudi Arabia-Jordan-Israel-Greece-EU. Rail + shipping + digital/electricity cables. Counter to China's BRI. Stalled by Israel-Hamas war October 2023.

pol_doklam_standoff_2017.label: Doklam Standoff (June-August 2017)
pol_doklam_standoff_2017.subject: polity
pol_doklam_standoff_2017.detail: 73-day military standoff at Doklam plateau (Bhutan-China disputed area) near India-Bhutan-China tri-junction. Started 16 June 2017 when Indian troops blocked Chinese road construction. Ended 28 August 2017 by mutual disengagement. Largest India-China standoff since 1962 until Galwan 2020.

pol_galwan_clash_2020.label: Galwan Valley Clash (15 June 2020)
pol_galwan_clash_2020.subject: polity
pol_galwan_clash_2020.detail: Violent clash between Indian and Chinese troops in Galwan Valley, eastern Ladakh, 15-16 June 2020. First military casualties on India-China border since 1975. India lost 20 soldiers (Col Santoshi Babu), China 4+ (officially). Sparked Indian curbs on Chinese apps, FDI, PLI localisation push. Troop disengagement ongoing 2020-24 via 21+ rounds of Corps Commander talks.

pol_wuhan_summit_2018.label: Wuhan Informal Summit (April 2018)
pol_wuhan_summit_2018.subject: polity
pol_wuhan_summit_2018.detail: First informal summit between PM Modi and President Xi Jinping at Wuhan, 27-28 April 2018. Post-Doklam rapprochement. No joint statement; 'strategic guidance' exchanges on bilateral ties, border management, global issues. Paved way for Mamallapuram Summit 2019.

pol_mamallapuram_summit_2019.label: Mamallapuram/Chennai Informal Summit (October 2019)
pol_mamallapuram_summit_2019.subject: polity
pol_mamallapuram_summit_2019.detail: Second informal Modi-Xi summit at Mamallapuram (Mahabalipuram), Tamil Nadu, 11-12 October 2019. Discussed bilateral trade deficit, terrorism, India-China cultural links. Goodwill eroded by 2020 Galwan clash.

pol_operation_ganga_2022.label: Operation Ganga (Feb-March 2022)
pol_operation_ganga_2022.subject: polity
pol_operation_ganga_2022.detail: Indian evacuation mission from Ukraine during Russia-Ukraine war. Started 26 February 2022. Evacuated ~22,500 Indians (mostly medical students) via Poland/Hungary/Romania/Slovakia/Moldova. Four Union Ministers dispatched as special envoys. Naveen Shekharappa, medical student, killed in Kharkiv shelling.

pol_operation_kaveri_2023.label: Operation Kaveri (Sudan, April 2023)
pol_operation_kaveri_2023.subject: polity
pol_operation_kaveri_2023.detail: Indian evacuation from Sudan during conflict between SAF and RSF. Launched 24 April 2023. Evacuated ~4,000 Indians via Port Sudan to Jeddah, Saudi Arabia. IAF C-130 Js and Indian Navy INS Sumedha used.

pol_vaccine_maitri_2021.label: Vaccine Maitri (January 2021)
pol_vaccine_maitri_2021.subject: polity
pol_vaccine_maitri_2021.detail: India's COVID-19 vaccine diplomacy launched 20 January 2021. Supplied Covishield/Covaxin to 95+ countries — initial gifts + commercial + COVAX. Paused April 2021 due to Delta wave domestic demand; resumed Oct 2021. ~29+ crore doses exported by 2024.

pol_rafale_deal_2016.label: Rafale Deal (France, 2016)
pol_rafale_deal_2016.subject: polity
pol_rafale_deal_2016.detail: Inter-Government Agreement signed 23 September 2016 for 36 Rafale fighter jets from Dassault Aviation (France). Rs 59,000 crore. First delivery October 2019 (Ambala). All 36 delivered by December 2022. Political controversy over pricing, offsets (Rahul Gandhi's 'chowkidar chor hai'). SC cleared deal Nov 2018.

pol_s400_deal_2018.label: S-400 Triumf Deal (Russia, 2018)
pol_s400_deal_2018.subject: polity
pol_s400_deal_2018.detail: Inter-Governmental Agreement signed 5 October 2018 by Modi-Putin for 5 S-400 air defence systems from Russia. Rs 35,000 crore. First squadron delivered November 2021, three operational by 2024. Covered potential CAATSA sanctions waiver concerns.

pol_brahmos_joint.label: BrahMos Cruise Missile
pol_brahmos_joint.subject: polity
pol_brahmos_joint.detail: Indo-Russian supersonic cruise missile, joint venture DRDO + NPO Mashinostroyeniya. First launched 12 June 2001. Mach 2.8-3. Induction: Indian Navy (2005), Army (2007), Air Force (2017). Export: Philippines (2022, $375M — India's first major missile export). Range upgraded to 800 km post-MTCR entry (2016).

pol_agnipath_2022.label: Agnipath Scheme (June 2022)
pol_agnipath_2022.subject: polity
pol_agnipath_2022.detail: Short-term military recruitment scheme announced 14 June 2022. 4-year tenure for Agniveers (17.5-21 years). 25% retained permanently; 75% exit with Rs 11.7L Seva Nidhi. Triggered violent protests across North India. First batch inducted January 2023. ~50,000 recruited annually.

sci_navic_2018.label: NavIC / IRNSS (2018)
sci_navic_2018.subject: history
sci_navic_2018.detail: Navigation with Indian Constellation, regional satellite navigation system. 7-satellite constellation (IRNSS-1A to 1G). Declared operational 2018. Coverage India + 1500 km. L5 + S band. NavIC chips mandatory in smartphones from 2023 in phases. Complement to GPS.

sci_astrosat_2015.label: Astrosat (September 2015)
sci_astrosat_2015.subject: history
sci_astrosat_2015.detail: India's first dedicated multi-wavelength space observatory. Launched 28 September 2015 by PSLV-C30. 5 instruments covering UV to X-ray. Studies binary stars, AGN, galaxies. Operational beyond design life. ISRO + TIFR + IUCAA + IIA + physical research lab.

sci_nuclear_liability_2010.label: Civil Liability for Nuclear Damage Act 2010
sci_nuclear_liability_2010.subject: polity
sci_nuclear_liability_2010.detail: Enacted 22 September 2010 to operationalise Indo-US Nuclear Deal. Capped operator liability at Rs 1,500 crore; supplier liability under Section 17(b) delayed reactor imports. Indian Nuclear Insurance Pool (INIP) 2015. Ratified Convention on Supplementary Compensation 2016.

sci_kudankulam_reactors.label: Kudankulam Nuclear Power Plant
sci_kudankulam_reactors.subject: history
sci_kudankulam_reactors.detail: India-Russia civil nuclear cooperation project at Kudankulam, Tamil Nadu. Units 1-2 (1000 MW each) operational 2013 & 2016. Units 3-6 under construction (Rostatom partnership). Protests 2011-13 over safety. Plant to have 6 VVER reactors total, 6000 MW capacity — India's largest.

sci_semiconductor_mission_2021.label: India Semiconductor Mission (2021)
sci_semiconductor_mission_2021.subject: history
sci_semiconductor_mission_2021.detail: Approved by Union Cabinet 15 December 2021, launched 2022. Rs 76,000 crore outlay. Aims to build fabs (semiconductor manufacturing) + display fabs + compound semiconductors + ATMP. Major approvals: Tata Electronics (Dholera), CG Power, Micron (Sanand). Targets 2027 onwards.

sci_india_ai_mission_2024.label: IndiaAI Mission (March 2024)
sci_india_ai_mission_2024.subject: history
sci_india_ai_mission_2024.detail: Approved by Union Cabinet 7 March 2024. Rs 10,372 crore outlay. Seven pillars: Compute Capacity (10,000+ GPUs), IndiaAI Innovation Centre, Startup Financing, AI in Applications, Future Skills, IndiaAI Datasets Platform, Safe and Trusted AI. DPIIT + MeitY implementation.

sci_indian_space_policy_2023.label: Indian Space Policy 2023
sci_indian_space_policy_2023.subject: history
sci_indian_space_policy_2023.detail: Approved by Union Cabinet 6 April 2023. Opened space sector to private players (NGEs — Non-Governmental Entities). ISRO focus shifts to R&D. IN-SPACe as single-window regulator. NSIL as commercial arm. Legislation (Space Activities Bill) pending.

pol_nhm_2013.label: National Health Mission (NHM, 2013)
pol_nhm_2013.subject: polity
pol_nhm_2013.detail: Launched 2013 merging NRHM (2005) + NUHM (2013). Accessible, affordable, quality healthcare to rural and urban areas. Indicators: IMR, MMR, TFR, CHC/PHC upgrades. Sub-missions: RMNCH+A, Communicable Diseases, Non-Communicable Diseases. ~70% of central health budget.

pol_mission_indradhanush_2014.label: Mission Indradhanush (December 2014)
pol_mission_indradhanush_2014.subject: polity
pol_mission_indradhanush_2014.detail: Full immunisation coverage programme launched 25 December 2014. Targets unimmunised/partially immunised children (0-2 years) and pregnant women. Intensified (IMI) from 2017, IMI 2.0 (2019), 3.0 (2021). Raised full immunisation coverage from 62% (2014) to 87%+ (2023). 8+ vaccines in UIP.

pol_aarogya_setu_2020.label: Aarogya Setu App (April 2020)
pol_aarogya_setu_2020.subject: polity
pol_aarogya_setu_2020.detail: COVID-19 contact tracing + self-assessment mobile app launched 2 April 2020 by MyGov + NIC. Bluetooth/GPS based. 15+ crore downloads by May 2020. Linked to CoWIN for vaccine certificates. Privacy concerns addressed via Aarogya Setu Data Access and Knowledge Sharing Protocol.

pol_sonia_gandhi.label: Sonia Gandhi (Congress President 1998-2017, 2019-22)
pol_sonia_gandhi.subject: polity
pol_sonia_gandhi.detail: Italian-origin Indian politician. Widow of Rajiv Gandhi. Congress President 1998-2017 (19 years, longest ever) + 2019-22. MP Rae Bareli since 2004. Declined PM 2004. NAC chairperson. Credited with UPA-I policies (RTI, NREGA). Retreated from active politics 2022.

pol_rahul_gandhi.label: Rahul Gandhi (Congress, Leader of Opposition 2024-)
pol_rahul_gandhi.subject: polity
pol_rahul_gandhi.detail: Congress MP (Amethi 2004-19, Wayanad 2019-24, Rae Bareli 2024-). Congress President 2017-19. Led Bharat Jodo Yatra (Sept 2022 - Jan 2023, 4,000 km Kanyakumari to Srinagar). Bharat Jodo Nyay Yatra (Jan-Mar 2024). Leader of Opposition from June 2024 — first since 2014.

pol_arvind_kejriwal_aap.label: Arvind Kejriwal / Aam Aadmi Party (2012)
pol_arvind_kejriwal_aap.subject: polity
pol_arvind_kejriwal_aap.detail: Former IRS officer, RTI activist, Magsaysay 2006. Broke with Anna Hazare and founded AAP November 2012. Delhi CM (Dec 2013-Feb 2014, Feb 2015-Feb 2025). Punjab CM Bhagwant Mann. Resigned CM post after bail September 2024. Arrested in Delhi Liquor Policy case March 2024.

pol_nitish_kumar.label: Nitish Kumar (Bihar CM)
pol_nitish_kumar.subject: polity
pol_nitish_kumar.detail: Bihar CM since 2005 (multiple terms). Alliance-hopping champion — switched between NDA and Mahagathbandhan 5+ times. JD(U) leader. Known for Bihar's law-and-order revival post-Lalu era and Patna Sahib women's reservation experiments.

pol_mamata_banerjee.label: Mamata Banerjee / Trinamool Congress
pol_mamata_banerjee.subject: polity
pol_mamata_banerjee.detail: TMC founder (1998), West Bengal CM since 2011 (three terms, first woman CM of WB). Former UPA Railway Minister. 2011 wrested WB from 34-year Left rule. 2021 victory despite Modi-Shah BJP challenge. Strong federalism advocate.

pol_naveen_patnaik.label: Naveen Patnaik (Odisha CM 2000-2024)
pol_naveen_patnaik.subject: polity
pol_naveen_patnaik.detail: BJD founder (1997), Odisha CM 5 March 2000 - 11 June 2024 (24 years — one of longest-serving). Lost 2024 to BJP (first BJP majority in Odisha). Cyclone response (Phailin 2013, Fani 2019, Amphan 2020). KALIA scheme, Odisha Millets Mission.

pol_yogi_adityanath.label: Yogi Adityanath (UP CM 2017-)
pol_yogi_adityanath.subject: polity
pol_yogi_adityanath.detail: BJP leader, Gorakhnath Math Mahant. Gorakhpur MP 1998-2017. Uttar Pradesh CM from 19 March 2017 (two terms). Flagship: law-and-order 'bulldozer raj', anti-Romeo squads, Purvanchal Expressway, Ram Mandir consecration.

pol_mayawati.label: Mayawati (UP CM 1995, 1997, 2002-03, 2007-12)
pol_mayawati.subject: polity
pol_mayawati.detail: Dalit politician, BSP President since 2003 (Kanshi Ram's successor). UP CM 4 times — 1995 (4 months), 1997 (6 months), 2002-03 (1 year), full 2007-12 (first BSP majority). Declined post-2017. Advocated Bahujan politics — SC/ST+OBC+Muslim coalition.

pol_mk_stalin.label: M.K. Stalin (Tamil Nadu CM 2021-)
pol_mk_stalin.stage: Modi-II: Art 370, CAA, COVID, Farm Laws
pol_mk_stalin.subject: polity
pol_mk_stalin.detail: DMK President since 2018, Tamil Nadu CM from 7 May 2021. Son of M. Karunanidhi. Longtime Chennai Mayor (1996-2002). Led DMK's 2024 Lok Sabha INDIA bloc in TN (winning 22/39). Advocated fiscal federalism, opposed delimitation based on population.

pol_maratha_reservation_case_2021.label: Jaishri Laxmanrao Patil v. CoM Maharashtra (Maratha Reservation, 2021)
pol_maratha_reservation_case_2021.subject: polity
pol_maratha_reservation_case_2021.detail: 5-judge SC bench, 5 May 2021. Struck down Maharashtra's 16% Maratha reservation (SEBC Act 2018) as violative of Indra Sawhney 50% ceiling. Held 102nd Amendment deprived states of power to identify SEBCs — overturned by 105th Amendment (August 2021). Landmark on state power over OBC list.

pol_anoop_baranwal_2023.label: Anoop Baranwal v. UOI (CEC Appointment, 2023)
pol_anoop_baranwal_2023.subject: polity
pol_anoop_baranwal_2023.detail: 5-judge SC Constitution Bench, 2 March 2023. Ruled CEC/EC appointments must be by committee of PM + LoP + CJI until Parliament legislates. Parliament enacted CEC and Other Election Commissioners Act 2023 to replace CJI with a Union Minister — controversial as diluting SC's intent.

pol_marriage_equality_case_2023.label: Supriyo v. UOI (Marriage Equality, 2023)
pol_marriage_equality_case_2023.subject: polity
pol_marriage_equality_case_2023.detail: 5-judge SC bench, 17 October 2023. Unanimous refusal to grant legal recognition to same-sex marriages (3-2 on civil union). Held marriage falls within legislative domain, not judicial. Recommended committee for entitlements/benefits. Setback for LGBTQ+ marriage rights post-Navtej 2018.

pol_bilkis_bano_case_2024.label: Bilkis Bano Case (Convict Release 2022 → SC reversal 2024)
pol_bilkis_bano_case_2024.subject: polity
pol_bilkis_bano_case_2024.detail: 11 convicts (2002 Gujarat riots rape-murder of Bilkis Bano + her family) released by Gujarat government August 2022 under 1992 remission policy. SC bench (Justice Nagarathna) on 8 January 2024 quashed remission as illegal — Maharashtra (trial state) had jurisdiction, not Gujarat. Convicts returned to prison.

pol_vishaka_guidelines_1997.label: Vishaka Guidelines 1997 → POSH Act 2013
pol_vishaka_guidelines_1997.subject: polity
pol_vishaka_guidelines_1997.detail: 12-point guidelines by Supreme Court in Vishaka v. Rajasthan (August 1997) for preventing sexual harassment at workplace — borrowing from CEDAW. Internal Complaints Committees. Codified into Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act 2013 (POSH).

pol_subhash_chandra_agrawal_2009.label: Subhash Chandra Agrawal v. CPIO (2009)
pol_subhash_chandra_agrawal_2009.subject: polity
pol_subhash_chandra_agrawal_2009.detail: Delhi HC ruled CJI's office falls under RTI Act 2005. Upheld 2019 by SC 5-judge bench. Required disclosure of judges' asset declarations. Strengthened judicial transparency while preserving collegium deliberation privilege.

pol_women_permanent_commission_2020.label: Women Army Officers Permanent Commission (2020)
pol_women_permanent_commission_2020.subject: polity
pol_women_permanent_commission_2020.detail: SC bench, 17 February 2020 (Babita Puniya case). Granted permanent commission to women officers in 10 Army cadres (earlier only Short Service Commission up to 14 years). Similar rulings for Navy (Feb 2020), Air Force follow-on. Ended decades-long gender discrimination in military career progression.

eco_fc_14th.label: 14th Finance Commission (Y.V. Reddy, 2015-20)
eco_fc_14th.subject: economics
eco_fc_14th.detail: Chaired by former RBI Governor Y.V. Reddy. Report submitted December 2014 for 2015-20. Raised states' share of central tax pool from 32% to 42% — biggest devolution increase ever. New horizontal distribution formula (population 2011, income distance, forest cover, demographic change, area).

eco_fc_15th.label: 15th Finance Commission (N.K. Singh, 2020-26)
eco_fc_15th.stage: Modi-II: Art 370, CAA, COVID, Farm Laws
eco_fc_15th.subject: economics
eco_fc_15th.detail: Chaired by N.K. Singh. Two reports — 2020-21 (one year), 2021-26 (five years). States' share kept at 41% (1% withdrawn for new UTs J&K/Ladakh). New weights — demographic performance (12.5%) + tax effort (2.5%) introduced. Health grants. Revenue deficit grants.

eco_fc_16th.label: 16th Finance Commission (Arvind Panagariya, 2026-31)
eco_fc_16th.subject: economics
eco_fc_16th.detail: Chaired by Arvind Panagariya (former NITI Aayog VC), constituted 31 December 2023. Report due 31 October 2025 for period 1 April 2026 - 31 March 2031. Key issues: demographic shifts, revenue-raising capacity, cess/surcharge controversy, GST compensation expiry.

env_forest_conservation_amend_2023.label: Forest (Conservation) Amendment Act 2023
env_forest_conservation_amend_2023.subject: polity
env_forest_conservation_amend_2023.detail: Passed 2023, renamed Van (Sanrakshan Evam Samvardhan) Adhiniyam. Exempted forest land within 100 km of LAC/LoC from prior approval for strategic projects. Exempted land up to 10 hectares for linear projects, 5 hectares for security. Controversial dilution of Forest Conservation Act 1980 scope.

env_wildlife_amend_2022.label: Wildlife (Protection) Amendment Act 2022
env_wildlife_amend_2022.subject: polity
env_wildlife_amend_2022.detail: Passed December 2022. Rationalised WPA 1972 schedules from 6 to 4. Enhanced CITES compliance (new schedule for CITES species). Standing Committee of NBWL. Stricter penalties. Notable: vermin declaration power retained with states.

env_single_use_plastic_ban_2022.label: Single-Use Plastic Ban (1 July 2022)
env_single_use_plastic_ban_2022.subject: polity
env_single_use_plastic_ban_2022.detail: Ban on manufacture, import, stocking, distribution, sale, use of 19 single-use plastic items from 1 July 2022 under Plastic Waste Management Amendment Rules 2021. Includes straws, cutlery, earbuds, ice-cream sticks, balloon sticks, wrapping films. Carry bags <120 microns banned from 31 Dec 2022.

env_green_bonds_2023.label: Sovereign Green Bonds (2023)
env_green_bonds_2023.subject: economics
env_green_bonds_2023.detail: India's first Sovereign Green Bonds issued 25 January and 9 February 2023. Rs 16,000 crore raised (both tranches). 5-year and 10-year tenors. Proceeds for renewable energy, energy efficiency, clean transportation, sustainable water management. Listed on BSE/NSE; FPI access permitted.

eco_gift_city_ifsca.label: GIFT City + IFSCA (2019)
eco_gift_city_ifsca.stage: Modi-II: Art 370, CAA, COVID, Farm Laws
eco_gift_city_ifsca.subject: economics
eco_gift_city_ifsca.detail: Gujarat International Finance Tec-City (GIFT City), India's first IFSC (International Financial Services Centre) in Gandhinagar. Operationalised 2015. IFSCA (International Financial Services Centres Authority) established 2019 as unified regulator. Aircraft leasing, bullion exchange, GIFT Nifty futures.

eco_narcl_2021.label: National Asset Reconstruction Company (NARCL, 2021)
eco_narcl_2021.stage: Modi-II: Art 370, CAA, COVID, Farm Laws
eco_narcl_2021.subject: economics
eco_narcl_2021.detail: 'Bad Bank' launched 2021. PSBs' ARC to aggregate stressed assets >Rs 500 crore. NARCL + IDRCL (management) model. Rs 50,335 crore first tranche approved September 2021. Took over Srei Infra, Future Retail, Jaypee Infratech debts.

eco_crypto_tax_2022.label: Crypto / VDA Tax Regime (2022)
eco_crypto_tax_2022.stage: Modi-II: Art 370, CAA, COVID, Farm Laws
eco_crypto_tax_2022.subject: economics
eco_crypto_tax_2022.detail: Budget 2022-23 introduced 30% flat tax on Virtual Digital Assets (crypto, NFTs) + 1% TDS (from 1 July 2022). No set-off against losses. Digital Rupee (CBDC) pilot launched November 2022 (wholesale) + December 2022 (retail). Registered with FIU-IND for AML compliance 2024.

eco_air_india_privatisation_2022.label: Air India Privatisation (2022)
eco_air_india_privatisation_2022.stage: Modi-II: Art 370, CAA, COVID, Farm Laws
eco_air_india_privatisation_2022.subject: economics
eco_air_india_privatisation_2022.detail: Tata Group acquired Air India for Rs 18,000 crore, officially handed over 27 January 2022. First major PSU privatisation by Modi government. Tata regained airline it founded in 1932 and government nationalised 1953. Merged with Vistara (Feb 2025) to create consolidated Tata airline group.

eco_vivad_se_vishwas_2020.label: Vivad Se Vishwas Scheme 2020
eco_vivad_se_vishwas_2020.stage: Modi-II: Art 370, CAA, COVID, Farm Laws
eco_vivad_se_vishwas_2020.subject: economics
eco_vivad_se_vishwas_2020.detail: Direct tax dispute resolution scheme, operational March 2020 - October 2021. Settle pending IT appeals by paying disputed tax (with waiver of interest, penalty, prosecution). Rs 99,756 crore collected from 1.46 lakh cases. Vivad Se Vishwas 2024 relaunched for pending disputes as of 22 July 2024.

pol_russia_ukraine_war_2022.label: Russia-Ukraine War (Feb 2022-)
pol_russia_ukraine_war_2022.stage: Parallel — Recent World (Arab Spring → Trump → Russia-Ukraine → Israel-Hamas)
pol_russia_ukraine_war_2022.subject: polity
pol_russia_ukraine_war_2022.detail: Russian invasion of Ukraine began 24 February 2022. India abstained at UNGA/UNSC resolutions condemning Russia. Refined Russian oil imports rose from 2% to 40%+ of imports. Grain Initiative through Turkey/UN. Over 1 lakh Indian casualties evacuated via Operation Ganga.

pol_israel_hamas_war_2023.label: Israel-Hamas War (October 2023-)
pol_israel_hamas_war_2023.stage: Parallel — Recent World (Arab Spring → Trump → Russia-Ukraine → Israel-Hamas)
pol_israel_hamas_war_2023.subject: polity
pol_israel_hamas_war_2023.detail: Hamas attack on Israel 7 October 2023 (1,200 killed, 240 hostages). Israel's Gaza offensive killed 40,000+ Palestinians by 2024. India condemned Hamas attack (first country to do so) + backed two-state solution. Complicated IMEC corridor progress. Gaza ceasefire January 2025.

pol_trump_1_president.label: Donald Trump Presidency-I (2017-21)
pol_trump_1_president.stage: Parallel — Recent World (Arab Spring → Trump → Russia-Ukraine → Israel-Hamas)
pol_trump_1_president.subject: polity
pol_trump_1_president.detail: 45th US President, 20 January 2017 - 20 January 2021. 'Howdy Modi' Houston Sept 2019. 'Namaste Trump' Ahmedabad Feb 2020. Trade tensions (GSP withdrawal 2019). Abraham Accords 2020. Withdrew from Paris Agreement, Iran Deal, TPP. Lost 2020 to Biden. Re-elected 2024 for second term.

pol_trump_2_2025.label: Trump Presidency-II (January 2025-)
pol_trump_2_2025.stage: Parallel — Recent World (Arab Spring → Trump → Russia-Ukraine → Israel-Hamas)
pol_trump_2_2025.subject: polity
pol_trump_2_2025.detail: 47th US President, inaugurated 20 January 2025. Tariff wars — 'Liberation Day' global tariffs April 2025 (India 26%). Withdrew from Paris Agreement, WHO again. Executive orders on immigration, federal workforce, AI. Modi visited Washington February 2025.

pol_arab_spring_2010.label: Arab Spring (2010-12)
pol_arab_spring_2010.stage: Parallel — Recent World (Arab Spring → Trump → Russia-Ukraine → Israel-Hamas)
pol_arab_spring_2010.subject: polity
pol_arab_spring_2010.detail: Revolutionary wave starting Tunisia December 2010 (Mohamed Bouazizi self-immolation). Egypt Tahrir Square 2011 (Mubarak fall); Libya (Gaddafi killed Oct 2011); Yemen; Syria civil war. India evacuated citizens from Libya, Egypt, Syria. Led to ISIS emergence.

pol_syrian_civil_war.label: Syrian Civil War (2011-24)
pol_syrian_civil_war.stage: Parallel — Recent World (Arab Spring → Trump → Russia-Ukraine → Israel-Hamas)
pol_syrian_civil_war.subject: polity
pol_syrian_civil_war.detail: Begin 2011 as Arab Spring uprising against Bashar al-Assad. ~500,000 killed, millions displaced. Russian intervention 2015 saved Assad. ISIS rose & fell (2014-19). Assad fell 8 December 2024 after HTS offensive — regime fled to Russia. Fragmented Syria 2025.

pol_isis_rise_fall.label: ISIS / Islamic State (2014-19)
pol_isis_rise_fall.stage: Parallel — Recent World (Arab Spring → Trump → Russia-Ukraine → Israel-Hamas)
pol_isis_rise_fall.subject: polity
pol_isis_rise_fall.detail: Declared caliphate 29 June 2014 under Abu Bakr al-Baghdadi. Controlled parts of Syria/Iraq incl. Mosul, Raqqa. Peak 2014-15. Territorial defeat March 2019 (Baghuz). Baghdadi killed Oct 2019. Ongoing insurgency in Syria/Iraq. ISKP (Khorasan) active in Afghanistan post-2021.

pol_brexit_2020.label: Brexit — UK leaves EU (31 January 2020)
pol_brexit_2020.stage: Parallel — Recent World (Arab Spring → Trump → Russia-Ukraine → Israel-Hamas)
pol_brexit_2020.subject: polity
pol_brexit_2020.detail: 2016 referendum (51.9% Leave). UK formally left EU 31 January 2020 after 47 years membership (joined EEC 1973). Transition period ended 31 December 2020 under Brexit deal. Triggered India-UK FTA negotiations (ongoing 2024-25).

pol_sri_lanka_crisis_2022.label: Sri Lanka Economic Crisis (2022)
pol_sri_lanka_crisis_2022.stage: Parallel — Recent World (Arab Spring → Trump → Russia-Ukraine → Israel-Hamas)
pol_sri_lanka_crisis_2022.subject: polity
pol_sri_lanka_crisis_2022.detail: Forex collapse April 2022, sovereign default May 2022 (first in SL history). Protests forced President Rajapaksa to flee July 2022. India's $4 bn financial assistance via credit lines, currency swap. IMF bailout $2.9 bn March 2023. Ranil Wickremesinghe → Anura Kumara Dissanayake (Sept 2024).

pol_new_states_2000.label: Three New States (November 2000)
pol_new_states_2000.subject: polity
pol_new_states_2000.detail: Chhattisgarh (carved from Madhya Pradesh, 1 November 2000), Uttarakhand (then Uttaranchal, carved from UP, 9 November 2000), Jharkhand (carved from Bihar, 15 November 2000). Tribal/regional demands. 27th, 28th, 29th states respectively. Increased total states to 28.

pol_telangana_formation_2014.label: Telangana Formation (2 June 2014)
pol_telangana_formation_2014.subject: polity
pol_telangana_formation_2014.detail: 29th state of India carved from Andhra Pradesh on 2 June 2014. Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act 2014. Led by TRS (now BRS) under K. Chandrashekar Rao. Movement since 1969 (Jai Telangana). Hyderabad as joint capital for 10 years (till 2024). First CM: KCR. Congress won assembly elections Dec 2023 (Revanth Reddy).

pol_jk_reorganisation_2019.label: J&K Reorganisation Act 2019
pol_jk_reorganisation_2019.stage: Modi-II: Art 370, CAA, COVID, Farm Laws
pol_jk_reorganisation_2019.subject: polity
pol_jk_reorganisation_2019.detail: J&K Reorganisation Act 2019, effective 31 October 2019. Bifurcated J&K state into UT of Jammu & Kashmir (with legislature) and UT of Ladakh (without legislature). First instance of a state downgraded to UT. Upheld by SC December 2023. Elections held September-October 2024.

pol_punchhi_commission_2010.label: Punchhi Commission (2007-10)
pol_punchhi_commission_2010.subject: polity
pol_punchhi_commission_2010.detail: Second Commission on Centre-State Relations, set up April 2007 under former CJI M.M. Punchhi. Submitted 7-volume report March 2010. 310 recommendations — Art 356 use, Inter-State Council, grants-in-aid, AIS, communal violence, environment clearances. Partially implemented.

pol_verma_committee_2013.label: Justice Verma Committee (January 2013)
pol_verma_committee_2013.subject: polity
pol_verma_committee_2013.detail: Three-member committee chaired by former CJI J.S. Verma, constituted 23 December 2012 after Nirbhaya case. Report 23 January 2013. Recommended enhanced penalties for rape/sexual assault, new offences (acid attack, voyeurism, stalking), explicit recognition of marital rape exemption issue. Led to Criminal Law (Amendment) Act 2013.

pol_transgender_act_2019.label: Transgender Persons Act 2019
pol_transgender_act_2019.subject: polity
pol_transgender_act_2019.detail: Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act 2019, notified 10 January 2020. Self-identification principle (post-NALSA 2014 SC). National Council for Transgender Persons. Criminalises bonded labour, exclusion, denial of services. Criticised for mandatory district magistrate certificate.

pol_nalsa_2014.label: NALSA v. UOI (Third Gender, 2014)
pol_nalsa_2014.subject: polity
pol_nalsa_2014.detail: 2-judge SC bench, 15 April 2014. Recognised transgender as 'third gender' under Article 14, 15, 16, 21. Right to self-identify. OBC reservation entitlement. Government obligations — social welfare, health, legal recognition. Basis for Transgender Persons Act 2019.

cul_cricket_wc_2011.label: ICC Cricket World Cup 2011
cul_cricket_wc_2011.subject: history
cul_cricket_wc_2011.detail: India won Cricket World Cup 2 April 2011 at Wankhede Stadium beating Sri Lanka. Captain M.S. Dhoni's six to win. Indian hosts (joint with Sri Lanka, Bangladesh). Tendulkar's last WC. Gautam Gambhir 97, Dhoni 91 in final. India's first WC since 1983.

cul_olympics_india_era11.label: India at Olympics (1996-2024)
cul_olympics_india_era11.subject: history
cul_olympics_india_era11.detail: Medal count era 11: Leander Paes tennis bronze Atlanta 1996; Karnam Malleswari weightlifting bronze Sydney 2000 (first Indian woman medalist); Rajyavardhan Rathore shooting silver Athens 2004; Abhinav Bindra shooting gold Beijing 2008 (first individual gold). Peak London 2012 (6 medals), Rio 2016 (2), Tokyo 2020 (7 — Neeraj Chopra javelin gold), Paris 2024 (6).

cul_neeraj_chopra_2021.label: Neeraj Chopra Javelin Gold (Tokyo Olympics 2021)
cul_neeraj_chopra_2021.subject: history
cul_neeraj_chopra_2021.detail: First Indian athletics Olympic gold medal, won 7 August 2021 at Tokyo 2020 Olympics (held 2021). 87.58m throw. Silver at World Championships 2022, Gold 2023. Padma Shri 2022. Paris 2024 silver.

cul_bharat_ratna_era11.label: Bharat Ratna Recipients (era 11)
cul_bharat_ratna_era11.subject: history
cul_bharat_ratna_era11.detail: Era 11 Bharat Ratna recipients: A.P.J. Abdul Kalam 1997, Satyajit Ray 1992, Aruna Asaf Ali 1997, Lata Mangeshkar 2001, Bismillah Khan 2001, Bhimsen Joshi 2008, C.N.R. Rao 2014, Sachin Tendulkar 2014 (youngest), Pandit Madan Mohan Malaviya 2015 (posthumous), Atal Bihari Vajpayee 2015, Pranab Mukherjee 2019, Nanaji Deshmukh 2019, Bhupen Hazarika 2019, Karpoori Thakur 2024, L.K. Advani 2024, Narasimha Rao 2024, Chaudhary Charan Singh 2024, M.S. Swaminathan 2024.

cul_amartya_sen_1998.label: Amartya Sen Nobel Economics (1998)
cul_amartya_sen_1998.subject: history
cul_amartya_sen_1998.detail: First Asian to win Nobel Prize in Economic Sciences, awarded October 1998 for work on welfare economics, social choice theory, poverty/famine, human development. Bharat Ratna 1999. Master of Trinity College Cambridge 1998-2004. Harvard Professor. HDI architect with Mahbub ul Haq.

cul_satyarthi_2014.label: Kailash Satyarthi Nobel Peace (2014)
cul_satyarthi_2014.subject: history
cul_satyarthi_2014.detail: Indian children's rights activist, shared 2014 Nobel Peace Prize with Malala Yousafzai. Founded Bachpan Bachao Andolan (1980). Global March Against Child Labour 1998. Rescued 91,000+ children from bonded labour, trafficking. Advocate for education rights.

cul_banerjee_duflo_2019.label: Abhijit Banerjee Nobel Economics (2019)
cul_banerjee_duflo_2019.subject: history
cul_banerjee_duflo_2019.detail: Shared 2019 Nobel Economics with Esther Duflo (wife) and Michael Kremer for 'experimental approach to alleviating global poverty' (RCTs in development economics). Kolkata-born, MIT Ford Foundation Professor. Co-founded J-PAL.

pol_indian_political_parties_era11.label: Key Political Parties Era 11
pol_indian_political_parties_era11.subject: polity
pol_indian_political_parties_era11.detail: INC, BJP (1980), BSP (1984), SP (1992), TMC (1998), AIADMK, DMK, NCP (1999), RJD (1997), JD(U) (2003), JD(S), SS-UBT and Shiv Sena (split 2022), Biju Janata Dal BJD (1997), TRS→BRS (2001→2022), AIMIM, AAP (2012), TDP, YSRCP (2011), SS, CPM, CPI, NC, PDP, Akali Dal, IUML, RSP, KCM, Apna Dal, AIUDF, Lok Janshakti LJP.

pol_cag_vinod_rai.label: Vinod Rai CAG Reports (2008-13)
pol_cag_vinod_rai.subject: polity
pol_cag_vinod_rai.detail: CAG (2008-2013). Exposed 2G spectrum scam (Rs 1.76 lakh crore presumptive loss, Nov 2010) + Coalgate (Rs 1.86 lakh crore, Aug 2012) + Commonwealth Games audit. Triggered UPA-II credibility crisis. Post-retirement: BCCI COA chair.

pol_covid_delta_wave_2021.label: COVID-19 Delta Wave (April-June 2021)
pol_covid_delta_wave_2021.subject: polity
pol_covid_delta_wave_2021.detail: Catastrophic second wave April-June 2021 driven by Delta (B.1.617.2) variant. Daily cases peaked 400,000+ (7 May 2021). Oxygen shortage, crematorium queues, Ganga bodies. Estimated 3-5 million excess deaths (WHO). Kumbh Mela + WB elections super-spreaders. Vaccine push accelerated.

period_s30.label: Recent World (2010-2026)
period_s30.stage: Parallel — Recent World (Arab Spring → Trump → Russia-Ukraine → Israel-Hamas)
period_s30.subject: history
period_s30.detail: Major global currents bridging India's Modi era. Arab Spring (2010-12) → Egypt/Libya/Tunisia/Yemen regime change → Syrian Civil War + ISIS rise (2014, fall 2019). Snowden leaks 2013. Brexit referendum 2016, UK leaves EU 31 Jan 2020. Trump-I (2017-21) — Howdy Modi, Namaste Trump, Abraham Accords. COVID-19 reshapes geopolitics 2020. Russia invades Ukraine 24 Feb 2022 — energy crisis, food crisis. Sri Lanka collapse April 2022. Israel-Hamas war from 7 Oct 2023. Trump-II re-elected Nov 2024 (inaugurated Jan 2025) — global tariffs.

gap_kalaripayattu.label: Kalaripayattu
gap_kalaripayattu.subject: history
gap_kalaripayattu.detail: Kerala martial art, traditionally dated to ~4th c. AD; Malayalam 'kalari' means training hall/gymnasium. Legend attributes origin to sage Parasurama. Emphasises footwork, kicks, strikes, armed and unarmed combat; no drumming/song. Popularly (and dubiously) credited via the Bodhidharma legend with seeding East Asian martial arts. Banned during British rule, revived post-independence. Practised mainly in Kerala and northern Malabar.

gap_fanam.label: Fanam (South Indian gold coin)
gap_fanam.subject: history
gap_fanam.detail: Small-denomination gold coin of medieval South India. In the Vijayanagara monetary system, gold fanams were fractional units sitting below the pagoda (the higher-denomination gold coin with a running-warrior figure); silver taras and copper coins handled smaller transactions. The term persisted into colonial-era South Indian coinage.

gap_champaka_chamba.label: Champaka = Chamba
gap_champaka_chamba.subject: history
gap_champaka_chamba.detail: Champaka is the Sanskrit / ancient name for the medieval Himalayan hill kingdom of Chamba in the NORTH-WEST (present-day Himachal Pradesh) — NOT Central India, which is the distractor pairing. Founded 10th c. by Raja Sahil Varman; survived as a princely state into the colonial era. Commonly listed alongside Durgara (Jammu), Kuluta (Kullu), Trigarta (Kangra).

gap_durgara_jammu.label: Durgara = Jammu
gap_durgara_jammu.subject: history
gap_durgara_jammu.detail: Durgara (also Dugar) is the Sanskrit/ancient name for the Jammu region in the western Himalayas. The Dogra dynasty took its name from this root. A medieval hill principality on the outer Himalayan range between the Ravi and Chenab. The PYQ pairing Durgara = Jammu is the ONLY correct match among its set.

gap_kuluta_kullu.label: Kuluta = Kullu
gap_kuluta_kullu.subject: history
gap_kuluta_kullu.detail: Kuluta is the Sanskrit/ancient name for the Kullu valley kingdom on the upper Beas (present-day Himachal Pradesh) — NOT Malabar, which is the distractor. A medieval Himalayan hill principality in the NW. The later Kangra school of painting extended to Kullu, Chamba, and Mandi as daughter ateliers.

gap_vijnanesvara.label: Vijnaneshvara (Mitakshara jurist)
gap_vijnanesvara.subject: history
gap_vijnanesvara.detail: 11-12c Dharmashastra commentator at the court of the Western Chalukya king Vikramaditya VI. Author of the Mitakshara, a commentary on the Yajnavalkya Smriti that became the authoritative text of Hindu law across most of India outside Bengal. The Mitakshara school governs inheritance outside Bengal; Dayabhaga (Jimutavahana) governs Bengal and Assam.

gap_hemadri.label: Hemadri (Chaturvarga Chintamani)
gap_hemadri.subject: history
gap_hemadri.detail: 13c polymath and minister under the Yadava rulers Mahadeva and Ramachandra of Devagiri. Author of the Chaturvarga Chintamani, an encyclopedic Dharmashastra digest in four sections (Vrata, Dana, Tirtha, Moksha). Also associated with the Hemadpanti style of stone temple architecture widespread in Maharashtra.

gap_jimutavahana.label: Jimutavahana (Dayabhaga jurist)
gap_jimutavahana.subject: history
gap_jimutavahana.detail: 12c Bengal Dharmashastra jurist; author of the Dayabhaga (a digest of inheritance law that became the Hindu-law authority in Bengal and Assam; contrast with the Mitakshara of Vijnaneshvara followed elsewhere) and the Vyavaharamatrika (procedural law). Distinct from — though name-sharing with — the Bodhisattva prince Jimutavahana of Harsha's Sanskrit play Nagananda.

gap_rajasekhara_poet.label: Rajasekhara (poet, Kavyamimamsa)
gap_rajasekhara_poet.subject: history
gap_rajasekhara_poet.detail: 9-10c Sanskrit court poet under the Pratihara rulers Mahendrapala I and Mahipala I. Author of the Kavyamimamsa (treatise on poetics), Karpuramanjari (Prakrit play), Balaramayana, and Viddhasalabhanjika. NOT a jurist — commonly the trap option in PYQs that list medieval jurists (e.g., PYQ #307), where 3 of 4 names are Dharmashastra authorities and Rajasekhara is the literary/poetician outlier.

gap_bilhana.label: Bilhana (Vikramankadevacharita)
gap_bilhana.subject: history
gap_bilhana.detail: 11-12c Kashmiri Shaiva Sanskrit poet who migrated south and became court poet of the Western Chalukya king Vikramaditya VI (Kalyani Chalukyas, r. 1076-1127). His best-known work, the Vikramankadevacharita, is a Sanskrit mahakavya biography of his patron. Also wrote Karnasundari (drama) and Chaurapanchashika (love lyrics). Commonly paired with Sandhyakara Nandi (Ramacharita, Pala-era Ramapala) in 11-12c biographical literature.

gap_devichandragupta.label: Devichandragupta (Vishakhadatta)
gap_devichandragupta.subject: history
gap_devichandragupta.detail: Fragmentary Sanskrit drama by Vishakhadatta (~late Gupta, ~5-6c CE, though some place him as late as 9c). Depicts the ignominious episode where Gupta king Ramagupta agreed to surrender his queen Dhruvadevi to a Saka chief, and his brother Chandragupta II disguised himself, killed the Saka, and eventually replaced Ramagupta. The text is lost — only extracts survive in later commentaries. Vishakhadatta's other major play is the Mudrarakshasa (Chandragupta Maurya / Chanakya / Nanda-overthrow). Attributing Devichandragupta to Bilhana (as PYQ #179 tests) is wrong.

gap_mahasanghika.label: Mahasanghika school
gap_mahasanghika.subject: history
gap_mahasanghika.detail: 'Great Assembly' school of early Buddhism that split from the Sthaviravadins (~4c BCE, traditionally associated with or following the Second Buddhist Council at Vaishali) over questions of monastic discipline and the nature of the arhat. Later subdivided further (Lokottaravada, Ekavyavaharika, etc.). The Mahasanghikas' doctrinal tendency to emphasize the Buddha's supramundane (lokottara) nature is seen as a precursor to Mahayana. Their patronage of stupa-centred worship in coastal Andhra (Dhanyakataka/Amaravati, Nagarjunakonda) is strongly attested archaeologically.

gap_patanjali_mahabhashya.label: Patanjali / Mahabhashya
gap_patanjali_mahabhashya.subject: history
gap_patanjali_mahabhashya.detail: 2c BCE Sanskrit grammarian and author of the Mahabhashya ('Great Commentary') on Panini's Ashtadhyayi. Contemporary of the post-Maurya Shunga king Pushyamitra Shunga — the Mahabhashya references Pushyamitra's horse sacrifices and also mentions the Mauryas and the assembly of Chandragupta (but notably does NOT reference Kautilya by name, a fact used in debates over Arthashastra's authorship). Distinct from Panini (5-4c BCE, pre-Mauryan) — PYQ #183 tests the common confusion that Panini (not Patanjali) was contemporary of Pushyamitra, which is incorrect.

gap_shramanic_anti_vedic.label: Shramanic anti-Vedic stance (Buddhism + Jainism)
gap_shramanic_anti_vedic.subject: history
gap_shramanic_anti_vedic.detail: Core doctrinal common ground between Buddhism and Jainism as shramana traditions: (1) rejection of the authority of the Vedas, (2) denial of efficacy of Vedic sacrificial ritual (yajna) as a path to liberation, (3) challenge to the Brahmanical ritual order and caste-grounded access to salvation. BOTH Buddhism and Jainism are anti-Vedic in these ways. They DIFFER on extremity of penance: Jainism embraces severe asceticism; Buddhism explicitly rejects it via the Middle Path — so 'avoidance of extremities of penance' is NOT common to both (PYQ #227/#239 trap).

gap_acaranga_sutra.label: Acharanga Sutra (1st Anga)
gap_acaranga_sutra.subject: history
gap_acaranga_sutra.detail: First of the 12 Angas — the core canonical texts of the Shvetambara Jain canon in Ardha-Magadhi Prakrit. Describes Mahavira's parents as followers of Parshvanatha (pointing to a Jain pre-history of Parshvanatha's community) and contains foundational monastic conduct rules for Jain ascetics. Distinct from the later chhedasutras (disciplinary texts like Brihatkalpasutra).

gap_brihatkalpasutra.label: Brihatkalpasutra (chhedasutra)
gap_brihatkalpasutra.subject: history
gap_brihatkalpasutra.detail: A chhedasutra (disciplinary text) in the Shvetambara Jain canon — chhedasutras handle rules of monastic conduct, expiation, and internal jurisprudence. Along with Nishitha, Dashashrutaskandha, and others, forms the disciplinary corpus distinct from the Angas (Acaranga, Sutrakritanga, etc.) which deal with doctrine. Being Jain literature disqualifies it from the 'not Jain' answer in PYQ #238 (where Therigatha — a Buddhist Theri text — is the correct odd-one-out).

gap_bhaskara_i.label: Bhaskara I (7c Aryabhata commentator)
gap_bhaskara_i.subject: history
gap_bhaskara_i.detail: 7c CE Indian mathematician-astronomer; first significant commentator on Aryabhata's Aryabhatiya (his Aryabhatiyabhasya, c. 629 CE, is the earliest known prose commentary). Also composed the Mahabhaskariya and Laghubhaskariya. One of the earliest texts to use a positional decimal numeral system with word-numerals in Sanskrit. Distinct from Bhaskara II (12c, Lilavati, Bijaganita) and from the inventor of zero (which PYQ #65 correctly leaves 'an unknown Indian' — zero as a concept and symbol evolved over centuries rather than being invented by a single named figure; Brahmagupta in 628 CE gave it formal arithmetic treatment).

gap_brahmagupta.label: Brahmagupta (Brahmasphutasiddhanta 628 CE)
gap_brahmagupta.subject: history
gap_brahmagupta.detail: 7c CE mathematician-astronomer from Bhinmal (Rajasthan). Composed the Brahmasphutasiddhanta in 628 CE — one of the earliest texts to give zero full arithmetic treatment (as a number, with rules for addition/subtraction/multiplication; though division by zero he got wrong), and to use negative numbers systematically. Also wrote the Khandakhadyaka. Field: astronomy and mathematics (NOT drama, medicine — PYQ #63 match-list).

gap_ashtadikgaja_cosmology.label: Ashtadikgaja (eight directional elephants)
gap_ashtadikgaja_cosmology.subject: history
gap_ashtadikgaja_cosmology.detail: Hindu cosmological concept: the eight elephants that support the eight cardinal and inter-cardinal directions (dikpalas' mounts/guardian elephants). Appears as a DISTRACTOR in PYQ #123 on merchant corporations (correct answer: Manigrama). NOT to be confused with 'ashtadiggajas' — the eight literary luminaries at the court of Vijayanagara king Krishnadeva Raya (most famous: Allasani Peddana), which is a completely different usage of the same root.

gap_anuvrata_mahavrata.label: Anuvrata vs Mahavrata (Jain vows)
gap_anuvrata_mahavrata.subject: history
gap_anuvrata_mahavrata.detail: Two-tier Jain ethical vow system. Mahavrata (five great vows) — for monks and nuns: ahimsa (non-injury), satya (truth), asteya (non-stealing), brahmacharya (celibacy), aparigraha (non-possession). Anuvrata (five lesser/partial vows) — for lay followers (shravakas): the same five, observed in attenuated form (e.g., non-injury to mobile beings only, not all life). The triratna (right faith, right knowledge, right conduct) is the overarching framework. Anuvrata is distinctively Jain — NOT Buddhist (PYQ #244 distractor).

gap_ajanta_waghora.label: Ajanta caves — Waghora river gorge
gap_ajanta_waghora.subject: history
gap_ajanta_waghora.detail: The ~30 Ajanta rock-cut Buddhist caves are carved into the U-shaped gorge of the WAGHORA (Waghur) river — a tributary of the Tapi — near Aurangabad, Maharashtra. Site rediscovered by John Smith (British officer) in 1819. Earliest caves Satavahana-era (~2c BCE); most paintings Vakataka/post-Gupta (~5c CE). PYQ #134 tests precisely this river-gorge fact.

gap_amaravati_krishna.label: Amaravati stupa — Krishna river
gap_amaravati_krishna.subject: history
gap_amaravati_krishna.detail: Amaravati Mahastupa stands on the south bank of the KRISHNA river (not Godavari — PYQ #134 trap) in present-day Andhra Pradesh. A major Mahasanghika-patronized Buddhist center (see Dhanyakataka = ancient name of Amaravati), Satavahana-era origin with extensions under the Ikshvakus. Its carved limestone marbles were famously removed in the 19c — many in the British Museum and the Chennai Government Museum. Often named in PYQs alongside Nagarjunakonda as twin Andhra Buddhist sites on the Krishna.

gap_southeast_asia_pivot_3_4c.label: 3-4c CE maritime pivot to SE Asia
gap_southeast_asia_pivot_3_4c.subject: history
gap_southeast_asia_pivot_3_4c.detail: From ~3c CE onwards, the collapse of Roman demand (weakening of the Red Sea / Mediterranean trade axis) and instability on the overland Silk Route (Hun incursions from 4-5c) pushed Indian merchants to redirect toward Southeast Asia — the lands collectively called Suvarnabhumi ('Land of Gold' = Malay Peninsula, Java, Sumatra, lower Myanmar/Thailand) and Suvarnadvipa (island archipelago). This pivot seeded the later Hindu-Buddhist 'Indianized' kingdoms of SE Asia (Funan, Champa, Srivijaya, early Khmer). Note: the PYQ's phrasing 'Hun invasion ended the Roman Empire' is historically loose — but the answer it tests (South-East Asian trade) is correct.

gap_dhanyakataka.label: Dhanyakataka (ancient Amaravati)
gap_dhanyakataka.subject: history
gap_dhanyakataka.detail: Ancient name of Amaravati (on the Krishna in Andhra Pradesh), a prominent Buddhist center flourishing under Mahasanghika patronage. Strong Satavahana and later Ikshvaku association. Kalachakra-tradition Buddhism holds the Buddha preached the Kalachakra Tantra here.

gap_sthaviravada_theravada.label: Sthaviravada = Theravada
gap_sthaviravada_theravada.subject: history
gap_sthaviravada_theravada.detail: Sthaviravada ('Way of the Elders') is the Sanskrit name for what is preserved today as Theravada Buddhism (the Pali-canon tradition of Sri Lanka and mainland SE Asia). NOT a form of Mahayana — it is one of the two original schools that emerged from the early schism (Sthaviravada vs Mahasanghika ~4c BCE). PYQ #213 tests the error 'Sthaviravadins belong to Mahayana' — which is WRONG.

gap_lokottaravadin.label: Lokottaravadin (Mahasanghika sub-sect)
gap_lokottaravadin.subject: history
gap_lokottaravadin.detail: A sub-sect that branched off from the Mahasanghika school of early Buddhism. The name means 'those who hold (the Buddha) to be supramundane (lokottara)' — they emphasized the Buddha's transcendent, trans-worldly nature, prefiguring later Mahayana Buddhology. Their best-known surviving text is the Mahavastu (a hybrid Sanskrit biographical compendium of the Buddha). PYQ #213 statement 2 'Lokottaravadin sect was an offshoot of Mahasanghika' is CORRECT.

gap_sanchi_vidisha_hill.label: Sanchi Stupa — Vidisha hill
gap_sanchi_vidisha_hill.subject: history
gap_sanchi_vidisha_hill.detail: Sanchi stupa complex sits on a HILL near Vidisha (Madhya Pradesh) — NOT in any river gorge (PYQ #134 distractor: 'Chambal river gorge' is wrong). Founded under Ashoka (3c BCE), enlarged under the Shungas (2c BCE) and later — the famous gateways (toranas) are Satavahana-era. Ashoka's queen Devi was from Vidisha, explaining early royal patronage here.

gap_pandu_lena_godavari.label: Pandu-Lena (Nashik) caves
gap_pandu_lena_godavari.subject: history
gap_pandu_lena_godavari.detail: Pandu-Lena (also Pandavleni / Trirashmi) — ~24 rock-cut Buddhist caves near NASHIK in Maharashtra. Situated in the GODAVARI river catchment (not Narmada — PYQ #134 distractor). Early caves Satavahana and Kshaharata (Nahapana) period, 2c BCE to 3c CE; important inscriptions of Gautamiputra Satakarni and Ushavadata.

gap_korkai.label: Korkai (Pandyan pearl-port)
gap_korkai.subject: history
gap_korkai.detail: Sangam-age Pandyan port on the south-east Tamil Nadu coast (near the Vaigai delta / Gulf of Mannar), famous for pearl diving and chank fishery. Forms the Sangam-era port-city trio with Puhar / Poompuhar (Chola capital-port at the Kaveri mouth, founded by Karikala) and Muchiri / Muziris (Chera, on the Periyar / Kerala coast; Romans kept two regiments there). Three different coasts, three different kingdoms — the PYQ tests whether you can pair each port to its dynasty.

gap_taxila_location.label: Taxila location (Indus-Jhelum)
gap_taxila_location.subject: history
gap_taxila_location.detail: Ancient Takshasila (Taxila) sat in the Indus-Jhelum doab (present-day Rawalpindi district, Punjab, Pakistan) — NOT on the Ganga-Yamuna doab (PYQ #85 distractor). Capital of the Gandhara mahajanapada; an ancient learning centre on the Uttarapatha trade route linking the Ganga plain to Bactria and Central Asia. Once an Achaemenid Persian satrapy, later visited by Alexander (326 BCE) and absorbed by Chandragupta Maurya.

gap_devabhuti.label: Devabhuti (last Shunga)
gap_devabhuti.subject: history
gap_devabhuti.detail: Last Shunga king (r. ~83-73 BCE), assassinated by his Brahmana minister Vasudeva — who then founded the Kanva dynasty (Harshacharita account). The pattern parallels Pushyamitra Shunga's earlier overthrow of the last Maurya Brihadratha: a minister toppling a weak king to start a new line. Per the Puranas, ten Shunga kings ruled ~112 years in total; remnants of Shunga rule may have lingered in central India till the Satavahanas rose.

gap_vishti_gupta.label: Vishti (Gupta forced labour)
gap_vishti_gupta.subject: history
gap_vishti_gupta.detail: Gupta-period vishti was forced / unpaid labour owed to the state by peasants and artisans, treated as a form of revenue alongside land tax (bhaga) and customs. A recognized royal prerogative, not a private feudal exaction — though the distinction blurred in the early-medieval period as vishti rights were transferred to land-grant beneficiaries. Later texts (Narada Smriti) distinguish categories and durations. Traceable earlier to Mauryan usage but institutionalized under the Guptas.

gap_bhaja_caves.label: Bhaja Caves (Pune)
gap_bhaja_caves.subject: history
gap_bhaja_caves.detail: Rock-cut Buddhist caves near Pune, Maharashtra — Satavahana-era, ~2c BCE. Among the earliest Hinayana (Theravada-lineage) rock-cut monasteries in India; contains a chaitya hall with imitation wooden rafters in stone (showing the transition from wooden to stone architecture) and a cluster of viharas. Paired with nearby Karla caves (where Vashishthiputra Pulumavi left donative inscriptions) and Pitalkhora as a western-ghat cluster of early rock-cut sites.

gap_bagh_caves.label: Bagh Caves (MP, Gupta paintings)
gap_bagh_caves.subject: history
gap_bagh_caves.detail: Rock-cut Buddhist caves in Dhar district, Madhya Pradesh, Gupta-era (~5-6c CE). Along with Ajanta, one of only two well-known surviving examples of Gupta-period cave mural painting — the PYQ asks which of the only two it is. Paintings have suffered severe damage (climate + 19c neglect); modern copies preserved at Gwalior Archaeological Museum. Rediscovered 1818. Palette and style close to Ajanta's Mahayana-period murals.

gap_panini_dating.label: Panini (5-4c BCE grammarian)
gap_panini_dating.subject: history
gap_panini_dating.detail: 5-4c BCE Sanskrit grammarian from Shalatura (in Gandhara) — PRE-Mauryan — whose Ashtadhyayi codified classical Sanskrit grammar in ~4000 sutras. Traditionally placed before Alexander's invasion. Distinct in time from Patanjali (2c BCE, Mahabhashya) who was contemporary of Pushyamitra Shunga. The PYQ-#183 trap 'Panini is associated with Pushyamitra' is wrong — that's Patanjali. Panini preserves an older grammatical tradition building on Yaska's Nirukta.

gap_sthanakvasi.label: Sthanakvasi (Shvetambara sub-sect)
gap_sthanakvasi.subject: history
gap_sthanakvasi.detail: Non-idol-worshipping reformist sub-sect WITHIN Shvetambara Jainism (not Digambara — PYQ #216 trap). Emerged ~17c as a revival / purification movement, building on the 15c reformist Lonka Shah's anti-idolatry teachings. Name from 'sthanaka' (prayer hall), since they worship in plain halls rather than idol-housing temples. Later spawned its own 18c reformist sub-branch — the Jain Shvetambara Terapanth of Acharya Bhikshu (distinct from the Digambara Terapanth sub-sect).

gap_nirvana_blow_out.label: Nirvana as 'blowing out' of tanha
gap_nirvana_blow_out.subject: history
gap_nirvana_blow_out.detail: Buddhist Nirvana is literally the 'blowing out' / extinction of the flame of craving (tanha) — cessation of desire, aversion, and ignorance, ending the cycle of rebirth (samsara). NOT annihilation of a self (Buddhism denies an eternal self via the anatta doctrine), but extinction of the fires that perpetuate suffering. Goal of the Four Noble Truths / Eightfold Path. Parinirvana is the final release at death of an arhat.

gap_padmapani.label: Padmapani (Avalokiteshvara epithet)
gap_padmapani.subject: history
gap_padmapani.detail: 'Padmapani' = 'lotus-bearer', an epithet and iconographic form of the Bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara in Mahayana Buddhism; depicted holding a blue lotus (utpala). The 5-6c CE Ajanta Cave 1 'Bodhisattva Padmapani' mural is the definitive iconic representation, paired on the opposite wall with Bodhisattva Vajrapani. Avalokiteshvara evolved later into Guanyin (China) and Chenrezig (Tibet). One of the eight great Bodhisattvas of Mahayana.

gap_lokayata_charvaka.label: Lokayata / Charvaka materialism
gap_lokayata_charvaka.subject: history
gap_lokayata_charvaka.detail: Materialist / atheist school of ancient Indian philosophy. Charvaka expounded it; 'Lokayata' means 'ideas derived from the common people (loka)'. Denies afterlife, divine agency, Vedic authority, and the efficacy of rituals — accepts only perception (pratyaksha) as a valid means of knowledge. Classed with Buddhism and Jainism as a nastika (heterodox) school that rejects Vedic authority. The Ajivikas (another heterodox sect contemporary with the Buddha) also carried materialist strands. Associated Barhaspatya Sutras survive only in fragments.

gap_pradeshika.label: Pradeshika (Ashokan officer)
gap_pradeshika.subject: history
gap_pradeshika.detail: Senior provincial / district officer of the Mauryan (especially Ashokan) administration, responsible for local governance, revenue oversight, and judicial supervision. Under Ashoka's Rock Edict III (regnal year 12), Pradeshikas — along with Rajukas (whose remit covered larger territorial units and justice) and Yuktas (subordinate accountants) — were directed to tour every five years to propagate dhamma.
